9.title: Elaborate, complex, and silently exciting, if slightly tiring, Nolan biopic
9.content: This is the first biopic film Nolan directs, and it truly has a tremendous result! It uses an unconventional way to narrate the events which lead to the rise and fall of one of the most important, complex and brilliant individuals in human history, meaning that the scenes that are centered around Robert Oppenheimer are shot in color, whereas the scenes exploring the life and actions of Lewis Strauss, president of the U. S. Atomic Energy Commission (played by the astonishing Robert Downey Jr.) are shot in black-and-white. It really sags a bit at some points, and there's almost too much characters, too much information and too many facts, not to mention special quantum physics' knowledge which may go over some viewers' heads (me included!), but in general it's a gripping, layered biographic film that makes it to keep you on the edge of your seat at some moments! It shows us how the development of the A-bomb affects the titular character in every aspect of his life (in social, professional, mental and interpersonal level). We get to see that Oppenheimer was a communist, extremely unfaithful, but above all a bright mind that had the power to make something dangerously powerful and destructive. This movie raises some interesting moral questions about the latter, especially when somebody doesn't know the scope of the impact the object he's developing will have to the world. As I see it, the most memorable quote from this picture is the line Einstein speaks to Oppy near the end: "If your country, which you have served so well, rewards you this way, turn your back on them!", or something like that. Also, the surrealistic scenes showing Oppenheimer fantasizing (among others) about the devastating effects the toss of the atomic bomb must have had on the residents of the cities only add to the film's odd charm and anti-nuclear weapons' message, which is primarily gotten across by the gradual provocation of a sense of fear to the viewers towards them. Cillian Murphy's performance is a masterclass in acting, making him the odds-on actor for the Academy Award for Best Actor, (it's even enriched with close-ups on his pale but beautiful face!), Emily Blunt is great as Kitty Oppenheimer, a smart woman whose brightness went to waste due to the societal position of the women in general, Florence Pugh stands out as the well-known psychiatrist Jean Tatlock, who had an affair with Robert Oppenheimer while he was married and Matt Damon is really convincing as the rough general Leslie Groves, a high-ranking member of the U. S. Atomic Energy Commission who pays a lot of attention to the success of the Manhattan Project. The sex scenes between Oppenheimer and the contextually woman are essential, in my opinion, and transfuse heat to his relationships with them, and they are tasteful without being explicit. Finally, the Trinity Test sequence is suspenseful and exciting, making you unable to take your eyes away from the screen. This motion picture demands to be seen on the big screen, and is recommended not only to Nolan fans, but also to the ones who want to have a «first meeting» with him, and to the ones who want to watch a biographic film different from the others, as well. It's sure to be one of the highest contenders for many of the categories of this year's Academy Awards (especially in the basic categories!).

9.title: The road to hell is paved with good intentions.
9.content:
Oppenheimer is a biographical film about Robert Oppenheimer, one of those brilliant physicists who created the nuclear bomb. Sadly, a very relevant and topical movie.

The basic moral of the movie is that the road to Hell is paved with good intentions. A story about a brilliant mind who has created something horrifying, and who is trying to come to terms/cope with the consequences of what he has done. Throughout the movie there is a subtle message that such destructive power should never have fallen into the hands of man, the most violent and bloodthirsty creature on the planet. People often don't appreciate the consequences of their actions and only when confronted with them do they realize what they've made a mess of. It was really bitter to see how joyfully the people who had a hand in the creation of the nuclear bomb reacted to every success in this way, thinking that by doing so they would put an end to WWII. Most of them didn't realize that they were opening a Pandora's Box that would change the world forever and likely cause its destruction.

The most painful episode for me was how cynically and routinely the politicians and military chose bombing targets. The movie showed us once again how dirty the politicians play and that they will use and destroy anyone they can get their hands on for their ambition, revanchism, greed and lust for power. What was even more painful was how brilliantly the propaganda of the time worked, that it wasn't until decades later that people realized how horrible those events were. However, some people still don't realize it.

In addition to the plot component, the brilliant performance of Cillian Murphy, who with his facial expressions alone conveyed all those emotions raging inside his character, caught my eye. He pulled all three hours of timing due to his unreal charisma, although the rest of the cast of the movie was also on top, but even among such mastodons that Nolan gathered, Murphy stood out brightly. I've had no doubt since 28 Days Later that he's a talent, but here he delivered something phenomenal. If he doesn't get a Best Actor Oscar, then screw the Academy.

The visuals, soundtrack and direction are brilliant as always, but I didn't doubt it knowing those who worked on the project. While I really missed my favorite Nolan-Zimmer tandem, Ludwig Göransson didn't let down either.

As a bottom line, a brilliant movie, unequivocally the best movie of 2023. This movie is heavy, relevant, and meant for thoughtful viewing. Christopher Nolan is one of my all-time favorite directors and he has once again pulled it off.

9.title: Subject Matter versus Art
9.content:
Thousands have evaluated this film, most finding it good or outstanding. Although it was a bit long and slow at times, the cerebral nature of what went on in Los Alamos was painstaking and filled with risk. Oppenheimer was a great physicist and, despite his taciturn qualities, was able to motivate scientists with his competency. War was raging. Hitler was on the skids and the Russians were the last straw for him and the Nazis. But Japan had attacked Pearl Harbor and were steadfast in their "fight to the last man" mentality. The Emperor was not going to give up. Americans were tired of war and new that more of their sons would pay a huge price. Conventional warfare probably would have taken much longer. The thing with Oppenheimer and his people, for a time it was nearly a game, putting the pieces together until they built the thing. The incredible affect on lives by such a monster wasn't being discussed. The Russians were being ignored as to their capacity, for the most part. Then, of course, Teller comes forward with the hydrogen bomb and put forth the possibility that much of the earth's population was in jeopardy. Oppenheimer was the architect and took all the blows for act against humanity when, indeed, the politicians (Harry Truman included) were the perpetrators, if you will.

The last third of the film involves the "trial" of Oppenheimer. Because he voiced his opinions about disarmament and detente and the lack of need for an H-bomb, he was persecuted by his own country. The political world we live in right now is full of crass politicians who have no respect for the people of this country. I hope that one them isn't going to decide to use something that could spell armageddon.

9.title: Cubism Lends itself to Ingenious Historical Accuracy
9.content:
Oppenheimer takes on a very difficult job, to accurately illustrate a complex man who must reconcile his love for theoretical physics and scientific discovery with his fear of being the American Prometheus, capable of giving the country he loves the power to destroy itself.

Nolan takes a cubist approach to formulate a depiction of Oppenheimer with many sides and many faces. For the majority of the movie, we observe the world subjectively through his eyes. However, at times we also observe the world from the point of view of his bitter rival, Lewis Strauss (Robert Downey Jr.).

At a critical moment in the movie, Strauss gives a fiery monologue about the man he sees Oppenheimer to be, and we are left wondering what to believe about who the man truly was. Nolan commonly uses this tool of unanswerable, ambiguous, cliffhanging questions to invite discussion amongst his audiences.

There is merit to the historical accuracy of Nolan portraying Oppenheimer as Pablo Picasso portrays The Old Guitarist or as William Faulker portrays Thomas Sutpen in Absalom! Absalom! In a work published in 1973 by Hayden White titled Metahistory: The Historical Imagination in Nineteenth-century Europe, White argues that the way a historical event is told is more valuable to any given culture or society than its truthfulness and accuracy. The stories that prevail are the ones that are interesting. Historiography is also inherently reductive, he writes, because it charges historians with creating simple cause and effect relationships that explain history in an understandable way.

In Oppenheimer, Nolan's account of history includes a full breadth of points of view, indescribable emotions and ambiguity. He offers both objective facts of history and subjective character viewpoints, leaving us with inconclusive ideas of who J. Robert Oppenheimer really was. We are tasked with making our own decisions as to who he was because, as Nolan highlights, nobody can really say for sure.

9.title: Triumphant, Tragic, and Explosive
9.content:
Written by Ian Chandler - July 21, 2023

Film director Christopher Nolan's "Oppenheimer" is one of his most ambitious projects yet. From the fact that it is not a sci-fi thriller to it being Nolan's first R-rated picture in over two decades, "Oppenheimer" is quite experimental for Christopher Nolan, who happens to be a very experimental filmmaker. Even so, the film has plenty of his trademark methods, including a strange, but effective way of playing with time itself. Even more impressive is his commitment to minimizing VFX shots and shooting every frame using expensive IMAX film. Though many will not have the pleasure to see it in its 70mm glory, it is still great to see a modern motion picture sticking with it. Additionally, the film manages to feel just as massive in scope despite being a gripping drama rather than an action-packed thriller.

J. Robert Oppenheimer, played by Cillian Murphy, is a complex character who expresses so many emotions in the film without going overboard. His behavior is never extreme, with that said, he can be considered the most emotional person on the Manhattan project. Speaking of the Manhattan project, the film achieves something not often seen in movies: the lead character does not get all of the credit for the mission. No, he does not figure out every formula needed for the A-bomb. No, he is not responsible for the idea of a hydrogen bomb. He works with other fellow scientists as a team to create a devastating weapon in desperate times. This includes strong performances from Matt Damon, Alden Ehrenreich, Kenneth Branagh, and more. The blood-pumping "Trinity" test is impressive as a piece of storytelling, a representation of history, and as a sequence of stellar practical effects.

His scientific projects are not the only aspects showcased in "Oppenheimer." His relationships with Jean Tatlock (Florence Pugh) and Kitty (Emily Blunt) are explored several times throughout the film. Tatlock's complicated story with Oppenheimer is interesting, but in some ways distracting. Not to be prude here, but some interactions could be seen as needlessly edgy instead of fascinating due to the decision of the characters' nude bodies being shown for an extensive period. Not only does it encourage immodest behavior from the audience, but it also will distract many from the film as it is an adult drama that happens to contain two scenes that are gratuitous and uncomfortable. It would be preferable for Nolan to focus more on Tatlock's dialogue than her breasts. A removal for the explicit content does not mean that Oppenheimer's sexual life should be removed entirely, as it is important to his character later on. The film, simply put, would feel more mature if it were to be less vulgar; perhaps shoulders and up would keep the tension alive without making some of the viewers feel like perverts. Finally, this wouldn't be so distracting if it weren't for the fact that the rest of the film is at a PG-13 level. Kitty's relationship with Oppenheimer is a more gripping story and a better showcase of an independent woman from the 1940s. She's hot-tempered, but strong in her opinions, especially in the film's final hour. Emily Blunt's performance as the character is a solid one, and just about matches Murphy's excellent performance as the film's protagonist.

"Oppenheimer's" score, composed by Ludwig Göransson, is atmospheric and wonderful. Emphasizing on the violin and intensifying the bass levels, the soundtrack enhances the weight of Oppenheimer's actions, emotions, and the events surrounding him. The score alone warrants the film to be seen in theaters, preferably those with the best sound equipment. "Ground Zero" and "Can You Hear the Music" in particular were the ones that stood out to me. Göransson has cemented himself to be among the greatest film composers such as Hans Zimmer and Thomas Newman.

A major part of the film happens to be about shifting perspectives, which is told by changing between black-and-white and color. It is best to experience its purpose upon viewing the film instead of reading it from a review. If one is quite rusty with their WWII history, the film may be a bit daunting to follow; however, if one is aware about the basics, such as when mentioned U. S. presidents were in office, then the rapidly changing time-periods should not be a problem to keep track of. Robert Downy Jr. May have played his best performance yet as Lewis Strauss. If this review were to provide more details about his character, it may damper the mystery and complexity of his story before one decides to view it for themselves.

"Oppenheimer" shines not only as a historical biopic, but also as a tense thriller. There is no action (thankfully), but there is constant suspense as well as several characters to care about in this film. If one is a fan of WWII history, a fan of Nolan's filmography, and a fan of cinema, "Oppenheimer" is a wonderful picture that will please them immensely. Please see Oppenheimer's story on how he transformed from a brilliant scientist to a disturbed embodiment of "death, the destroyer of worlds."

Oppenheimer - 89/100 Oppenheimer is a gripping biopic that keeps one interested throughout its three-hour runtime, despite being plagued by occasional, needlessly vulgar scenes.

A ridiculous achievement in filmmaking. An absurdly immersive and heart-pounding experience. Cillian Murphy is a stud and RDJ will be a front-runner for Best Supporting Actor. T seems the aim here is to probe Oppenheimer and understand him, his character, his motivations, his conscience. And the film largely finds that elusive, even though he is clearly tormented over his role in mass death.

There is an incredible sequence in the middle(?) that, to me, is worth the price of admission alone: when Oppenheimer has to give a speech to a raucous crowd after the bombs are dropped. It's THE sequence of the movie to me (I guess it has to be 2nd only to the bomb test), and I would even go so far as to say it's one of the best sequences of Nolan's career. A nightmarish short film in and of itself.

Performances across the board are impressive. Cillian was born to play this role. Bennie Sadie's Edward Teller is a standout.

Overall, it's an impressive piece of work. I just don't share the fascination with some of the details Nolan chose to focus on. I think as a meditation on empire and atrocity it doesn't reveal or explore any new depths in the way I was hoping it would. But maybe I was expecting too much.

9.title: The tragic story of a genius doomed by his discovery
9.content: Christopher Nolan narrates in this drama the rise and fall of the physicist Robert Oppenheimer, author of the atomic bomb that was dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki. It is a well written and directed movie with acceptable performances. Of course, due to the 3 hours duration and the amount of dialogues it has, it can be heavy. The entire film recounts the process of creating the bomb during World War II and how Oppenheimer later had to deal with serious charges and incriminations after opposing the use of his discovery for military purposes. It is a story of a man who discovered something powerful, but in the wrong hands it could be dangerous to many human lives. In many respects it is a tragic story of a prodigious genius who was cursed by his discovery. Oppenheimer is a fascinating historical film about the mind behind one of the most catastrophic events in human history and how this brilliant mind was doomed by it. My final rating for this movie is 9/10.

9.title: Oppenheimer: The Ethical Paradox of Creation and Destruction
9.content:
"Oppenheimer," directed by Christopher Nolan, is a cinematic tapestry that weaves together complex moral threads and the stark realities of scientific pursuit against the looming shadow of global conflict. It's a biographical drama, but also so much more: a meditation on the seductive allure of knowledge and the heavy burden of its consequences.

Cillian Murphy, as J. Robert Oppenheimer, delivers a riveting performance, encapsulating the profound nuances of a man caught between his groundbreaking scientific endeavors and their chilling implications. The cast, comprising Emily Blunt, Matt Damon, and a particularly striking Robert Downey Jr. As Louis Strauss, presents an intricate array of characters, each adding depth to the narrative through exceptional performances.

The film's sound design is a character in its own right. With a less-is-more approach, it utilizes silence and carefully chosen sounds to create an immersive experience. The lack of constant musical score makes every footstep, whisper, and breath feel significant, enhancing the intensity of the storytelling.

Through the lens of Oppenheimer's life, the film delves into the intricate web of politics, loyalty, betrayal, and the relentless quest for progress. It grapples with the dichotomy of the destructive power of the atomic bomb and the optimistic drive of scientific discovery. Nolan deftly balances these elements, crafting a historical recount that is both intellectually engaging and emotionally resonant.

Nolan's "Oppenheimer" does not seek to pass judgment but instead offers a platform for contemplation. It's a film that resonates on multiple levels - as a piece of history, a commentary on human nature, and a reflection on the price of genius. The cinematic experience is as complex and challenging as its subject, leaving audiences to ponder the moral dilemmas posed by technological advancement. This is not a film to be taken lightly; it demands attention and thought, and in doing so, achieves a level of storytelling that is as profound as it is provocative.

9.title: Oppenheimer Could Be A Darker Knight
9.content:
There are few people who as individuals make an indelible mark on history, for good or evil here is one of them. Perhaps good and evil are labels we apply after events, and while they are in train they just are what they are. Oppenheimer changed the world forever, the all-in world we live in today.

The film is a dense and intimate character study of a towering historical figure, one that is part saviour and part devil. Critically Nolan lets the viewer decide which is which.

There are moments where you feel Oppenheimer is going to descend into the pit of madness - in fact he spends a decent part of the film skirting its edges and peering into the abyss while somehow managing not to fall in. Nolan conveys this inner chaos with the masterful use of camera work, vision, sound, and pacing.

It's not a perfect film. Some of Oppenheimer's more egregious failings such as his womanising are given a very gentle brush and some of his enemies are a little too one dimensional. Also, I would like to have seen Emily Blunt's character given more air, her performance is amazing, but I suspect a little too much of it was left on the cutting room floor.

Towards the end we witness Oppenheimer's redemption after a sustained and malicious character destruction by Lewis Strauss play brilliantly by Robert Downey Jr who almost steals the show with his shamelessly corrupt and self-serving ambition.

Oppenheimer made a lot of choices on behalf of humanity, the film asks were they the right ones, the moral ones, the only ones that could be made given the circumstances? Even with the benefit of hindsight there is no clear answer, those choices are still controversial and will probably remain so forever.

Nolan reminds us that we all live in the moment and choices have consequences - some bigger than others.

9.title: Nolan's does it great - But I'm dissapointed
9.content:
Oppenheimer is a film that does what it wants to do amazingly immersive. The first part is an character study, the second part dwells around the trinity test and is shot in an kind of eerie almost horrific way, the soundtrack makes the trinity test even more horrifying, and the third part is a court drama. I was fascinated by the character of Oppenheimer and the chemistry and physics behind the bomb in the first two parts, I wanted to learn a lot more after every scene, but the third part left me cold.

The whole build-up to the detonation was heart-pounding, Ludwig Göransson's score builds that tension so high, I was scared for that bang and shockwave. But there is no terror in the bang, only in the anticipation of it.

The world since then never was and will be the same. The film has two or three scenes after the detonation that give off that feeling of desperation, guilt and regret, but not enough to really empathize or understand Oppenheimer. The scene with the stamping foots is breathtaking, but it's not enough.

I wanted to feel the catastrophic natural effects the bomb brings within, I wanted to see how horrifying a detonation is. But Nolan doesn't understand, it's not the fire that's horrifying, it's the consequences on the ground. The people, the animals, the plants, everything gets vanished or horribly devastated in seconds. And even Hours, days, months later, the ground and people do not recover, it gets even worse. Horrible pain surrounds the whole explosion Radius even months after it's detonation. And it expands through the wind.

After my viewing, I had a scene In mind. A young mother is bringing her child to school, it's her first school day. The mother and daughter are happy and smile, they talk about daily things they need to do. Then the sirens start, and people start to run away and scream, and nobody knows what is going to come now, the daughter sees the fireball in it's glory, high and bright, she looks right into it and is amazed by it. It's coming closer towards her, the sound gets louder and louder as more the shockwave and fire approaches. They try to run away, but this is there end. There's no place to hide. Then there is another boy which tries to run away, he's more away from the explosion, and has more time, but still the fire gets him, he does not die, he is on the ground burning down, waiting for death. This is real, and it is horrifying.

This is the moment where I realize I don't really care or wanted an courtroom Oppenheimer story, I wanted an personal story about the Father of the Atomic Bomb.

The courtroom part, is an hyper-realistic representation from the world of politics. Nolan could've dived even deeper into the nature of every character that sits there. Which role they've had, which strategy the followed. Some stand beside Oppenheimer, some against him. Some just needed to protect themselves or were forced or convinced to be against him. Everyone with their own background and own reasoning. Just like in real life. And you can't escape that when you're important. Even when you just want to be a physician. There's only one person who could escape that, Albert Einstein.

The switch from color to black and white makes the whole picture even more immersive, and delivers a story that is not one-sided, but rather seen from one more perspective.

But I didn't really care for the Strauss and Oppenheimer Relationship. It's necessary, but it should've been just a tool to deliver what problems the creation of the bomb brings within, like political conflicts, feuds, arms race, and many more.

The scenes I love, are the ones which dwell around the bomb and the consequences. The eerie horror feeling in the trinity test, the aftermath of the bomb.. there's so much greatness. And what it does right for me, Is Nolan at his best.

While I understand Nolan's approach, it's not for me. I still see what is great about this film, but I expected a very different experience. I wanted it to be more personal and intimate.

9.title: Peak Nolan but what's with the sound?
9.content:
This is how to make a biopic of a complex historical figure without boring the audience! Oppenheimer is my most favourite Nolan's movie so far.

The chemistry between the actors is unbelievable, and the visuals are stunning. It's not just wide open spaces of New Mexico, but even elementary particles when Oppenheimer talks about them.

I have to say that after the first part where everyone was a Marxist intellectual, the military were a welcome change. The secondary characters are as memorable as the leads. Everyone praises Murphy's performance for a good reason, but Matt Damon's Groves steals the show as a reluctant bridge between the two worlds on a cat-herding assignment gambling an enormous amount on money in the middle of a war. Brief but ominous appearance of Casey Affleck's Boris Pash is probably one of best parts of the movie. Also memorable, even if small, is Tom Conti's Einstein, with his bit of wisdom, and President Truman, played by unrecognizable Gary Oldman.

One gripe I'm sure I'm not the only one having: after Tenet, you'd think Nolan would fix his sound problems. Most of the time the dialogue is audible, but there are still parts where I caught myself thinking, "what did he just say?"

9.title: 🎬 A Cinematic Masterpiece!💫
9.content:
Christopher Nolan's latest film, Oppenheimer, is an absolute triumph of storytelling and visual artistry. The IMAX experience elevated the already mesmerizing narrative to a whole new level! 🌌

Cillian Murphy's portrayal of the lead character is nothing short of astonishing. He embodies the role with such depth and nuance that an Oscar nod seems inevitable! 🏆

The film's thought-provoking themes and powerful messages left me wishing I could assemble all the world leaders in one giant IMAX theater to share this experience together. #FoodForThought #NolanMagic

If you haven't seen Oppenheimer yet, you're missing out on a true cinematic gem. Prepare to be spellbound and awestruck!

9.title: Watch it TWICE
9.content:
Okay so I watched Oppenheimer twice. The first time in 70mm and to be very honest ... I didn't like it the first time around. I felt it to be slow paced and confusing at times with a lot of things happening at once. It honestly felt like a documentary. However, I also like close to one of the world's 30 cinemas that project the movie in IMAX 70mm and I had booked the tickets a month earlier. When I tried to get a refund and cancel the tickets after watching the movie the first time, the customer service at the cinema said that they couldn't cancel my ticket at the moment, and the cancellation was only possible after the movie had been played and my ticket shouldn't be scanned. So I decided to go again as I thought it was a once in a lifetime experience.

Oh my god, the second time the movie felt awesome. Although I watched it in the best possible way, I certainly like the movie the second time. Catch on the things I missed the first time I really appreciated the cinematography and the direction of the movie. The second time the movie didn't feel at all slow and everything fit in perfectly. I was able to better understand the characters point of view, and what they were thinking.

So I would recommended if possible watch it twice to understand the true beauty Oppenheimer holds. Thanks.

9.title: Arguably the best Nolan movie
9.content: Personally, i think Christopher Nolan is the best director of all time. You have a different experience in each of his movies. The cast is great and this movie was one of my first times seeing Cillian Murphy and he was spectacular to say the least. It felt like every expression had a meaning. His performance will be talked a lot over the years. RDJ stole the show every scene he was in and i wish he got more screen time. Although the movie was dialogue driven every dialogue and every scene was like an action scene courtesy of Nolan. And the music REALLY helped this film given most of the movie was based on dialogues. I'm gonna watch the movie for the second time tomorrow because i couldn't get all the information and couldn't completely understand the film although it was pretty straightforward. There were a lot of stuff to unpack in the movie. I liked it very much and i highly suggest you watch this movie.

9.title: good
9.content:
"Oppenheimer" is an absolute masterpiece that left me in awe from start to finish. Christopher Nolan's direction combined with Cillian Murphy's captivating performance as J. Robert Oppenheimer creates a cinematic experience that is nothing short of extraordinary.

From the stunning visuals to the intricate storytelling, every aspect of this film is meticulously crafted. Nolan's ability to weave together historical events with personal narratives is unparalleled, drawing the audience into Oppenheimer's world and the moral complexities surrounding the development of the atomic bomb.

Murphy's portrayal of Oppenheimer is mesmerizing, capturing both the brilliance and the inner turmoil of the man who played a pivotal role in shaping the course of history. His performance is complemented by a talented ensemble cast who bring depth and authenticity to their respective roles.

But what truly sets "Oppenheimer" apart is its exploration of profound philosophical themes. The film raises thought-provoking questions about science, morality, and the consequences of technological advancement, leaving a lasting impact on the viewer long after the credits roll.

In conclusion, "Oppenheimer" is a cinematic tour de force that pushes the boundaries of storytelling and leaves an indelible mark on the mind and soul. It's a must-see for anyone who appreciates filmmaking at its finest.

9.title: Once you get into the film's Rhythm, its an amazing ride!
9.content:
As the story opens you discover that this is not a "begin here and end there" type of Drama. In fact, it seems to be flying all over the place in time and location. It takes the viewer a few rounds of this type of flashback, "flash-forward," "flash-middle" storytelling to get into the rhythm of this ultimately amazing film about the life of Robert Oppenheimer, who was the director the Manhattan Project that created and unleashed the Atomic bomb on the world, and who was later chastised severely for his early flirts with Communism and various social protests.

The film follows the known history of this man, in it's non-linear style, while delving deep into his highs, his lows, and his inner uncertanties and conflicts. The basic story of Oppenheimer is easily available with a few keystrokes on any computer, but this film gives us the emotion of the man and his contemporaries.

The film is well cast, even to using actors who actually resemble their real-like counterparts. Although it concentrates in Oppenheimer , wonderfully played by Cillian Murphy, with all of his neurotic conflict, the full cast must also be applauded. Matt Damon and Robert Downey Jr's well-know public personas are all but lost in their portrayals of General Leslie Groves, The military man in charge of creating "The Bomb," and Senator Lewis Strauss, a high ranked member of the Atomic Energy Commission who was instrumental in Oppenheimer's difficulties after WWII.

Another major nod goes to Emily Blunt, who plays Oppenheimer's loyal wife though a variety of scandals and praise.

In fact I found no poor performances in this epic story.

The settings are either real, as in the meeting with Albert Einstein (Tom Conti) at Princeton, or in the recreations of the top secret "village," Los Alamos created in New Mexico for the scientists and their families who worked on the Manhattan Project. Most impressive was the recreation of the ignition of the First A-Bomb. The reality of the detonation is eerily spot on!

At nearly 3 hours a film like this might become tedious, but "Oppenheimer" is able to kleep the audience involved throughout!

Well worth the price of the ticket.

9.title: How can you live with blood-stained hands?
9.content:
Last Sunday, I immersed myself in the darkness of the cinema to experience "Oppenheimer." While on an immense screen, the detonation of a nuclear bomb unfolded, outside, my country (Argentina) convulsed due to the crossroads of choosing its future leader.

But in that cinematic dimness, I delved in like a child with a new toy, without prejudices, but (I won't deny) with high expectations. It's not my habit to pen down such reflections, but when Christopher Nolan unveils a new work, I feel compelled to rush to the theater.

Although my preference usually leans towards original plots, this movie achieved what only a few visual works have managed to do to me: genuine wonder. I left the cinema clouded by astonishment, and as the minutes passed, my obsession to absorb every flash of information, both within and beyond the film, grew in a logarithmic progression, like atomic reactions that release the energy contained in uranium nuclei.

I've fought in vain against the irresistible attraction, for I find myself inexorably drawn to everything surrounding this immersive story.

Your mind is brilliant, the bloody future undeniable and unstoppable. What would you do if a slightly less bloody future depended on your ingenuity? Inevitably withdrawing from the race would probably lead to a worse outcome. I believe these questions are what J. Robert Oppenheimer faced when he was summoned to the development of the Manhattan Project.

Though my question as the minutes ticked away was: How can you live with blood-stained hands?

Perhaps for someone seeking a blast on a giant screen, the movie might seem like mere ClickBait, but if we understand that we live in the world we do due to the repercussions of Hahn and Strassmann's 1939 article on nuclear fission, we will perceive this film as a gem of modern cinema.

It's marvelous to see how the puzzle of history comes together for those of us who didn't live in that time to tell the tale. Germany surrendered, the battles had ended, but a very bloody chapter remained, if not the bloodiest one to be told.

Three hours that pass like a handful of minutes if you're interested in the history and geopolitical context of the era, and a masterpiece deserving of all possible awards, as everything related to the film is worth highlighting.

9.title: Could be Nolans Magnum Opus
9.content: This could easily be Nolans best work yet or ever. The only nit pick I have is the audio mixing with music and dialogue that Nolan has struggled with in his past couple movies, is still a slight problem here. Other than that, the casting (Cillian and RDJ are oscar bound), epic music, dialogue, cinematography, storytelling is all a masterpiece. THIS IS NOT A MOVIE ABOUT THE ATOMIC BOMB. ITS ABOUT OPPENHEIMER. Nolan tells the story of oppenheimers insane life pre, post and during the war to perfection and Cillian Murphy makes you feel everything he went through along the way. At no point did I feel like the movie was dragging because it has a breakneck pace that could be tiring but it keeps you glued to the screen. If you don't give yourself the chance to see this movie in theaters (IMAX preferably), you are robbing yourself of an opportunity to see one of the most important movies in recent memory.

9.title: Physics
9.content: After watching this, I regretted not continuing science studies. The inner conflict any scientist may face is explained well. The loyalty towards one's country, the amount of time and effort to create a reputation, the amount of time that it takes to destroy, years of worth scientific research and seeing the after effect it will bring, how it affect one's mentality, how hard one can have hatred feeling to another, all these depicted well. The salvation Oppenheimer was looking for may be the same for many. Really great cinematography, amazing background music, good character selection, really great location. It showed a whole new world of Physics. Would love to recommend it to anyone who is interested in Physics and WWII.

9.title: Oppenheimer .... The destroyer of worlds
9.content:
Oppenheimer..... Nolan masterwork

May be the best anxiety inducing music and claustrophobic inducing photography I ever witnessed

You feel all of the horror and the weight of guilt and emotions of Murphy , the score will hit your soul so hard like a bomb , you will be crushed under tension.

Everybody waiting for bomb explode , but the bomb not the star , here , it was everything else in this movie may be the best biography movie I ever watched

The cast did an amazing job portraying every character

I will not forget the early flickering light and atoms scenes in the beginning of the movie ,So good

I wish everyone enjoy this masterpiece as I did.

9.title: In terms of Non -Ganster or Celebrity Biopics
9.content:
This was historically accurate, though long by the 80 minute mark you are sucked in.

If you know WWII history well, There are a few large and small characters to look up.

I steamed the film I'm sure the visuals were stunning. You must at least know Strauss's background until he was the head of the Atomic Energy commission. After that wait for the film.

I've read moronic statements not displaying Hiroshima...that wasn't what the film's objective. Which was Oppenheimers live, his brilliance a bit of social Naivety and he wasn't out of control but he did not pick women well. And he assumed the best of people.

He carried guilt for years that's speculation. But based on Brittanica and segments of his kangaroo Court.

Truman decided to do that...with the ongoing carpet bombing the US government killed a lot more civilians from a decimated country just to attain an unconditional surrender.

There are psychological components that Nolan would associate just with the way he conducted himself.

Taking away Gangster Biopics.

Entertainment wise not as Good as The Aviator, Catch Me if you can, or what I feel the best Biopic ever SERPICO.

Again I'm leaving out Athletes, Singers etc.

9.title: Megaton Drama!
9.content:
Oppenheimer: This film was everything I expected it to be. An exploration of the man within a divided scientific community during WW2 in the backdrop of a nuclear arms race between the Axis and Allied powers and then between the US and Russia. But that's only half of the essence of the film, the other half is the politics behind this race which leads to the rise and fall and then rise of Oppenheimer in the corridors of power in America. There is more courtroom drama than science drama. The screenplay and treatment with which the various periods are juxtaposed make it feel like JFK by Oliver Stone, who incidentally was close to making a movie about Oppenheimer.

Nolan's vision is as grand as ever in his first biopic. Breathtaking shots, surreal haunting music that's always on in the background, and big cinematic moments are peppered generously throughout this 3-hour+ epic. But I think it's his simplest, most straightforward film yet, even though it makes no effort to explain physics and chemistry concepts, the gravity of situations, and the motives of the characters involved. That's where the brilliant actors come in. You don't need to know anything about that era and still, you will feel the tension in the air and understand the stakes involved.

People with a background in STEM or an interest in US history can understand and appreciate the movie better.

I loved Cillian Murphy and he's a deserved lead and excellent as always, but Robert Downey Jr. Stole the show with his performance as a saboteur politician. All the other actors were top-notch as well.

Ludwig Goransson looks like he's the next Hans Zimmer with his eerie rumbling score.

Coming to the events of the film and how things were portrayed, there is a lot of American exceptionalism and naivete on Oppenheimer's part after the atomic bombs were dropped on Japan. There's a clear attempt to whitewash his reputation as a scientist just making a bomb for science's sake and thinking they're never gonna use it.

Having said that, it's still a cracking film and worth the wait to watch in IMAX. 9/10.

9.title: One of Nolans most mature films yet
9.content:
While there was barely dialogue and mostly action in "Dunkirk", Nolan took almost the opposite approach for "Oppenheimer". The (for Nolan) unusual amount of dialog scenes are handled surprisingly well and allows most of the cast to really shine. Cillian Murphy gives, in my opinion, the best performance in a Nolan movie since Heath Ledger. Benny Safdie surprised me his fantastic portrait and Robert Downey Jr. Really proved his chops as a charismatic actor who can also go deep.

I personally felt most involved with the moral questions the story and the building of the bomb. The movie seemed to hit a climactic peak after the testing of the bomb and its use in Japan. I expected the film to end soon after but at least 30 more minutes were spend showing court room discussions about Oppenheimers conflict with Lewis Strauss, which I felt could have been wrapped up sooner. Especially when Nolan used the same effect twice and showed Oppenheimer imagining the catastrophic consequences of the impact of his bomb for the second time, I felt like the movie had lost some of its momentum and tried to build it up again for the fantastic ending, that could have happened sooner.

The court room stretch at the end is the only negative that comes to mind. Cutting between court scenes for 30 minutes and underscoring it with a soundtrack that seemed to copy some of Zimmer's Inception Themes felt like lesser filmmaking that I'm used to from Nolan. I've seen more exciting scenes in most court room dramas.

In general Oppenheimer is one of Nolans most mature films that tells an unbelievably important story extremely well. Its the first time I walked out of a Nolan movie thinking less about his style and craft but more about the performances and story, which in this case, is a compliment.

9.title: A movie made for theaters
9.content:
Everything goes in line here. Acting, directing, scenes, music, ambient, effects both visual and sound. This review is subjective as I watched the movie in cinema and it impressed me a bit more that if I'd watched it at home (I think so). Regardless, the reason I did not give this movie a 10 is that I would hardly if ever watch it for another time. It just doesn't make sense to rewatch. It should be felt as live experience occuring only once, but be prepared - this movie is packed with dialogue.

Some would say overpacked, as it can be dull at times due to the way of portraying the events that had happened, making it seem 'bueracratic' (you will know after watching) without so much of an organic purpose other than 'cheap' exposition...

9.title: Incredibly well written and astonishingly shot
9.content:
A deep-seated reverence for meticulous cinematic production design results in a dazzling world class performance of Christopher Nolan's staggering achievements in this historical biopic masterpiece, which features the philosophical atomic concepts of American theoretical physicist, J. Robert Oppenheimer.

This heavy movie goes straight into 3 hours full of intense dialogue and provokes a deep sense of curiosity. The overall scenario is tragic as it dives into humanity's darkest hour.

Activating mindful focus is highly important. It requires your full attention, as it can easily slip away from an inattentive viewer. Do a little research about the world wars and the characters involved. It would be an addition if you knew quantum mechanical physics theory and how the mechanism of an atomic bomb in simple terms. There is no need to understand, just know.

However, Oppenheimer is more concerned with shifting perspectives related to time. The colour pictures represent Oppenheimer's point of view, while the black and white pictures are the objective view of his story told in the third person.

"Now I am become Death, the destroyer of worlds."

J. Robert Oppenheimer, Father of the atomic bomb.

The world would not be the same.

A fitting end that leaves you staring into oblivion, the most immersive and riveting experiences are encapsulated in movie form.

9.title: What would you do when your dreams go mad?
9.content:
I was born in the late 70s, so my childhood was spent in fear of atomic and nuclear weapons being dropped on my head, even though it was not as intense as those in the generation before me. I knew Mr. Oppenheimer's name, but that was about it. So, going into this movie, I was fascinated to hear his biography, his story and his mistakes that led us to the creation of what could be our annihilation.

Nihilistic isn't this? However, as a scientific mind, I can sympathize with the beginnings of the story. Sometimes you pursue what you cannot stop. You know that a theory can be proven. You know that it will change the world. But, too often, it's not in the way that one would hope. As soon as the science is discovered, and you realize it can be destructive, then perhaps just because you can do something, doesn't mean you should. This sounds a little judgmental, but I only mean that decisions have consequences. I could go into more detail about the feelings of revenge, the lust and focus on all consuming thought, or political bull crap that makes me sometimes lose faith in humanity, but we all know what happened in Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

I gave this movie the full 5 stars, not because it was a heart warming, fun for the whole family romp, but because it was well produced, well written, very well acted, and the story is told. That's what I wanted: to know the story. I even bought the book after I saw the film, because I wanted to delve deeper into the psychology of hyper focus.

9.title: It will never end
9.content:
An insane film, combining typical Nolan traits with a maturity seen very little in recent times. One of the best casts in cinematic history plays those who were the most influential scientists of the 19th century, resulting in a masterpiece.

"As beautiful as it is heavy," one can read on the web. An opinion that can be shared, as upon leaving the theater there remains a sense of bewilderment, of concrete fear, as much as of awareness of having re-experienced what changed humanity.

"The destroyer of worlds" is a cynical but remorseful person, a living contradiction, ultimately a "good" character (or rather, less bad than the others), for whom one builds a certain empathy. Some of the scenes are incredible, goosebumpy. 3 hours that fly by, making you reason about the cruelty of humans but making you understand how, in a way, it was all inevitable: killing lives to save others. A somber thought that has unfortunately become a sad reality.

Oppenheimer changes you. That is the best summary that can be made.

9.title: It was good
9.content: Storyline is quite good. Compared to the films of Christopher Nolan in this movie the coordination, vividity and balance of music/bgm was greatly done. The whole movie from start to end has bgm, only 2min after the scene of bomb there is silence. The time period is shown with minute details. Transition of black and white scenes is a great way to show two scenarios at a time. Scenes and there cuts are wonderfully taken. You will not feel any abrupt shot or moment. Not a single scene is wasted to elongate the movie. Overall the acting of each actor was exceptional especially the protagonist himself 'Cillian Murphy'.

9.title: Phenomenal Account Of The Most Important Part Of Human History
9.content:
Few inventions throughout the history of mankind have been of more consequence than the creation of the nuclear bomb. Robert Oppenheimer is one of few men who single-handedly changed the course of history. This film did a great justice to his legacy.

Christopher Nolan masterfully throws you into the world of 1940s theoretical physics and the lives of these incredibly brilliant scientists, under the backdrop of the most important contest of all time - the race to build the atom bomb. Oppenheimer leading America, Heisenberg leading Germany. For all of the moral dilemmas explored in the film, the bottom line is that if America didn't succeed, our adversaries very well would have. Dropping Little Boy and Fat Man on Japan may have killed hundreds of thousands, but Oppenheimer's work and campaigning may have saved millions and billions over the course of time.

The historical accuracy was incredible, and it was electrifying to see the portrayal of these great minds of science and the choices they were faced with. From the start of the movie, we see Oppenheimer portrayed as a savant that sees a dimension of the world out of reach to the common man, reminding me of John Nash in A Beautiful Mind.

We see the massive investment that went into the Manhattan project, and how much freedom and power FDR gave in the form of a blank check to these scientists, trusting in their process - Hitler, on the other hand, never had the same conviction or investment on the German side. Cillian Murphy gave an Academy award winning performance as the lead role, and was supported by countless terrific performances by other A-list actors.

I am astounded by the amount of effort Nolan invested into the history and science of this film, while still keeping the pace captivating and thrilling. Really outstanding movie, and a refreshing break from the many action-packed, superhero type of movies that drive the box office today. I hope there will be more blockbuster films like this in the future.

9.title: Stunning
9.content:
Wow. This film is just so multifaceted, beautiful, and sublime-it carries an underlying sense of awe, power, and terror that is palpable. Truly a masterpiece. Acting, cinematography, sound, effects, score, writing. Ah, love it.

It seems like people on here think that it was too long, boring, and confusing. That is partly because the vast majority of films that are produced today are just lame mindless shutter-spam. This movie has it all. Characters worth caring about. Problems of a global scale. Decisions that have consequences. Choices that stick. People who are just that: people-the good, the bad, and the ugly.

I highly recommend this film. Honestly, the only thing I wish it didn't have was the nudity. Outside of that, this would be a perfect film in my opinion. I u destined why it has it though. Just not for me.

9.title: Unconventional, but stunning
9.content:
First things first, before seeing this movie, set your expectations straight. You will not see high paced action, you will not see an intriguing plotline, you will not see a conventional movie. Rather you see a master-class in acting from an incredibly talented cast.

Cillian Murphy's acting is nothing short of phenomenal. He was already incredible before I had seen thus movie, but this just confirms it. The amount of emotion you see in his face and eyes can only be experienced not described. His acting alone had me lost in his character, and the psychology of Oppenheimer.

And Nolan's dedication to the art of cinema, recreating the visuals of the explosions without CGI did not go Un noticed, rather knowing that going into the film had me in awe.

I repeat, this film is NOT for most audiences. Do NOT expect what you normally expect from a film, rather have an open mind and observe the incredible acting and cinematography.

9.title: Compelling Narrative Paired with Stunning Visual & Audio Mastery
9.content:
The story, centered on the eponymous protagonist, Oppenheimer, showcases the complexities of human nature brilliantly. The nuances of Oppenheimer's changing attitude before and after the creation of the bomb are worth savoring. They might not conform to typical dramatic patterns, but are truer to reality in my opinion.

The visual and audio effects are on par with Nolan's other films. I highly recommend watching in an IMAX theatre for the best experience.

However, apart from the points mentioned above, the story has a somber tone; it's not a light-hearted or optimistic movie. Also, characters other than Oppenheimer aren't as fleshed out. The second most developed character might be Strauss, but he's not as convincing as Oppenheimer and is far less intriguing. In particular, his righteous aide at the end came across as both annoying and unrealistic.

The above critiques are minor, so I won't dwell on them. For the overall experience: the depiction of the bomb, the insights into humanity's peaks and valleys, and the exceptional visual and audio effects, I give it a 9/10.

9.title: Nolan at this finest
9.content: Nolan's best work since the release of Interstellar. It's a 3 hour long biopic/political drama about J Robert Oppenheimer and Manhattan Project from the beginning of World War 2 to the Cold War. It's a deep dive into the life and mind of Oppenheimer and the circumstances during that era. Some shots are absolutely breathtaking and I'm surprised that not a single one of them was CGI. A true technical achievement. RDJ was absolutely brilliant in every scene he was in as well as other actors. Everyone was cast perfectly. But the jewel in the crown is without a doubt Cillian Murphy. He embodied the role and stole almost every scene he was in with his sheer scene presence and body language. He's definitely getting nominated and possibly winning best actor for this one. Best movie released this year so far.

9.title: Kept me locked in for 3 hours - Nolan is a hero
9.content:
POSITIVES:

1) Cillian Murphy is absolutely spellbinding. He carries the whole film on his back and plays Oppenheimer during so many different parts of his life, yet he never for a second seems to falter in any way. He should be guaranteed a Best Actor nomination. I also think Robert Downey Jr should be guaranteed a Best Supporting Actor nomination 2) This almost goes without saying for Nolan, but the film has been made unbelievably well. It looks like a painting during so many sequences and I loved the way in which the changing of timeframes and the changing of colour was used 3) The score and the sound design were both incredible. Incredible. The score had me feeling so engaged and literally gripping my seat, whilst the sound design of the explosions made me feel like the cinema was going to take off 4) The moral / philosophical questions at the heart of the film are really thought provoking. I also think this is helped by the fact that none of the characters are perfect, they're all very flawed which makes them all incredibly interesting

NEGATIVES:

1) There are too many side characters, most of whom aren't really given any backstory or time to shine, so it ends up being very difficult to remember exactly who is who 2) There is a scene near the end where it shows all the characters in their old age, and I thought the old age makeup looked bad and it took me out of the scene.

9.title: One of the finest films of the century
9.content: Oppenheimer is indisputably one of the best films of the century. The production is an intense character study of one of the world's most complicated scientists whose mark on the world was lesser known to the general public, until now. Christopher Nolan creates a spectacular and unsettling story that is complete with suspense and ethical difficulties. Cillian Murphy is amazing in one of the most enthralling performances of his career. The story has numerous characters and each cast member brings a spectacular addition to the story. RDJ plays a disturbing role, Florence Pugh plays a tragic part, and even Tom Conti plays a charming Albert Einstein. The final scene is so impactful it will leave a lasting imprint on your psyche.

9.title: An Transfxing Experience
9.content: I love history but rarely enjoy biopics. Usually they glamorize the person while being overly simplistic. Such is not the case with Oppenheimer. This is a multilayered tale which explores not just what the brilliant man achieved, but how he felt and what he thought. As such, it is a psychological introspective of a man's intellectual, emotional and sexual motivations. The story flashes back and forth between time periods but really isn't difficult to follow. The use of flashbacks effectively illustrate how Oppenheimer's past experiences influence his future actions. The whole story is brilliantly framed by a professional/personal conflict between Oppenheimer and a politically ambitious Lewis Strauss. The film has already been extensively reviewed and lauded so I won't go on. Suffice it to say I highly recommend it.

9.title: A cinematic experience that gets better over the course of its runtime
9.content:
Focused on the story of Robert Oppenheimer, his struggles and passion for theoretical physics, Christopher Nolan does an excellent job with his ability to portray the possible struggles and barriers a man of his intellect have to overcome.

Other than the need to get used to the non-linear method of storytelling Nolan adapts, and the fast cuts between scenes I see no other issues with Oppenheimer.

It is clear as day that this movie was not intended for an audience that wants a fun entertainer, rather was intended to an audience that is willing to revisit our history, and learn more about a man that was tasked with a job very few in history have been tasked with.

If expectation are set accordingly, this movie can be rather inspiring.

9.title: This one hit like an A-bomb
9.content: I just got back from the cinema and I have to say, the hype is real. What a complete masterpiece of a film. Cilian Murphy is fantastic, but I already knew that. I think it's RDJ's performance that is absolutely magnificent and beyond anything I thought he was capable of. This isn't so much a typical Nolan film, like Interstellar, Inception or Tenet. It is much more a political thriller. It still has great cinematics and audio, but it goes a lot deeper into the psychology of the characters, especially Oppenheimer himself, than characters in other Nolan films. The ensemble of A-list actors in support roles in the film is impressive and all delivered good to great performances, including Matt Damon, an otherwise somewhat one dimensional actor in my opinion. No film is perfect, but with Oppenheimer Chris Nolan is getting very close to achieving that.

9.title: One of Nolan's best works
9.content:
A monumental achievement. A powerful story told on the grandest scale possible. Christopher Nolan's new film is based on the 2005 book "American Prometheus". The story follows the life of theoretical physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer (Cillian Murphy, finally starring in a major Hollywood feature film) and his development of the atomic bomb. From the opening sequence, Nolan lights the fuse for an explosive narrative that unfolds with incredible intensity.

The scientist is torn apart by the scientific and ethical side of his creation. Due to the non-linear structure of the narrative, the tension is maintained throughout the entire 180 minutes of running time, although the film is built entirely on dialogue. Ludwig Göransson's bombastic score adds another layer of drama, creating an emotional crescendo that explodes with devastating effect.

Overall, each character brings their own explosive energy to the screen, creating a chain reaction of exciting performances. After all, the cast here is magnificent. Even in minor roles that only appear for a couple of minutes (e.g. Rami Malek). And also the fact that the entire picture was created without any use of computer graphics.

Oppenheimer is not just a film. This is a powerful explosion of ideas and themes that, I hope, will find a deep response among the mass audience. After all, what consequences could there be for the most destructive creation of mankind?

9.title: Wonderful movie but not for everyone
9.content: This movie is amazing, like really amazing and a masterpiece and not a disappointment from christopher Nolan. Howerver the movie is not for everyone, its sophisticated and not all people will grasp it from the beginning. It's twisting and you have to concentrate with everything begind said, every name and every character in the movie because this movie is like a puzzle and you put the pieces together to get the full picture. 3 hours long and really slow rhythm and that's it's only draw back. Sone dialogues were boring in parts of the movie but once you finish the movie you will realise that these boring parts were needed but towards the end the rhythm is accelerated and that was necessary. People who like the spoon like info and pop corn movies would definitely say that this was a bad movie and would give it a 1-3/10 but that would be a disgrace for the movie. And RDJ was giving the performance of his life. It is an oscar performance and he is going to be a strong nominee. Overall this movie can only be watched in the cinema because at home, you will never get the magic of it. The black and white scenes were my favourite in this movie.

9.title: New perspective on what ended/triggered the wars
9.content:
I watched the movie and I had a great discussions in the queue to the WC with other people after.

The transition between the conviction/post-conference in mono-colour filming and the pre-scenes (I coin the term as the time before Hiroshima-Nagasaki event) coloured filming is slightly confusing, but you can compare what "happened" and what was framed at the conviction in your own way. I recommend watching the trailer or have a glance at the background, otherwise the beginning is also a bit perplexing.

One of the questions the movie brought was about explanation of Hiroshima-Nagasaki event, why it needed to happen. Who should take the responsibility the most, the one who invented the atomic bomb, who ordered the bombing, or the bombed as what it deserves? Normally in many educations, the incident is described as the means to end the world wars, but, in the movie, it could be seen that Japan was chosen because there was nowhere else to throw the bombs on. In a way, the two cities in Japan were the perfect locations to experiment the impact of the bombs.

The movie also nicely show the mental transition of Oppenheimer himself. From the excitement of materialising his own theories, the confidence to be the most admired man in the US and to the devastating emotion and guilt, possibly being the killer of thousands of people,Cillian Murphy and others played it so well.

9.title: Destroyer of Worlds
9.content:
I've been waiting for this movie for like two years ever since the very first news broke. Cillian Murphy has made a deep impression on me as Thomas Shelby and I knew how he had insane screen presence. It's not often you see a movie that you've been anticipating for years. There's very few directors like Chris Nolan (perhaps none) who can pull people to the theaters the way he does (I watched a 2pm Saturday movie in a small-ish town and the cinema was packed).

My experience with Oppenheimer was largely positive, which is a feat considering how much anticipation I had going in and was well aware of the widespread praise it was receiving. It truly was a cinematic experience and a very maximalist movie in a sense. The ensemble cast consisting of Murphy, Blunt, Damon, Downey, Pugh (although her role was not super significant) and many other recognizable faces, worked well and nobody dropped the ball. I would love to see Cillian win Oscars for this movie because portraying a complex character as Oppenheimer with such weight is a monumental feat. The audiovisual experience was quite top notch with Ludwig Gorasson and van Hoytema for music and cinematography. The one scene where Oppenheimer gives a speech after the bombing was one of the most disturbing scenes I've seen on cinema in a while.

In a way, Oppenheimer is a near perfect movie. Its 3h runtime surprisingly did not feel long and I was a little sad that the movie ended. My one complaint about the movie is that it's almost TOO maximalist. The movie's source material was Oppenheimer's 700 page biography called "American Prometheus" and the movie did condense that into a movie. It felt like the movie was on full gas for 3 hours (especially the score barely ever actually stopping for 3 hours). There was no loose moment, no room for breathing and was overall very fast-paced that was almost hard to keep up, especially with so many events and characters. This does make me think that multiple viewing of this movie will help better appreciate it but it will definitely lessen the magic of viewing it for the first time.

I love movies that embody the art of subtlety and Oppenheimer was not that. It was dramatic for all of its duration and that worked successfully for me as I was completely engaged in the movie for that long. But I wish that the writing was trimmed a bit more and spent more time in key moments instead of rushing through them. The 4.5 I am giving is a 4.5 that's very close to a 5 but I just couldn't feel the same way. I do want to make clear that it was an amazing experience and worth the hype. It just was not a 5 movie for me.

9.title: Simply phenomenal cinema!
9.content:
In classic Nolan fashion, this story is not told in a straightforward manner, but in an action packed and thrilling way. Encapsulating the messy, chaotic and important life of Oppenheimer.

There is never a dull nor boring moment in the movie. And it's all tied together perfectly by the amazing score of Ludwig Göransson.

Everyone acted their roles perfectly, especially Cillian Murphy.

Only 2 nitpicks are the scenes being hard to follow at times and the lack of those crazy practical effects.

Simply a masterpiece & near perfection of a film. This 3 hour long biopic is a must watch for every movie lovers.

9.title: One for the books

The only down part to me is, it is not a movie you can enjoy more than once. But other than that. Loved it.

9.title: Oppenheimer A Visually Stunning and Thought-Provoking Biopic Cillian Murphy Gives a Tour-de-Force
9.content:
Oppenheimer is a biographical drama film about J. Robert Oppenheimer, the scientist who led the Manhattan Project to develop the atomic bomb. The film explores Oppenheimer's moral dilemma as he grapples with the implications of his work and the potential for nuclear destruction.

Review: Oppenheimer is a visually stunning and thought-provoking film that offers a complex and nuanced portrait of one of the most important figures in the history of science. Cillian Murphy gives a tour-de-force performance as Oppenheimer, bringing to life the scientist's brilliance, charisma, and inner turmoil. The supporting cast is also excellent, with Emily Blunt, Matt Damon, Robert Downey Jr., Rami Malek, and Kenneth Branagh all giving memorable performances.

The film's direction by Christopher Nolan is masterful. Nolan uses his trademark visual style to create a film that is both visually arresting and emotionally resonant. The film's use of sound and music is also effective, helping to create a sense of tension and dread.

Oppenheimer is not without its flaws. The film is long, and some viewers may find the pacing to be slow. Additionally, the film's depiction of the Bhagavad Gita has been met with criticism from some viewers.( In possitive ony one cannot miss the Bhagawat Gita and in negative way it's the inappropriate time to discuss on it it's would be better if presenting as per Karthik 2 when anupam kher explain about shree Krishna) Overall, Oppenheimer is a powerful and important film that offers a unique and thought-provoking perspective on one of the most important events in human history. The film is beautifully made, and Cillian Murphy gives a tour-de-force performance. However, the film's length and the depiction of the Bhagavad Gita may be off-putting to some viewers.

Recommendation: I would recommend Oppenheimer to viewers who are interested in science, history, or war films. The film is also a good choice for viewers who are looking for a thought-provoking and challenging film.

9.title: A 70mm Masterclass
9.content:
Oppenheimer delivers on its expectations, though in a different way than I was expecting.

I was expecting a film similar to another Nolan treasure like Interstellar. A deep story packed with progression and constant adventure. Instead, I was greeted with a layered, politically dramatic storyline that gave way to its character development rather than solving problems.

I came into the film completely blind, (besides an in cinema trailer that I couldn't miss). I was also able to see it at Arizona Mills IMAX in genuine 70mm film format. This (in my opinion) must be the greatest way to experience a film like this.

Oppenheimer delivers an onslaught of dialogue throughout its entire runtime. Make sure to come into this film very prepared.

This film falls short of Interstellar for most of its runtime, even dragging a bit right after the nuclear fission test. The film picks up in a way I never expected in its final sequence.

Masterpiece.

9.title: Masterpiece!!
9.content:
Oppenheimer is a biographical thriller film written and directed by Christopher Nolan, based on the book American Prometheus by Kai Bird and Martin J. Sherwin. It stars Cillian Murphy as J. Robert Oppenheimer, the theoretical physicist who led the development of the atomic bomb during World War II, and explores his personal and professional life, his moral dilemmas, and his legacy.

Oppenheimer is a fascinating and impressive film with an incredibly visceral pacing to it. It is a testament to Nolan's vision and craftsmanship, as well as Murphy's acting prowess. The direction, editing, sound, cinematography... everything in this is just top tier. It is a film that is certainly worth watching for its cinematic achievements and its exploration of the human condition in the face of scientific discovery and moral dilemma.

9.title: Give Cillian Murphy the Oscar!
9.content: This was a magnificent performance by most of the actors. There are a few glaring exceptions (notably, Florence Pugh, whose performance degrades the entire enterprise) but for the most part, this is a truly excellent film. The musical score is really just not very good. The music is so tense throughout the film, there is no build up to the climax. I really dislike the music that accompanies the film. Wow, Hans Zimmer could have done such a magnificent job on the music for this film. I wish Mr. Nolan had used him for the musical score. It would have made a much better film, in my opinion. Other than these rather minor criticisms, I found the film magnificent. Bravo Mr. Nolan, Mr. Murphy, Ms. Blunt, Mr. Damon, and Mr. Downey.

9.title: If Kanye West's "Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy" album was a movie
9.content: A movie that just absolutely captures the importance of profound scientific and global affairs in a spectacular way. It was would be like if Kanye West's "Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy" album was a movie. Cillian Murphy puts on a virtuoso performance encapsulating the deeply complicated and contradictory life that Oppenheimer lived. The pace that the movie runs at is so intense and the music is used perfectly to capture that. The explosion of the bomb is so realistically filmed that you feel fully immersed in Los Alamos. The subtle themes of "The Fission" and "The"fusion" floated at the beginning of the movie is an incredible way to depict to the two separate courtroom like battles Oppenheimer and Strauss are involved in. Nolan has many great movies under his belt but this movie tops them all.

9.title: Amazing film

You can feel it towards the end. The run time is worth it however to make sure that you get the entirety of Oppenheimer's life from the start and post WW2.

9.title: Destroyer of Worlds

9.title: What else can be said, it's a masterpiece.
9.content:
Oppenheimer, directed by Christopher Nolan, is a masterpiece of a character study, building up suspense and most importantly dread like no movie I have ever seen. What I found so particularly amazing about it is the fact that you know what's coming, you know what the titular man and character releases and yet the buildup to that faithful test keep you on the edge of the seat.

Now, before you go into the movie you have to get one thing clear: this movie is not about the Trinity nuclear test, nor the bombings of Nagasaki and Hiroshima. It is, as stated by the title, about Oppenheimer. It's about him, his problems, his actions and the consequences of those actions. We see most of the movie through Oppenheimer's perspective, how he interprets and feels about the events taking place and I've seen one too many people complain about a few scenes because they simply did not understand this.

Lastly I want to bring up the editing, it's sublime but not easy to follow. The movie jumps back and forth through time periods, being almost reminiscent of a documentary in terms of it's structure and it respects the audience enough to let us piece all of it together ourselves. This means that you actually have to sit down, listen and think about what is being said and what is happening.

In short, this is the best movie released in quite some time and should be enjoyed by everyone who enjoys a good film. Watch it on the biggest screen you can and enjoy the experience of watching one of the greatest movies ever made.

9/10, simply a masterpiece.

9.title: WOW

I'm not gonna lie and say I was 100% excited for Oppenheimer because I wasn't at first, I remember seeing the trailer in the cinema and thinking "yeah I'm gonna watch that one day" anyway the whole Barbenheimer thing happened and my hype grew for the film (more for Barbie if I'm being honest) but I just left the cinema and wow.
