8.title: Excellent storytelling
8.content:
The cast of the movie is insane every single star deserve an award for his performance. Biographical more than pure drama but Murphy played it very well. I enjoyed it although it is very long. RDJ, Matt Demon and Emily Blunt were all amazing in their characters. I was expecting more ww2 scenes especially the bombing moments but it was not there.

Overall the movie is excellent but was overhyped and marketed very well that made a lot of people think it was about the ww2 and involving more war scenes some was disappointed later and see the movie as boring long biography one. Thank you Mr. Nolan.

8.title: 'Oscar Worthy' - but lacking Nolan's Charm
8.content:
Nolan has a reputation for mind-bending, twisty-turny movies that leave your brain in knots, right? Well, despite it's magnificence, "Oppenheimer" doesn't exactly fit that bill.

Oppenheimer takes a different approach. It aims to give us a true portrayal of the protagonist, the man behind the atomic bomb. It's a more linear narrative than what we're used to.

There's one little thing that caught me off guard - and not in a satisfactory way: the nudity scenes. Thy felt forced, graphic, and out of place.

The other surprise was the intensity of the dialogue. It felt clunky and sometimes killed the momentum of the film. Nolan usually has this knack for sharp and memorable lines, but this time around, it fell a little flat.

I found myself waiting for those powerful, mind-bending exchanges, but they were few and far between.

On a positive note, the acting is absolutely stellar. Robert J. Oppenheimer (Cillian Murphy) and Edward Teller (Benny Safdie) were unbelievable and authentic performances the likes of which we have NEVER seen on screen.

Visually, it's still a Nolan film, so you can expect some stunning cinematography and breathtaking shots. The attention to detail is, as always, on point, making the experience a treat for the eyes and ears.

Without a doubt, the 70mm used to make this movie makes you feel like you're back in 1945.

In the end, "Oppenheimer" might not be the Nolan mind-bender we've come to expect, but it does offer a sincere and more grounded look at the life of a historical figure who changed the f*cking world.

If you're expecting twisty narratives and jaw-dropping moments (apart from a couple of scenes), you might leave the theater feeling a tad disappointed.

Still, you cannot miss seeing this in the cinema. Even if it's not entirely up to his usual mind-blowing standards.

Bravo again, Sir Christoper Nolan.

8.title: Could had been a masterpiece if focus was on interesting science & psychology and not trivial trials.
8.content:
Movie was fine. I was expecting more physics and engineering and excitement of real science and emotional phases of Oppenheimer, suspense before tests, not focus on trivial human trials by dumb politicians. Since its about great geniuses, i cant rate it low. Could have been better!

Could focus on collecting all the scientists, building up of the town in middle of nowhere. How the russian spy worked to transport message. The emotional phases, debate for righteousness. Suspense during testing. Betting on quantity of explosion. How technical and engineering marvel was achieved. Not knowing if it works, etc. Its nice, but could had been one of the great movie of all time. Missed the chance.

8.title: Oppenheimer Review
8.content:
Oppenheimer review Let me start with the positive aspects of the movie first: 1. The cinematography of the movie was very good 2. The soundtrack of the movie was very good 3. The acting is great, obviously. I especially liked the acting of Cillian Murphy and RDJ.

4. The movie describes the birth of the atomic bomb very well 5. The character of J. Robert Oppenheimer is well portrayed 6. The pace of the movie was fluid and despite the criticism I would make, the movie was still interesting and good.

7. I liked that the movie was deep 8. I like what the movie does to make us nervous Things I didn't like about the movie:
Except for Oppenheimer, the characters weren't that deep. I don't even remember the names of any of the characters except Oppenheimer, Strauss, and Kitty. For example, the character played by Florence Pugh. The character is overly sexualized. After investigating Jean Tatlock, after Tatlock's death in 1944, letters and accounts from his friends were uncovered, revealing that he was having affairs with women. According to American Prometheus, his "homosexual tendencies" were evident during psychoanalysis. I think some of the characters in the movie could have been worked on.


The movie is not understood by many. Nolan likes his movies to be unintelligible, but I think it's a plus that the movie is easy to understand.


I don't think there was a need for so many Oscar-winning actors. Okay, the actors are playing very well, but I don't think even extras should be actors with such a reputation.


I liked the movie overall. My rating for the movie is 8/10.

8.title: There was nothing special about the 70 mm IMAX
8.content:
I recently had the pleasure of watching a highly anticipated movie that had been generating a lot of buzz. I was excited to see it and had high expectations, and I have to say, I was not disappointed. The movie had a great story that kept me engaged from start to finish, and the suspense was palpable throughout. The characters were well-developed and the acting was superb, which only added to the overall experience.

However, I have to agree with some other reviewers that there was nothing particularly special about watching the movie in 70 mm IMAX format. While it did provide a larger and more immersive viewing experience, I don't think it added much to the overall enjoyment of the movie. In fact, I think the movie would be just as enjoyable on a regular IMAX or even a regular screen.

That being said, I still highly recommend this movie to anyone who enjoys a good story and well-crafted suspense. It's a great example of how a movie can be successful without relying on flashy gimmicks or special effects. The story is what matters most, and this movie delivers in spades. So if you're looking for a great movie to watch, give this one a try. You won't be disappointed.

The film was great maybe even perfect for the first 2hrs, the last hour was confusing and felt like it moved at a slower pace than the first 2hrs. However the Movie was great no matter the length, great characters and visuals, However the best thing about this was the music, just perfect. The movie Could be Top tier if I wasn't so tired after the movie, Oppenheimer is A great,cinematic, dramatic and visually outstanding Movie, that is only pushed down by its pacing. In all honesty the movie is my Second favourite Nolan film next to the Dark Knight. I will give the Movie a 8/10, worth A watch.

Don't worry no spoilers: it might need a second rewatch for me though.

8.title: Great Adaption
8.content: Let me tell you about Christopher Nolan's take on Dr. Openhimer-it's a bit of a departure from his usual style, but in a good way. Instead of the usual action-packed scenes, this movie delves into the backstory of the atom bomb's creation in a really cinematic way. As a huge Nolan fan, I was drawn in by the way he meticulously explains the events leading up to such a monumental moment in history. Sure, it's not the high-octane thrill ride we're used to from Nolan, but I found the cerebral approach to be just as captivating. It's a different side of Nolan's filmmaking that showcases his versatility and storytelling prowess.

8.title: Oppenheimer: A Masterpiece of History, Science, and Cinematic Brilliance
8.content:
Oppenheimer is a gripping and thought-provoking journey into the life of J. Robert Oppenheimer (Cillian Murphy), the man behind the atomic bomb. Christopher Nolan once again proves his filmmaking genius by weaving a complex story of morality, ambition, and the devastating consequences of scientific discovery. The movie's non-linear narrative, meticulous attention to detail, and intense pacing keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish.

Cillian Murphy's portrayal of Oppenheimer is nothing short of extraordinary. He brings depth to a character conflicted by his genius and the horrors he unleashed. The supporting cast, including Emily Blunt and Robert Downey Jr., elevates the film even further, each bringing their own gravitas to the story.

Christopher Nolan's direction is a masterclass in how to tackle a historical event while blending human emotion with intellectual tension. His ability to turn a historical figure's internal struggles into an epic cinematic experience is unparalleled. Nolan's meticulous craftsmanship, from sound design to cinematography, only enhances the impact of the film.

While the film can be dense at times with its scientific explanations, it never loses its emotional core. Oppenheimer isn't just about science or war-it's about the cost of invention and the burden of knowledge.

Christopher Nolan has created something truly special here, and I give Oppenheimer a solid 8/10. His vision and storytelling abilities are as potent as the bomb itself.

8.title: Soooo long but captivating
8.content: Soooo long but captivating But Oppenheimer was actually really good. At times it just made me feel really dumb lol. I'm like, am I supposed to know what words these people are stringing together to make a sentence? The drama did help with the in between parts. A solid 8 stars. 1 star off for it being freaking 3 hours long!!! That was just ridiculous and just mean to make it that complicated of a story. I admit I knew nothing about the atomic bomb though, so I definitely googled afterwards. Everything seemed pretty factually correct for the most part, parts were just sensationalized for the drama.

8.title: Good but
8.content: I am not convinced this movie represents the brilliance of Oppenheimer. It appears to be a drama that goes back and forth in ths space time continuum of his past relations as a womanizer, a complex marriage, a neurotic selfish wife who is full of her boring pathos, a neglected child. Lots of meetings with scientists but not enough physics to share quantum theories which it skirts a lot of issues at once: past and present , communist witch hunts, etc. Interogation can be boring and to me it breaks the storyline too often. An intriguing appearance by Kenneth Braghnah as Bohr, which is for me the best part of the movie. A sad love life and many compromises are endured by Oppenheimer. The film focuses on the development of the bomb at Los Alamos and the culture he managed at this site.the excalation of the arms race continues. The history appears to be true. Great acting by Cillian and Robert Downing jr. Yet the script is too wordy might have worked better as 3 parts to give homage to this scientist.

8.title: Genius yet soulless
8.content:
If you're looking for a movie that has a great storytelling, amazing acting and the right amount of astonishing cinematography, you should not search any further. 'Oppenheimer' has it all. But if you're expecting a breathtaking piece of media, you should continue in your journey.

Honestly, it is quite saddening that such a beautiful piece of media lacks something so important as is the spark of originality.

As someone who comes from a nation that releases one big biopic in cinema per year, I have seen a lot of different artistic visions for this genre. Now, combine this with my love for psychological dramas and thrillers and you get a pretty solid base for understanding what I'm trying to say.

As much as I loved all the physics talk, the contrasts between the inner world of Oppenheimer and the reality around him and the suspense, it was not something I've seen for the first time ever. After three hours, I was not leaving the cinema bored, yet, I was rather annoyed. Everywhere I looked were 10/10s, 9/10s, but I just felt like I'd watched a blank template filled with really cool words and sentences.

Some might say "omg, she does not understand, she does not know her film stuff", but that's it...for 6 years of my life I've been preparing for studying at a film university (though unsuccessfully for practical reasons), I know the basics of film theory and I undertook some courses on the matter...and from film theory standpoint the movie IS basically immaculate, but that's all. Plain. Distant. Overhyped. Just another movie.

Calling 'Oppenheimer' Christopher Nolan's best movie and maybe the best movie to ever exist is even over its beauty certainly an overreach and to be honest if you say this, I think you might need to see more movies.

8.title: What an experience!
8.content:
Oppenheimer.

Wow! Movie was truly an experience. The visuals with the black and white juxtaposed with color throughout and the sound effects were amazing. The use of sound is what really stood out.

From the deafening sounds of blasts to the foreboding bass and other instrumentals throughout, the sound really set a great mood for the film.

Cillian Murphy killed it with his performance, I think he was Oscar worthy. Robert Downey Jr., also was outstanding. Movie is very long but I felt the pacing worked well and the movie never dragged or got boring.

Also loved how morality was highlighted and Oppenheimer's struggle with his own conscience in building the bomb.

Best movie I've seen this year.

8/10.

8.title: Good Historical Content
8.content: Oppenheimer is a Christopher Nolan story of American scientist J. Robert Oppenheimer who is played by Cillian Murphy. The film was less about the development of the atomic bomb and concentrated on Oppenheimer's political stance than his unkind gift he gave to mankind. He was put on trial for his supposedly supporting the Communist party of America. Lewis Strauss (Robert Downey Jr) was the head of the Atomic Energy Commission (AEC) and he gave Oppenheimer his job and at the same time wanted to discredit him. Dr. David Hill (Rami Malek) was a theoretical physicist who worked at the Los Alamo's laboratory and he testified against Strauss especially what he did to Oppenheimer. I wish the storyline was not all over the place why can't we just watch movies in a normal time frame, it would not make it so confusing especially when the screen changes from black and white to color which also caused it to boring at times. The assemble cast included Matt Damon as the General who put together the Pentagon and spending close to a few billion to create the atomic weapons. Emily Blunt played Oppenheimer's wife, Andean Ehenreich as a Senate Aide along with Scott Grimes, Jason Clarke, Tony Goldwyn, Kenneth Branagh, Tim Dekay, Tom Conti as Albert Einstein, David Krumholtz, Josh Hartnett, Matthew Modine, David Dastmalchian, Jack Quaid, Casey Affleck, James Remar, and Gary Oldman as President Harry Truman. Overall I liked the movie but I don't think it is worth a Best Picture Nomination for the Academy Awards. I do hope Murphy and Downey win awards for their roles.

8.title: The emotions of a man who pulled the biggest trigger after Lord Krishna
8.content: I'm a physicist and I watched this movie in IMAX (which made a slight difference) after doing my homework. I saw exactly what I expected which was unusual in itself for a Nolan's film. The movie is set at a period when philosophy mattered as much as physics for a scientist. The movie is all about one person who sees the world around him differently. This visionary genius is now under the terrible predicament of finding the most horrible weapon for the greater good which also happens to be his passion, nuclear fission. The same predicament which Krishna put himself under to instigate destruction. Sadly, he is also put on trial for his exact achievement later. So, He has to bare the cross and get crucified for it! Cillian Murphy recreated Oppenheimer like a magician. The tempo of the movie along with its wave-natured background score using it to pump your adrenaline at key moments. Unfortunately, it got to me in the last 30 minutes at which point I felt the movie is starting to get uninteresting. Overall, a must watch for Cillian Murphy.

8.title: Two words about Oppie.
8.content:
The movie that I recommend to those who are going to watch the movie not to have watched the peaky blinders series in the last 1-2 months before watching it.

After finishing a 6-season series, cillian murphy is now tomy shelby for you. When you see it on the big screen at least another 6 months after that, your brain may signal "aha our tomy shelby is out la". Who knows, this is a disaster for a movie viewer.

Cillian murphy was excellent in the series, but of course he outdid himself in this movie. There is no doubt that he will be nominated for an oscar with this performance, but I don't know if he can win because there will be other solid movies this year.

8.title: Cillian Murphy has lived this role.
8.content: Oppenheimer is a cinematic masterpiece that brilliantly captures the complexity of J. Robert Oppenheimer's life and the creation of the atomic bomb. Christopher Nolan's direction brings together a powerful blend of history, drama, and suspense, offering a thought-provoking exploration of morality, science, and the consequences of human invention. The performances, especially Cillian Murphy as Oppenheimer, are outstanding, with deep emotional nuance and intensity. The film's pacing and editing are exceptional, keeping the audience engaged from start to finish. Overall, Oppenheimer is a visually stunning and intellectually stimulating film that leaves a lasting impression.

8.title: A powerful film
8.content: Christopher Nolan proves once again why he has become such a well renown and respected director in such a competitive industry. The hype for this movie was real and as much a product of Nolan's incredibly reputation as it was the subject matter and man the film was based on. The movie is a slow burn and harkens back to an older style of film that Nolan has become so beloved for in an era of CGI bloated blockbusters. Void of CGI and overblown set pieces Oppenheimer is akin to an older film simply because it is carried by its drama, themes, and outstanding cast performances more than it is by spectacle. The cinematography is second to none , using both visual and audio cues to tie into the films deeper themes. The one that comes to mind is the stomping that Oppenheimer hears in his head throughout the movie that grow louder and louder almost like an oncoming train , the source of the sound that tortures him for most of the movie is revealed closer to the end. He is also haunted by quick cuts and flashes of the bomb exploding and fire expanding etc etc. Before the trinity test scene even happens. The way the trinity test was presented was tasteful. Going on premiere night in a sold out theater, you could hear a pin drop in the room during that scene. The movie tackles heavy subjects as Oppenheimer wrestles with moral qualms and guilt over what he helped create. While powerful I do believe that the latter half of the movie involving a hearing for Dr. Oppenheimer with regards to his ongoing security clearance for the U. S. and it's nuclear program could have been condensed a bit. While I do believe that the tail end of the movie used it's time effectively to bring some weight to the movie after the trinity test and tie together some strong themes that become clear by the end. I do believe that these hearing scenes could come off as long winded at times. At best the latter half of this movie and thus it's run time is appreciated by those not bothered by long run times , who likely enjoy other long dramas in vein with Oppenheimer like The Godfather, Scarface, and more. Even those not normally used to sitting in the theater watching a movie for so long might find the film and the superb performances to be engaging enough to justify its runtime. At worst Oppenheimer suffers from an ending that feels drawn out and caused the pacing of the film to suffer. Some modern audiences who do not understand or appreciate much of the important historical context to this movie as well , might find themselves bored sitting through what feels like a court hearing towards the end of the movie. For those type of moviegoers , they probably came to see the spectacle of the trinity test scene, likely thinking it would be a finale of sorts. But on the contrary the trinity test scene merely serves as catalyst to move into the second half of the movie (thematically) speaking. I suppose the latter type of audience is not who Oppenheimer was intended for exactly. If you are a fan of film, if your a history buff, If you don't mind a slow burn and enjoy a good character piece with some good drama and themes, then Oppenheimer is a great movie for you. If you are someone who didn't know who Oppenheimer was before they announced this movie, if you don't care much for history , If your a casual movie goer whose looking for an action packed thrill ride or just decided to check it out to see what the hype was all about... then you might get mixed results. Best advice is to tailor your expectations accordingly. For me this movie was not perfect but it came pretty damn close. It's cinematography, themes , character studies, historical significance, actor performances, audio work, and of course Nolan's signature dedication to practical effects combine to deliver a film that weights up to the reputation of a man who for better or for worse changed the world as we know it. This movie solidified Nolan's place amongst names like Martin Scorsese, Stanley Kubrick and more... in other words the best of the best Hollywood has to offer! Nolan is one of if not the last of a dying breed of director. His contributions and dedication to his art help keep the original spirit of filmmaking alive at a time when the majority of what we see in theaters encompasses very little of what made the roots of the art form so compelling and special.

8.title: Powerful...
8.content:
"Oppenheimer" is a Biography - Drama movie in which we watch the life of J. Robert Oppenheimer, the scientist behind the development of the atomic bomb. The movie offers a deep exploration of Oppenheimer's moral struggles, his complex personality, and the weight of his invention on both a personal and global scale.

What I found most compelling about Oppenheimer was its portrayal of the ethical dilemmas faced by those involved in the Manhattan Project. The film doesn't just focus on the scientific achievements but also on the consequences of unleashing such destructive power. The interpretation of Cillian Murphy who played as J. Robert Oppenheimer is nothing short of spectacular, he brings both the intellectual depth and inner turmoil of the character to life with precision and nuance. Christopher Nolan's direction is sharp, and the screenplay is engaging, making this a thought-provoking movie that challenges the viewer to consider the cost of innovation. Lastly, I have to say that "Oppenheimer" is an exceptional movie and I highly recommend it to everyone.

8.title: Amazing work
8.content:
In simple words this movie was epic. Spectacular work of storytelling and execution. Framing was epic too.

There shouldn't be much else said. It was an enjoyable movie, kept me entertained and held my focused throughout the entire movie, almost like my life did not exist during the watching of this movie. Seriously good work.

Christopher Nolan once again creating a master Class film. One thing that I was very glad about was how this movie focused more on the father of the atomic bomb and how the real life events affected him as a person. Should of been expected with the title of the movie being his name.

Cillian Murphy was the perfect person for the role of Oppenheimer, very cool seeing him on screen.

I believe an 8/10 is fair for a movie that is basically a retelling of actual real life events. It wasn't anything surprising. But an 8 is basically a 10, 3 hours sounds long but feels too short when it comes to this movie. That is all.

8.title: I loved Oppenheimer a lot!
8.content: This movie was amazing overall I never thought I'd really ever watch it But I finally gave it a chance and really enjoyed it! The digital effects and everything are also especially the effects they used for the atomic bomb. I loved the casting. Every character was unique in his or her way. I thought the movie was also very good at carpuring what really happened in the Manhattan project. I think many would really overall enjoy this movie if they like the history of the atomic bomb. It's so crazy to think these very bombs were the ones we used to drop on Japan during WWII and the destruction one of them caused was unbelievable!

8.title: Solid 8 but not for everyone to understand
8.content: This movie is like solid 8 but really not easy to understand. There are several layers like politics, moral, family, history, science and if you want to get the full experience you might need to be like 60-70 years old professor from US who has vivid interest in politics and is really open-minded. Seriously, I was prepared although not falling into this category but most of the audience I think did not understand a lot as they were too young and politically fragile. And that is not even touching the morals of the story or ancient history mentioned briefly. Or consequences for the Japanese that were so terrible. Go there, watch and come back to this movie in 10-15 years again if you are under 45.

8.title: It's but doesn't deserve the Oscar
8.content: Was expecting a lot from C. Nolan but he didn't deliver as expected. Music score was alright. Bomb detonation scene was solid. But the scenes following the detonation were boring. Half the audience slept half way through the movie. I think they really stretched out the whole thing a bit too much. Endgame being 3 hours made the audience sir tight every frame but it's the exactly opposite for Oppenheimer. Should have been a 7 max but the Bomb detonation scene being filmed without CGI made it a 8. Compared to Interstellar or Inception this is 5 i swear. I love Nolan but this isn't what i expected.

8.title: EPIC BIOGRAPHY!!
8.content:
I decided to watch it yesterday, even though it wasn't in IMAX. But like all of Nolan's previous films, his ability to build a story is always intriguing to discuss. Even for a biography film, he managed to turn it into an epic movie that can't be watched just once.

I might say this is the biography film with the most realistic set locations I've ever seen. Watching Oppenheimer is like witnessing a classical Mozart piano performance: it's hard to understand if you don't grasp the context behind it. Perhaps in a fictional film, the filmmaker would gladly explain to us what's happening, but a biography assumes that we already understand the subject's background. I might watch it for the second time after relearning the background of J. Robert Oppenheimer.

8.title: Effective and Powerful
8.content: It's always good to witness parts of the history through the lens of a filmmaker. It's a big subject to make a movie about and who better to do it than Chris Nolan. It's great to see Cillian Murphy leading the cast and he does an exceptional job. Him and Nolan have managed to create a good balance for the character so it's not clear to the audience if Oppenheimer was driven by good will or by his ego. Although, just like other Nolan movies, the dialogues felt too explanatory at times, it's a small price to pay to watch another great movie from one of, if not the most ambitious filmmaker of our time.

8.title: Better than Tenet!
8.content: After having a fun time at Hoyts Cinemas with my Dad here's my spoiler-free review of Oppenheimer! As usual, I'll be talking about my thoughts, my favourite moments of watching this movie & my conclusion/rating! Christopher Nolan is back with his latest instalment after the mixed reviews of Tenet and you know what? It's better than that! Cillian Murphy looks older than he does in the director's previous films he's starred in! The rest of the cast is great too, Robert Downey Jr. Is such a talented actor since he is Iron Man and I've only seen the first Sherlock Holmes movie but I'll watch A Game of Shadows before the third one arrives (If it comes out). Along with brilliant performances by Florence Pugh, Emily Blunt (who used an American accent which was weird cuz she's British IRL), Oscar winners; Rami Malek & Gary Oldman (who I didn't recognize while watching it). It was 3 hours long, I was careful not to drink too much water (just like Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning Part One), I fell asleep in bits of it and I stayed awake for the rest of it which was funny! Overall this is not only better than Christopher Nolan's last blockbuster but also Barbie which I won't watch! That's why I'm giving this an 8/10! I look forward to watching movies at home while I wait for Kraven The Hunter to release in October! ;-)

8.title: "I hope nobody was seeing that for fun"
8.content: That was the first thing I heard someone in the audience say when the movie ended, and I tend to agree. This film was very densely packed and required all of your attention from start to finish. Also, as someone who was not previously familiar with Oppenheimer's life, I found myself having to be twice as attentive. Of course Cillian Murphy was brilliant as Oppenheimer, his performance is truly what kept me engaged throughout those 3 hours. I really liked the cinematography as well, Nolan did a great job at communicating both the beauty and horror of the atomic bomb. Overall I'd say this isn't a film for the average movie goer, or someone just looking to pass the time on a Friday night. This will require your brain to be flipped on and it will take some time to digest after the fact.

8.content:
I love nolan as much as the next guy but movie not without a few flaws imo.

Strengths
a dialogue driven movie that sustains 3 hours ( no small feat)
bomb explosion build up/ tension
3 timelines that can follow
sound/ cinematography.

the movie is too long after the explosion. Im happy w final conclusion but def coulda tightened up without compromising.

8.title: Suspenseful without Suspense
8.content:
The story behind the father of the atomic bomb.

I enjoyed this movie to be sure! It is surprisingly thrilling and suspenseful despite having literally no true suspense or thrill scenes to speak of. The writing is great, the filmography spectacular, and for many actors this movie has proved to me that they can indeed act!

Some issues I have with it are the difficulty in following the story during the first act. But once the audiences is used to the format it is easy to follow. I also could have done away with the fairly explicit sex scenes. One could argue that the one serves a purpose, but most nudity was unnecessary and didn't add to the plot.

Nevertheless, the movie does well in keeping its titular character a controversial figure, and excels in suspense through conversation.

8.title: New Nolan Emerging
8.content: Oppenheimer is not a typical Nolan films like Inception or Interstellar. It is a three hour long biographical thriller film which was running like a fast moving car. As an IR student i've found it very relatable but thats not the case with most of the Indian audience. This movie has lot of characters like Strauss, J Hoover, Roosevelt, Kennedy and many more American scientists. You should have fair idea about their role in American history then only you could relate it better. First half was very much setting up the plot of the film which revolves around Oppenheimer's Journey. But the second half right from the "Trinity test" to the mystery of the end was an absolute amazing. The background score was tense and will held you till the end of the movie. Cillian Murphy and Robert Downey have given their career best performance. Eventually, all i can say it is more of "Dunkirk" kind of film rather than Dark Knight or Interstellar. 8.title: Not Nolans best work.
8.content:
The majority of performances are great but there are few exceptional performances by Robert Downy JR and Emily blunt.

Although Cillian Murphy once again plays the role a brooding individual a role he has almost recently become typecast.

Cillian performs well throughout with a highlight during one scene of hard questioning you can see the desperation and despair almost erupt underneath his surface.

Matt Damon plays the role of a military man Although a fair performance you can not hide from the fact that you see Matt Damon on screen and do not feel the presence of the character he is playing.

The remaining cast members pull their weight with great performances.

Although the climax of this film feels slightly anticlimactic ironic given that it is a large explosion.

The delivery of the sequence left me feeling unsatisfied.

Given the constant reassurance of the atomic bombs destructional capability the sequence under delivers to the point that you do not fear the atomic bomb in this movie.

Given the footage many of us have seen of atomic bombs this movie doesn't match the real destruction and fear that its real world counterpart truly shows.

The one outstanding highlight in this movie is the soundtrack.

Ludwig Göransson really captured the sound of scientific wonder within the music and the fear and daunting sound of the consequences.

8.title: Oppenheimer
8.content:
A brilliant film from master director Christopher Nolan, whose catalogue of unforgettable movies continues to grow.

Perhaps the most concentration required of myself at the cinemas since Daniel Day Lewis in Lincoln. But what a brilliant film, telling the story of J. Robert Oppenheimer and, as must be the case, the development of the atomic weapon that was eventually unleashed twice on the Empire of Japan to end the Second World War. 8.title: Thought provoking
8.content:
Was not sure if a long film about the development of the atomic bomb would keep my interest , but it did

Mainly down to the performance of his life by Cillian Murphy as Oppenheimer, with a great supporting cast of Blunt,Damon and in particular Robert Downey Jr. Also thought the under rated Jason Clarke stole the scenes he was in

8.title: "Oppenheimer" - A Compelling Dive into a Complex Genius
8.content:
"Oppenheimer" - A Compelling Dive into a Complex Genius

Christopher Nolan's "Oppenheimer" is a cinematic tour de force that masterfully blends historical drama with deep character study. Anchored by a mesmerizing performance from Cillian Murphy as J. Robert Oppenheimer, the film offers a gripping and poignant exploration of one of the most pivotal figures of the 20th century.

Nolan's storytelling prowess shines as he adapts the Pulitzer Prize-winning biography "American Prometheus." The narrative oscillates between Oppenheimer's early academic pursuits, his crucial role in the Manhattan Project, and the subsequent moral and political fallout of his work on the atomic bomb. This non-linear structure, a hallmark of Nolan's style, enhances the complexity and urgency of Oppenheimer's internal and external conflicts.

Cillian Murphy delivers an outstanding performance, capturing Oppenheimer's intellectual brilliance and the profound moral dilemmas he faced. Emily Blunt, as Kitty Oppenheimer, adds depth with a portrayal that balances strength and vulnerability. Robert Downey Jr. And Matt Damon also provide strong support, enriching the film with their nuanced performances

The visual splendor of "Oppenheimer" is undeniable. Shot on IMAX cameras, the film's cinematography by Hoyte van Hoytema is breathtaking. The practical effects used to recreate the Trinity test explosion are particularly striking, creating a visceral and immersive experience that underscores the magnitude of Oppenheimer's work. The detailed period settings and costumes further transport the audience to the 1940s.

Nolan's dedication to historical accuracy is evident. The film meticulously portrays the scientific and political challenges of the era, providing viewers with a comprehensive understanding of the Manhattan Project's complexity. This commitment to authenticity enriches the narrative, grounding it in real-world stakes and consequences.

At its core, "Oppenheimer" is a meditation on genius, responsibility, and the ethical ramifications of scientific advancement. Nolan delves into the paradox of Oppenheimer's legacy: a man who brought about unprecedented destruction while grappling with the moral weight of his creations. The film's emotional resonance is profound, inviting viewers to reflect on the dual-edged nature of progress.

While the film's depth is commendable, its pacing can occasionally feel uneven. The dense scientific and political discussions, although necessary for context, might challenge some viewers' engagement. However, these moments are balanced by intense character-driven scenes that maintain the overall momentum.

"Oppenheimer" is a triumph of biographical cinema. Nolan's meticulous direction, combined with stellar performances and stunning visuals, makes it a compelling watch. It is both an intellectual and emotional journey, shedding light on the complexities of a man who changed the course of history. Though slightly uneven in pacing, its strengths far outweigh its flaws, earning it a well-deserved score of 8/10.

For those seeking a thought-provoking film that marries historical depth with cinematic excellence, "Oppenheimer" is an unmissable experience.

8.title: Now I am become Death, the destroyer of worlds 8/10
8.content:
If there is anyone who knows how to direct tragic characters, it's Christopher Nolan. If you look at his resume, most of his movies focus on tragic characters, broken, victims of their own creation.

J. Robert Oppenheimer is no stranger to that category, the man who created the atomic bomb in order to put an end to World War 2, has been haunted for the rest of his life with guilt and trauma over the results of his creation. Not only that, but after the war he was wrongfully accused of cooperating with the Soviet Union and was backstabbed by his friends and partners.

I could go in depth over any aspect of the movie: the amazing assemble cast, the practical effects of Nolan in his movies and how his visual effects feel so real, the tragedy of the character, or the fear over a threat that still exists till this day (If you're aware of the Great Power Competition and the tension between nations, than the threat of nuclear war is lurking in the shadows).

But I do want to focus on how the movie is trying to be so many things until it's not clear to determine what the movie is entirely about.

Some may say it's a personal biography on how the atomic bomb affected the life of it's creator.

Other people will say the movie focuses on the Manhattan project and the trinity test, the type of movie that focuses on a certain event or project in human history (movies like The Social Network, The Founder, etc.).

There is also the option that the movie focuses on the aftermath of the Manhattan project and the ugly politics that happened behind the scenes, false accusations and political games (just like House of Cards and Succession).

The problem I'm trying to point out is that Oppenheimer is a really complex film, this complexity is a bit overshadowed by how amazing and good the movie is, and I admire it too. The three hour run doesn't feel long to me at all.

I guess the only problem the movie suffers from (but at the same time doesn't suffer) is it's lack of identity, a lack that I have a hard time to determine myself. Perhaps reviewing this movie will help understand it better.

My favorite scene had to be the final one, when Oppenheimer is speaking to Albert Einstein and telling him that he fears of the chain reaction he has created. And then the camera shifts to Oppenheimer's face and he's imagining the destruction of the world, knowing it was caused by him, becoming death.

In conclusion I just have to say on a personal note, that I wish more people would make movies like Nolan, Fincher and others. Movies that have a certain impact on the world of cinema. Forget about movies that are being used as a political tool for agendas or superhero movies like Marvel and DC that would not be remembered in a few years.

Movies like Oppenheimer and many other good films that came out this year should be the ones to inspire young filmmakers to create something captivating and meaningful.

8.title: The Movie Constructed Like a Nuclear Bomb
8.content:
It should be known that Oppenheimer is, in many ways, a massive departure from previous Christoper Nolan films, and even includes nude scenes which have gained some media controversy. (On that note, there is an absolutely bizarre sex scene in a board room.) While many Nolan films always have a profound contemplative tone that is coupled with gunshots, constant explosions and doomsday clocks, Oppenheimer most definitely appeals to a different audience that is more ruminative, introverted, and startled by loud bangs. If you are expecting a cathartic roller coaster ride, you should not be paying for admission (or an IMAX ticket for that matter). It will be a waste of your time and you can immediately reduce my rating to five stars or lower. But if you are the ruminative introverted type that loves a profound drama great enough to send you into contemplation for a time, the film will give you what you're looking for.

With that taken into consideration, the film is the ultimate portrayal of the father of the nuclear bomb. From the time your curiosity is piqued before the film, to the hours during the film that you are bombarded with its endless dramatic chaos, the film buries us in the emotions and thoughts of Oppenheimer's world. In doing so, the film invites us to consider the immeasurable consequences of the bomb as felt through Oppenheimer, but also as people who have to live in a world that constantly teeters on the verge of transforming into a radioactive wasteland. Much like the mysterious wave-particle duality of Quantum Mechanics, the movie itself is a duality. The fusion and fission of opposites defines the movie and its tortured lead protagonist. The plot itself is structured like the bomb. At the core of the film is Los Alamos, and the film's events both prior to and after it are surrounded with all the modern dysfunctions of the human being. The fallout of the test includes internal and external politics reminiscent of Julius Caesar, disordered relationships, neurotic breakdowns, endless civilian deaths. And yet in the midst of all that is also patriotism, ingenuity, victory, glory, and a willingness to put aside all kinds of differences to have the bomb before the Nazis do. And while we do not physically witness a single casualty from a bomb explosion in the entire film, this chaotic chain reaction of performances are so effectively conveyed that we don't need to see people dying to understand how dreadfully terrifying it is for man to have the power to destroy the known world. The depths to which the movie plunges you in thought comes from the exceptional performances of the film's cast, which are so adept at conveying the horrors, the guilt, the tragedy, the joy, the victory, and the dichotomy that is the nuclear bomb. Cillian Murphy's portrayal of Oppenheimer is aesthetically exceptional, reflecting Oppie's mannerisms, tone of voice, and silent charisma such that he may as well be in the 1950s black and white films of old. More than anything, Cillian exceptionally communicates Oppenheimer's dichotomies: his gentleness coupled with his power, his hubris and humility, his charm and his ugliness, his sense of moral right and his tortured conscience. Opposite of him, Robert Downey Jr. Puts aside his charismatic whimsical typecast and portrays a very serious, humorless, and subtly vicious Lewis Strauss. And although I felt Robert Downey was not nearly as convincing as Cillian, he damn well gave one of the best performances of his life. The two are supported by an all-star cast that are so effective at bringing Oppie's world to life.

The movie perfectly captures Christopher Nolan's vision: it has complexity, sophistication, and multiple timelines converging into the core of the bomb conceived in Los Alamos. For better or worse, we experience Oppenheimer totally on Nolan's terms rather than through our own cinematic sensibilities. This may feel boring to some, pretentious to others, or infinitely and morbidly fascinating for the rest of us. For the most latter group, they will be greatly rewarded.

8.title: I Got Bombs But I'm Not a Bomber
8.content:
Oppenheimer posed a tricky question for perennial hit maker Christopher Nolan. How do you make a three hour biopic of a scientist compelling enough to bring in big money? Turns out the answer is to not make a biopic at all.

While J. Robert Oppenheimer is indeed the focus of the film it eschews any traditional biopic format, instead serving up what is essentially a heist or even sports movie wrapped up in a courtroom drama. This allows the director to indulge his favourite hobby of playing with time, as the story jumps between two different panel hearings while also covering Oppenheimer's early career and of course the work of the Manhattan Project. This approach works incredibly well with the three hour runtime flying by. In fact, if you go to see this in the cinema you might want to skip the large cola as there really isn't any time when little enough is happening to sneak in a toilet brake.

Technically the film is outstanding. Cinematographer Hoyte van Hoytema, following on last year's Nope, is at the absolute top of his game and sound design is also great, with very little of the hard to hear dialogue that Nolan films are sometimes ridiculed for. The centre piece of the film is the first atomic bomb test and it is spectacular, you may have seen a million on screen explosions but you've never seen one shot like this.

It goes without saying that the cast is absolutely stacked, from Robert Downey Jnr's spurned official to Matt Damon's scenery chewing general. When you've got Kenneth Branagh filling out a relatively small role you know Oppenheimer is a prestige film. It all centres on a barnstorming performance by Cillian Murphy, who absolutely devours the role of J. Robert Oppenheimer. It's the type of role he has been ready to take on for decade or more and he nails his chance, expect to see him front and centre come award season.

Murphy's performance is central to the films biggest strength, keeping the titular character at just the right length from the audience. Scientist, schemer, leader, egomaniac, mythological figure. He is shown as all of these and more but never to the point where the film tells the viewer how much of each he was or what the you should really think of him. It's obvious he craves recognition but is it more important than accomplishment? He feels the weight of unleashing horror on mankind but does he feel it enough? All these types of question are left for the audience to decide.

One thing the audience is not asked to judge him on is his philandering, which is mostly left on the back burner here. Maybe because, in the face of creating nuclear weapons, marital indiscretions aren't considered a particularly important part of a man's legacy. Especially when it seems to be par for the course with famous scientists of that era. Or maybe it's because Nolan's major weakness as a film maker remains his inability to portray convincing relationships, leading here to a frankly bizarre sex scene.

Oppenheimer also isn't going to do anything to quiet critics who say Nolan underserves female characters. In the all star cast are Florence Pugh and Emily Blunt, two of the best around but (one scene aside) there is little for them to really get their teeth into. Perhaps Nolan will get a pass on this one given the male dominated nature of the time period.

Overall, the ambition and efficiency of Oppenheimer can't be denied. It ranks amongst Christopher Nolan's best work and one of the most entertaining historical dramas in a long time.

9 split atoms out of 10.

8.title: A spectacular production and cast in a film that needed to be a tad shorter
8.content: This is a very long, too long, excellent film about Robert J. Oppenheimer and since he is known as the father of the atomic bomb, we know exactly what this is about. It has been made by a master craftsman, Christopher Nolan, and it is impeccable in nearly all aspects other than the need for a little trimming. That's not saying any of it's really boring, but there's just a little more information here than the average moviegoer is going to want to sit through and primarily due to the length, it can get a rad tedious. We of course also deal with his private life which is less well known. Cillian Murphy portrays Oppenheimer and this is certainly his greatest performance among an enormous cast of many, many well known actors and none come even remotely close to giving a weak performance. Robert Downey Jr., getting back to acting after years of pretty much the same likable performance in comic book movies, is the clear major costar here, but many others are exceptionally good in much smaller roles. This is mostly a cast of men, but the two principal women portrayed by Florence Pugh and Emily Blunt are quite memorable. As a matter of fact they have two of the more memorable moments in the film. Pugh in a startling and unexpected sex scene in an unusual environment and Blunt in her final scene as an older woman with not a word of dialog is something you will remember. The film is a major undertaking that mostly succeeds, and while it is not my favorite Christopher Nolan film, it surely must be seen, but considering the amount of money this film made, most probably have, which I must say is a surprise now that I have seen it. It is far, far from any kind of popcorn movie. I suspect the Barbenheimer phenomenon helped this more than the other half of that moniker. Was it the best film of 2023? It's very, very good, but I saw a few others that I thought were better.

8.title: the destroyer of worlds
8.content:
It's only the middle of summer and we are almost half a year before the Academy nominations, but I think we already have one of the serious contenders for collecting many of the 2024 awards in Christopher Nolan's 'Oppenheimer'. It's the kind of movies adored by American audiences and critics alike, the story of a great American adventure and the biography of a personality who made history. The biographical docu-drama brings to the screen the life story of the scientist who led the Manhattan Project and raises questions relevant then and relevant today about the responsibilities of scientists and the risks of research and technological achievements put at the service of militaries and governments. The cast features an impressive gallery of Hollywood stars, and the special effects sprinkled throughout the film give it an extra dimension of appeal (and a Nolan touch). There are also plenty of political drama aspects, but ultimately the main qualities of this film, the ones that will remain after the initial excitement wears off, are related to the extremely truthful and well-documented portraits of the personalities who contributed to the success of the Manhattan Project.

The story in 'Oppenheimer' is structured in three temporal planes that unfold in parallel with dizzying speed. The biographical plot begins in the 1920s, Oppenheimer's years of study in Europe, and ends in the months after the end of World War II and the nuclear bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. The staged 1954 investigation into a secret committee aimed at denying the scientist, who had become uncomfortable by his pacifist political views, an extension of security clearance to allow him access to and collaboration with US nuclear programs constitutes the second level. Finally, the 1958 public hearings for the Senate confirmation of the politician Lewis Strauss - initially a supporter, later a personal enemy of Oppenheimer and the main person responsible for his downfall - represent the third plan. The second and third levels provide the flashbacks that recreate the first. Throughout the development of the biography are interspersed short and spectacular images that visually project Oppenheimer's thoughts: the mysteries related to the structure of the universe on a sub-atomic scale and on a cosmic scale in the first part of the film and the nightmares of destruction during the dawn of the atomic age. The result is a three-hour film in which the sequences often follow one another with the rapidity of video editing, while in other cases, long, documentary-like scenes record the endless debates in secret or public commissions. Color and black and white alternate to give the feeling of authenticity. 'Oppenheimer' seems like an encyclopedia of editing styles, but all adapted to the purpose. Spectacular, even impressive at times, but not easy to watch.

Do we understand Robert Oppenheimer, those around him and the era they lived in better after watching this film? Probably yes, in some ways, but not completely though. The book that inspired the film, 'American Prometheus', one of the many biographies and science books written about the scientist, has over 700 pages. Some aspects of the scientist's enrollment in the program, personal life and collaboration with his contemporaries are well rendered, others are treated superficially or completely ignored, such as those related to Oppenheimer's Jewish identity or his decisions to abandon fundamental scientific research in favor of the managerial practicalities of the military program (for this reason Oppenheimer never received a Nobel Prize). Cillian Murphy got into the character's mind and soul perfectly. The gallery of actors around him played their roles with precision: Robert Downey Jr. In the complex role of Lewis Strauss; Matt Damon as an excellent General Groves, Oppenheimer's military partner; Benny Safdie - very accurate and expressive as Edward Teller, Oppenheimer's rival (except for the biographical detail that Teller limped because of an accident in his youth, a detail omitted in the film); Gary Oldman with one single but memorable scene as President Harry Truman. The scenes that take place at Los Alamos during the work on the project and especially in the days and hours leading up to the first atomic explosion are formidable. The dilemmas of Oppenheimer and of his colleagues regarding nuclear weapons and the race between superpowers that has led to the balance of nuclear terror and the possibility of the destruction of all life on the planet are well brought to the screen. My feeling was that some of the aspects of American domestic politics are presented in too much detail and get lost, especially given the length and pace of the narrative. I have read some reviews where it is mentioned that details missed initially can be noticed or understood better on a second viewing. That would be true with many movies, but most moviegoers can't afford or don't want to watch a three-hour movie twice (or more!) times. I think that in this case two hours more filtered to the essentials would have been a more suitable format. 'Oppenheimer' is a remarkable film in many ways, but in this case I don't believe that size added quality or depth.

8.title: Flawless, but not one of his best.
8.content:
Oppenheimer is a great film by any standard. Important subject matter. Good script. Fantastic cast. Brilliant acting. Cillian is killing it, and pretty much every supporting actor performs beautifully. The special effects are impressive.

Oppenheimer is more or less flawlessly done. And yet it isn't one of my favorite Christopher Nolan movies. Just like Dunkirk wasn't. For me, some of his best qualities get wasted when he's telling a reality based story like Oppenheimer. Or Dunkirk, for that matter. Why? Because he can tell a fantastical story and have me believe it. In a way nobody else can.

My favorite film by Christopher Nolan remains Inception, which got better and better the second, third and even fourth time I watched it. Each time I found new details and clues that I had missed the first time. Tenet was similar in that respect, and Interstellar as well. Even his earlier work, like Following and Memento, had elements of this. But I doubt that I will find anything new the next time I see Oppenheimer. It will still be very, very good. But it won't be better.

8.title: Speechless
8.content:
This is the most amazing, beautiful movie I ever watched.

Then I was watching Oppenheimer I was left with wanted more.

Being in the cinema and watching it then the explosion go off you can feel it in your chest, like if you was really there with them.

I would recommend watching if you like WW2 movies or even movies about people in funny hats that want to blow stuff up.

I bet you £20 after watching Oppenheimer you will guarantee recognise at least one of the actors and actresses in the film.

I will be buying the movie on a streaming platform then it's available.

My Review from Billy Browning.

8.title: Nolan is always a legend
8.content: The best drama ever witnessed, one of the best dramatic experience . Its Nolan's masterpiece, every scene written is a master piece every dialogue, every screenplay has been crafted soo good. Cilian murphy who has just nailed with his performances, he just lived the character of oppenheimer. Oppenheimer is gem in the field of physics and atomic matter.
