Oppenheimer is a decent film about an important subject that gets bogged down with minor politics, we also have the nolan cut... But a nolan cut with a poor pay off.

Much of the film is full of close ups and facial expression but little else in the way of cinematography that we have come to enjoy in other Nolan films.

The sound was good however and is purposefully jarring. The whimsical early soundtrack is slowly obliterated by orchestral, human or explosive rumblings. Everything utilised to nail down the power of the bomb.

When the story follows the bomb and the challenges Oppenheimer had running the project it makes interesting viewing. The film constantly cuts between court like sequences set 8 or 9 years later. The problem with these cuts is that the pay off was of minor importance to the overall story.

The acting was good, Murphy and Depp did a great job its a shame their rivalry was pushed under the carpet while also being at the forefront of the finale. Its difficult to try and create drama over such a small footnote in the titular characters life and then infer it rather than show it.

The costumes and sets and the overall appearance of the film was very good and pulled me in a lot its just a shame the story wasn't as strong nor gripping as it could have been as well as failing to even mention many aspects of the real life project.

7/10.

7.title: A Good Film. Not Great.
7.content:
'Oppenheimer' could have been great. And here's how. Shave off 30 to 40 minutes. That's it. That's all it would have taken. I don't want to find myself impatient while viewing a film as important as this. Nor do I want to check my watch. More than once. But I did. And did it again. And maybe even a third time.

Point is, the message in Oppenheimer is repeated again and again. And it's: Not everyone who worked on the Atom Bomb was a blond-haired blue-eyed All-American Boy. The scientists and engineers had backgrounds that differed from the American stereotype. Their values and beliefs were different from 'ours'. Some were Communists. Others were former Communists. Still others were Anti-Communists. Some were great family men, others were womanizers and brought pain to their spouse. But about two things they agreed. (1) World War II had to be brought to an end. And (2) Nazi Germany could not be allowed to beat the Allies to the technology to build and use The Bomb.

Again and again, through character after character, that message is brought home. In government hearing after hearing that message is brought home. I wanted to stand up and yell, 'OK OK I got it.' No more. Let's move on. But moving on took quite a bit of time. And it's there, in those Post War government hearings and interrogations that the film seemed to slow. By this time we knew who the film's heroes were, we knew the villain to be unmasked. And knowing what I knew I was anxious for the obvious to be stated. But the film's final hour refused to give us what we wanted until - it seemed - the production ran out of film.

Other observations:

a. Cillian Murphy is great as a hard-to-define Oppenheimer. He's odd, but odd in a way that's hard to pin down; we like him and respect him but there's something going on in that mind of his that I found disquieting.

B. Florence Pugh is sensational as Oppenheimer's lover; as sensual a performance as has ever appeared on the screen.

C. Emily Blunt as Oppenheimer's wife is equally good but in a vastly different way. She ages, and ages badly, right before our eyes. She suffers and we suffer right along with her.

D. Robert Downey Jr. As a hopeful member of the President's cabinet is fabulous. He was one with his character. Best Supporting Actor qualities.

E. There are many - too many? - foreign scientists. Truth be told I could not always tell one from the other. Not a good thing. As one of them is a spy for The Soviet Union and when the spy is uncovered, I had no real idea of who it was. Or how important was his role.

F. Christopher Nolan's films play with time. Think Dunkirk. Think Tenet. Think Interstellar. They all took hard work on the part of the viewer to know where and when we were. Likewise Oppenheimer. We've got flashbacks by the dozen. Flashbacks within flashbacks. Maybe a flash-forward as well. Too much playing around with time for me. Just tell the story, Nolan. Stop being cute.

Anyway, See Oppenheimer. It's heart and mind are in the right place. It's an important film. Well made. Good to look at.

But long. Too long. By far.

7.title: Cillian Murphy was good but the movie lacked in some aspects
7.content:
Don't get me wrong, the main actor did an outstanding effort, but I felt like the physics visions represented in particles were cheesy, the moment with Jean where he was quoting Bhagavad Gita, when in real life he was quoting it in an interview where he clearly had PTSD was tasteless to be portrayed in a sex scene, the portrayal of his wife as an empowered strong woman when in real life she had severe alcoholism and even broke bones and had car accidents due to her alcoholism was inaccurate, the scene showing him and his affair partner sleeping together in the interrogation room as she was staring his wife into the eyes, when his wife was quite detached from the whole affair ordeal, also unnecessary.

Furthermore, why would you portray Niels Bohr, a Dane, and give him a vague Dutch accent when he's clearly Scandinavian. Why would you show Niels Bohr nearly biting into the apple when that never actually happened, no one bit the apple, and actually Oppenheimer was almost expelled due to what he'd done. And why would you portray Einstein as a man who behaves like a semi-homeless man is beyond me. Also, the PTSD scenes were underwhelming at best. And also, Jean was a psychiatrist, in the movie she was portrayed as a lesser intelligent younger girl he was sexually infatuated with.

Great acting, but the script and production could have been better.

7.title: Music interfered with the acting
7.content:
I thought the acting in this film was exceptional, to a person. I also didn't think it was too long, and it covered everything that seemed important. My only gripe is the fact that the musical score dominated the film and felt manipulative. In that I mean that there was enough tension and excitement without hearing a thousand violins ramping up the tension. It often was simply too loud. And it made it harder to really hear the dialogue. The scenes I found most satisfying were those where the music was muted and the dialogue came through.

I guess as a woman, I felt the portrayals of the two main women, his wife and his troubled lover, probably made them look less capable than they really were. The exception being the late scene when his wife faces the investigating panel.

7.title: The good for the greater bad
7.content: I took a couple of days to digest three hours of slow burn drama so here we are, ready to blast an impossibly objective review. Let's begin with the obvious: this is 100% Nolaned; the script is clean and meticulous; Robert Downey Jr stands out for best acting followed by Cillian Murphy and Emily Blunt; Matt Demon isn't credible; the music is too insidious; the visuals and the story itself aren't worthy of a big screen. Now that the most evident is dissected, here is the trick. The movie portraits an American patriot that oscillates between pride and guilt with enough elements to pull in both directions simultaneously. And when you think the script was a straight line without twists (and you would be right), subplots emerge to at least complete three hours of dialogues with emoted tension and resolution in the life of a scientist, the father of the atomic bomb, turned both monster and hero. My biggest turn off is that he story and the film deserve two hours - not three.

7.title: I'd probably like it better without the hype
7.content:
I try not to buy into hype. Rarely does a movie exceed high expectations. The Barbenheimer phenomenon basically ended in a thud for me: BARBIE was a horrendous toy commercial disguised as an existentialist statement, while OPPENHEIMER was competent Oscarbait enlivened only by a fantastic lead performance. Cillian Murphy deserves all the praise in the world for his delicate, almost Shakespearean work as the tragic Oppenheimer. He carried this movie like Atlas. The rest of the actors are great too (RDJ is a great antagonist). The visuals are fantastic, with Nolan using shallow depth of field to give the sense that the protagonist's world is closing in on him.

However, this is otherwise just an expensive run of the mill biopic, the kind of movie designed to win Oscar gold. It doesn't take any significant risks and it tells its story in a swift fashion-- almost too swift, actually. I often felt like I was watching a clip show. The movie never drags, but it also barely breathes.

Not a bad movie at all, but the kind where you leave the theater saying, "Yeah, that was good" while trying not to run to the bathroom.

7.title: So....unsure if I liked it or not
7.content: Actors did a great job, visuals were great and it was about important subject matter. I did NOT like the disjointed storyline and it felt like they left out so much of Oppenheimer's actual story. We see him at college and then at his great Atomic bomb building level. Story alludes to his greatness but not why. Also left out his wife's bio completely and in real life he got grief for that. Timelines were wonky too... made story hard to follow. Oh and they completely left out pearl harbor and the pivot to bombing Japan vs the original idea to use it on Hitler. Was also very long....they had ample time to tell the story but it was shown as more of a collage of times and events. Was it worth a watch? I think so. If only to bring up the conversation and go home and research everything. Cillian's portrayal was great tho...acting in this was really superb and believable.

7.title: Kind of heavy
7.content: "Oppenheimer" showcases impressive technical prowess and strong performances from its cast, notably Cillian Murphy's compelling portrayal. The cinematography and production design are visually striking, capturing the era's atmosphere authentically. However, the film's narrative feels overly dense and fails to maintain a consistent pace, making it challenging to fully engage with the story. While it delves into complex historical events, the heavy-handed approach may alienate viewers seeking a more accessible or cohesive storytelling experience. Overall, "Oppenheimer" is a visually impressive film with standout performances, but its narrative execution leaves room for improvement.

7.title: Good Nolan Stuff
7.content:
I was excited about the film, but my expectations were not that high. In this case I don't like being approved.

I hate politics, too much talking, because that is there reason, why I don't gave it 8 stars. It was pure salvation, after the movie was over.

But it's a good Nolan-movie. Good Casting, good camera movement, emotions etc.

At the end, after i went to imdb and watched the casting list, I was shocked, that I did not recocnized Robert Downey jr. XD And I know many actors after watching hundreds of films...

What do I miss or would do better?

Less politics, more physics.

If I would compare it to Tenet, I would say tenet was less boring than this, BUT I am excited for Memento!

7.title: visuals drowned out
7.content: The film is outstanding with so much fascinating and historical material however the constant musical score, woven into every scene for 3 hours, was a bit aggressive and often drowned out key dialogue-- it was almost as if the musical score was another character in the film- all of the acting warranted a score of at least an 8 yet my experience with the musical score lowered my score to a 7- the best part of the film for me was the actual test in the desert-- one of the few moments of silence during the entire film was during this scene and truly captured the enormity of it- i would recommend this film-

7.title: Not for everyone, but if you know his story it's done well
7.content:
Good watch if you have patience, scientific temper and desire to see a dramatized version of Oppenheimer's personal story.

This is not a background movie, you'll need to actually watch the movie.

It is not for everyone, if you want quick-action-satisfaction, this is not for you. The a-bomb explosion is not the main part of the story.

The main story is about how Oppenheimer was involved in the twisted world of politics for speaking his mind. It is HIS story, not of the war or the project.

For what the story is trying to show, it's very well done.

I have rated it seven stars because while it was good, I do not think it was thought inducing or a movie that'll end up to become a classic, at least not in my books.

7.title: Good but flawed.
7.content: Stylistically very competetent, visually pleasing and giving good insight into the different characters around the story of the bombs creation & their history. Most actors deliver a convincing and well thought out performance. At times it is easy to get lost as the time period queues are very subtle from Pre-War Europe through to Post War US Communist paranoia so you have to keep your wits about you. Where this film really falls down is it's attempt to make the audience feel sorry for the main character during an inquest, given he just helped masacre two civilian cities. That idea is rediculous and an impossible feat. The movie should have ended at the deployment of the weapon and not an attempt to make the audience feel pity for a then rich scientist involved.

7.title: 1st half feels like collection of tiktok/IG reels
7.content:
I have a mix feeling about the movie.

The 1st half of the movie feels like collection of tiktok/IG reels.

With jumps going so fast, it was harder to focus on any one character or character development or story flow.

It felt like the movie was going for punch line to punch lines like "the world with end with this bomb" and so on.

They built the Los Alamos, but if you have no idea why Los Alamos was built, the security, the secrecy, the bare bone structure of the city, the long and hard working hours of the scientist there, then from those jumping scenes, it was hard to understand the importance of Los Alamos.

Same way Niels Bohr flew from Germany, but the actor had a big smile on his face and he was asking can you make a bigger bomb. I mean, what was the reason behind him asking if the bomb is big enough. Why was Niels Bohr character even there, and why was he smiling.

Also, from jumping of scenes, it was also hard to grasp that it took them 2-3 yrs of long working days to finish the gadget. There was no sense of time how much they spent time in Los Alamos.

Like always Nolan's movie has of late got a real high music to the end that it has become difficult to hear the dialogues. If you don't have clear understanding of what happened from other sources, then the 1st half of the movie just felt like giving you an overview of the history but with a lot of jumps back and forth.

The 2nd half of the movie after the test gets better. They take time in scenes to develop a narrative enough before jumping to next scene.

I will definitely recommend watching season 1 of "Manhattan" tv show before watching the movie.

7.title: Pick a genre, any genre
7.content: I enjoyed the film, I knew a little bit about the Manhattan project but not much and I now feel I've learnt something historically and also in the very here and now which is scary. A very talented roster of actors with some cameos and brilliant performances from both Murphy and Downey Jr, I hated the latter in this film which just proves how good he is as I love him in most of his films. But I can't help but feel it was disjointed flicking back and forth between before, during and after. Other than the 2 mentioned actors the other characters don't make much of an impact, I felt like I'd watched about 4 genres rolled into 1 and there wasn't enough in about the actual bomb itself. Interesting film but it felt as if the different aspects of the storyline were all competing with each other as opposed to bringing the main focus of the film together. Not my favourite Nolan film.

7.title: Pachydermic? Certainly, it's not a step backwards in Nolan's filmography
7.content:
For the Christopher who cleared the author's blockbuster, to sublimate the superheroes with super torments, the depiction of his usual topoi and trademarks continues.

Proverbial dissertations on the arbitrariness of affections, in the course of Space Odysseys, through "dominant strategy", in Search of Lost Time in which to find a Yin & yang (inner and outer) that takes shape culminating in a relatively sinister, threatening and apocalyptic vision. Relatively. Because this time the dark side is only partially threatening, compared to the one depicted in Strangelove. In other words, the message creeps in that, for better or for worse, a future in Gotham City always awaits us around the corner.

Of a blockbuster, it has only the mainstream cast. And a workhorse montage of a major season. Elements that can already compete for nominations for the Academy Awards.

Julius Robert Oppenheimer is a Vitruvian man. A little different from the one described by Malcolm Gladwell in the non-fiction Outliers. Just look at his interactions, owing the Rule of the Game to an Altman-esque plot. At the same time Matt Damon, Downey jr. & co. Put on a mask, without turning into a "tench". We suspect and regret that Michael Caine would have been a perfect Einstein.

The plot is more usual than usual. Let me be clear, we have plenty of flashbacks and parallel montages. Also with surreal, futurist and hyper-realistic touches. With a total mastery of the set and the themes, already exhibited in Dunkirk, which fears no rivals in Aronofsky, Iñárritu or even in Paul Thomas Anderson.

Like Interstellar, in some sequences, the most obvious visual reference is the Cosmos docuseries (in particular the one with Neil DeGrasse Tyson). To go back to the masters of other times, there is more and more entrepreneurial spirit in the reconstruction of a set in the west(ern) on which Hollywood was born, following the tradition of John Ford and his pupils (or followers).

Instead, for the masses, despite the added value of a structured viewing for IMAX screens, it can come as a massive and exhausting work. That is, what happened and happens to those who see a film by David Lean like Lawrence of Arabia. In fact, Cillian Murphy, the former Peaky Blinder, already busily lunatic and spirited in a (professional) role similar to Danny Boyle in Sunshine, is increasingly Peter O' Toole's heir.

As Variety noted, the segment of the first nuclear test may be the center of gravity on which all the work revolves. And it can become a milestone of the seventh art. We live the stroke of the Atomic Age with our own eyes, just as we observed on our skin the symptoms of schizophrenia in A Beautiful Mind. Or the breaking of the sound barrier in the documentary Senna.

While a good storyteller like Ron Howard concocts chronicles for episodes with a known epilogue, moreover representing obstacles to their crowning, here we have an Author like Nolan who, among those of his generation, now competes only with Tarantino in terms of style. Like a famous sequence from Reservoir Dogs, we even feel a hidden anguish for that situation with a well-known and perhaps outdated outcome. Around this scene, throughout the rest of the film, revolves a story of the trial, which in its way follows the archetype of Caine Mutiny with Bogart, able to satisfy the needs of the plot, rather than the expectations.

Won't it be a masterpiece? Of course, it's not a step backwards in the director's filmography.

7.title: Like a three hour version of the helicopter scene in Apocalypse Now..
7.content:
Maybe fittingly. Coz that's the idea: Apocalypse Now. Right. Well the overbearing concert music over the top of the drama is ok for the first five minutes the viewer realises it's not gonna stop.

For three hours.

Nolan does this a lot. Batman and Heath Ledger was practically unwatchable for the same reason. He did it with Dunkirk too.

Most people are Nolan fans, but I'm not. Not really. Inception went wildly off course I wish he'd let me write the second half.

This is up there with the best he's created but the music is an unnecessary stain on an interesting and dramatic storyline.

Above average maybe worthy of a 7 n half or summat. I'd give it 8 without the noise.

7.title: Should have been better
7.content: Another movie by Nolan,with exceptional actors and impressive CGI (aka huge budget) but nothing special as far as the scenario and cinematography are concerned. Cliché-depicted the life of a scientist, the female role etc. I believe that with such great performances and interesting historical events, the movie should have been way more thrilling. Another thing is, that when you create a movie about the life of a physicist, it is essential that you comprehend at least the basic knowledge required and not just throw random stuff in the script. Historically speaking, the movie was more complete and the flashbacks, although used too many times, served well.

7.title: All gas no breaks
7.content:
This movie feels way to fast. There are no breathers except when they are detonating the testbomb, it was a welcome change of pace. The whole movie feels compressed and rushed. If this was an 10 episode (10 hour total) series like chernobyl this would have been phenomenal and maybe even out doing chernobyl itself. The story can easily do 10 hours of fotage.

Cillian Murhpy is what makes this movie reach for the higher ratings and together with Christopher Nolans excellent expertise in making outstanding griping scenes you dont even have to understand what is happening to appriciete this movie. That is why i have it an 8 even though it can be hard to follow.

7.title: Could have been a great film - hope they release a Director's Cut..
7.content:
There are a lot of reviews mentioning how the jumps between timelines are too erratic. It seems to me that this was due to two factors. Firstly IMAX limits film length to 3hrs and the original cut was 3 1/2 hours, but also Christopher Nolan never cuts scenes. Ultimately this meant scenes were cut down and the result was a very hard to follow first half of the movie. It might work for an action film or a mystery, but there were a lot of historical characters all of which had important roles, and working out who they were and what was happening was really difficult at times and not really an enjoyable movie experience.

The cinematography, acting, writing and music were perfect, but I would love to see the director's original cut, I imagine those early scenes are better paced and make much more sense..

7.title: A Riveting Tale with Room for Improvement
7.content:
While I was initially disappointed by 'Oppenheimer's' departure from Nolan's signature fantasy time-travel themes, it's still a great movie.

'Oppenheimer' delivers an impressive portrayal of a true story. The film excels in its storytelling, compelling acting performances, and captivating cinematography that deftly plays with light and darkness, all while embracing a distinct 1940s aesthetic. The seamless integration of visual effects and music enhances the overall experience, effectively building suspense that had me on the edge of my seat. Moments of humor artfully contribute to a well-rounded emotional journey.

However, similar to Nolan's past work, like 'Tenet,' there were instances where the dialogue proved challenging to discern, highlighting the need for improved audio clarity. While the commitment to historical accuracy is commendable, there is a noticeable lack of diversity among the cast. Additionally, certain instances of nudity felt gratuitous and could have been omitted without diminishing the story's impact.

In summary, 'Oppenheimer' shines through its compelling storytelling, stunning visuals, and skillful suspense-building, despite minor setbacks.

7.title: Underwhelmed, maybe unfairly so.
7.content: OK, full disclosure, I really feel I shoukd be rating this higher that a 7 on the back of other people's reviews, but that's all I feel I can do for now. I might actually re watch soon. Extemely important film, and very good acting all round, I was just looking for something more I think. I beleive the sheer enormity of the subject matter in hand deserved a more dramatic punch for the viewer. I really wanted to leave feeling utterly shocked and conflicted by the film. Maybe it's subtlety is what makes it so good? Just not convinced at the moment. Very much leaning towards an early second viewing.

7.title: Now i am become boring, the destroyer of time
7.content: This movie is not all boring, it has some amazing moments. But it does not feel like a movie rather than a over explanatory trailer about a great movie. It constantly feels like it's moving either to fast or to slow. Sometimes you feel like you are just being force feed information at a rate that no human ever would find pleasing. Other times you almost fall asleep beacuse of the low tempo. The movie also focuses more on the political side of the manhattan project rather than oppenheimer himself. Therefore when any emotional scenes with oppenheimer and his close ones would appear you would just feel like the third wheel of a relationship that you barely knew existed. I personally feel this is the problem with alot Cristhofer Nolan's movies. I do love some of his work, but constantly i feel like i never really knew the characters that well. With Memento as a exception. Cillian Murphy as Oppenheimer did well enough. In the start of the movie he was very interesting and displayed alot of emotions through his acting. By the half and the end it more felt like i was watching some sigma male tiktok compilation. This really made the movie alot harder to watch than it should have been. The only emotions displayed by Cillian at the end was intensly staring in to the distance, so the marketing team was perhaps not lying. This was made even more clear when seeing Gary Oldman as Truman. In my opinion he outpreformed every single one with his scene. His face shifted so slightly with each new emotion and really had you at the edge of your seat. Cillian's intensive stare quickly became exposed of its shortcomings by this preformance. I could go into the visual side of this movie but we all know they are the best as always with Cristhofer Nolan so im not gonna waste your time with that. I am going to say that Ludwig Göransson made an absolute banger with the score to this movie and it truly made the whole experience alot better.

7.title: I have some real mixed feelings
7.content:
There's alot of ways this movie was good. Let's talk about some of those first.

First of all, I like that this movie hewed pretty closely to real history. Much more so than most Hollywood 'historical' movies. There's just no excuse in my opinion to contradict a known fact when making a historical movie. And Oppenheimer doesn't from what I've read. Sure, conversations are imagined, and what not, but you can't really make a movie if you don't.

Second, I think the production values, the visual elements, the acting, etc. - all first rate. I'm sitting here trying to think of a performance to criticize, and I'm coming up blank.

The back third of the movie also got REALLY riveting. Once the confirmation hearing and the clearance hearing become actual showpieces instead of weak connective tissue to tie other scenes together, I think the movie really get compelling in a way I didn't feel for the first two thirds.

Which brings me to some of what I didn't like. I REALLY disliked the very chaotic time-hopping storytelling that occurs throughout the movie. But in particular the first third REALLY drug for me as I often wasn't sure when/where/who was going on until halfway into a scene. That really destroyed my enjoyment of the early movie.

The movie finally gets to the meat of Los Alamos in the middle third, and the history nerd in me loved that part. I feel like it maybe wasn't as compelling as it should have been, but they start to introduce characters that really livened up the action as opposed to the very boring bit about Oppenheimer's politics...which I understand was a part of his story, but just didn't make for compelling movie to me. The middle bit picked up, but also wasn't really the best part to me. It was the last third.

The movie was also just too dang long. Especially given the time jumps and narrative sameness early on. It was a real slog.

I also really found something about the dialogue kept rubbing me the wrong way. I felt like it was kind of stilted and awkward. I frequently found myself thinking 'who talks like that?'. And I don't just mean the 1940s and 50s style of it, but they often spoke very stiffly. No one really seemed like they were friends or even acquantances. That threw me a bit.

But overall, good movie. Uneven, and I had mixed feelings, but I think it was good.

7.title: History
7.content:
Great movie, but with a great fault; not a minor, but a major historical failure to show the central role that president Roosevelt played in the first years of the relevant period. Einstein and others convinced president Roosevelt that Germany was in the process of developing an atomic bomb and it was Roosevelt who decided to launch the Manhatten Project. It was also Roosevelt who sent a letter to Oppenheimer thanking him for leading the successful work in New Mexico. A film about Oppenheimer and the atomic bomb without a role for FDR is like making a film about The Battle of Britain without Winston Churchill.

Yours Gideon Zlotnik.

7.title: Ambiguous and indecisive but well done.
7.content:
I finally relented and watched this telling of the story behind the 2 greatest individual acts of genocide in the history of the world. I wasn't going to watch it for the same reason I don't seek out Mexican cartel murder videos, jihadist beheading videos or drone footage of men murdering one another at a remove in Ukraine.

Thankfully this was not the self congratulatory propaganda piece that it could easily have been. That said I'm not entirely sure what it is, other than ambiguous and indecisive. Is this deliberate? Was Nolan cowed by the disagreeable world in which we currently live? Could he have been anything other than ambiguous and indecisive and not have been crucified by whichever side of the political spectrum he offended?

This was a 3 hour tightrope act desperate to not cause offense when the subject matter is the most offensive act in human history.

Regardless, the acting is superb across the board, the cinematography superb, the storytelling superb. However, it lacks an opinion, it lacks courage and it does it's level best to hide it.

However, certainly 30 years ago, perhaps even 10 years ago, this film would not have been ambiguous, it would have been self congratulating and certain of itself so I suppose this is a step in the right direction, perhaps in another 30-40 years people will be able to make movies that acknowledge this act for what it was.

7.title: oppenheimer
7.content:
I realize that when making a film about the person most responsible for opening the Pandora Nuke Box (hey, at least I resisted genie out of the bottle!) lightness of tone and swiftness of pacing will be in necessarily short supply...although Kubrick managed to provide us with generous amounts of both in "Strangelove" now, didn't he? Still, this has to be the heaviest, most self important film on the topic since Stanley Kramer took us for a trudge on the beach (to mention nothing of judging us at Nuremberg). In other words, with one brilliant, extended exception, which I will get to and which is why it gets a 7 'stead of a 6, this is your basic Talking Scientist Head Movie and since the talk is courtesy of the director, Christopher Nolan, and since Nolan's dialogue is almost as oppressive as the film score, you have endless variations of characters going "My God, what have we done?" And endless permutations of the title character hand wringing and moaning and groaning and breast beating and hallucinating so that when Truman (nicely played by Gary Oldman) tells his aide to "not let that crybaby in here again" you sympathize with Give 'Em Hell, Harry, not Give 'Em Guilt, Oppie.

So, yeah, a fairly slow slog. And at least forty five minutes too long. I would have taken the scissors to most of the Lewis Strauss stuff, despite Robert Downey's very good performance, since the movie is, well, called "Oppenheimer", and not "Oppenheimer/Strauss".

However, I would be less than honest if I did not also mention that the long section dealing with the testing of the bomb at Los Alamos is amazingly good, with tension and immediacy and a notable, welcome lack of dialogue and music. It is a timely reminder that before he donned his VID (Very Important Director) mantle Nolan was one fine film maker. Give it a B minus.

PS...My favorite performance was neither the too actorish Cillian Murphy nor Downey but rather Emily Blunt's blunt, angry and hard edged take on Oppenheimer's spouse.

7.title: Leaves much to be desired.
7.content:
Quite a frustrating watch to be honest. Being a big fan of biopics, history, war, science, and Nolan, this film was going to be one to remember fondly. But it is not the case. As the film ends, I'm only thinking how it leaves much more to be desired.

Oppenheimer - a character study interspersed with events surrounding the Manhattan Project which feels more like a minor secondary plot. Unemotional and rather jarring to the point where one might be tempted to use the word boring were the political and courtroom plots. By trying to blend in two stories, one being the Manhattan Project and the other being the political/courtroom drama, it fails to deliver on both sides. Can't help but think it would do much much better just focusing on one or the other. Deliver 100% on one story rather than 50% on two mushed in ones. Personally, I feel much more excited whenever the story progresses on the Manhattan Project-side - the building of the bomb, the work differences of the scientists/military/politicians, the morals, the ethical dilemmas, the politics of the project. The film builds on those aspects then, deflates into the courtroom-like scenes, taking steam off any real weight, emotions, and connections.

However, it's not all bad. Nolan delivers on the technical filmmaking and the cast delivers on the acting. Film and filmmaking lovers will have much to enjoy and awards are almost guaranteed I dare say. The acting was the best part of the whole film. Needless to say, Cillian Murphy delivers as Oppenheimer himself and as many, many others mentioned, Robert Downey Jr. Also stands out.

All in all, it still is a Christopher Nolan film and it shows. Though, it leaves much to be desired for as it aspired to be much more but can't. Just like my life.

7.title: Very good, not the masterpiece some are claiming it is.
7.content:
Let me start by saying that this is a very, very good movie. The cinematography is fantastic, the actors are doing a terrific job, and the directing is top notch of course even if, like me, you may disagree with some of the choices. Back to acting performances, Cillian Murphy truly does deserve all the praise he got for this movie, but all the supporting cast is equally talented; for example this is the first time in years Robert Downey Junior does not immediately conjure up Tony Stark.

I do have issues with the time jumps. Honestly it is a strange choice here that is confusing, and do not necessarily bring anything additional to the story telling; moreover it causes us to take a lot longer than necessary to fully get into the movie at first. Which also doesn't help with the fact that it is a very long movie, with many scenes that could have been much shorter without any loss in quality.

So all in all, any cinephile should watch this movie and I do recommend it, but I can see why it might not satisfy a certain audience.

7.title: Great Story Questionable Sound
7.content:
Great Story from the start going into amazing details about all the characters and there lives. All the way to when they dropped the bomb, yes we was around 2hrs into the film but it was such a huge build up to a rushed bomb drop scene which left you feelinging disappointed. So much more could be done but saying this they would of probably had to add another hour to the already long film.

Another thing that bugged me through the whole film was the clash between music and voices. The sound track is 2nd to none but sometimes it's pushed to much you can not here what is going on or being said.

Final point this film is for someone who loves a very detailed not much action but a gripping story.

7.title: I finally understood Nolan films
7.content:
I had anticipated a more straightforward, character-driven study of the man who helped to develop the atomic bomb, but instead, I was met with a 3-hour long summer blockbuster and a possibility of hearing loss.

Thinking about this, I feel guilty for not understanding Nolan's summer films since I've seen all of them except Memento. Now it is clearer that this (Oppenheimer) is exactly what I should've expected, but for some reason, I didn't.

So now, understanding that I went to see it with a wrong impression or a misunderstanding of the director's style, I'll give my two cents on this one.

The film's editing was particularly problematic. The director is known for his use of quick cuts and jarring transitions, but in Oppenheimer, this style felt overused and gratuitous. The film's many plot threads were constantly being cut away from, making it difficult to follow the narrative up until the very end. Not much complaining can be done after Tenet and Dunkirk, but again, I expected something different for a bio-drama.

The sound mixing was also poor, with the dialogue often being drowned out by the music. This was especially frustrating during the film's tensest moments when I was desperate to hear what the characters were saying. Again, this was my IMAX experience. Maybe yours will be different.

Another problem is that there's just too much story. Oppenheimer wasn't a short film by no means, the creators wanted to make a deep dive into the political and historical background of some of the major characters, and there were so many of them. I don't think making this a solo film was a good idea, but a Chornobyl-style mini-series - would've worked great. They had so many good actors, but they were forced to fly through the scenes on an airplane bomber since they were limited by the runtime.

Despite these flaws, there were many redeeming qualities to Oppenheimer. The film's performances were all excellent, much so I cannot single out a particular one. The film's visuals were also stunning, with Nolan's trademark use of IMAX cinematography creating some truly awe-inspiring images. The soundtrack was plain gorgeous, and very memorable. Too bad that it was mixed into scenes where it shouldn't have been, and it also had some weird cuts, almost like clipping, ruining the tone. Like it was artificially cloned and stretched. Maybe I'm making this up.

Ultimately, Oppenheimer is a film that is both ambitious and flawed. It is a film that attempts to grapple with the weighty subject matter of the atomic bomb, but it ultimately fails to do so satisfyingly for me. I would recommend watching the film at home, where you can adjust the volume and take breaks as needed.

P. S. I also want to thank the creators for finally giving me an understanding of what to expect, and saving me from later disappointments.

7.title: I left feeling deflated
7.content:
This was definitely something I'd been looking forward to and was excited to see some 'real cinema'. What with all the excellent actors, top director, and interesting subject matter, I was ready to really 'feel something', and my initial feeling is a bit deflated, to be honest.

The acting here is top quality, there's no doubt, and all the characters, of which there are what feels like millions, all have depth and plenty of important dialogue. But by the second hour, I had succumbed to the sheer volume of detailed exchanges and personal motives. They just throw it at you scene after scene, and for the first time in a movie, I wished I was at home watching a 5-part limited series where I could debate and analyze with my wife what the hell was going on at times.

Christopher Knowlen is a master in my opinion because he creates such rich environments and thought-provoking movies like Interstellar and Inception that challenge the viewer while delighting them with a fast-paced story that is captivating to watch. This movie left me needing to watch it two more times to soak up every piece of detail, with none of the motivation to do it. The first 30 mins are so promising, and the visuals about the nature of reality are stunning and mind-expanding. This is short-lived before the reality of mechanics, ego, and politics are shuffled on our heads scene by scene.

I will watch this movie again, I've no doubt, but not soon and not for money.

7.title: Boring old news trapped in the past
7.content:
I used to have respect for Nolan before I realized he doesn't embrace the change of times. It' very simple. You either embrace great changes, grow, and become better or you just become old news trapped in the past. And this is the case with Nolan.

While all the great directors like Scorsese, Coppola, Cameron, Kosinski, McQuarrie, etc. Are shooting their great movies in 4-6K resolution digital IMAX cameras and Dolby ATMOS and DTS:X sound, Nolan is still trapped in the past with his stupid analog films and plain DTS-HD MA.

And his story telling is just getting worse and worse and more boring. It's all part of the same symptoms of people who are just trapped in the past and can't learn to improve. You just can't teach some old dogs new tricks.

7.title: Too many conversations
7.content:
Great movie but the hype is jus too much! The screen presentation is excellent but way too many conversations and talks rather than action and story . The scene in and out from past to the present makes it very difficult to grasp and I feel that it Should have been simple and plain ! Why is there no scene of the bomb in Japan 🇯🇵 ? Instead the blast from the trinity makes us to crave for more ! The acting is top notch and screenplay is brilliantly impressive.

The actors make their roles so very real and to life ! I feel the movie is too long and less actions or fights.... There is no scene of the war in that era or the enemy. Feels like is a documentary within a movie !

7.title: Flawed, solid enough, but not great
7.content: The story of J Robert Oppenheimer 'the father of the Atomic bomb' in the hands of Christopher Nolan is a somewhat over inflated dialogue heavy affair. The film flashes back and forwards in time, and is often engrossing, particularly during build up to the first A-Bomb test, but it also gets bogged down in talky scenes focused on political and scientific controversies both during and after WW2. I thought that perhaps a more economical approach could have made Oppenheimer truly gripping and great, and could have helped explore more effectively the post WW2 period when Oppenheimer fell foul of McCarthy era investigations. I also found the music score often unnecessarily intrusive and annoying, further highlighting a sense of the film being just a bit over done, however, there were still things to savour, not the least an uncannily vivid and convincing performance by Cillian Murphy as Oppenheimer, plus many other excellent performances, effectively making the acting the best thing about the film. I thought Oppenheimer was a largely coherent and informative though rambling portrait of the man, wonderfully performed, meticulously written and directed by Nolan, but just pretty good when just a bit more economy might have made it great.

7.title: Good Cinematography, Discombobulated Story
7.content:
By no means is Oppenheimer a bad film - in fact I would recommend anyone looking for an experience to go check it out. However I do believe the film is a bit unorganized and is largely saved by good performances and great cinematography, at least up until the last one-half to one-third. After that, the story takes a more "traditional" route and cleans everything up nicely, barring a few things which I wish were done differently.

Again. I highly recommend this film to anyone who is looking for an alternative and perhaps a bit more "high roller" drama in the same category as "The Theory of Everything" / "Goodwill Hunting" / " A Beautiful Mind"

7.title: Felt like I watched 3 hours of C-SPAN!
7.content:
I found the movie so boring, with a ton of exposition, unending dialog and undue screen time dedicated to the most boring issue which is his security clearance. How could a genius like Nolan not find a more cinematic way to reveal the the characters or consequences of strong opinions by scientific community, than a hearing, not just 1 but 2. . Also how can a movie about a scientist not have any meaningful or educative explanation of nuclear physics or anatomy of the bomb? Even the fictional setup in Inception was explained in a more detailed fashion.

Some highlights that I wish they spent more time on: 1) Silence during explosion. Loved that it was an Easter egg for people who love science. It was a choice made not necessarily for an artistic reason but a scientific one, as light travels faster than sound. Wish there were more such.

2) When one character tells Strauss that Einstein and Oppen were probably not talking about him, but something important instead. I wish Nolan applied that to his film and realized that spending majority of the movie on Strauss' trial is not as important when the world the movie is set in involves Oppenheimer, Einstein, Atom bomb, WW2, a world after the first nuclear attack, nuclear arms race, the dynamic of great scientific minds from the world coming together to build the bomb/advance science.

3) Psychological complexity and catharsis: there were hints at what caused the eventual change of mind within Oppen towards the bomb, but it didn't seem organic to me. Was it triggered by Matt Damon's character ending communication with Oppen, or because of the way the test bombing looked, or hearing Truman announce the attack on Hiroshima on radio? Or meeting Truman?

4) Terrific acting all the way.

I am huge Nolan fan and my favs are Prestige, Interstellar, Dark Knight Rises.

7.title: Know what to do expect from this movie
7.content:
If you know Chris Nolan movies, you will know the usual tropes
Non- linear story telling
Great background score but loud at times making dialogue non-comprehensible
-Studded star cast

So what else is there to write a review about? Two words- Cillian Murphy. Murphy was so convincing I forgot he was an actor playing Oppenheimer. If this movie does not land an Oscar for Murphy, it will surely be a lost opportunity. Also notable are the supporting performances by Robert Downey Jr., Matt Damon and Emily Blunt.

The biggest criticism I have on this movie, is that Nolan goes overboard with the non-linear story telling with too many time jumps making a relatively simple timeline too complex for an average audience to follow.

Furthermore, it is important for anyone keen to watch this movie to know what the movie is about- it is a movie about the life of Oppenheimer, not about the bomb..Infact, Nolan shows very little of the Trinity bomb and the dropping the bomb on Hiroshima and Nagasaki...using a rather muted way to show the latter.. perhaps to respect the sensitivities of the incident. The story follows the tribulations and trials of Oppenheimer before and after the bomb so there are many panel discussion and committee hearing scenes that may bore some who are not interested in history. All in all it's an important story to be told and Nolan manages to tell it in the way only Nolan can.

7.title: Big Hype, Experience Not so...
7.content:
Yep, just watched it. The whole 3 hours of it. True, it is a nice film. But man, the first hour there is not even 3 seconds to breathe. Just dialogue over dialogue over new character over new character.

That leaves you confused and bored. You are really trying to make sense but some part of you thinks to leave the cinema.

I think Mat Damon brought some positive feelings to the film. A little comedy, or a little "out of order".

Towards the end there are some conclusions, hints of truth, feelings which will fulfill you.

But it's not enough. IMAX is not needed at all. Half of the film is B/W.

7.title: Not a bad movie, but the marketing campaign made me expect a lot more than I saw.
7.content:
I am a big Christopher Nolan fan and went to see Oppenheimer with great enthusiasm. The marketing campaign presented the movie as something innovative, something you should definitely see on IMAX to get unforgettable emotions, but unfortunately the movie didn't live up to my expectations. The movie is good, not a bad plot, very good performance of actors. But going to the movie by CRISTOPHER NOLAN, you expect more than 3 hours of dialogues to a tense melody and 1-minute scene of the "Test" atomic bomb explosion.

Objectively speaking, the film is not bad.

But subjectively - not the kind of film that you want to watch over and over again, like Interstellar, Inception or Tenet. In terms of cinematography, I didn't see anything new, and it's hard to come up with a beautiful picture when the setting is a small room with 5-6 people talking continuously.

My verdict, if anyone is interested, is 7/10, for a good story, editing, and excellent acting.

7.title: Amazing performance by Murphy, but the social-political drama diluted the story.
7.content:
*spoilers* The movie was fast-paced in the early goings and settled into a good pace in the middle of the film. Then, the film slows down drastically in the last hour and drags.

For the first two hours, the film was enjoyable. There was an interesting cast/characters, held together by a riveting performance by Murphy. In these parts, the plot had real stakes with the race against the Germans and genuine interest for me as an audience in wanting to watch the bomb development process. The cinematography and sound editing were also lovely.

The last hour was filled with socio-political drama and was where the movie fell short. This last part drags on due to several things. One, audiences had no reason to buy into the character motivation of Strauss as he wasn't in the main story. Hence, the plot felt fragmentary. Two, it was a cold-war commie witch hunt again, which felt hardly relatable. Three, the film focused on building the A-bomb not the H-bomb. So, all the discussion regarding Oppenheimer's position on the H-bomb felt remote. And four, I couldn't really understand the purpose of having the last hour. Yes, the film reiterated the burden and consequences Oppenheimer felt and portrayed his loyalty and love to his country. But everything else about the hearing felt contrived and unnatural. Perhaps those events played a role in Oppenheimer's real-life timeline, but it felt like Nolan was trying to make the plot interesting.

Lastly, instead of having Oppenheimer speak his values/lessons/takeaways towards the end of the film, we got a cheeky conclusion from Albert Einstein. As a device in the film, it does leave the movie more open-ended for interpretation, but it feels like an opportunity missed.

It was a good film, but the ending was thoroughly underwhelming. I walk away with the feeling that Nolan is up to his usual tricks again. If the angle of approach to storytelling could be a bit less commie witch hunt and told more succinctly under 2.5 hours, I would definitely give an 8 or a 9 out of 10 instead.

7.title: Well thought out, poor execution
7.content:
Oppenheimer was an experience.

The film, in many ways, was exceptional and clearly made by Nolan. However, compared to his other films, this one is a mixed bag.

1. For a stacked cast filled with actors such as R. Downey Jr, Florence Pugh, Emily Blunt, and Cillian Murphy, you would expect the characters to be connectable. Well, not the case. There is no real emotional depth or storyline in this movie, which in succession caused it to lose intensity the farther you progress. Characters are rapidly introduced, all seeming to process some importance by the end in reference to Oppenheimer's final Security Check. However, during these final testimonies it is extremely difficult to feel any sympathy or connection with these characters. Though dramatized events in Oppenheimer's life are constantly explored, he still remains a distant protagonist. Emily Blunts character is one of the only characters to show emotional expression. I feel the point of historical bio-pictures is to make the characters more connectable, dramatized even.

2. Though I see little to no one pointing this out, I feel like both nudity scenes in the movie were entirely avoidable. Both scenes added little to nothing to the plot, besides the reveal of Oppenheimer's affair, which could've shown without such,.

3. Personally, I feel this movie doesn't quite convey the significance of the events it follows after the initial bomb test. The non-linear typically Nolan timeline downplays the events. The bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki we only hear Truman over the radio? The announcement of the bombings almost initially passed over me due to the quiet audio during this scene as well. After watching a 3 hour movie centered around the atomic bomb, selfishly, I would've at least liked to have see at least one of cities get actually bombed. Flashing scenes between alleged communism and choppy dialogue left a quite boring and rather confusing second half. A whirlwind of heavy dialogue and different timelines/perspectives that ultimately conveyed a rather confusing story of Oppenheimer. For a viewer going into this movie with little to no previous knowledge on the psyche that came with the atomic bomb, you will be confused. This movie provides little to no exposition for characters political sides regarding the bomb or general morals. Typically, I understand not having a large amount of exposition for the sake of keeping the plot rolling. However, for a 3 hour movie this courtesy was not granted.

4. Overall, the soundtrack wasn't stellar, though it was extremely loud. The constant intrusion of music and loud noises took away from the film itself. In many cases I found myself reaching to gasp bits of unintelligible dialogue.

5. The cinematography in this movie was amazing, along with the set designs, and hidden details. Granted, there were your traditional terrific Nolan details which made the film gratifying, but overall maybe little to no impact.

7.title: Disappointing
7.content:
It's so hyped but I think It's only above average.

Non-linear story telling as usual. But did the parts match? But it got the punchline right.

It doesn't have much shock value; maybe as Newscientist reports it, "(the movie) addresses the paranoia around nuclear power" so basically it tries to show the true nature of nuclear power that it is not a creation of the devil. Or maybe Nolan sacrificed the shock value for historical accuracy. But was it historically accurate even? I don't know.

IMO, Chernobyl mini series delivered everything better. The shock, the politics, the story, aftermath, and all.

7.title: Boring, epic and then a courtroom thriller
7.content:
After an hour or more of pure dialogue in different rooms, different time layers and ever-changing protagonists, the film starts finally when they start composing the first bomb.

Then also the score starts matching with the story, which was in the first half sometimes over the top.

In opposite to some comments, claiming that the last part should have been shorter, for me this was the most satisfying third, a thrilling courtroom story, where the fast time changes definitely made a lot of more sense than in the first half, where they just made it difficult to get into the story and develop some sympathy or at least understanding for the characters.

Robert Downey jr. Outshines a great cast with a multifaceted Cilian Murphy (Oppenheimer is definitely not my favorite character), a very sympathetic Matt Damon and a pretty believable Emily Blunt.

I'm not sure if the dialogue part is necessary, maybe even good the second watch, but the effort is worth it.

7.title: Masterful storytelling, yet yearns for more impact
7.content:
Perhaps the first Nolan film that could have potentially benefited from computer-generated effects. Nolan is a master at narrating a visual story through traditional means, but this time the wonder of splitting the atom remained somewhat remote. Traditional explosions and spark showers, created with pyrotechnics, even seemed naive in depicting the incredible power of nuclear fission.

The film was long, but not tediously so. The complex navigation of Oppenheimer through the jungle of human relationships and political connections was skillfully executed. The only thing that distracted in the story was the excessive focus on Oppenheimer's interrogations - this could have been trimmed down.

7.title: Feels like a one-watch film but still really good
7.content: Overall, a very good watch. Sadly, I was unable to see this one in cinemas, because I didn't realise I would need ID. Apparantly I don't look a day over 15, thanks I guess?? Personally, the film is a little too long, with the most notable part of the film happening over the half-way mark. And the relationship between Robert (Murphy) and Jean (Pugh) confused me a little, don't know why because it was pretty self-explanatory. It's just the way that she decides to end her life because he said they couldn't see eachother anymore... After all the times that she gave hints that she was only in it for the 'fun'...Hmmm. What I do like about the film, and I mean I REALLY like it, was the lead-up to the testing of the bomb. The tension that was created just in the scenes of the creation and when they were hoisting it up. Plus, the weather. The weather should have been paid for it's job because WOW. But, when the testing scene came, I literally stopped breathing. I don't know how to describe how beautifully made that scene was. Nolan is in my good books for this film.

7.title: Unpopular Opinion. Oscar worthy? NO!
7.content:
My IMDb Rating: 6.5/10 1) Nolan's Oppenheimer (2023) is a historically accurate film.

2) But sadly, the movie feels like Made-for-TV drama! Interesting but not engaging enough!

3) The focus should have been on making of the bomb! But, what we see is Oppenheimer's communist past, his messy love life, his trial and his tussles with Lewis Strauss etc.

4) There is almost no science in the movie, just politics! Names of scientists are thrown randomly: Einstein, Bohr, Feynman, Fermi, Heisenberg etc. - but with no real character development & arcs. So the film feels hollow and pretentious.

5) This movie is crammed with too much story! Every scene feels rushed. Every scene is loaded with dialogues. You move on to the next scene and its even more dialogue. Nolan is guilty of not letting any scene breathe by itself, and he does not allow the audience to absorb and process the scenes! It feels like a marathon of scenes trying to reach the finish line! So in the end, even a 3-hour run time is simply not good enough!

6) The entire IMAX thing was a gimmick. The cinematography was nothing special. That's completely fine given the kind of movie it is. You can't really have any breath-taking shots when shooting a realistic biopic set in small to medium sized rooms (classrooms, labs, living rooms, offices, senate...). The only scenes with potential were the shots in the desert. But the filmmakers made a conscious decision to opt for realism. It's just that they hyped-up the IMAX experience so much that it felt truly disappointing.

7) Nolan's film is neither a feature film nor a documentary, and is abjectly floundering in-between! A feature film even when re-telling history, must evoke emotions - one reason why filmmakers like: Spielberg (Saving Private Ryan, Lincoln, Schindler's List, The Terminal, Catch me if You Can, Bridge of Spies, The Fabelmans); Ron Howard (A Beautiful Mind, Cinderella Man); Brian de Palma (Scarface); Asif Kapadia (Senna, Amy) are a class apart!

(Anurag Kashyap's Black Friday (2007) is a brilliant docustyled feature and an unique anamololy.)

7.title: Nolan Explores A New Genre
7.content: Christopher Nolan is a mastermind at coming up with novel concepts like in Inception, Memento and Tenet. That's what makes him Nolan in my humble opinion. He has also proved to be a genius when it comes to action fantasies like in The Batman Trilogy. Nolan is also the best when it comes to thrillers whether they are sci-fi thrillers such as Interstellar or war thrillers such as Dunkirk or psychological thrillers such as The Prestige and Insomnia. So he experiments with different genres and here he is, yet again, embarking on a whole new genre, biographical movies! Most biographical movies are boring, lame and empty but this one is the best biopic I've ever seen. I mean, the black and white scenes, the loud bombing in the IMAX theatre, the storytelling and the phenomenal score in the background, all of that fits together really well in a 3 hour screenplay that takes you away from reality and makes you lose your sense of time. When the credits rolled I was in shock knowing that 3 hours had just passed by because to me it literally felt like 30 minutes. It was unbelievable. However, I think Chris Nolan is poor at writing drama. It's his biggest weakness and unfortunately Oppenheimer is only about personal drama so it doesn't have any aspects at which Nolan could show his strengths. The drama in Oppenheimer was not deep enough and didn't hit hard enough. I would give it 7.5/10 but this website doesn't allow fractions so I can only choose between 7 or 8 and I went with 7 haha. I think you can find poor drama in all Nolan movies as well but that's not always obvious because most of his work is not about drama alone unlike Oppenheimer. The most obvious example is Tenet, it doesn't have any emotions or drama and If not for the brilliant concept in Tenet, the whole movie would have been a total waste of time. I don't know how can Nolan improve in drama writing. It's the only flaw in Oppenheimer. Nonetheless, I'm a big fan of Christopher Nolan and I enjoyed watching Oppenheimer.

7.title: Excruciatingly long!!!!
7.content:
The movie drags and drags until your last two brain cells stop working. It was painfully long. You even consider stepping out of the theatre. Apart from that the casting was great. Acting by Cillian, Emily, Florence, Robert Downey was exceptional. We actually feel that we are in the 1940s as the costume, makeup, set was perfect.

The bomb making and testing scenes were awesome and it makes us feel everything is real. (Literally it felt the ground was shaking during these scenes)

The storyline was simple. It followed personal and professional life of Oppenheimer also involving characters that were in and out of his life. Must watch in IMAX if you want to experience the cinematic beauty of this film.

7.title: Not a 10
7.content: Solid 7.5. Great acting, great visuals, so-so editing. Nice to see Ciliian Murphy getting a leading role. No actor is better at acting w/o saying anything. It's the semi-watering eyes. I'll have to look into all the non-bomb making aspects of his life, I know so little. Didn't know about the commie ties, the losing security clearance (whatever), and all the rest. Ni ce to so many actors having 1-2 lines and doing a great job, I guess they all wanted to be in it. Musta sucked to be a part of making a weapon so powerful, but if they didn't someone else worse woulda. Anyway I'll never put on another life jacket.

7.title: GOOD BUT ...
7.content:
Christopher Nolan is an ambitious director who is always trying to impact and surprise. He is able to do it sometimes BUT NOT ALWAYS. TENET his previous movie was too difficult to follow for many people and not that satisfying at the end.

OPENHAIMER is basically the same. The first hour or so is about a very particular (far from humble, almost mad) person who suddenly become incredible recognized to the point of being the chief of the Manhattan Project. Cillian Murphy is excellent but is never clear how a semi communist, semi womanizer suddenly became so recognized.

Then another hour is about the project itself and discussions with a fellow scientists until the the bomb is made; even without much knowledge is basically the most appealing part; but his wife crisis (she is an alcoholic who despises his children) shown and strangely resolved. Also; how a person the created such thing could become so pacifists and worried about humanity.

It is something logic but the movie changes the characters without any kind of progression or moral dilema.

The third part of the movie; a very complicated political situation were Truman (play by Gary Oldman who also did Churchill) is depicted not as a nice or grateful person and lots of other politicians are shown even works (outstanding Robert Downey Jr. Who started a naïve person to become the worst of all enemies); but is resolved by Rami Malek (in his only real scene ) in from of the Congress.

Suddenly Oppenheimer about to be CRUCIFIED and the next scene shows him receiving a medal from the President

The point is the movie three hours long has big continuity issues. Most of us know, history and understand what happened but will young people really be clear ?

In brief; is not bad but is unnecessary long in empty parts and to too short in many important aspects.

7.title: N
7.content:
Positives: Cillian Murphy is amazing, Robert Downey Jr really shows up, The B&W photography is beautiful

Weaknesses: The analog Nolanisms are a distraction (Fincher contended with period-isms better in Manhunter using digital processes and CGI), Audio mix is muddled and hard on the dialogue, 70MM film stock is over-sold for a movie that largely takes plan indoors, the non-linear timeline gets a bit confusing

Biggest problem: Nolan's work in this film is extremely derivative, 1st 1/3rd directly quotes T Malick and A Beautiful Mind, Last 1/3rd (the interrogations) is very Lumet, The internal conflict noisey white-out bits is very Villeneuve (but, done badly), The first kissing scene in the desert is poorly and distractingly blocked

Great story, amazing performances, but a strike against Nolan as an auteur. All the previously referenced directors, even the ones working recently, developed a coherently new thing for audiences. Nolan really fails that attempt in this movie. While sitting in the movie theater, I pretty quickly wished someone else had made this movie

Worth seeing for the acting and the story, not as an accomplishment in film-making or directing.

7.title: Watchable once only
7.content:
Good CGI on nuclear explosions. Jumps around rather than a linear presentation. It would be hard to sit through another look. Once and done. We saw it in IMAX which was nice. The Lewis Strauss portrayal reminds me of the current Democrat Party.

The other part of the Strauss legacy is overwhelmed by his machinations against Oppenheim.

Robert Downey Jr. Played the role so well one can only look down on any positive contributions Lewis Strauss did before or after what he did to Oppenheimer. I hope people take what he did to Oppenheimer as a warning on how the search for absolute power as Lord Acton the British historian coined " Absolute Power Corrupts Absolutely"

See the movie if evil political intrigue does not raise your blood pressure too high.

7.title: Overrated, More a Documentary than a Movie.
7.content: It's good, but it's not worth anyone's time. It is incredibly overrated, I love Christopher Nolan, I had very high Expectations. But what I got was 90% politics, and 10% actual blockbuster. It's sad, because I was expecting to see more of the bomb, or the suffering of the Japanese, but all we got to see was 5 seconds on the tv that the bomb hit it's target. We where forced to see 2 hours of building the bomb but only 5 seconds of the actual impact? What's the last hour for then? It's all about Oppenheimer still having his seat on some absolutely boring politician whatever. And they even made the second part more important than the first one? Who cares about that. I was expecting to see some Christopher Nolan, tenet level like action or something but I got an documentary. I know I'm too harsh, but there were ways to make it more epic. It's not even creepy or anything it's just plain boring. And Downey Jr. As a villain? Doesn't work for me, don't know about everyone else. The movie was one hour too long, everyone ran out of the theater after 3 torturing hours. Movie was good, especially the church scene, but not 8,0/10 good.

7.title: The film is good but...
7.content:
I got hit by the hype train.

It couldn't be different, though: a movie directed by Nolan (who made the all time greatest Interstellar) about the frontman of the project that conceived the doomsday weapon couldn't help but raise high expectations.

Well, I fell off the horse.

It seemed to be that the script was a little to hurried, specially in the early part, with many abrupt cuts; scenes that seemed interrupted. With all due respect, an horrorshow.

The plot is good, after all it is based on one of the most fascinating stories of humanity.

The use (I mean abuse) of the greatest scientific discoveries of the time to build a weapon with the potential to destroy the world is something that, I believe, will take centuries of meditation to be properly understood.

But I don't know, something seems to be missing... I didn't feel that touch of wonder Nolan usually puts in his films, that we know so well from Interestelar, Inception or even Tenet.

PS: For those who haven't read "un Verdor Terrible", by Benjamin Labatut, it's really worth it, as the book explores the boundaries between reason and madness of these characters involved with quantum physics (and with weapons of mass destruction, consequently).

The movie is good, but the book is much better.

7.title: Peaky Blinders Does Math, Destroys Planet
7.content:
Don't drink and science, you'll end up joining the communist party, pioneering physics, assembling a team, supervising the construction of a small town, building a bomb, fighting a senator, arguing with federal agents investigating everyone you know, and eventually taking the lives of billions in a nuclear holocaust. And stay away from women of loose morals, they'll lead you straight into a hastily assembled interrogation room orchestrated by a guy you embarrassed during a work meeting 6 years ago.

This movie is exactly what you think it would be given who worked on it, the runtime and the budget. It's not Nolan's best(and certainly not his worst), which is why I think anyone rating it a 10 is out of their mind. He could have knocked 30 minutes off and improved the pacing dramatically. Could have used less time on security clearances and team assembly, and more time making the characters more dimensional. Definitely worth watching, but you'll want an intermission after they blow up the first bomb.

7.title: "I am become Death, the destroyer of worlds"
7.content:
The film "Oppenheimer" is a biographical drama that tells about the life of the American theoretical physicist Robert Oppenheimer. During World War II, he was the head of the Manhattan Project, the secret development of nuclear weapons. This film not only tells the story of a great scientist, but also raises important moral dilemmas he faced and the consequences of his actions. Christopher Nolan's film is a cinematic journey that allows us to look into the life and work of one of the most significant figures in the history of science. This is a deep and penetrating study of the personality of one of the most famous scientists of the 20th century. The film tells about his life, work and contribution to the development of nuclear weapons, but at the same time does not forget to show the human side of Oppenheimer.

* Idea, plot, dialogues:







Oppenheimer's Dialogues with Einstein: These scenes reveal the depth of Oppenheimer's character, his views, and the moral dilemmas he faces.

* Key actors and their characters:







There are many scenes in the film that demonstrate the great acting of the actors. For example, in the scene where Oppenheimer and his team conduct the first successful nuclear test, Murphy conveys his character's euphoria and excitement when he realizes that their work has been crowned with success. The moment when Oppenheimer quotes from the Bhagavad Gita is also beautifully played in this scene: ""I am become Death, the destroyer of worlds"." This moment shows how Oppenheimer realizes the terrible power of what they have created.

In another scene where Oppenheimer testifies before the Atomic Energy Commission, Murphy shows how his character tries to maintain calm and dignity despite pressure from the commission. In this scene, Oppenheimer also quotes from the Bhagavad Gita: "If the radiance of a thousand suns Were to burst at once into the sky That would be like the splendor of the Mighty One The terrible glow of this earthly star." This moment shows how Oppenheimer realizes the consequences of his work and tries to find meaning in what he has created.

* Directing work:

Christopher Nolan, as always, is on top. His ability to tell complex stories using the visual language of cinema is unique. He works masterfully with the frame, creating a unique atmosphere and mood. One of the key scenes in the film is Oppenheimer's conflict with Professor Patrick Blackett at the Cambridge Laboratory. Here Oppenheimer leaves a poisoned apple on the table. This moment demonstrates the complexity of the main character's character and his internal conflicts.

* Script writer and director:

The screenplay, co-written by Nolan with Kai Bird and Martin Sherwin, is a strong point of the film. It accurately conveys the historical details and personal experiences of the characters. For example, the scene of Oppenheimer's interrogation in the U. S. Senate illustrates the political problems Oppenheimer faces because of his views and past.

* Camera work:

Hoite Van Hoytem has created stunning shots that are not only beautiful, but also carry a deep meaning. Each scene is expertly shot, creating a unique atmosphere and mood. The scenes of work on the Manhattan project show the complexity and intensity of the work on creating an atomic bomb, as well as the interaction of key characters.

* Musical accompaniment:

Ludwig Goransson's music adds emotional depth and emphasizes the drama of events. The musical accompaniment in the film is performed at a high level, fits seamlessly into the plot and helps to create the right atmosphere.

* Editing, frame composition, special effects:

Jennifer Laim's editing allows the scenes to flow naturally, the composition of the frame is thought out to the smallest detail, and the special effects are convincing and do not distract from the plot. The nuclear explosion scene was used without the use of computer graphics. Several explosions were carried out practically, using a mixture of gasoline, propane, aluminum and magnesium using large miniatures. They were shot at high speed from different angles, and then superimposed on each other using digital effects to create the iconic mushroom cloud. This scene demonstrates the power and horror of nuclear weapons, emphasizing the skill of the director and cameraman.

* Comparison with other films:

Oppenheimer can be compared to other biographical films such as The Aviator, but it stands out for its focus on scientific and moral responsibility. And also with such biographical dramas as "The Theory of Everything" or "The Imitation Game". However, Oppenheimer has its own unique atmosphere and style that make it special.

* Advantages and disadvantages:

The film impresses with its detail, acting, fascinating plot and high-quality direction. However, in some places it may seem overloaded with information. The film captures and keeps you in suspense, but watching this three-hour film in one go can be difficult due to the large amount of information. The tension starts to build up after half the movie.

Despite the fact that the outcome of the story is known, the film skillfully maintains interest and creates suspense.

The film evokes strong emotions and makes you think about the consequences of scientific discoveries for humanity.

The film is worth watching for anyone interested in the history of science, and I would love to review it.

The film can change the way we look at scientific achievements and their impact on the world. It makes us think about many issues, such as morality, responsibility and the consequences of our actions. The film is striking in its strangeness and depth.

* Personal impressions:

The film "Oppenheimer" made a deep impression on me with its skill and depth. This is one of the most vivid and memorable films of recent years.

Cillian Murphy, Robert Downey Jr. And Christopher Nolan were awarded Oscars for their outstanding roles in this film. This is a recognition of the high level of skill of all project participants and their contribution to the creation of the film, which has become a notable event in the history of cinema.

"Oppenheimer" was also awarded for the best cinematography, editing and soundtrack, which speaks to its technical excellence and visual appeal. These awards recognize the talent and hard work of everyone who worked on the film and highlight its importance as one of the best films of the year.

7.title: Very Good - but better would do
7.content:
First up, I must say that Cillian Murphy's performance was outstanding. I've always rated him as an actor but this took it up a notch (or more). His facial expressions alone are worth an Oscar nomination. If you see this film for no other reason than his acting then it will be worth it!

Now to Nolan; Sometimes I find him something of a desired taste. He so often hits the mark and produces work of the highest standard but then he also missies so badly. Having read, a few years prior to this movie, the book on which its based I am so very pleased he 'kept to the script.' Unfortunately, for me this time, his perennial desire to mess around with the timeline backfired. ( I must add it worked brilliantly in Dunkirk- another masterpiece). Not only that but it detracted from the story and its flow on screen.

Also the movie seemed to drag in the middle section for reasons I cannot put my finger on. There was still plenty going on but I was wishing to get to something better (but what, I didn't know). Its this a masterpiece? In my opinion, not quite. Worth seeing - most definitely. But I left the movie feeling it could have been better. Which is a hard thing to say when your speaking of Christopher Nolan.

7.title: Can get pretty exhausting, but tons of quality.
7.content: Tons of quality but the movie's length made it exhausting to watch. There was much I enjoyed about the film.
