10.title: no words, amazing
10.content:
The cinematic marvel titled "Oppenheimer" stands as an unparalleled testament to the power of visual storytelling. With impeccable videography and visionary direction, the film transcends the limitations of spoken language, captivating audiences through the sheer force of its evocative imagery. Every frame is a brushstroke on the canvas of emotion, crafting a symphony of visuals that speak volumes beyond words.

The prowess of the director's vision is showcased in the lingering impact that "Oppenheimer" leaves on its viewers. Like a profound reverberation, the film's themes echo long after the screen fades to black, prompting introspection and sparking intellectual discourse. It's a cinematic experience that unfurls over time, compelling viewers to peel back layers of meaning and engage with the narrative on a profound level. The days and weeks that follow the viewing become an exploration of the film's intricacies, unraveling its tapestry of emotions and ideas.

While the film's ambition is laudable, it occasionally treads into bewildering territory. Yet, this is a testament to its willingness to challenge conventional storytelling. These moments of uncertainty are like enigmatic puzzle pieces that beckon audiences to piece together the narrative themselves, enriching the viewing experience by demanding an active and engaged mind.

10.title: Nuanced Topic that Inspires Thought
10.content:
This film deserves its own watch, separate from the double feature memes encouraged on social media.

First, Oppenheimer itself is a weighty subject for a biopic.

But mainly, this film is so nuanced, so rich, so textured in acting and videography, it just deserves time.

Maybe a couple of watches, in fact, especially when it eventually goes out of theaters to streaming.

Well worth the ticket price, however, so I might even pay that twice.

Director Nolan deftly handles time cuts back and forth and makes every bit of his three hours in the theater count. (I worried at such a lengthy movie, but honestly the time flew.)

Cillian Murphy is amazing as the.eponymous character. He manages to play all ages of Oppenheimer--I was dubious going in having heard this, but the man pulls it off.

Murphy's range as an actor is amazing and he conveys both the patriotism and ego that led Oppenheimer to sign up as well as the change of heart he had in later years.

Emily Blunt stands toe to toe as Oppenheimer's wife. She is strong enough to really act as his partner. And Blunt's rendition of Kitty responding to a board inquiry was so subtle (*chefs kiss*)

Rami Malek as David Hill had a moment in a senate hearing had the audience actually cheer, but every single scientist/cast member was just spot on in their struggle to pursue theories without becoming part of the military group think atmosphere.

And I really need to look up the real Leslie Groves and his story. Matt Damon played the part both as rather prickly, and yet with a strong sense of respect between the men.

This sort of heroic character suits Damon well and the character felt like a real backbone throughout the piece.

Now. Personally. I just want to give huge kudos to Robert Downey Junior as Lewis Strauss. RDJ has been in the big budget Avengers movies recently, a franchise which has been hit or miss for me overall.

In Oppenheimer the actor proves once again how skilled he is playing heavier drama outside of genre. The Strauss story line was complicated and kept us all engaged until the very end (another cheer went up when he wasn't confirmed)

Honestly, with such directing and acting, that should be enough.

But every single department hits a home run.

The effects--both sound and visual--are amazing.

The musical score was perfect and elevated the experience even more.

Frankly, you name it, I'd brag on it.

But again, the topic is weighty and might take a second watch to catch all that I want to say.

Even the feeling of existential crisis and messages for viewers were carefully enough placed that I felt "reached" rather than "preached to" and the payoff of that means digging into some books as well.

Editing hit a couple of jump scares that actually caught me (and I usually never flinch at all.)

10.title: Amazing
10.content:
This movie was phenomenal, from beginning to end I enjoyed almost every second of it. When the movie came out I was on a vacation and by the time I got back all of my friends who were interested in seeing it had already done so. Fast forward almost 2 months later and I was still wanting to see Oppenheimer as I had heard so many good things about the movie and that I have to see it in theaters to get the best "IMAX" experience. I ended up going to see the movie alone after school and was absolutely blown away. As someone who has a deep interest in chemistry and general sciences the movie was incredibly fun for me to watch. Near the beginning of the movie during Oppenheimers first lecture he says "Is light made up of particles or waves? Quantum mechanics says it's both. How can it be both? It can't. It can't. But it is. It's paradoxical, and yet, it works." This genuinely brought a smile to my face and was one of my favorite scenes throughout the movie. Not only did it show us amazing aspects of scientific studies but it also began to discuss the possible global effects of these weapons in the second half which added a very philosophical connection. All in all amazing movie, while I was watching it I was either thinking deeply, smiling, or experiencing my heart about to jump through my chest.

Great movie, highly recommend 9.5/10.

10.title: An unforgettable experience
10.content: Before I say my opinion, many people thought that the movie was classified as dynamic and expected fighting scenes, and so on. This is a grave mistake. The movie is a biography, all of it on Robert Oppenheimer. A conversational experience that is one of the most enjoyable. This is the strength of the movie. It is the language of dialogue between the actors. This is the basis of the movie. Not to mention the scenes of the nuclear bomb, which I classify as one of the best scenes that I could have seen in my life, the powerful acting, and more than expected from Robert Downey Jr. The whole experience is more than wonderful, and we must not forget the soundtrack from heaven, and I expect an Oscar for this music.

10.title: Nolan at his best
10.content:
Christopher Nolan at his very best. Impossible to follow for the first half an hour with different times running simultaneously, one might mistake it for a time travel doc... Cilian Murphy is given a chance to shine in an incredibly demanding role, and showcases every aspact of the complex character that is J. Robert Oppenheimer. If he doesn't win the Oscar for best actor, I'm not sure what the point in it is.

All the supporting actors are fabulous, and it's a film that's designed to lure you in and that's exactly what happened to me the first time I saw it, and the second, and the third.

I could go as far to say it's one of the greatest films of the century, if not all time.

10.title: Overwhelming, powerful and emphatic, a film that stays with you
10.content:
Christopher Nolan's grandly ambitious film about J. Robert Oppenheimer takes on incredible dimensions such that it reaches beyond the contours of the typical Hollywood biopic. This film is also a retelling of America's desperate effort during WW2 to successfully construct a nuclear bomb before the Nazis could. It's also a sobering depiction of America's intense paranoia toward alleged communist sympathizers during the Cold War and beforehand. On both fronts, Nolan's portrayal is remarkably effective.

Cillian Murphy gives the best performance of his career thus far as the utterly determined scientist whose brilliance was able to overcome his incidental flaws as a husband, coworker and government mercenary. We see the world at the dawn of startling change through his quietly terrified eyes. It's a magnificent breakthrough for science but for humanity, a new age of fear and uncertainty and Murphy's performance is the guiding hand. Strong supporting performances abound. Emily Blunt is effective as the thick-skinned wife. Matt Damon is the straight-talking Lt. General Leslie Groves who oversaw the Manhattan Project. Robert Downey Jr. Plays against type as Lewis Strauss, a founding member of the Atomic Energy Commission whose working relationship with Oppenheimer turns into a point of contention later in the film.

The film's emotional high points are toward the end after a very early preview of the psychological turmoil that Oppenheimer goes through in comprehending the ramifications for humanity in the wake of his miraculous breakthrough. Without going into too much detail, it's a portrayal of the pitfalls of genius and immense responsibility. You leave with gratitude and humility for this part of history as a lesson but also as a cautionary tale on whom you can trust. Whether you watch as a film buff, a history buff or someone with a science background, it's a rare, rewarding film experience. A superb achievement and highly recommended.

10.title: If perfection were something from this world, it would certainly be directed by Nolan
10.content:
I don't even know where to begin.

Not every director can bring out the best in a star-studded cast, but that's definitely not the case with Nolan.

It's a true pleasure to be alive and witness his work, along with Cillian Murphy, Robert Downey Jr., and many others giving their best.

The film's cinematography is one of the best I've ever seen, from the set design to the screenplay, sound, and costumes; everything borders on perfection in the most literal sense.

Few movies bring to the senses, even to those less familiar with the art of cinematography, such distinct aspects of audiovisual elements.

The only negative aspect is that at some point, the movie ends.

Can't wait to watch It more times.

10.title: The masterpiece of the decade
10.content: Oppenheimer is a captivating masterpiece that skillfully combines drama, history, and humanity. With stunning cinematography, powerful performances, exceptional score and sound design, and thought-provoking storytelling, it immerses viewers in the complex world of J. Robert Oppenheimer. The film explores his personal journey, from leading the Manhattan Project to grappling with the moral implications of his scientific breakthrough. It raises profound questions about the consequences of scientific progress and serves as a reminder of the ethical dilemmas that accompany it. A must-watch for those intrigued by science, history, and the human experience.

10.title: Extraordinary Movie for an extraordinary scientist by an extraordinary director
10.content:
If you are not from a science background, you may want to stay away from it unless you have a great interest in science topics and you are used to Nolan movies. Please, don't rate it slow, fast blah blah.

The movie is non-linear as you expect from Nolan and gives you sufficient information about how atomic bomb works or how a hydrogen bomb can be designed. The scientific discussions, lab culture, typical egoistic behaviour of scientist community are portrayed beautifully in this movie. Robert Downey Jr. Nailed his role of Lewis. Cillian Murphy deserves an Oscar for this role.

For me, it was a perfect movie. One advice is, don't try to remember names of all the scientists. If someone is important for the story, he will be given enough screentime show that you get to know him eventually. Have an excellent ride with this excellent movie.

10.title: Nolan's One Hit Wonder
10.content:
I've just witnessed the incredible work of Director Christopher Nolan, who successfully crafted a suspenseful thriller intertwined with a documentary about Robert J. Oppenheimer. I couldn't be more thrilled and amazed by his talent once again. The movie captivates with its fast pace and compelling characters, particularly Oppenheimer, who finds himself questioned in a hearing room, struggling to obtain security clearance.

I must express my admiration for Robert Downey Jr., who delivers a pivotal performance in portraying Oppenheimer. Cillian Murphy also shines brilliantly as the father of the Atomic Bomb, showcasing Oppenheimer's guilt and humanity. The film delves into the profound impact of his actions, forever haunting him. Nolan skillfully weaves together the development of the atomic bomb, accusations of manipulation, and the fragile trust surrounding leaked information, creating a truly remarkable narrative. This director's ability to transform a documentary into an emotionally charged character-driven film is truly outstanding. It's an absolute pleasure to have experienced such a fantastic piece of cinema.

10.title: Not even a great mind can figure out Humans
10.content:
It's just astonishing how with such high expectations from everyone, Nolan still manages to deliver this master work, he has been my favorite director for quite some time, and there were many occasions where his films felt unrecognized (not by his peers which ultimately is more important) but by the award community, I hope this year things change.

Cinema in its purest form, a high pace thrilling experience, one of the first aspects that amazed me about this movie in fact is that it's a biopic, and most biopics no matter how interesting the person they are telling the story about is, they tend to become tedious but somehow Nolan transformed this into an anxiety inducing exhilarating story.

It feels as tragic as educational, while Nolan did an amazing job finding that balance of simply telling the story from Oppenheimer perspective without polarizing the political matters in place, and potentially antagonizing his audience, this is still a cautionary tale.

How is it that we as a species manage to achieve greatness and we go back to our most tribal instincts when it comes to harm each other?

How is it we are so good in bringing people together and with such great minds we have in the world we point them to fabricate the weapons of our own destruction instead of fomenting that knowledge and apply it to make our species a better peaceful version of ourselves?

This movie has many layers to it, but the one that sticks out the most is redemption, we corrupt the people who are responsible for the development of our civilizations and contribute to further our knowledge and we discard them unless there's a use for them in the big war machine.

Its hard to make a review about the film but be mindful that this is indeed a masterpiece, it's not the usual mind bending Sci-Fi experience Nolan usually creates, it might be even scarier as its an actual real life story that we should all learn from it and I can't finish this review without mentioning the Oscar worthy performances from Cillian Murphy and Robert Downey Jr.

10.title: What a mind blowing movie!
10.content:
This movie had made me wonder so much more about Robert J Oppenheimer, what a man he was! This movie was just a masterpiece directed by a legend Christopher Nolan.

The annoying part about seeing this movie was, there was a guy, deliberately snoring a few times right next to me, and his phone was on sound as well, which was a nuisance.

Still I loved this movie, the acting from the main lead actor, Cillian Murphy had put me a smile in my face, but I won't forget Robert Downey Jr's astounding performance too. Still this movie is so interesting and terrifying because this is based on the father of the atomic bomb. Even though it was too long, I would still would love to rewatch it again. Some scenes were unnecessary but this movie still tops as one of the greatest movies of the 2023.

Hoping for Cillian Murphy to win his first Oscar Award!

10.title: Astonishing and haunting; Nolan's best film
10.content:
With his affinity for mind-bending, time-bending action spectacle blending brains and brawn, Christopher Nolan's blockbusters have a dedicated following among cinephiles. For Nolan, no amount of practical affects is too ambitious, no amount of IMAX cameras. I've always been a huge Nolan fan, and while it may sound a bit cliché to say this, films like "The Dark Knight," "The Prestige," and "Inception" have had a formidable effect on my understanding of film. They taught me how audience expectations from blockbusters can be subverted by a formidable auteur, how action sequences can be combined with a cerebral narrative that conceptually integrates intellectual concepts as the backbone of the storytelling, and how to expect the unexpected from original and creative storytelling. Nolan's new film, "Oppenheimer," may sound a bit more conventional and by-the-numbers than some of his other films, but viewers should rest assured that he has plenty of tricks up his sleeve to keep viewers engaged and thrilled. It is a completely riveting and extraordinarily well-made work that, in my opinion, is Nolan's best film.

From the first frame to the moment the credits roll, viewers feel that Nolan is in total control of his craft throughout. Nolan's immaculate technical precision is on full display here, alternating between color and black-and-white sequences to stunning results. The precision and framing of nearly every shot in the film feels concise, controlled, and just like the highest possible levels of art--from wide shots of the New Mexico desert to intimate shots of a character's face. It all feels immaculately controlled and derived from a singular vision, to thrilling results rarely seen in modern movies. But what makes "Oppenheimer" so extraordinary is how it differs from Nolan's other films. It is not really an action film compared to most of his others, but the film is just as adrenaline-pumping, visceral, and intense. This effect is achieved by gripping nuclear test sequences as well as intense scenes of Oppenheimer's dreams and visions, as well as audio-visual depictions of the physical properties behind the atomic bomb. Credit is owed to an extraordinary sound design (perhaps some of the most gripping and intense sound design I've ever heard in a movie theater) and a powerful, melancholy score that accentuates every scene and further serves to demand the viewer's attentiveness throughout. Fortunately, the dialogue is completely audible and the score is never overbearing, which has been a complaint before about some of Nolan's other films.

Some of Nolan's detractors have criticized his films in the past as simply clinical and cold intellectual exercises. I don't agree with them in general (although I was not a fan of "Tenet," his weakest film) and am very much of a fan, but to some extent I can understand their arguments. However, the character development in "Oppenheimer" is comprehensive and brilliantly complemented by Nolan's screenplay, and the attention to a more character-driven film is something that sets this film above Nolan's others in my book. The actors further help the character-driven backbone of the narrative, particularly Cillian Murphy, who provides the best performance of the year. He truly inhabits Oppenheimer in every way imaginable, portraying a full acting range based on scientific inquiry, worry, and sorrow. "Oppenheimer" is both a gripping, IMAX-shot thriller and an intimately character-driven story that builds suspense, drama, and emotion in equal measure. For its uniquely character-driven scope and new, authentic ways to grip the viewer in thrill and suspense that are completely creative from Nolan, I consider it Nolan's best film (and I never thought anything of his could top "Inception" and "The Dark Knight.") I cannot recommend it highly enough to patient and sophisticated film lovers. 10/10

Note: I saw the film in The Big Show, Alamo Drafthouse's premium large format screen. This was an outstanding Big Show presentation, with the film's aspect ratio fully utilizing the entire screen and utterly flawless use of the Dolby Atmos sound system (even causing the seats to rumble at times, similar to Dolby Cinema screens at AMC.) This is a must-see in an excellent premium large format screen...but if you're a Nolan fan, do you even need me to tell you that?

10.title: One of the best Biographical movies of all time!!!
10.content:
I watched this movie both in English and Hindi languages,and no doubt this could become one of the highest grossing R rated movies.

Positives of the movie is Christopher Nolan's screenplay,direction, performances of the lead cast and soundtrack. These type of movies would easily become slow paced and dull,what makes this movie interesting is fast paced editing, brilliantly crafted non linear story telling.

It's true that this movie is not for everyone, but everyone is on for watching it. Oppenheimer is a masterpiece that blends emotions,drama, suspense and horror. CLIMAX of this movie hits harder than a cricket ball!!!

10.title: Pay no attention to a review from an individual that can't grasp the use of an ellipsis.
10.content:
I can't think of an adequate superlative to describe Nolan's latest masterpiece.

Seldom will I rate a motion picture with 10/10 but in this case, it is well-deserved.

Cillian Murphy can expect to pick up his Oscar early into 2024 following an exemplary and unrivalled performance.

The only thing I couldn't even force myself to enjoy was Emily Blunt's arguably excessive endeavours to portray a character that required much more subtlety.

Make yourself comfortable, remove any distractions and enjoy the best 3-hours of your life...

Nolan's flawless legacy continues to accumulate speed, and I look forward to his next production.

10.title: Cillian Murphy
10.content: Cillian Murphy what a legend. This movie would not be the same without his performance, he's given 100% and he deserves finally an Oscar for it. One of Nolan's best film and the soundtrack is out of this world. Murphy elevates the performances of the whole cast which is stellar with RDJ finally doing a role worthy of his talent. It's three hours long but despite that I was locked in the whole time and I went to see it twice in the theatre, once in IMAX (worthy to watch there). I haven't enjoyed a movie so much in a long time and it's the first time I got back to the cinema after Covid and this movie made me do it and brought back my passion for cinema. Thanks for the experience.

10.title: A masterpiece which leaves you moved and heartbroken.
10.content: Being a WWII history buff, I was deeply moved watching this movie. Murphy's brilliant depiction is breath taking. Felt like he was able to show us emotions on his face for feeling which we just feel 'internally'. A gorgeous walk through the history and how we reached here. Highly recommend for history buffs, sciece buffs and also anyone and everyone who wants to watch a gorgeous biopic. Perfect pace , great writing, cannot find fault with this one. Right up there as the best Nolan movie for me personally. Cannot wait to watch it again for the sheet intensity of it. Special mention: Emily Blunt who has delivered an extremely powerful performance.

10.title: The Fastest 3 Hours Of Your Life
10.content:
Really. A movie that is just nonstop talking will fly by to a confusing point. How did I just see all that and ingest it all in 3 hours and it's like the previews just ended? The people who thought it dragged on forever... I mean... are you trying to make Americans look stupid? I usually really, no matter what, can barely make a 2.5 hour film without getting restless. That would include other Nolan films (all of which are great). This goes by faster than a kid's 75 minute movie as long as you know it's a biopic. Now that should be apparent based on the description of this movie being a biopic of Robert Oppenheimer, but I digress.

It's my new favorite movie of all time and a film professor's wet dream. Nothing like it ever made or ever will be. I would liken it almost to a non mocumentary Citizen Kane. Can't wait to see it again.

10.title: Masterpiece! One of the Best Films I've Seen!!
10.content: I had high hopes for this film, but it far exceeded my expectations. I highly recommend seeing it in IMAX, because it is visually stunning. On any screen it's still a masterpiece. There were so many stories that could have been told about Oppenheimer, but the way they told the story was so respectful yet captured so many important aspects of his life. With all the controversy, complexity, and mystery that surrounds this story, be it politics, ethics, or science, this film artfully layered it's scenes with a deep understanding, using metaphors and parallels that left me reeling with contemplation. There are so many layers, that this film can be a completely different movie depending upon how much of this story you knew before, yet still leave you dumbfounded by how beautifully these messages are delivered. The cast is nothing short of magnificent. Christopher Nolan is one of my favorites, but this may be his best yet. It's been more than 24 hours, and I'm still mind blown over how good it really was!

10.title: Alluring Jaw Dropper
10.content: Jaw dropping intensity and allure. A sequence filled with enigma. Sequences carefully curated in the highest quality. Filled with scenes and cinematic with the most delicate care, intrusive details, emotional intensity delivered in the most impactful way. Knowing little about the figure that is J. Robert Oppenheimer, or knowing far too much, this doesn't miss a dot. From perfect edge-of-seat timing, to precision of words and delivery by a profound set, this is an absolute homage to the complexity that makes this physicist and relative figures. Hero or villain, martyr or heathen, is beside every point, as this film goes to challenge every point of view and leaves a pondering, critical, thought provoking moment that in of itself leaves a most bittersweet feeeling.

10.title: A masterpiece
10.content:
This movie... the values it portrays and the history it has combined with the brilliance of C. Nolan, Van Hoytema and the cast put it into the 'must see' section.

It showcases the negatives of capitalism and all wars. It brilliantly showcase of what happens to a person whether they're a genius of Oppenheimer's ranks or not, when they have to choose between evils, the only difference being one will be attributed to them while under their control at the same time.

The movie's presence today is more than needed, in a time which can be defined by rapid change. Oppenheimer reminds the audience to always thoroughly think about their options while deciding.

The film, of high quality, has deep thoughts scattered all through it. A 10 out of 10 class.

10.title: Undeniable Masterpiece
10.content:
There's never been a movie like this before. Hopefully there will be more like it in the future. Thank you to Nolan and the entire production team and cast. This film delivers in every area - it's a piece of art produced by masters of their craft.

It's also a very dense and heavy film. It's sweeping but taut. It's calm but urgent. It feels like an immense energy that may either explode or collapse in with violent force, but is kept at a tenuous balance.

And as others have said, after it's done you may not know how to feel. (Unless you're the ~6 year old who I saw walking out of my screening, I'm pretty sure he didn't like it, because there's no way in hell a child A] should watch this film or B] can comprehend this film. I digress).

It's a film that will stick with you. It's intelligent and demanding storytelling that I hope we'll get to see a lot more like it in the coming years. It's also a good idea to watch it in theaters. The 3 hours fly by.

10.title: One of Christopher Nolan's Best Films
10.content:
I love when a biopic doesn't play it safe. Having very little knowledge of the life of J. Robert Oppenheimer, I was very interested in how his studies eventually lead to the creation of the atomic bomb. Being directed by Christopher Nolan, I was already going to check out the film, but it also exceeded my expectations. This is filmmaking in its purest form (especially today). Here's why I believe this excellent film deserves to be seen in theatres.

Essentially, Oppenheimer is about the life of J. Robert Oppenheimer (Cillian Murphy) and his influence in making the atomic bomb, but the way the film is structured makes it feel like so much more. Told in non-linear fashion, the audience is shown the trial afterwards, the planning beforehand, and the event itself. The majority of the film is a series of scenes with people talking in rooms, which may not seem all that exciting or appealing, but score did wonders for that. Many people complain about Christopher Nolan's films being frustrating in terms of hearing the dialogue, but I never felt that here and the bombastic score sucked me in even more. I was on the edge of my seat for the entire three hour run time.

As always, Nolan directs the hell out of this film and brought out probably the best performance in Cillian Murphy's entire career. His performance is worth the price of admission alone. On top of that though, Robert Downey Jr. Also gives one of the best performances of his career in my opinion. Their scenes together were electric. Oppenheimer is also filled with endless celebrity cameos, but that just goes to show how badly everyone clearly loves working with Nolan. From the cast to the direction, from the score to the fact that there were no CGI shots, everything about this film was remarkably done.

Oppenheimer is one of my favourite films of 2023 and it may just end up becoming my favourite after a second viewing. I was also blown away that the point of the film isn't really about the bomb itself, but rather Oppenheimer's life and how this bomb is such a negative thing in our world. It's eye-opening in ways I wasn't expecting and the screenplay only furthered that. With an insane amount of terrific dialogue that all flies at you at a mile-a-minute, I never once felt an ounce of boredom. I loved this film from start to finish and you can now catch it in theatres. Highly, highly recommended.

10.title: "I am Become Death, the Destroyer of the Worlds."
10.content:
In a compelling fusion of biography, hisotry, and cinema, "Oppenheimer" proves once again that Christopher Nolan is an unwavering cinematic innovator. Dedicated to his craft and unconstrained by techonological boundaries, Nolan creates an intimate yet expansive narrative that is as explosive as the atomic bomb itself.

Watching this film in 70mm IMAX is a true honor to me, just thinking about the fact that I got the chance to experience this materpiece in the greatest way makes me feel happy. From the awe-striking, grandeur of the cinematic shots to the immersive richness of each frame, the experience was as bombastic as it was beautiful.

As for the story, "Oppenheimer" beautifully marries fact with fascination. Although biographical films often struggle to balance truth with intrigue, Nolan have transformed a piece of history into a compelling narriative that remains respectful to the facts while never losing sight of the need to entertain.

The performaces in this film are nothing short or remarkable, and none more so than Cillian Murphy's portrayal of J. Robert Oppenheimer. Murphy conveys a spectrum of emotions that are as nuanced as they are powerful, and his performance is a testament to the art of screen acting. Through his vivid embodiment of Oppenheimer, Murphy invites us into the physicist's mind, allowing us to share in his excitiment, his struggles, triumphs, and ultimately, his burden. His performance elevates this film to the realm of cinematic masterpieces.

10.title: A Masterpiece of Intellectual Brilliance - Oppenheimer (2023)
10.content:
As an avid fan of historical biopics, Oppenheimer left me utterly mesmerized and profoundly moved. Directed by the unparalleled talent, Christopher Nolan, this film delves into the life of J. Robert Oppenheimer, the brilliant physicist who led the scientific team that developed the atomic bomb during World War II.

From the very beginning, it was evident that the production team spared no expense in recreating the era with stunning attention to detail. The cinematography and visual effects were nothing short of breathtaking, transporting the audience back in time to witness the monumental events that shaped modern history. Nolan's signature style of blending non-linear storytelling with intense character-driven arcs elevated the narrative to unparalleled heights.

Casting Cillian Murphy as J. Robert Oppenheimer was a stroke of genius. Murphy's performance was nothing short of extraordinary, capturing the essence of Oppenheimer's complex personality - his brilliance, struggles, and the moral dilemmas he faced. The supporting cast, including seasoned actors like Tom Hanks, Viola Davis, and Helen Mirren, delivered outstanding performances that added depth and authenticity to the story.

The screenplay, penned by Aaron Sorkin, was a work of art in itself. The dialogues were gripping and thought-provoking, delving into the ethical questions surrounding scientific advancements and the consequences of harnessing the power of the atom. Sorkin masterfully weaved together personal relationships, scientific discoveries, and political intrigue, keeping the audience engaged from start to finish.

The film's score, composed by Hans Zimmer, perfectly complemented the atmosphere, enhancing emotional moments and driving the tension during critical scenes. Zimmer's music has the power to linger long after the credits roll.

Oppenheimer is not just a biographical account; it is a philosophical exploration of humanity's potential for creation and destruction. It forces us to confront the consequences of our actions and ponder the true meaning of progress.

While some may argue that the film took creative liberties with historical events, it is important to remember that it is a work of art, not a documentary. Nolan skillfully balances authenticity with cinematic flair, creating a powerful and thought-provoking narrative.

In conclusion, Oppenheimer is an intellectual masterpiece that will resonate with audiences for years to come. It showcases the brilliance and flaws of a man who played a pivotal role in shaping the modern world, and it does so with cinematic prowess rarely seen in historical dramas. Christopher Nolan has once again proven himself as a visionary filmmaker, and Oppenheimer stands tall as one of the finest films of its time.

10.title: A riveting epic of man usurping life
10.content:
What is the creation of an atomic bomb other than harnessing life itself, hijacking the power of atoms and corrupting them to destroy themselves? Is this not the ultimate act of man becoming God, claiming ultimate dominion of the world that created him, possibly making man a patricidal creature?

Perhaps physicists are the preachers of life and genius their gospel, their invention of the bomb their eschatology and the consummation of the peak man has sought to scale.

Here we follow Oppenheimer, the father of the atomic bomb, from his early days as a brilliant and young intellectual to a man who creates perhaps the most consequential invention since fire - the next Prometheus - to the archetypal trope of the scientist haunted by his own invention. Genius is no guarantee of wisdom, as one character says in the film and just because we can do something doesn't mean we should.

And he lives to regret it. A bright-eyed man becomes jaded and maligned by the world and zeitgeist he helped create. Just as Prometheus was tortured, so too will Oppenheimer suffer for his invention.

An incredible biopic that sears into your mind. I was worn out from the viewing experience last night but have been pondering it with more clarity this morning. SEE IT. A rare, generational excursion into the Faustian and Promethian nature of humanity and creation.

10.title: Amazing
10.content:
"Oppenheimer" is an extraordinary cinematic experience that leaves audiences awe-inspired with its mesmerizing visual elements. The film's visual prowess is unparalleled, taking viewers on a breathtaking journey through time. From the elaborate set designs to the captivating special effects, every frame is a work of art that transports you to the World War II era.

However, what truly sets "Oppenheimer" apart is its impeccable audio work, masterfully synchronized with the movie. The sound design plays a pivotal role in creating an immersive experience. During the pivotal scene when the atomic bomb explodes, I was left utterly shocked by the sheer intensity of the moment. The synchronized sound wave reverberates through your very being, leaving you with a sense of awe and terror at the immense power of the event.

The performances by the cast are exceptional, with the lead actor bringing J. Robert Oppenheimer's complex character to life with depth and emotion. The supporting cast adds layers of authenticity, making the narrative all the more compelling.

The film's direction is commendable, skillfully weaving together historical accuracy and artistic vision. The director's ability to balance the personal and historical aspects of Oppenheimer's life is remarkable, giving the audience a profound understanding of the man behind the science.

As the credits rolled, I found myself reflecting on the profound impact of scientific discovery and the ethical dilemmas faced by those involved in the Manhattan Project. "Oppenheimer" is not just a movie; it's an intellectual and emotional journey that lingers in your thoughts long after the screen fades to black.

In conclusion, "Oppenheimer" is a cinematic marvel that impresses on all fronts. Its stunning visuals, exemplary audio work, and compelling storytelling make it a must-watch for any cinephile or history enthusiast. Be prepared to be moved, challenged, and deeply affected by this cinematic masterpiece.

10.title: Shall we hand over all Oscars now!
10.content:
Theres very few movies that have an impact on cinema like this one will. The star studded cast, direction, story and the other very pink opponent releasing on the same day. There are trends that Hollywood will try and manufacture unlike this freak chance of these movies being released on the same day. I truly hope that the film industry are taking note of true storytelling, heart and classic film making with little to none enhancements to the moments that truly matter.

Where can i start with this cast, there can truly be 5 or 6 up for the 4 acting Oscars in 2024. Cillian Murphy is a shoe in for Best Actor, his harrowing portrayal of a genius that has the fate of the world on his mind and on-one truly understands the factors of what he has created. With a look he conveys a thousand words, with the support of Emily Blunt these 2 together weren't on screen a tone but yet again the impact they have on each others performances drive this to another level. From a sweet English legend (mary poppins) to an alcoholic American shows the breath of her acting range. When i heard the interview from RDJ that he was scared of taking this role and having to act again after his role as Iron Man this broke me. He smashed this role! In a film that spans hours his minutes on screen may beat Sir Anthony Hopkins Hannibal Lector record but the same impact across the board! Honorable mentions for Matt Damon, Jason Clarke and Alden Ehrenreich who keep all their stories flowing to allow a 3 hour film to be a a joy to watch.

Then we come to an influential director that may be pushing for his Oscar with this film without making it Oscar bait like so many others in the past. If we get to Feb 2024 with people talking about this film its Nolans for the taking. Allowing natural, real and non-cgi scenery grounds this movie with the rawness on the forefront of movies just like the scientific breakthroughs that were happening on screen. Nothing has come close to this film this year! These are the films that when a director who writes his movies is allowed to create his vision and produces an epic. This is why he left Warner Bros. Over the last few years the medaling in directors creations stops the truest visions coming to realization.

This is a word of warning though as proven by Thor Love and Thunder where Tiaka was allowed to run off and produce one of the dumbest marvel movies of all time!

All of the effects have been highlighted as practical and this is the revaluation in bring back practical effects since Mad Max Fury Road in 2015. With the Atomic test being a practice effect i'd love to see how this is made. From visual effects to sound effects and editing, one word... perfection! Recently watching Interstellar and this had the same affect on me as that film!

Theres no other words than prefect, actors, direction, story, score and above all the feeling of impending doom in a way that allows everyone to take a different take on who is right and wrong.

10.title: ONE OF THE BEST MOVIES OF ALL TIME!
10.content:
First of all if you have a true IMAX cinema near you i would recommend that you go see this movie in that theatre.

Oppenheimer is a movie about J. Robert Oppenheimer, the American physicist who played a significant role in the development of the atomic bomb during World War II, it has the potential to be a compelling historical drama. The story of Oppenheimer and the Manhattan Project is a fascinating and complex one, filled with ethical dilemmas, scientific discoveries, and the implications of nuclear weapons.

Cillian Murphy and RDJ were absolutely amazing in this movie and their acting blow me away.

For anyone who was hesitant about going to see this movie i would recommend that you see it right away.

10.title: Nolan is back with another gem
10.content:
I know I have seen a great film when I spend the remainder of the day after viewing, with my brain firing with thoughts and ideas provoked by the viewing.

A story of perhaps the man that oversaw the greatest of moral dilemmas. Navigated perfectly Cillian Murphy. A film that can leave you with an impression of how haunted he lived out his days with.

Science = can we do it?

Religion/humanistic principles = should we do it?

A war ravaging inside Oppenheimer.

A very important representation of the damaging McCarthyite attack era in America still very much alive today. Stifling debate and reducing the Overton windows in western governments to Neo liberalism with a dash of identity politics on either side.

Also the inception of the military industrial complex shifting away from the concept of true American values into the tyrannical path that has ravaged too much of the world and America itself.

10.title: breathtaking!
10.content: I thoroughly enjoyed this breathtaking political thriller (which, in my opinion, is mistakenly marketed as psychological horror movie)! As a form, it is very close to Nolan's 'The Prestige.' The rivalry gradually unfolds, and at the end, we get the whole picture. Best suited for those who have some interest and understanding of the development of Physics during World War II and the political scenario of America at that time. 10.title: A cinematic masterpiece
10.content:
Christopher Nolan's "Oppenheimer" is a thought-provoking and visually stunning biographical drama that delves into the life of J. Robert Oppenheimer, the father of the atomic bomb. The film is a masterpiece of storytelling, weaving together the complexities of Oppenheimer's personal and professional life, set against the backdrop of one of the most pivotal moments in human history.

The movie opens with Oppenheimer (played by Cillian Murphy) as a young man, struggling to find his place in the world. We see him as a brilliant, yet troubled, student at Cambridge University, where he becomes enamored with the works of Niels Bohr and the principles of quantum mechanics. As Oppenheimer's fascination with physics grows, so does his sense of purpose, and he eventually finds himself at the forefront of the Manhattan Project, tasked with developing the atomic bomb.

Nolan's direction is, as always, meticulous and deliberate. He takes his time to establish the characters and their motivations, slowly building tension as the stakes grow higher. The film's pacing is deliberate, mirroring the slow-burning intensity of Oppenheimer's own personality. Murphy's performance is phenomenal, capturing the essence of Oppenheimer's complexity and nuance. He brings a depth and vulnerability to the character, making it easy to become invested in his story.

The supporting cast is equally impressive, with standout performances from Emily Blunt as Kitty Oppenheimer, Matt Damon as Leslie Groves, and Robert Downey Jr. As Lewis Strauss. Each character adds a unique perspective to the narrative, highlighting the personal and professional struggles that Oppenheimer faced throughout his life. The chemistry between the actors is palpable, and their interactions are often tense and emotionally charged.

One of the most striking aspects of "Oppenheimer" is its visual aesthetic. Nolan's use of black-and-white cinematography is a bold choice, but it pays off beautifully. The monochrome palette adds a sense of timelessness to the film, while also emphasizing the stark contrast between the beauty of the natural world and the devastation wrought by the atomic bomb. The special effects are seamless, and the recreation of the Trinity test is both awe-inspiring and terrifying.

The film's themes are just as thought-provoking as its visuals. Nolan explores the moral implications of scientific discovery, and the responsibility that comes with playing God. Oppenheimer's famous quote, "I am become Death, destroyer of worlds," is a haunting refrain throughout the movie, serving as a reminder of the devastating consequences of his creation. The film also touches on the personal costs of genius, as Oppenheimer's relationships and mental health begin to fray under the pressure of his work.

Nolan's script is meticulous in its attention to detail, drawing heavily from historical records and personal accounts. The film's portrayal of the Manhattan Project is meticulously researched, and the attention to period detail is impressive. However, the movie is not just a dry historical retelling - it's a deeply personal and emotional exploration of Oppenheimer's inner world.

If there's one criticism to be made, it's that the film's scope can feel overwhelming at times. Nolan tries to pack a lot into the movie's 3-hour runtime, and some scenes feel a bit rushed or disjointed. However, this is a minor quibble in an otherwise exceptional film.

In conclusion, "Oppenheimer" is a cinematic masterpiece that will leave you breathless and contemplative. It's a film that will challenge your assumptions and spark important conversations about the ethics of scientific discovery. With its outstanding performances, stunning visuals, and thought-provoking themes, "Oppenheimer" is a must-see for anyone interested in history, science, or the human condition. Nolan has outdone himself with this film, and it's a testament to his skill as a storyteller that he can make a movie about one of the most complex and troubled figures of the 20th century feel both deeply personal and universally relatable.

10.title: Phenomenal acting from Murphy & Downey Jr
10.content:
I went to watch Oppenheimer with a lot of hope, mostly because Nolan was at its helm and Downey was in it.

I was not disappointed at all; I must say, I did not expect at all that the movie would turn out this good. However, before I go further, I must point out that, for good or bad reasons, this movie is not for everyone. It demands utmost attention from its audience, since every single scene constitutes a crucial part of the story --- miss one scene and the story falls apart. Thus, even at a colossal runtime of 3 hr, the story feels amazingly tight-knit.

The story is adapted from a very nice book on Oppenheimer called The American Prometheus, but Nolan does not shy away from giving the movie his own vision. His non-linear storytelling shows itself again, but it is used extremely effectively (though, I suspect, at a risk of confusion to some audience members). The story zigzags between three connected tales: Oppenheimer's story from his student-days at Patrick Blackett's lab in Cambridge to his involvement in the Manhattan Project, Los Alamos, culminating in the Trinity Test; his subsequent security hearing; and the hearing of Lewis Strauss (whose character is absolutely nailed by Downey Jr).

The acting is... flawless, and that is an understatement. Particularly Murphy & Downey Jr. This is probably the best performance from RDJ in his career, and undoubtedly the career-best for Murphy yet. Other performances are noteworthy too: Florence Pugh, who plays Jean Tatlock, uses her relatively shorter screentime amazingly efficiently, and Matt Damon delivers a solid performance. Emily Blunt is at her best.

I must mention the background score. It is a.m.a.z.i.n.g., down to the last chord --- Goeransson's dedication is pretty obvious. The cinematography is also exceedingly good, particularly after Tenet, with some shots that are likely to be etched into the viewer's memory for a long time.

Overall, VERDICT: Please watch it! It will probably be the best movie you'll watch in this year... or maybe this decade.

10.title: Powerful
10.content:
A powerful movie in more ways than one, this is just Nolan once again at the top of his game.

The cast are incredible, from Cillian Murphy's titular J. Robert Oppenheimer and Emily Blunt's Kitty Oppenheimer all the way 'down' to David Dastmalchian's William Borden, Gary Oldman's President Truman, and Florence Pugh's Jean Tatlock. Everyone is sublime. Extra praise should perhaps be given to RDJ as Lewis Strauss for showing that he IS still a great actor after seeming to have become so comfortable as Tony Stark in the MCU. It's nice to see that he hasn't become as complacent in his craft as one might be tempted to be after so much work in the MCU.

Praise must also be given, of course, to Nolan's screenplay which stays remarkable close to the reality of how everything went down at the time, only taking small liberties with who said certain lines, and whether or not certain people even said certain lines in reality.

It's a long movie, at 3 hours, but never really quite feels like it's that long because the score and sound design help keep the tension ratcheted at times when what you're watching may not SEEM tense, the editing is masterful, never lingering too long at times when lesser movies would nor cutting away too soon. And then of course we have the usual sort of tricks Nolan employs, though never unreasonably, to help drive home the mental state of the protagonist at certain times. Be it here for Oppenheimer himself, or in Memento, or Inception, or anywhere really. Nolan knows his craft well, knows his tools well, and knows exactly when to employ them and for how long in order to get the most out of his movies.

It may not be something you could easily rewatch, but I cannot recommend highly enough that you at least watch this movie once.

10.title: "Between Complexity and Beauty: Why 'Oppenheimer' is a Uniquely Demanding Cinematic Experience"
10.content:
Watching *Oppenheimer* demands your full attention and intellectual engagement, as its intricate narrative can easily overwhelm a distracted viewer. This is a masterclass in intelligent filmmaking that treats its audience with respect, challenging them to keep up with its rapid-fire dialogue and frequent jumps across different periods of Oppenheimer's life. Spanning three hours, the film is relentless in its pacing, weaving together a dense tapestry of historical and personal moments. While visual cues help orient the viewer through these time shifts, they require quick comprehension. This unyielding intensity mirrors the urgency of the U. S. race to develop the atomic bomb before Germany, adding a layer of thematic resonance.

Cillian Murphy delivers a career-defining performance, anchoring the film with a portrayal that is nothing short of Oscar-worthy. The supporting cast is equally stellar, with Robert Downey Jr. Making a triumphant return to serious acting after years in blockbuster roles. Emily Blunt, though occasionally veering into melodrama, holds her own in a talented ensemble. The screenplay is richly layered, akin to a literary masterpiece, while the cinematography alternates between stark minimalism and bursts of vivid color, particularly in scenes featuring Florence Pugh. The score, often tense and foreboding, complements the film's urgent rhythm, though it occasionally offers moments of beauty.

Despite its three-hour runtime, the film feels remarkably brisk, a testament to its gripping narrative and technical brilliance. *Oppenheimer* is an intense and demanding watch, but one that rewards viewers with a profound cinematic experience. It represents filmmaking at its finest-a truly exceptional piece of art that lingers long after the credits roll.

10.title: One of the Best work from Christopher Nolan, Simply Extraordinary
10.content:
My favourite movie of all time is Christopher Nolan's 2008 Batman Dark Night. He did it again, delivering historical magic to the Imax cinematic world, and also changed our modern filmmaking method. Astonishing performance from Cillian, with beautiful cinematography capturing the magnificence of an atomic explosion. A refreshing and innovative film highlighting the challenges Oppenheimer faced as the person controlling the life and death of people through his invention, his struggles due to his background and his jealousy of his peers.

I particularly love the usage of the B&W 70mm film describing the time frame of events, separating the present and the past, more importantly colouring the dynamic of people. B&W film separates characters from the background, drawing the focus to the facial expressions and movements of the actors. We see how Lewis's extraordinary performance on how his jealousy and delusion drove his anger towards Oppenheimer, how people are easily blinded by fame. Using handheld camera movement for most of the scene builds up the tension, in short truly immersive.

Oppenheimer is known to be the father of the atomic bomb. In his previous interviews, he had expressed his concerns about the usage of these bombs and how his invention conflicted with his view on morality. He used his talent to invent such a bomb but everything comes with consequences. Likewise, a bomb can destroy or create destructions and contains greatness in good use but with massive consequences. Oppenheimer was aware of this fact, and the introduction visuals and after-effects complimented this conflicted feeling.

The most breathtaking scene has to be the last scene. A close-up of Oppenheimer following an image of the world where it was covered with atomic bombs, end of the world. The fear lived within Oppenheimer. Another remarkable scene would be the explosion of the first successful atomic bomb. The scene started with clouds of dark gas, swallowing the sky, everything was silent, observing the power of it. Then soon later, a loud noise followed. Excellent method of immersing everyone to witness history, and the mightiness of the bomb alongside incredible soundtracks, creating an effect that could only be achieved in cinema.

Yet this movie is not all about the process of how the atomic bomb was invented, it is a biography about Oppenheimer. The storyline includes his love affairs, marriage, family and politics. Oppenheimer had been accused of having a connection with the Russian communist party during the second world war. The majority of the movie was about his security clearance. Colleges of his were introduced one by one, some betrayed him, some told half-truths. A mentally draining trial for Oppenheimer but was important to the overall story as in the end cleared his name and his loyalty to the country.

A great movie needs to provide a sense of connection with the audience, a reflection that the audience can carry even outside of the cinema. Oppenheimer is a must-watch movie though it is quite lengthy, a total of 3 hours. It gives you a glimpse of what it meant to be "with great power comes with great responsibility". The struggles behind the most magnificent invention of the century. Everything comes with a price, a price that Oppenheimer has to pay was his time with his children and family, and the betrayal of people he trusted. A phenomenal cast of actors, and I have nothing to critic about their delivery.

10.title: Oscar worthy

10.title: A must watch Animation
10.content:
In a world where animation has become increasingly sophisticated, it's rare to come across a film that truly redefines the boundaries of the medium. Arcane Animation is a groundbreaking achievement that not only pushes the limits of animation but also delivers a richly layered narrative that will leave you spellbound.

From the opening frames, it's clear that Arcane Animation is something special. The film's unique blend of traditional animation and cutting-edge computer-generated imagery (CGI) creates a visually stunning world that's both fantastical and eerily familiar. The attention to detail is staggering, with every frame meticulously crafted to transport viewers to the world of Runeterra.

One of the standout aspects of Arcane Animation is its complex characters. The film boasts a diverse cast of multidimensional personalities, each with their own distinct backstory and motivations. From the enigmatic Vi to the charismatic Jinx, every character is meticulously crafted to evoke a specific emotional response from the viewer.

The narrative itself is a masterclass in storytelling. Arcane Animation weaves together multiple plot threads, expertly balancing action, drama, and humor to create a cinematic experience that's both thrilling and emotionally resonant. The pacing is relentless, with each episode ending on a cliffhanger that will leave you desperate for more.

What truly sets Arcane Animation apart, however, is its thematic depth. Beneath its surface-level action and adventure lies a rich tapestry of social commentary, exploring complex issues like oppression, rebellion, and the consequences of unchecked power. The film's portrayal of a world on the brink of chaos, where the haves and have-nots are locked in a struggle for survival, feels eerily prescient in today's world.

The voice acting in Arcane Animation is equally impressive, with a talented cast bringing the characters to life with their performances. Hailee Steinfeld shines as Vi, infusing the character with a depth and nuance that's rare in animation. Similarly, Ella Purnell's portrayal of Jinx is both captivating and unsettling, perfectly capturing the character's mercurial personality.

If there's one criticism to be made, it's that Arcane Animation can feel overwhelming at times. The sheer volume of characters, plot threads, and world-building can be daunting, especially for viewers unfamiliar with the League of Legends universe. However, this is a minor quibble in what is otherwise a masterpiece of animation.

Arcane Animation is a game-changing cinematic experience that redefines the boundaries of animation. With its stunning visuals, complex characters, and richly layered narrative, it's a must-watch for fans of animation, science fiction, and fantasy. Even if you're not familiar with the League of Legends universe, Arcane Animation is an immersive and engaging experience that will leave you eager for more.

10.title: "Oppenheimer" and the power of cinema
10.content:
There's a point in the second half, right after the interval when an eye piercing flash, golden flames, followed by an earth shattering sound send tremors through the behemoth theatre where I watched this film. All eyes glued to the screen, some sighing out of the wonder that they had just witnessed. That recreation of a milestone moment in US and world history that changed the course of the World War II and the world order in general has been able handled by the brilliant hands of Christopher Nolan. Those five minutes or so truly stand out as one of the most epic moments in cinema history and in the Nolan universe in general.

Nolan's collaboration with a long-term associate Cillian Murphy is a stuff of cinematic brilliance. Murphy, who had proven himself as a reputable actor through his performances in the television giant "Peaku Blinders" and in shorter roles in films like "Dunkirk" and "Inception", was the perfect choice for the protagonist in the eponymous film. He executes every scene, every emotion with a sheer brilliance that we have come to expect of him. Murphy effectively brings to the screen a brilliant mind, an enigma to his associates, a man torn between responsibilities to his country and to mankind, a man willing to rip off all strength from Nazi Germany using the atom bombs but unsure whether using them on Japan serves the cause any longer, a man who has to wear the medal of a scientific genius and America's hero but be bigger down by an aching sense of guilt over the immediate and long-term catastrophic effect that his invention has led to. An Oscar nomination and a potential win is on the cards.

It has been rightly pointed out again and again that underneath all the science and physics and time travel, Nolan's ventures have an emotional core, tied to a guilt-ridden or guilt-driven protagonist. Nolan has mounted "Oppenheimer" on a massive scale but he never let the emotions get suppressed under the grandeur. There are scenes that will shake your emotional core. He is ably supported by a plethora of talented artists: Hoyte van Hoytema's black and white and colour frames facilitated in building up a top-notch ambience for the project; Ludwig Göransson's score took the film to a different level, his music is haunting with an inherent sense of urgency, anxiety-inducing, and prophetic of an imminent catastrophe; the sound designers took the film to greater heights befitting a story on the father of the atom bomb. Nolan is known for using practical effects and he mounts those effects exceptionally in the Trinity testing scene at Los Alamos. It has been evident now and again that he is a creative genius and with "Oppenheimer" he delivers a groundbreaking film cementing his status further. He also took full control of the screenplay this time and it doesn't falter for a moment. Three hours went by without a twitch. Nolan has hardly made a film with a linear narrative, a rule he doesn't break in "Oppenheimer" and Thank God he didn't as a chronological narration would have defeated everything that the screenplay and the editing of this film have achieved.

The film rides high on Murphy and Nolan's shoulders but it would be unfair to not give a shout out to the supporting cast. Robert Downey Jr. In an unrecognisable make-up is viciously good as a bureaucrat willing to make it big in the US Senate and makes waves, particularly in the last act. Emily Blunt is effortlessly brilliant in the few scenes that she has and so is Florence Pugh. The latter casts a stronger impact in her limited screentime. Matt Damon does well as an officer in the US Army and also gets to deliver some comic relief. The rest of the supporting cast gave their best throughout.

"Oppenheimer" is not about the science of it all. You won't get to see the actual creation of the atom bombs or their application on Hiroshima and Nagasaki. You get to see the world around its creation, application and consequence through the lenses of Robert Oppenheimer. The science and horror of it all and the resultant consequence that US politics has on the creator of these bombs become palpable through the exceptional direction of Nolan and the cast and crew. It is a team effort that didn't go wrong.

10.title: WATCH TWICE
10.content: "Oppenheimer ", Christopher Nolan's 11th feature film, is a character study of the man behind the Manhattan project, J. Robert Oppenheimer. This film peers into his life, achievements, relationships and flaws with the backdrop of the race to make a functioning atomic bomb first before the Nazis and then before the Soviets. Although this film, on paper, could read much like a biopic, a more accurate genre for this film would be "thriller" edging on "horror". From the first sequence, the viewer is gripped by the momentum of the film and never given a chance to recover. The editing, acting, sound design and cinematography all work in unison to push the viewer along through this complex narrative and create a truly transfixing experience. Although the initial viewing was an impressive experience, the pace of the narrative and complexity of the cast and dialogue lended to an amount of confusion that was not negligible. Upon second viewing, it was much easier to follow the plot and characters, allowing me to have a different and even more immersive and emotional experience than the first viewing. This may be a problem for some viewers who do not wish to see the movie twice, but as many Nolan fans will understand, his style of movie making challenges the viewer, and this film is no different. Though I have only seen it twice, I strongly suspect this is a film that keeps giving with every additional viewing.

10.title: Class filmmaking.
10.content:
It is filmmaking at its best. This is CLASS A. It is in my Nolan top 4 for sure. Not ahead of Inception or Tenet, but somewhere near Dunkirk.

The atmosphere of it intoxicates you. It gets under your skin and never leaves. This is how biopics about such historical figures should be made. This is Nolan's "12 Angry Men" meets "Memento". Brutally 9.5/10 for me.

The decision of making it from the POV of Oppenheimer is extraterrestrial intelligence. The treatment of how to show the world the way he saw it is an amazing choice.

Cinematography is revolutionary. Nolan, Hoyte, and Imax films are the Trinity of modern filmmaking. It makes me feel like if I was living in 1968 and watching Kubrick's 2001 for the first time. Rebellious filmmaking. Extreme to the core.

The haunting experimental score of Ludwig Görannson is traumatizing. It captures the weird combination of history, science, science fiction, philosophy, horror, nervousness, self doubt, triumph, and tragedy.

The acting in general is phenomenal. Cillian Murphy lost himself in the magic of the role, and Robert Downey Jr is Oscar contender. These performances will be remembered for a long long time. The small parts are also amazing. Bennie Safdie, Casey Affleck, and Matthias Schweigoffer are mesmerizing.

The custom design, production design, and the whole decorations are capturing the spirit of the terrifying, yet astonishing 1940s.

What really captured me is the work on clothes and make ups. The characterizations are so accurate and yet creative.

The pace, scenery, dynamics, and themes are all showcases of Nolan's abilities as a world designer.

So terrifying and satisfying. One of the most important films in the history of filmmaking.

10.title: A 20th century warning for our time

More specifically, nations that still see it opportune to rely on fossil fuels and coal as they grow their economy as time to prevent our planet being uninhabitable is running out. Oppenheimer is brilliant with its fantastic visuals, immersive score, and pulsating dialogue.

By the time you put the pieces together of what is going on, you find yourself in the same bind that J Robert Oppenheimer is in. The way the film escalates and finishes with a weighty parting scene will leave you to contemplate the trajectory of humanity, and whether or not we can stop a seemingly insurmountable problem. 10/10.

10.title: A certified Nolan masterpiece
10.content:
I've seen this film twice. Once just simply isn't enough to truly appreciate everything. There is a LOT to unpack here. But let me first start by saying this movie isn't for everyone. In a world where people are used to over-the-top action movies, Oppenheimer is certainly way out of left field. It's very scientific, very historic, and frankly too high-brow for a large portion of the American public. But if you're the type that enjoys truly good cinema, you're in for a treat.

Cilian Murphy delivers a career performance as the titular character. His demeanor, his mannerisms, his eyes (man, his eyes!), Murphy nails it. From a humble grad student to a middle aged man defending his actions against a ruthless counsel, Murphy executes the role with perfect poise. If he doesn't win Best Actor, then the Oscars are a sham.

The cinematography was fantastic. Van Hoytema is at the top of his game in this film. Practical effects are used exclusively and to great effect. In a movie that's predominantly dialogue driven, it's important to nail the moments where effects take over, and he certainly did just that. The bomb scene was spectacularly executed. As was the subatomic symphony going on in Oppenheimer's head throughout the film.

The set pieces and inclusion of historical figures was outstanding. We got to see all of the world's premiere scientific institutions and the world renowned scientists that studied there. It really felt as though you were watching the culmination of centuries of physics...because you were.

The dialogue was exceptional. Murphy and Downey Jr. In particular delivered their lines with such mastery. Even the supporting cast of Damon and Blunt stole the show when given the opportunity.

There were so many fantastic historic moments, excellent one-liners, and jaw dropping scenes, it's hard to even recall them all.

This is Nolan at his best and a true masterpiece.

10.title: Nolan's and Murphy's Best Work
10.content:
You must experience it, rather than reading my review.

I cannot express it in words that how great this is.

As an avid fan of historical dramas and biopics, I was thrilled to watch "Oppenheimer," the highly anticipated film that chronicles the life of J. Robert Oppenheimer, the enigmatic physicist who played a pivotal role in developing the atomic bomb during World War II. Directed by the brilliant Christopher Nolan and starring an exceptional cast, the movie delivers a compelling narrative of a complex figure and the morally ambiguous era in which he lived.

The film's production values are truly remarkable. Nolan's visionary direction, combined with masterful cinematography, creates a visually stunning experience. From the sweeping shots of the New Mexico desert, where the Los Alamos laboratory was set up, to the tense and atmospheric laboratories, the movie succeeds in immersing the audience in the historical context of the 1940s.

Cillian Murphy's portrayal of J. Robert Oppenheimer is nothing short of captivating. He embodies the physicist's inner turmoil, intelligence, and ambition flawlessly. Murphy's performance brilliantly captures Oppenheimer's transformation from an ambitious young scientist to a conflicted man grappling with the ethical implications of his groundbreaking work. The supporting cast, including Marion Cotillard as Katherine "Kitty" Puening and Michael Caine as Richard Tolman, provide stellar performances, adding depth and emotion to the narrative.

The movie effectively balances the scientific aspects of the Manhattan Project with the personal and ethical dilemmas faced by the characters. It delves into Oppenheimer's complex personality, portraying him as more than just a brilliant scientist. The film highlights his relationships with colleagues, particularly his often-fraught interactions with Edward Teller (played convincingly by Tom Hardy), and his romantic entanglements, particularly his affair with Kitty Puening.

One of the film's most commendable aspects is its willingness to confront the moral implications of the atomic bomb's development. It doesn't shy away from the devastating consequences of the bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, forcing the audience to grapple with the ethical ambiguity surrounding Oppenheimer's actions. The movie raises important questions about the cost of scientific progress and the responsibility of scientists in the face of unprecedented power.

10.title: Damn
10.content:
