And of course a lot of the usual "what have we done?". So the moral aspect also played a role here. Perfectly visualized but still... kinda boring. I really feel like this movie doesn't live up to the hype. My rating would be something like a 6.5 maybe. Its okay to watch it once but i don't think i will every watch it again. The current rating on imdb is way too high.

6.title: Overhyped FS
6.content:
Yeah man, that was hard.

Very well made cinematically, great acting, great effects but still very hard to finish without checking how much is left every 10 minutes.

Severely overpowered with pointless dialogues /pointless for the average human being I guess/.

Seems more like a documentary than anything else.

I am giving it a 6 simply because of the few moments in the movie that are sending shivers down your spine knowing the importance of Oppenheimer nowadays and the influence he had and will continue to have in human history.

Other than that, I was averagely engaged, averagely entertained and fully disappointed knowing the potential this movie had with all those S tier actors.

6.title: I struggled with this film ..
6.content:
The acting is incredible, it's an A list cast and man do they deliver. The sets, production quality and period accuracy is astonishing. There's a problem though. I felt like they made a superb 3 hour film, chopped it into 100 parts, and then stuck them all back together again at random.

It would have been far better if they had made a more conventional chronological biopic. Instead it leaps about through time and styles, with elements of fantasy thrown in too for good measure. For much of the film I was just confused. "What's happening and when?" Was my main question throughout the film. Just as I picked up a clue what was going on it jumped to another time frame.

Overall a bit too much style over substance. Only one person to blame for that.

6.title: Standards of film quality in decline
6.content:
Oppenheimer and the hype and praise around the movie let me believe that this is another masterpiece by the acclaimed director Christopher Nolan, but at best I could say this is a decent film, sadly nothing past that.

The beginning and parts of the movie feel rushed, the pacing is simply terrible, the main character isn't very relatable, but on the upside the remaining cast are. Strong performances are mostly given by everyone but I felt like the main guy was a slight miscast.

The movie builds up to the moment of explosion quite effectively, there's lots of tension and anticipation through the film and for what its worth, the politics in the movie are sometimes intriguing, but sometimes I couldn't keep up due pacing suddenly accelerating like mad, there's a lot of unnecessary flashbacks and timejumps back and forth. Nolan clearly wanted to movie to be deeper than what he could achieve here, perhaps too ambitious of an attempt.

The "climax" if you will (aka the detonation of the bomb) was so lackluster that it alone removes a star from my rating... Anyone who has seen footage of real atomic bombs will notice that the explosion here wasn't one. It was a gasoline explosion, there was no mushroom cloud to be seen! For the sake of immersion and believability, Nolan should've settled for CGI for once...

The hype, expectations and overall praise of the movie felt misleading after having watched this, the status of some directors and actors seem to mislead into believing that what they're watching is deep, meaningful and mysterious, when in fact that's just the surface with very little beneath it.

It's an alright movie with some fancy visuals sprinkled here and there, but the pacing in the end is the biggest letdown especially considering how long the film was.

6/10.

6.title: Underwhelming
6.content:
I do think this is a well made film. The acting is good but nothing spectacular or memorable. How Emily Blunt who I think is an amazing actress is getting her first Oscar nomination for her least interesting performance. There just isn't much for her to work with.

One of the most pivotal events in history and this is one of the dullest movies I have watched lately.

I don't hate it but I think it's lacking something. After the bomb is dropped we see a bit of the emotional reaction and fallout from some of the scientists who worked on it. The unfortunate part is that angle isn't explored enough. The court room drama isn't that compelling either. It's just lacking in juiciness.

6.title: A Classic or just Hollywood Hype?
6.content:
The Manhattan Project and the man who headed it to create the atomic bomb that eventually destroyed Hiroshima and Nagasaki, is a compelling story. The background in OPPENHEIMER is the revolutionary physics of the 20th century and the destructive power of the atom.

Let me say up front that the ending was commendable for exposing the petty perfidy of Lewis Strauss (of the Atomic Energy Commission) and Edward Teller (the rival H-bomb physicist) in dishonoring Oppenheimer as a communist agent in Congressional hearings. As a result, Oppenheimer lost his security clearance and ended his career in disgrace.

I'm not a filmmaker or a nuclear physicist, but just a photographer, so this is my amateur opinion. Cillian Murphy as Oppenheimer is excellent and understandably comes across as a morally conflicted person. But many others like Emily Blunt, Florence Pugh and Matt Damon were mediocre. Damon was overacting.

First, it's way too long. I was actually getting a bit bored 15 min in and thinking the recent PBS documentary OPPENHEIMER was more engrossing.

Second, the ambient dreamy music is extremely annoying and very distracting. The film would have greater impact if there was just dialogue and much less music.

Third, the editing is jagged and erratic. There are too many jump cuts and cutting between characters that I found disorienting.

Fourth, they edited in many annoying fake explosions and pseudoscientific montages right in the middle of dialogue. I assume it was to make it look more "scientific" and dramatic. (I once read a French critique that said the problem with American films is that there are "too many explosions." Christopher Nolan is British, but is he playing up to an American audience..?) Fifth, the gratuitous nudity was absurd, awkward and had absolutely no aesthetic or erotic value. In fact it's vulgar.

Finally, it was a mistake NOT to show the devastating bombing of Hiroshima and/or Nagasaki. This was a glaring omission given that the dénouement of Oppenheimer's efforts was the climactic bombing of these targets with a vast human toll. The Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists in 2020 estimated 210,000 people died as a result of the bombings.

In this age of heightened moral awareness and political correctness, was Nolan afraid of the blowback from American audiences? Was he concerned about opening a discussion about the ethics of bombing the Japanese people a second time? Or that the US would not have used atom bombs against Europeans? Is this a movie about one of the most important scientific events in history or just an incomplete biopic of Oppenheimer? These are questions that leave me dissatisfied.

Regretfully, not a movie I'll see again.

6.title: 3 hours about the least consequential thing that happened during WW2
6.content: Hundreds of thousands of people died, but the movie dares us to worry about Oppenheimer losing his security clearance and having to make a lateral career move. It's not even the government or system turning against him, just one petty man. You learn very little about the Manhattan Project or McCarthyism or anything pertinent. The film is competently shot, and the acting is great, but I stop short of saying that it was interesting drama because it really wasn't. The obnoxious score when very little was happening on screen - too much! I was expecting a greater exploration of complex themes, a nuanced take on the ethics surrounding the creation of the bomb, but there was none of that. The fact that Oppenheimer lost his security clearance should be nothing more than a pub trivia question, but instead, we get this three-hour monstrosity.

6.title: I had low expectations going in..
6.content: Sadly it couldn't even meet them. I thought this would at least be a good telling of historical drama but as in Tenet, Nolan seems to have lost the ability to actually tell a meaningful story and cares more about his latest ideas for cinematic style than his need to actually build emotion. The movie does conclude powerfully but cheaply, in literally the last 10 seconds, but I can't forgive it for wasting 30 minutes of my life before that. I thought the movie was 3 star entertainment, an IMDB 6.7 until somewhere around that 2 hour 30 mark when I actually checked my watch -- something I haven't done in any movie whatsoever -- in who knows how long. Why was this 3 hours long? Why was this offered in IMAX? Not only wasting 30-45 minutes more than necessary but more of my money as well. And why does one of the most powerful directors of my time need to rely on inserting 10 seconds of doom to create an impression at the end of his movie instead of actually building a story with a meaningful plot (to the movie, not to history). I'm hopeful the director of some of the greatest Hollywood movies of the last 20 years will strike gold again, but I won't trust him with my cinema dollars again.

6.title: Not Nolan's best work, but one to watch at least once
6.content:
What was good?

Cillian Murphy - hands down his performance was brilliant and he would be a strong contender for the Oscar, subject to whatever else comes out. There are too many moments to highlight, but ultimately I think he nailed all the moments, as well as the complexities of what he was creating, and the impact it had.

Emily Blunt - phenomenal performance - I loved every scene she was in (except the one with Florence Pugh), but she was brilliant. That scene when she didn't shake that scientist's hand at the end- I laughed out loud. Every women would not forget that. That scene where she was being "cross examined" (although that was not a court and was an utterly unfair process) was also amazing, I hope she gets recognized for her work. Supporting Actress Oscar for sure.

Matt Damon - a solid performance even though his character was morally questionable - I enjoyed watching his scenes. In fact, side note - recently watched him in Air, and he was brilliant in that too, and I forgot how much I enjoy his work.

The bad?

You create a film about the atomic bomb and you don't show the actual effect either through flashes of newspaper clips or news stories?! I mean what the hell was that? I was researching on my phone whilst in the cinema to remind myself of the history. I.e. Japan attacked Pearl harbor, and USA retaliated in the worst way with the atomic bomb killing hundreds of thousands of people in two Japanese cities. I remember being in school and history lessons learning of the after effect. So, from a philosophical and morality perspective this was a really weak part of the film. The moral questions only came up briefly in certain ways such as through Oppenheimer's hearing to see if he should have his security clearance. Of course, the moral repercussions of what Oppenheimer and his team did in the Manhattan project was only explored through Oppenheimer after he considered the mass deaths of innocent lives - but even then, it was only in his mind and there were no visual images shown. I think it would have been better to show the reality of what happened to make us the viewers make our own moral judgments about him too. How can scientists create something and not consider the impact or the potential use of that item by the government - i.e. The atomic bomb. This for me was the weakest part of the film. Whilst Oppenheimer tried to do this later, if we saw the truth of the destruction juxtaposed with the remorse he clearly felt and the actions he then took towards trying to stop the hydrogen bomb being created, then maybe I would have found the film more interesting.

Finally, Florence Pugh's character was totally not necessary or relevant to the story and I would have preferred if she was cut out completely and nothing would have been lost. Again, it would have been more fitting to explore the humanity and the concepts of good and bad within Oppenheimer in relation to the bomb he created. Further, the nudity was completely unnecessary and not integral to the story at all. I found O's story with his wife much more fascinating - a realistic exploration of being married through the good, the bad and the ugly. I mean we knew nothing about FP's character other than seeing her nude, and her not liking his flowers, and being incredibly needy. So not a great role for her at all and would not have been missed.

There were some other strong supporting cast, but to be honest, there were so many men in the film that their names were lost on me. But Rami Malek was used in a key scene, and I thought he did a good job, as did the aid to Robert DJ - who was happy when he got his comeuppances.

Whilst Robert D J was ok, there was too much of him, and the film could have been edited down and less of him would have been good.

6.title: Overrated movie
6.content:
I decided to watch this movie last night,whilst it was still on theaters.

The movie is not bad, it is not perfect either.

I gave it six stars because it had some interesting parts, food for thought let's say. The acting was great .All the actors chosen for the movie did their job well without overacting or exaggerating.

But the plot is killing the movie. It is an endless back and forth ,back and forth of the same thing. The focus on the connection between Oppenheimer and the communists. I understand that this could be interesting to some people,for me it wasn't.

I did not go to the theaters expecting to watch a blockbuster/action movie. But I did not expect a legal drama either.

There was no development and even though the movie was named Oppenheimer, it does not mean that Oppenheimer should be in 95% of the screen time , mostly staring vaguely in to the camera ,all dreamy-eyed.

I just do not get the extremely high reviews. I have rated many movies much higher than 6 stars. Does this make this movie a garbage? No. By no means this is a garbage. It is a high profile movie with an all star cast BUT the plot is non existent ,it makes you feel that it is not going anywhere, the character development is non existent as well.

I feel that Nolan made a movie that mocks our intelligence the same way he did with Tenet. I sat 3 hours through this but I wanted to walk out really bad.

6.title: Overhyped
6.content:
Not every scene needs a climatic music. God it was from start to finish. Even a normal casual conversation doesn't have to start or end with high pitch climax music. This is the issue with Nolan's movie. This was the same template he used for The Dark Knight Rises and I remember not liking the movie as much as i would have wished.

This movie is a fight between communist and right wing Americans from start to finish and they have sprinkled some Second World War, some science in between.

From start you get a feeling that people just assumed Oppenheimer and the team are going to build the bomb and Oppenheimer is going to regret it later. There is a big continuity issue with this movie.

I agree the best part is the court drama after bomb attack on Japan. But they were totally building towards it.

There is quite a lot Oppenheimer did for the Manhattan Project, some of the really smart work but it's been given hardly any screen time.

6.title: Put me in the didn't get it column
6.content:
Go see this in an IMAX they said. It's the only way to see they said. Then I go to the regular theater and at the two and a half hour mark I start to wonder what would the IMAX experience have provided? This movie is straight drama. Interesting story. Great acting. Good cinematography. But 3 hour snooze fest I'd much rather have seen in my pajamas on my recliner at home.

Then, the only reason it's rated R is for some random unnecessary sex scene for some actress that apparently really wanted the world to see her breasts.

I suppose if the trailers showed what this movie was really about it wouldn't have done as well.

Whatever. Nolan is on notice at this point. Stick to what made him stand out. This was a long drawn out drama.

6.title: A Gary Oldman Truman Biopic, Please
6.content:
A Truman biopic with Gary Oldman playing the lead is what this film really left me wanting to see. Sadly, the Truman scene was maybe 5 minutes long but it was clearly the most honest dialogue in the movie.

This movie is not about the Manhattan project. This movie is liberal hand-wringing over two things: (1) having used the bomb and (2) the hunt to get communists out of sensitive government positions. I get that immediately following the use of the bomb people thought we had opened Pandora's box. But here we are 78 years later and neither we nor anyone else has used one again. And we now know communists were in sensitive positions. Yet the tears continue to flow.

Beautifully shot, well acted, but boring. I guarantee you will google "How long is Oppenheimer" during the movie. You will also say, "Hey, why is the music so loud all of the sudden? They are just walking down the street."

This was a bail and switch.

PS ... whatever reviewer says this is the greatest war movie ever is high on crack.

6.title: Had potential; confusing and long.
6.content:
Character: 7/10 Story: 4/10 Plot: 5/10 Setting: 8/10 Execution: 6/10 Total: 30/50 (6 stars)

If I'm gonna be honest, I have no idea why this movie is so high-rated.

This movie follows a physician named Oppenheimer who developed the atomic bombs in the USA that were to be dropped in Hiroshima and Nagasaki. That's about as simple as it can get. I don't see why it needed 3 hours to get to that point; had to check my watch about 5 times to see when the movie was over. Even some of my friends checked their phones about three times.

By the way, the characters? Banal and trivial, except some of the main ones. Oppenheimer's personality was charming and nonchalant, and I enjoyed his wit. Einstein's too. But that's it! You don't get much more of the other characters, not even their backstories or motivations in life.

The one aspect I did enjoy, however, was the discordance the movie could portray. Although disturbing for some people, I enjoyed the sudden bursts of sound or light, not to mention the suspenseful pauses! It used effects such as whitespace or jump cuts to convey these. But that's really the only thing I was looking forward to.

I had high hopes for this movie. I really did. But I hope that, in the future, Chris will step up his game. If you're planning to spend 3 hours watching a movie, just go watch Barbie instead.

6.title: Failed on many levels
6.content: As an aficionado of quantum physics, and the history of science, I had high hopes for this film but the writing and direction were a major disappointment, with the first and most important mistake being the choice of a feature length film! It should have been a 3-4 season series on Netflix or HBO. The entire movie was too fast, not giving time for the incredible cast to strut their stuff, or the viewers to absorb the complexity of science, moral choices or the fine acting of Murphy. There were single lines in the film that could have been made into a one hour episode. Nolan's choice of animated depiction of quantum physical matters was amateurish at best.

6.title: Oppenheimer - *** out of *****
6.content: I realize this is a VERY minority opinion, but here it goes... I think because this is a film about extraordinary people in extraordinary circumstances, the film itself is being mistaken as extraordinary also. And I just don't think it is. Now don't get me wrong - there are awesome, inspiring, jaw-dropping moments scattered throughout. And I was more appreciative of the film in the last third when some of the supporting characters start getting a chance to shine. Maybe it's my lack of intelligence, but the first couple hours were a confusing slog for me to sit through. I couldn't keep track of who was who, and everyone spoke like they were in a 1940s newspaper comedy. I can't help but think those not familiar with the story beforehand are going to be lost. I will say this - Murphy is outstanding throughout, and I won't holler if he wins the Best Actor Oscar. Downey and Blunt do what they can, but the roles are not awards-worthy. I found Blunt particularly underutilized - I'm so happy she FINALLY has an Academy Award nomination, but I wish it was for something more substantial. As I said, the last third is what leads me to an overall recommendation. The scenes in which Oppenheimer's loyalty and allegiance are being questioned feel brutal and often heartbreaking. And this is where Murphy gets to shine brightest. Technical aspects are unsurprisingly top notch - the sound work is especially amazing. I can imagine this being a more overwhelming viewing experience when seen in a theater. But right or wrong, my thought has always been a good movie is a good movie no matter where you're watching it. I sadly can't jump aboard the OPPENHEIMER express, but this is an occasion on which I totally understand why others love it and would never question why. I'm glad I watched it, and I'm glad to know more about the subject, but I wouldn't call it one of the best of the year. - Jeff Marshall,.

6.title: Good but overrated
6.content: Oppenheimer is a film about a team of Physicists led by J. Robert Oppenheimer (Murphy) who are desperate to beat the Germans in the race to create the atomic bomb. The acting is solid but that's to be expected from a cast that houses Damon, Malek, Oldman, Casey Affleck to name but a mere few. The trouble is, the film feels entirely exaggerated. There are scenes where the music is so loud, Nolan esque in nature, but very little is actually happening on screen. The visual specticles are random and seem misaligned. Now, without being deemed a philistine, the scene pasting and cinematography is very good and smooth, but when you strip away the fact that many of us get excited at the idea of a Nolan based historic drama starring Enstein about a bomb, you are left with a good to average film at best. I think there have been so many incredible original masterpieces from Nolan, it's easy to get carried away with it all, and forget that not every Da Vinci painting is a masterpiece. It's worth a watch, and it made the evening enjoyable, but it is not all its hyped up to be, and it could easily have been cut an hour short and still achieved the desired effect.

6.title: Atomic jump scares
6.content:
Atomically loud jump scares are littered throughout the film. The film immediately starts with a sudden huge noise then plods quietly through barely discernible dialogue until other sudden huge noises occur regularly to inject adrenalin into the audience. The first hour urgently needs sub titles due to the garbled words. This is strange because the first hour had some scientific theory which, if heard better, would have really added to the film.

Sudden irrelevant sex scenes occasionally replace the sudden loud noises obviously to break the monotonous talk fest.

Some great acting by both major and minor actors. This saved the film from outright boredom and makes it passable. The theme is of such importance that the talk fest is warranted so we can get a better understanding of those times.

The musical score was mainly sudden and loud. Forte forte FORTE.

6.title: So Boring
6.content:
With so many awards and accolades, I expected this film to be compelling and entertaining. It was not for me. The first half is mostly talk with too many flashbacks and flashforwards. The second half has its exciting moments but there are too few to keep momentum.

The actors do reasonably well but the movie is simply too long to hold interest. I guess that's why the director inserted very loud sounds periodically to wake up viewers who drifted off to sleep, including my wife.

The story could have been told more effectively in two hours or less. I'm glad we streamed it at home so we could break it into two 90 minute segments. I would not watch it again.

6.title: Overhyped and Weakest movie of Nolan so far but .......
6.content: It is the weakest movie of Christopher Nolan but it is still watchable and far better than many movies that came this year and previous years. Thanks to its bgm. Feels like suspense Horror movie, but it's not. Nothing much to say about it's acting. Nothing extra ordinary. Story is Bah. Nothing that you may find exciting. Best thing in entire movie is the bgm. Save your money and watch in ordinary screen, no need of going for IMAX. It's a dialogue heavy and totally a dialogue driven movie. Don't expect great visual as per the current going hype. It's a overhyped movie. Weakest work of Nolan. I think it's the topic or the theme of this movie. What else can you expect. Nolan tried to do his best. Unlike other Nolan movies, It is just, One time watch only, strictly.

6.title: The Devil is in the Details...
6.content: Making quality historical biopics is hard. First, a director wants to be true to history. Second, a director wants to entertain a broad audience. So here, master director Chris Nolan took on the task of a biopic of Robert Oppenheimer - the "father of the atomic bomb". I am sure the movie will get an oscar nod or two. But for this reviewer, it fell short of that lofty mark. First major flaw was the length of the film. It ran THREE HOURS. Yikes. I would almost go so far as to say no movie should run that long. That may go too far, but as to this particular film, the key part of the Oppenheimer life story should have taken 2 hours. Second major flaw, at least in IMAX, was a loud "boomy" audio that made dialogue tough to follow. "Boomy" bass is fine for atomic test explosions and the like, but not for dialogue. With that said, the quality of acting by Cilian Murphy, Florence Pugh, Matt Damon, Emily Blunt and others was natural and convincing. I won't fault them.

6.title: Too fast, too many cuts, Am I getting old?
6.content:
Maybe I'm getting old, I don't know.. Im 31 so I guess that's not the case probably. I love love love love Nolan's movies. But this one didn't quite get me. Of course really good acting and the story was intriguing.

But I really don't like the fastness of the cuts. Same as Elvis (weird comparison, I know) It's like they fill in for us viewers, that we are bored really easily. Slow down!! I want to see real people, dialogue, so that the big gestures really mean something. I found it almost a bit boring because the story went so quick and fast. Like I was missing the point all the time (what was probably true;)

6.title: A potentially good drama ruined by a catastrophic edit
6.content:
This review contains some minor spoilers.

I'll start this review by saying that I have been a huge Nolan fan for over a decade now and that every new movie of his I consider as The Movie Event of the year. However, after Chris' last picture "Tenet", which turned out to be a smaller letdown due to obvious signs of repeating of motives used in previous of his films, I lowered my expectations for "Oppenheimer" also because it is a very challenging theme to be turned into a three hour long summer blockbuster film.

But even with all that in mind, "Oppenheimer" was a disappointing, and at certain points of the movie timeline even painful experience for me. The main cause for this is the catastrophic editing of Jennifer Lame who started her collaboration with Nolan on "Tenet" and actually did a decent job there. In "Oppenheimer", on the other side, the scenes and shots are exchanging so quickly you get to think the movie has only one hour to tell the story rather than three. This especially comes to expression within the first forty minutes or so of the film where we don't even get a brake to think and relax for a second, the movie just keeps changing and going from scene to scene with each scene lasting approximately five to ten seconds (and that is not an exaggeration). Nolan never really used to implement long shots or scenes in his movies, but this was just another level of short shots intertwined with each other.

Another problem is the poor use of soundtrack. This movie has no action at all, it is a drama that could well be performed on an actual stage, so having loud music in the background during scenes in which two characters have a tense, long dialog in order to emphasize that tension, really brings these same scenes to the level of ridicule. Speaking of soundtrack, Ludwig Göransson did a fine job here, but he tries way too much to be Hans Zimmer.

I also have a problem with the script itself. Like, why do we have two narration lines in this film? One line is Oppenheimer hearing intended to remove his security clearance, shot in color, and the other is Senate confirmation hearing of Lewis Strauss (played by Robert Downey Jr) to become Secretary of Commerce, shot in black and white. At the end of the movie they come together and the black and white line transfers to color, which seems to be an hommage to Nolan's second film "Memento", but other than that I don't see any purpose in having those two hearings tell us the story in parallel.

There are things that save the film from being a complete catastrophe, first and foremost the performances. I mean, when you have an ensemble cast of over twenty known actors, five of which who are Oscar winners, than you don't expect anything less. There are also some scenes that are very well made. The famous Trinity test scene where they set the bomb for the first time is well delivered, but I would also advise not to expect too much because it's not all that impressive. The ending is also neat, and there are a few more scenes that save the experience and are well made mostly thanks to the cinematography of Hoyte van Hoytema, which, again, is decent but not all that impressive like in "Dunkirk" for example.

All things considered, "Oppenheimer" is nowhere near bad as it is disappointing, but Nolan has accustomed us to a higher standard, a that's why a 6/10 is a very low rating for a director and writer of his caliber. I can see that the audience and the critics went crazy about this film, given the fact that its metascore is at 89/100 (highest ever for a Nolan film after Dunkirk) and IMDB rating 8.8 at the time I'm writing this review, and it wouldn't even surprise me him finally winning an Oscar for this. How ironic would that be? He didn't get one for "Memento", as he should, for the "Prestige" and "The Dark Knight" he wasn't even nominated, and yet something tells me he will finally get one for "Oppenheimer", possibly the worst movie he ever made.

6.title: Movie by men to men
6.content:
English is not my first language, so bare with me.

What I liked: the casting, acting, few good scenes, the ending.

What I didn't like: You could tell this was written by men. The female characters were paper-thin: no motives, no logic. The women of Oppenheimer's life: one was crazy and the other drank. Why? Nobody knows.

The music was too heavy throughout the film. Even in scenes where there was nothing going on, the music was building up for something that never happened.

The sex scene: What kind of woman stops riding a man to look at his books? That are behind her? And the line about the destroyer of worlds was destroyed at the same scene. It had more power behind the words in the trailer than in the movie, even though the words are spoken twice in this. Why couldn't he read something else from that book to impress her and to show that he really did read the Bhagavad Gita, then sex? That would have saved a lot.

The movie tries to tackle it all: Oppenheimer's youth, the building of the a-bomb, his private life, the politics around him, who he was as a person... When it tries to do it all, it fails in all of them. Even though the movie is 3 hours long (!!), it feels we run through everything. Except the hunt for communists, the movie dwells on that like it is the most important thing ever.

The movie tries to take into consideration the feelings of the Japanese by showing short flashes of the destruction, but this is in no way tied to the feelings or thoughts of Oppenheimer himself. It is a side note, like everything in this movie. He feels as cold as his eyes are blue.

If I have to sum my feelings into one word, it is 'why'. Why did Oppenheimer break all those glasses? Why was her wife yelling? Why did Oppenheimer stay loyal to the country that suspected him in every turn? Why couldn't we keep the man himself as the main character, why the whole thing about the scientist turn politician?

The ending was emotional, I give you that. When the genie is out of the bottle, there's no going back. The future will show us will humankind destroy itself with the fire it was given.

6.title: Underwhelmed
6.content:
The acting and production values are up to Christopher Nolan's standards. Cillian Murphy was a great choice to play J. Robert Oppenheimer - that said, there were long stretches where his deadpan portrayal evoked little emotion (in me) regarding his complex character.

If anyone stole the movie, it was Robert Downey Jr. As Lewis Strauss. RDJ moved seamlessly through the time shifts and was ultimately perfect as a foil to Oppenheimer. I won't get into any of the rest of the ensemble cast, but they all played their supporting roles quite well.

So, why the six star review, then? Even at 3 hours, the film and character development felt incredibly rushed, and there were many aspects to this expansive story that weren't adequately fleshed out. To me, it would have been much more engaging as a 6 or 8 episode biopic mini-series. Oppenheimer didn't need to be IMAX film. The story was about his life's work and personal idiosyncrasies.

At the end of the movie, I walked out of the theater to my car & never once said "wow!" While it was technically flawless, and was well cast, it never emotionally engaged me. YMMV.

6.title: You were told that a bomb was about to explore but then... you heard "pffftttt....."
6.content:
I went in with a lot of expectation. Knowingly that this is a biography and it's based on an actual event that we already knew - an invention that changed the course of the world.

So with a stacked casts consisting of some of the greatest actors of our time, 3-hour run time and all the hype surround this film, I came out feeling hollow and confused!

It's overly long - the run time could be cut short to 2-hour or 2-hour 15 at most. The runtime and subplot are overstuffed!

It's over-stylized - too many time jump (Nolan's signature) but I don't see the need of deploying this. It's overused and VERY SELF-INDULGING!!! And then... there is these black and white scenes that are supposed to represent something. I don't know what I'm suppose to watch, one moment I'm given the lecture on science and physics but the next it's all bureaucratic and political and conspiracies. And then there's drama and affair. It's just too much! I like movies that are non-linear, to serve the purpose of storytelling and for the twist. But this one, just NO!

It's overblown - and overhyped. I know this movie is about atomic bomb and its impact to humanity but I cannot feel the real impact of it for the most part. Probably only towards the last 1 hour. The explosion scene is supposed to be the climax but I didn't feel it that way.

At some point in the cinema, I felt like I needed to look up Oppenheimer on wikipedia and get over with it rather than to sit through the remaining hours of self-indulging piece of work that some may call it art. Yes maybe it is, perhaps too artistic to the point I don't know how to appreciate it?

To be fair, the acting is really good but I somehow often got distracted with the overly long dialogues. It reminds me of Quentin Tarantino's Inglorious Basterds long dialogue but Nolan did not pull this one off!

Great production, yes. But I can't say the same for the screenplay.

Cinematography is beautiful but the jump cut to the "imagination" (supposedly) of the lead character is more distracting than it is to serve its purpose.

Not forgetting also the soundtrack. It's trying to make the audience feel tensed but it did not do anything to me. I felt it's more distracting to me than to make me feel tensed or engaged.

I'm a fan of Christopher Nolan's earlier works. Like Memento and Inception, both are very original and groundbreaking. Batman, Dark Knight and The Prestige are great movies.

But not this one! So distracting that I kept looking at my watch and I'm struggling to connect with the story.

It's like a bomb that did not detonate.

6.title: Overrated but solid movie
6.content: I like Chris Nolan movies, biopics, and the subject of this movie but score was over the top and gave me a headache. Think people would have been falling asleep if not for the exaggerated score that makes you feel like you're having an anxiety attack for 3 hours. Topic is interesting but more befitting a documentary and would have been way more relevant if someone made this movie in the 80s when cold war and nuclear holocaust were still a concern of people. Felt like they didn't explain Robert Downey Jrs' character enough for him to be the antagonist they used him as. Not a bad movie, just not the masterpiece people are calling it. Kind of movie you may never rewatch.

6.title: This was definitely a film that I watched
6.content:
So there has been an undoubted amount of anticipation for this movie so I was very much seated in the cinema, looking forward to watching it, especially as I usually enjoy whatever Christopher Nolan has to offer. At the end of the movie I was neither underwhelmed nor overwhelmed, just merely whelmed.

There's lots to admire in the movie, great production, some really interesting ways of building up tension and strong performances. Murphy does the role justice, even if his accent slips for certain moments (a very pedantic thing for me to detect since he has some Irish mannerisms deeply rooted in his voice). Emily Blunt and Florence Pugh make the most of the limited time they get, as their characters are engaging and bring some life to the screen. We don't really get any relevant or new insights into them though, so my main issue there comes with the screenwriting.

For a film about the inventor of a nuclear weapon, we don't actually see much of the making of the bomb. Or the science behind it. There are some calculations on blackboards etc, but I would've liked to have seen some real scientific discussion just so it would feel more authentic. I'm not even a mathematician or physicist, but come on - we get a few quick shots of the bomb shell being put together in some warehouse and that's it. This film goes on for three whole hours so I'm sure they could've cut many scenes to have a bit more proper science in it.

I didn't love Robert Downey Jr's performance. It was fine, it wasn't an immediate Oscar win. The temporal switches to his scenes were jarring and he wasn't engaging at all as a character even if he was so key to the story, the direction just didn't make it seem that way. Nolan is usually the master of temporality in cinema, however it was inappropriate in Oppenheimer and came off as a bit clumsy.

On the whole I thought the movie was fine, I was fortunate to see it in a cinema when there was still a lot of the hype so the atmosphere was great. But no film ever has to be three hours long, especially if it doesn't even show much of what it should be about.

6.title: Film should be called Strauss not Oppenheimer!
6.content:
I love Nolan but this movie did not do it for me! I was very disappointed after spending 3 hours in the cinema. First of all I really liked the setting, the story and the actors. Music was great too. That's pretty much it.

The rest: The story telling was just terrible. I was not emotional involved in the main character or any characters. I did not get to know who Oppenheimer really was. I was neither moved nor touched by the story.

Too much dialoge, too many names, too many characters, so many time jumps. All of this made this movie far too complicated although the plot itself is not complicated at all... it felt very forced.

It was also very irritating to me that Robert Downey Jr.'s character was given so much time and space in the film. I did not care about this "Strauss" character ... as the movie is about Oppenheimer?!

In my opinion the story revolves too much about the trial. It is about a man who built a deadly weapon and killed nearly 120.000 people... who cares if he was a communist or not? Totally missed the point, in my opinion.

Also why would you film everything in IMAX cameras if most of the plot is happening in an interrogation room?! You could totally watch it in a normal cinema.....

So overall not great!

6.title: Nolan fatigue
6.content:
Fantastic performances. Cillian deserves an Oscar. Great cinematography and score. Stellar casting. Gorgeous effects. Very effective portrayal of the frenetic pace of the Manhattan Project and the existential dread that comes along with the invention of these terrible weapons.

There are several flaws that are often present in Nolan's films. Swelling score drowning out important dialogue. Artificially fast-paced and complex dialogue filled with smug jargon. Unnecessarily complicated plots. The latter two are especially, unforgivably egregious in Oppenheimer without Nolan's well-shot action scenes to distract from them.

There is no reason to be jumping between different timelines, there is no reason for so many characters, and there is no reason for Strauss' plot to be actually portrayed on screen rather than just alluded to. This is an 8/10 film dragged down to a 6/10 because Nolan thinks he's too clever for us mere mortals and is determined to shove a miniseries' worth of content into a theatrical film. I never say this about Nolan films but there really is no reason to see Oppenheimer in IMAX. It's 95% people talking to each other.

I have long suspected that Nolan would be better served by making big-budget miniseries and Oppenheimer confirms that.

6.title: Great acting and directing attempt to make a boring story exciting
6.content:
I love Christopher Nolan and Cillian Murphy, plus I'm a physics nerd so I was looking forward to this movie more than any other in recent memory. Interstellar is my favorite movie of all time partially because the focus on science, namely quantum mechanics and general relativity (and our inability to rectify them).

Oppenheimer barely dips a toe in the water regarding quantum mechanics. There are a few moments when I thought they were about to talk about physics, but they turn into a single comment (light is both a wave and a particle) and then move on.

"Oppe" is portrayed as an emotionally fragile weakling with very limited ability in his profession, and his main talent is just managing people and the project. I don't feel this is an accurate portrayal because he truly was a prolific physics mind. The film meanders through his life with flashbacks and the opposing perspective of Strauss. It's mostly historically accurate with some annoying BS sprinkled in, such as when Oppe asks Einstein to check Teller's calculations on starting an unstoppable nuclear reaction.

The first half of the movie is quite good and then after they test the bomb it started to go downhill.

I had never heard of Benny Safdie (who plays Teller) before so I'm not sure if his face is always wet due to a medical condition or if something about his character necessitated this. Either way, it was weird.

Jason Clark seemed to be overacting a bit. He was so angry and loud during his interrogation of Oppenheimer and it didn't add anything to the film. If I was watching at home I would have cut the volume in half to endure it.

Overall Oppenheimer is portrayed as fairly unlikeable, and the amount of animosity Strauss has for him doesn't make sense. Strauss is unlikable too so I found myself thinking "who cares" throughout most of the second half of the movie. Who cares if his Oppenheimer's security clearance gets renewed or not? Who cares if Strauss gets confirmed in his new position? After enduring 3 hours of this I wouldn't have cared if they both got hit by a car.

6.title: Disappointing with respect to the hype (6.5)
6.content:
So, yesterday, I watched "Oppenheimer". After seeing reviews online (just below 9), which is similar to an all time favourite and fantastic movie "Shawshank Redemption" (with just above 9), I was indeed very excited to see it. Most of my friends loved it too. The only reason I didn't watch it immediately after it came out was because I thought I would be too homesick for the physics world, so I wasn't brave enough (I am a physicist by education).

Anyways, we finally went and safe to say, I was not homesick at all. The physics was very little and the world of academia was portrayed through a lot of big names and big words dropping, not all necessarily needed for the story. Fair, Hollywood movie.... expected. But, I would like to talk about something else.

So, the movie itself is good, don't get me wrong, with an absolutely excellent acting, fantastic visuals, deep dive into the politics of defence and good overall production and story. BUT, the portail of women.... OMG!!!! WHY, OH WHY do we have to keep having the same discussion!? IF YOU CAN'T WRITE FEMALE CHARACTERS, DON'T WRITE THEM AT ALL!!! Just like, for example, in the excellent "Shawshank Redemption".

Female characters in "Oppenheimer" were either morally deplorable and overly sexual, or winning and admiring the male protagonist, or crying as the main characteristic of their personality, or mentally sick because of their love for the man. Non of them said anything even remotely interesting and non of them added anything to the story at all. So why include them??? I'll tell you why. Because for some reason, still in 2023, we need to make women look like morons to tell a story about a man. Yes, let me repeat that, we need to portray women as morons to tell a story about A MAN.

What about all the women, who actually worked in the Manhattan project: the physicist and Nobel price winner Maria Mayer, the chemist Lili Hornig etc etc????

And here comes "Barbie". A movie, for which the biggest part of the budget was spent on advertising. Aka, I did not expect much. A fun, easy watch with the talented and Barbie doll like Margot Robbie. Maybe that's why there were no disappointments. So, anyway, in Barbie, that's precisely one of the main lessons Ken learnt, that he can be himself and do his own thing and he shouldn't need a woman in his life (especially bringing one down) to do so.

So, today, I'm just contemplating... how is it possible that a movie, which was not to be taken seriously had the right message and a movie, which was supposed to be the best thing out there this year, screwed up that badly.... 🤔

6.title: An overrated snoozefest
6.content:
I'm just coming from the cinema and boy, was this a drag. Long, dull and unexciting. You had one job, Nolan, do a great a-bomb explosion. Show, don't tell us how powerful it is. Show, don't tell us about the devastations in Japan. Show, don't tell us how remorseful Oppenheimer is after the bombings. It's all talk and nothing visually exciting to warrant a cinema visit. I'm not surprised by the low box office results of this movie. Sure, it's filmed well, lots of stars in it, but it's the wrong movie to make, it is very boring and way too long. We were 11 people, everyone was disappointed and one of the girls feel asleep multiple times, while others, including me, were constantly looking at their watches.

Anyway, you are warned. Now I'm getting back to studying Sanskrit.

6.title: 3 hours of boredom
6.content: Come on, after 1h30 I was hoping someone would shot Oppenheimer and the movie would end. This is way too long. It could have been an interesting movie of 2h (not saying good). Productors are lucky Nolan is directing and there is a very good cast otherwise that would be a complete failure. I believe this movie benefits from the social media factor where nobody thinks anymore and just repeats. A few "influencers" have manipulated the mass of zombies not thinking for themselves and now it is cool to see this movie and to brag about it. Well I left the movie after 2 hours. Too slow, I have better things to do with my life....

6.title: Snooze fest and overhyped
6.content: I have always felt Christopher Nolan has excelled in writing unique science-fiction stories and bringing these to life on screen. This creativity and type of film making was his niche and Inception remains one of the most creative and strong films I have seen. However I do not think he is cut out for historical features or even some mainstream type of films. Dunkirk, despite being praised, was dull and mundane. The same goes for Oppenheimer that is a complete snooze fest. This film is a chore to watch, it lacks flow, inspiration and weakly weaves the historical events together. There is no flair and I often got lost in so much unnecessary details and found myself asking what is the value of this particular scene, why is this part not fully explained? I am very surprised it scooped up any Oscars as this film is overhyped and dull in my opinion.

6.title: Oppenheimer is extremely overhyped
6.content: Oppenheimer is a remarkable and worthwhile film. However, I'm disappointed that my high expectations, shaped by others' misrepresentations of the movie as merely 'fun', resulted in me finding it to be a tedious classic. If approached with the right mindset, 'Oppenheimer' is indeed a fantastic film." ....... Oppenheimer is a remarkable and worthwhile film. However, I'm disappointed that my high expectations, shaped by others' misrepresentations of the movie as merely 'fun', resulted in me finding it to be a tedious classic. If approached with the right mindset, 'Oppenheimer' is indeed a fantastic film."

6.title: Another Nolan
6.content:
After catching up on some of Nolan's most popular work, I'm finding I'm not at all a fan. This is another slow paced, needlessly drawn out and unfocussed mess, topped off with an attention crushing stream of mediocre music which leave no room to find my own connection to the story or characters. I suffered through Inception and Interstellar, and this makes three.

I find it bizarly overrated by 'critics' and overhyped by the 'media', and find it truly hard to believe anyone would not skip through it.

There is some good acting, and considering the intruiging subject matter I'll give it a solid 50% for effort, and an extra 10% for Damon's moustache.

6.title: Spectacular And Amazing But Not Entertaining
6.content:
I'm an admirer of Nolan's movies. He casts or selects someone for his movie with utmost care, which he has done the same for this movie as well. Particularly C. Murphy, he is the best choice to play Oppenheimer's character. He lived in the character and has given his best. R. Downey & M. Damon were great supporting actors too. Nolan's display of Oppenheimer's life was spectacular and at times were outstanding. The bombing scenes or the trauma scenes or the flashback scenes, they were outstanding for sure.

Coming to the negatives, the movie is not at all gripping. Most of his movies gives edge of the seat kind of experience namely Inception, Dark Knight series etc., but this one actually is not at all entertaining in fact it made me boring at times. I felt it like a documentary. I feel, Nolan's standards have gone down.

Sorry this is in my opinion, but others might like the movie a lot or intact they might call it entertaining.

6.title: Good....But could have been better!!!
6.content:
Before i start my review i have to say that the acting in the movie by all of the actors was phenomenal, specially Robert Downey junior. The sound design was on point, but the movie lagged behind in story telling and the way the story was portrayed.

Most of the people wanted to know the story behind the successful Nuclear test, The use of bomb on Japan and the aftermath. But after the nuclear test was done the story was more focused on the court case on Oppenheimer and the politics behind it, and it went on for so long at the end, that it left a bitter taste. The take away of movie could have been the nuclear test and the sound design , but it rather was the monotonously long case that ended the movie (Again the acting was phenomenal and was one of the saving grace of the movie).

6.title: I'm among many who thought this was overrated
6.content: This film offers a deep dive into the portrayal of Oppenheimer's life, but it leans heavily into dramatization that breaks any sense of realism. Characters often feel more like caricatures than believable humans that actually had these experiences, exaggerated lines delivered in mannequin like postures that hold no emotional weight breaking any authenticity. The film's near-worship of scientific achievement comes off as uncritical, glossing over the moral complexities and consequences of the atomic bomb. While the cinematography was well ordered and everything seamed in it's place the overall dramatic flair detracted from an already interesting story without the need of this heavy support. There should have been deeper exploration of the moral conflict many of these participants would surely have endured. There were attempts that seamed laughably reduced to the equivalence of a person weeping into their hands as they peak out the side of their fingers to make sure someone is watching them show some emotion. To the laughable outburst of Matt Damon showing some rigid military force. I just had this nagging feeling the entire time that I just wanted to stop watching and I eventually buckled and walked out of the room. I listened to the movie from the other room and I could picture the scenes perfectly fine without any help and glad I drifted out of interest and eventually it was turned off in my absence, so I wasn't the only one who lost interest in this. And I wonder if I'm overcritical because normally I'd be drawn in by the historic context of the story, it should be enthralling for me. Another gimmick that got old fast was the flashes of simulated atomic activity that kept periodically appearing on screen. Holy crap did that bother me. Once, fine, twice, alright, but I lost count, middle finger to the visual director on this as there were a myriad of other ways to depict this without the jarring visual effects. Contrast these little flairs with the very stiff and dry investigative hearing scenes. Just grossly disproportionate.

6.title: Too loud, too long, too complex.
6.content:
But it wasn't boring for me. Its just that every bloody talking scene had some poor sod on a violin doing tension music. Completely lost track of the plot here and there (so many people and lts of mumbling). But good performances all round esp Downey.

I suppose my overriding thought is, to quote the film, "nobody in Hiroshima or Nagasaki cares who invented the bloody bomb." I guess I don't either. And he had a conscience. And problems with women. And a troubled childhood that was ignored in the film

Its like Nolan was worried it would be boring so peppered it with nipples, tricks and gimmicks.

I saw it on Imax and that was a waste of money - I was not blown away. We went home and re-watched the documentary. Fascinating story.

6.title: Way too long
6.content:
I'm giving this a six but only because the acting was so good. I fell asleep several times in the first hour but didn't feel liked I'd missed anything. The movie could have easily been one hour less. I will watch it again when it's available for home viewing. But I'll watch it in three stages. I have no doubt this movie will be up for a load of awards. The acting was amazing.

I'm giving this a six but only because the acting was so good. I fell asleep several times in the first hour but didn't feel liked I'd missed anything. The movie could have easily been one hour less. I will watch it again when it's available for home viewing. But I'll watch it in three stages. I have no doubt this movie will be up for a load of awards. The acting was amazing.

6.title: Too little about the Manhattan project itself
6.content: I was quite disappointed by the movie since so much time was wasted on the hearings / communist witch hunt and very little on the Manhattan project itself. Nothing about the usage of the bombs in Japan except a few words. And it was way too long for the contents. I quite liked the part about the time before the Manhattan projects with famous physicists like Einstein, Bor and Heisenberg. Special effects and acting were quite good and also the acting solid. But I would have loved to learn more in detail how the bomb had been developed, how they dealt with the time pressure vs the Nazis etc.. It had so much potential and ended in endless hearings and dirty politics.

6.title: Good - A Filmmaker's Film
6.content:
First of all, I should say that I'm a massive Christopher Nolan fan. I thoroughly enjoyed Oppenheimer, but it hasn't left me in the awe that I experienced through Interstellar or Inception. It goes without saying that the cinematography, the effects, and the acting are all incredible - an Oscar-worthy performance from Cillian Murphy, certainly.

I saw it in IMAX and was very impressed in parts. There are two really big moments in the movie and both of them are done so well that they are goosebump-inducing. But it felt more of a non-linear, post-war domestic political drama than scientific biopic (I'd hoped for the latter). There's a lot of dialogue and an enormous cast, so I'd probably recommend you watch it twice to really get to grips with who's who.

Overall, it was entertaining and very well made. But there's a part of me that thinks casual movie-goers won't have the patience for it, despite being a masterpiece within the industry. It's a film that will be studied in universities by aspiring directors and screenwriters, but I still feel Nolan is at his best in the realm of science fiction where he can be most creative.

6.title: good movie with some issues
6.content:
Let's get this straight form the start I'm not saying this is a bad movie, I'm saying it is a good movies with some issues. I know Christopher Nolan is the last director in Hollywood who gets a big budget to make original movies, but that doesn't make them automatically great.

Apart from the general current movie problem that movies are unnecessarily too long, my main issue is that the direction often feels what I would call "inelegant". Like someone had learned all the wrong lessons from watching Terrence Malick's movies. The movie bombards you with it's oppressive score and rumbling sound effects for pretty much 3 hours straight, only letting up once when they actually detonate the Trinity bomb. Usually a movies uses this amount of stirring score if it has nothing else going for it, which isn't the case here. You have great actors and awesome cinematography. Why doesn't Nolan rely those a bit more instead of drowning everything with Ludwig Göransson's score. During the Trinity test it becomes very apparent how hollow this approach is. Göransson's score becomes minimal, 2 repeating, increasing faster notes. People run around, a person throws a switch. The score lets up and a person says: "test minus 20 minutes". Yes, all this build up for a person flipping an insignificant switch. And I mean, I know a little history, I know how the Trinity test went, as I guess most people do. So I guess the outcome is not that exciting to me, because I already know what happens.

My other main issue is the female characters in Oppenheimer, which are embarrassingly badly written, like Nolan doesn't know what to do with them. I sort of felt bad for Emily Blunt give how little she gets to do in this movie. Basically looking pissed off and saying: "You got to fight Oppi !". But not to worry they gave her a bad-ass interrogation scene.

Which bring me to my final issue. Which is that Nolan wrote typical Hollywood badass comebacks and moments into this historical movie which at least to me felt sort of out of place.

I haven't quite decided yet if this is a 6 or 7 out of 10. At the moment I feel like it has too many issue to give it higher that a 6, which in my rating translates to "good movie with some issues". Don't hate me but I think I enjoyed the unapologetic Schlock of Tenet more...

On a side note: Gary Oldman is now the only actor who has played an American president and the person blamed for shooting an American president, isn't he?

6.title: TLDR... or simply put TL
6.content:
While watching this, I felt overwhelmed and confused, wishing I had read a book or two about Oppenheimer before seeing the movie. I was frequently lost by the jumping around in time - without anything to clarify what year it was. And all the scientists that he worked with! I kept hearing about the "Chevalier effect" which was apparently a bad thing, but I missed WHY was that bad?

And then there was the horrible interrogations of Oppenheimer's friends and family. There was so much in this movie that wasn't explained..... or it was and my brain was still trying to figure out what happened five minutes ago. And what year is it now (in the movie!) ????

Cillian Murphy was great. Robert Downey was great, and killed any memories of him being typecast as Iron Man. Matt Damon was more impressive than he's been in awhile. The test bomb exploding was good (not great... and it made me wonder about the fallout in 1945 - any health hazards to the workers?)

My brain still hurts. This is one 3 hour movie I know I won't be rewatching.

6.title: A movie that mistakes form for substance
6.content:
I went into Oppenheimer without particular expectations one way or the other, knowing I liked the historical context and type of question it centers on. This movie did some things well, but overall for me it just misses the mark.

Positive:
Some technical effects are very well-done and innovative. For example the stars or matter-themed visuals in the first part or the psychosis-like state in Oppie's speech late in the movie are very cool
Great acting esp. From Emily Blunt, Cilian Murphy, Matt Damon and Robert Downey Jr.


All in all you can tell they poured a lot of money into this thing

Negative:






Overall I can appreciate some of the technical prowess but I think it misses the mark as far as artistic value goes.

6.title: Effects of global impact of Manhattan Project not capitalized on
6.content:
Nolan's signature visual style was overshadowed by the excessive use of confusing time jumps that seemed more like a gimmick than a well-thought-out storytelling tool. The attempt to blend historical events I with a fictional narrative felt forced and disorienting, leaving me detached from the supposed emotional impact of the story.

Many of the characters lacked depth and development, creating a sense of little care about their fates.

The cinematic effort was certainly there, as you'd expect from a movie with this type of budget.

In the end, "Oppenheimer" left me frustrated and perplexed, with a lingering feeling of wasted potential. Christopher Nolan has proven himself capable of creating masterpieces, but this film is an unfortunate stain on his track record. Save yourself the disappointment and skip this one.

6.title: Nolan is a good director, but a bad writer
6.content:
So just came back from prague to see it in imax 70mm and got kind of mixed feelings. I it reminded me why i did not enjoy nolans movies in the past too much. He is a good director, because he choose the right actors, acting itself is great, everyone does a great job. Also locations and set design, the look, editing and cinematography are great. But in my opinion all of his recent films lack focus. He always tries to squeeze to much into the story and does not "kill his darlings". The writing is just not good, too much dry exposition. Often times charakters telling each other things they already know. Oppenheimer, even though he is in almost every scene, keeps a stranger to us. I could not disrcibe his character, since we only have external things happening to him. The exeption might be the hall scene, where the crowd cheers him after the bomb was used against japan. This was the best moment for me.

Too much is touched just a little, but always too short to really feel for the charakter. The oppenheimer story isn´t so complex as it seems, but nolan just keeps adding more people and time jumps to give us the feeling that this is an gigantic epos. This would not be that bad, but the music is almost playing in every scene. Therefore every dialog, every person is somehow emphasized and after a while it just feels like a never anding trailer.

My last point is imax. You do not need to see it in imax. I was curious technically, but it did not made much sense since this is 90% talking heads. I would make more sense for a movie with big landscapes or in space. I think 70mm is the way to go.

6.title: A dud bomb
6.content: I lasted about 40 minutes, and then gave up. This film was tediously boring, I knew it was going to be a long haul but I really couldn't face another two and a half hours of it. To be fair Cillian Murphy is a fine actor and is very watchable but even he couldn't hold my attention any longer. The story itself should have been enough to result in a good film. I think that often film makers believe that the longer the film the greater it will be received by the public. There have of course been many many great long films, but they have all had one thing in common and that is to have the audience and wanting more. As I didn't watch the whole film I know my criticism can be easily dismissed, but I cannot see the point in struggling to maintain any interest just for the sake of it.

6.title: Some great and some mediocre
6.content:
Let's start with the good: The cinematography and editing is pretty good. It's a nice film visually, especially after the Trinity sequence. I think the Ripley series is way better but still, the Oppenheimer is a good looking film. I also liked the acting, especially in the lead roles. It's an interesting historical snippet or biopic and it wasn't too boring for a 3hr movie.

And the bad: Although the general pacing of the movie is good, there are parts that are too long and some parts that were cut a bit short. It seems to be that some love interests should have weight in the movie but those doesn't really have depth so fall a bit short. And there are other parts like that. And the jumping between timelines and characters might seem smart cinema to someone, but to me it's just trying to be smart or trying to have extra layers. In reality it's just unecessary complexity that makes harder to watch and enjoy the film.

So all in all, I recommend watching it, and I liked it, but it's a one-time watch for me. There are good, sometimes great parts of it but bad directing and storytelling just ruins it enough so I can't call it a masterpiece.

6.title: Too much overated
6.content:
I think this movie got really good actors, it saves the movie but it was really boring. It's too much, 3 hours movie. After the test of the bomb, it became hard to watch. Nothing else was interesting.

Also it bothered me the parts when they show future and past intercaleted. It would be so much better if it showed only past in some parts.

The movie got cool effects, good actors and acting. The bad parts, too long, loses focus in some parts and make it tiring to watch.

Maybe I would give more points if I watched it at home, with some breaks.

Another idea, it could easily be a netflix series.

6.title: Another boring, inaccurate film about scientists
6.content:
It is very difficult to make a film about science and technology for lay people, and while some attempts have drawn crowds and high ratings, most make terrible films. This one is no exception. While the film does get some facts and incidents correctly, as a whole it does not give an accurate portrayal of what actually happened.

From a scientific perspective the science was already done in 1938 by German Otto Strassmann and British Lise Mietner and their collaborators. There was nothing secret about their work. Thus the Manhattan Project, named because that's where the project started, was simply an engineering project comprising tens of locations and thousands of employees. Something like building the Panama canal or sending men to the moon. The big difference is that it worked the first try. Like other large government projects, it finished behind schedule and over budget. The war with Germany was over. If any single individual deserves credit it was General Leslie Groves, not Robert Oppenheimer. Oppenheimer's contribution was to get John Von Neumann involved and push his suggestions. Somehow von Neumann, the most important scientist, was left out of the film.

The scientists were around only to do calculations for the engineers and spent much of their time debating the ethics of the project as the film does show. Many felt their stay in Los Alamos was a waste of their time. Von Neumann used his spare time to invent the computer.

The main secret was whether the project was in fact happening and how it was going. The very existence of Los Alamos was denied by the government. But with all the people involved, many from Europe, it was hard to keep the secret. The Germans to the contrary had no people or locations working on their project and so it was easy to keep their secret. Further our people had reason to promote the idea that Germany was working on it to keep our project alive. The Germans were already so spread out with their war that they knew they didn't have the resources to compete and did nothing with their head start in nuclear theory. We have consistently underestimated Russian science but if they had not found out before we dropped the bomb they certainly did then and would have caught up. So the whole secrecy thing was mostly a red herring.

So basically, this film was a bunch of one liners and some irrelevant noises and graphics mixed in together in sort of a random order. This is not all realistic about how scientists actually talk and act. The producers no doubt hoped that their big budget would carry the film. Financially it worked.

If you want to see a good film about what people in technology do, see the film Sneakers (1992) with Robert Redford and Sidney Poitier. I actually gave extra credit to my students who reported on the real lecture given by the River Phoenix character.

6.title: Likeable to only irrational Nolan Fans...
6.content:
Do you know why Christopher Nolan has never won an Academy Award for Best Director, despite being nominated only once? It's because he is not a good director. His weird directing style leaves the characters and scenes underdeveloped and ambiguous. As a result, we cannot connect with the characters or the scenes. The many short scenes clearly depict the hurried and desperate direction. While Cillian Murphy's performance was great, all of the other actors were over-the-top smartasses, as we have seen in previous Nolan films.

Additionally, Nolan's stubbornness in not using CGI for the Trinity test was a bad decision. His "anti-CGI" approach ruined the film for many. CGI is meant to be used when we cannot do something in reality.

6.title: Christopher Nolan's odd choices ruined the movie once again
6.content:
I'm beginning to think that Nolan has self-esteem issues and desperately tries to prove how deep, special and different he is. Hey look! Non-linear structure of the story to confuse you! Deafening sound mixing to destroy your ears! And no CGI! Can you imagine that bro? A modern film with no CGI! That's how special Nolan tries to be! By the way, there is CGI in the movie. They just lie to him that it's all VFX compositing of photoreal elements.

Yet another movie with a non-linear narrative so confusing that I could only suspect what's going on without being certain. I walked out about 30 minutes before it ended and one friend who was considering to watch it asked for my opinion. I literally didn't know what to say initially: "It's about building the atomic bomb. That's basically it."

I said the same things in my review for Dunkirk (which is not really Dunkirk but soldiers standing on a beach like ghosts). The constant back and forth in time, along with the terrible sound mixing ruin what could have been a fantastic movie. If the project was headed by anyone else it could have been one of my favourite movies.

The explosion of the bomb was the only thing I enjoyed and we've all seen images of it online. I didn't have to pay for it. I know this was the last Nolan movie I paid for because he will always mess with the time and sound, desperately trying to appear edgy and special.

6.title: No. Behave. it's a complete action less slog.
6.content:
I'm a decent lover of history and knew this would be a slog. It was. Enjoyable for me cos I was into it. But 3 hours of pure torture for anyone who isn't.

Great performances from cillian and Robert but no. This is not a summer blockbuster

Unable to recommend to a cinema goer.

Nolan misses twice with as many films and his star is on the burnout. Gravity has taken over and it looks after tenet and this it's a black hole.

Not an enjoyable experience sitting there for 3 hours and questioning why he chose to attempt this story. Wasn't a good time.

Dunkirk and interstellar make me want to go to day one release of a nolan film.

This and tenet. No.

I won't rush back for his next. If you don't like history or courtroom dramas. Avoid.

6.title: Didn't hit on all notes for me this time
6.content: Huge Nolan fan but felt a bit letdown on this adaptation of storytelling. As expected the edit had you moving to different times frames of the story, but to a fault. Sometimes less is more. It felt too disjointed in the story telling for me. It wasn't taxing to follow along and know where you were at in the overall story arch for most of the movie but it was enough that it really distracted from the story itself. I'd be curious to see the post production edit process and understand the thought process that goes into Nolan's specific style of story telling. The score at times is distracting and takes away from the movie. Less is more. Let the weight of the acting and dialogue along with camera angles and edit push the tension needed. Pumping louder and louder violin and other music and sound does build tension but to me felt overdone and unnatural. It really distracted and took away from the acting which is a shame. The lensing of the film is pure magic and I soaked it all in at a showing in 70mm film. It felt the full 3 hours and had me checking my watch to see how much time was left. I've seen other 3 hour movies and felt disappointed in reaching the end to quickly. It will win awards and I give big kudos on the filming, tackling this story and the acting. I think the film could have used some lighter moments in both expressing joy and humor to balance and tug the audiences around. The nudity scenes didn't add to the story and the one was a bit uncomfortable which is what he was going for in the scene. I most likely won't be rewatching the film but am interested in leaning a bit more about the story.

6.title: Beyond the Bomb: A Realistic Assessment of 'Oppenheimer'
6.content:
'Oppenheimer' is indeed an intriguing movie with a constellation of A-list actors all delivering stellar performances. The title is aptly chosen as it is primarily a biopic that intricately charts Oppenheimer's life trajectory. It delves into his early interests in quantum mechanics, the genesis of the idea to create a bomb, his struggle for inclusion in the program due to his affiliations, and the painstaking process of assembling a team to actualize the bomb. The movie also depicts the only explosion he witnessed - the Trinity Test - and emphatically highlights that he was not present in Japan during the actual bombings. Most importantly, the movie poignantly portrays his post-war change of heart and his subsequent fight against the further development of atomic weapons.

Remembering that this is a biopic, not a war or science movie, is crucial when approaching 'Oppenheimer'. From this perspective, the movie indeed delivers. However, I'm rating it 6/10 rather than 10/10 due to several shortcomings.

Firstly, the trailer is somewhat misleading as it gives an impression of a movie primarily about the atomic bomb rather than Oppenheimer's life. This discrepancy could potentially misguide the audience's expectations. Secondly, the runtime of the movie feels excessive. There are portions that could have been trimmed down to achieve a smoother flow without sacrificing the narrative's complexity and detail. There were times when the pacing lagged, and I found myself checking the time, which detracted from the overall experience.

Thirdly, while the non-linear narrative style can be an effective tool for creating suspense and atmosphere, it can be confusing for those not well-versed in Oppenheimer's life. The lack of clear timestamps during the transitions between flashbacks and flash-forwards makes tracking the events challenging.

Lastly, I think the hype surrounding the movie is somewhat overblown. Currently, it stands at a 9/10, which in my opinion, overstates the movie's overall quality. By rating it a point lower, I hope to contribute to a more accurate representation of its value.

In summary, 'Oppenheimer' is a commendable biopic that could have been improved with clearer marketing, tighter editing, better chronological markers, and less hype.

6.title: Missed opportunity for his next film.
6.content:
I struggle to see why Nolan chose to make this film over anything else. I'm a big Nolan fan, but feel cheated as this film has been completely over hyped. Good performances, but it's very difficult to follow as it keeps jumping. Yes technically it's great and got great reviews, but have the reviews been based on the film or the past record of the director. It this didn't have Nolan's name attached to it would it have really been given 5/5. My friends and myself felt completely underwhelmed by this film and it is too long.

For all the hype, it turned more into a courtroom drama. I'm glad I didn't waste my money and watch it at the Imax and just went to a normal cinema.

MI7 was way better than this. An important subject, but something any other director could have picked up.

6.title: Maybe I am not a Nolan fan
6.content:
Watched a video on YouTube by veritasium about the man and the subject before going to see the movie. The video was more informative and entertaining to me than the movie. We actually go through some technical details and challenges the scientists had to go through.

The movie on the other hand focused way too much about gossip and pity things that shallow people around the man and the project were saying or doing. How many affairs he had, which were numerous for a scientist, but didn't really focus on the bomb or technical challenges they had.

It's like seeing a heist movie with the heist cut out. Or a sports movie without showing parts of the matches.
