Didn't really focus on his internal struggles before making the bomb, and very little afterwards. There were a couple of scenes with stylized visual effects, but wasn't most of what the movie focused on.

Movie didn't explain or focus on why the famous Indian quote was important. It was mentioned a couple of times but It didn't focus enough on it or his thoughts the day before the test in my opinion.

The movie was too busy trying to be a complete biopic, that it didn't have time to focus on the project. There is a lot of surface level references all over the place but very little substance.

6.title: Three hours I can't get back.
6.content:
The film is very dense and technical, and it can be difficult to follow the plot if you are not familiar with the history of the Manhattan Project.

The film is very slow-paced, and there is not a lot of action or excitement.

The film is very talky, and there are a lot of long scenes of people talking about physics and philosophy.

The film is very long and it can be difficult to sit through for three hours.

The film focuses primarily on Oppenheimer's work on the Manhattan Project, and there is relatively little time spent on his relationships with his family and friends.

Overall, while Oppenheimer is a well-made film with some impressive performances, it is ultimately a flawed and disappointing work. The film's slow pacing, dense dialogue, and lack of emotional resonance.

6.title: Simultaneously morally corrupt and boring. Lacks complexity.
6.content: 6/10 simply due to the incredible acting performances all around. However, the premise of the movie is just so hilariously tone deaf and ridiculous in my eyes, and I'm surprised others don't feel the same. The movie is simply romanticizing something evil. And I'd understand if there was some depth, complexity, or nuance of any kind attached to this. Many movies involve characters that can be considered morally ambiguous, that provoke discussion. But there really is none here. Cillian Murphy's whole character arc is as simple as this: "I make bomb, it kill people, I regret it". That's the extent of it. Christopher Nolan and his team attempt to make this incredibly mundane arc seem profound using all sorts of vfx, sound effects, flashbacks, etc. But it just doesn't work. To me in many ways, this movie is a spiritual successor to "American Sniper". If the third reich had been successful in world war 2, they'd make movies like these. Just ridiculous.

6.title: Will never watch this again! Why?
6.content:
Two reasons I will never watch this again:

1. This is sooooo long and had so much talking! If I want a history lesson, I'd read a book!!! It can be soo boring, the first 30 minutes are USELESS to this story and movie.

2. They never mentioned this:

Tina Cordova is a sixth-generation New Mexican, hailing from a village of nearly 3,000 people an hour's drive downwind from the Trinity site. It's a community that has been fighting for decades to get recognition from the United States government about the Trinity test and compensation for millions of dollars-perhaps billions-in medical bills as locals have battled radiation-induced cancers for generations, stemming from the first nuclear test in New Mexico and dozens more above-ground tests in Nevada.

Nolan can go f himself, and his movie!

6.title: I'm tired
6.content: The acting in this movie is insane. Absolutely incredible. Everyone. The plot and the dialogue is too much. It's all over the place. I frequently had to ask my friend what somebody said. I found myself zoning out when they would talk. I felt like I had 3 hours of elevated heart rate. It's a good movie with a lot of impact, but it felt a little lost to me. I also wish it put a heavier emphasis on the impact of what the bomb actually did in total vs. What it did to the men involved, however, I understand that was not the main purpose of the plot. I'm not a history or physics buff, so I had a hard time digesting this movie. Overall, it did bring a lot of awareness to what has happened and the people involved. Grateful for that, but I am not recommending this for everybody.

6.title: I got the Nolan Chills, but was honestly was kinda bored
6.content:
I love Christopher Nolan, Inception might be my favorite movie of all time. But honestly this was just kinda boring and I wasn't super interested in the story. My roommate loved it but I miss when Nolan was doing more interesting fiction.

There was far less of the after effects of the bombing shown than I expected, and I was overall disappointed with how low budget this film seemed. I miss the action or at least interest and supernatural intensity and wonder Nolan has accomplished alongside the intellectual rollercoaster in his 2010's films. This was just kind of a documentary, gave me similar vibes to that McDonald's Founder film or First Man, though without any of the action First Man had. Not that I can't appreciate a movie without action, that's just something I miss how Nolan does, and was overall just bored with this movie.

6.title: Wrong focus and unnecessary non linear story telling
6.content:
I had high expectations but was disappointed. The performances are good.

But the story becomes too much about him and not about the Manhattan project.

The non linear story telling really spoils the rhythm and tempo of the Manhattan project.

The story of the project itself is more interesting but it has gotten sidelined.

In a sense Nolan tries so hard to keep you at the edge of your seat, by all the non linear story, you actually feel bored. Yes the movie drags!

It really depends on what you want from the movie.

Do you want a straightforward narrative that explains the chronology and challenges of the Manhattan project? Or do you care more about the thoughts and concerns and emotional issues and values and tribulations of Oppy with some of the chronology and issues of the project thrown in?

I would have liked the former. Hence I feel "Fat man and little boy" starring Paul Newman is a more interesting story. That story focuses on the project and also the various characters associated with the project. Though even in that movie Oppy has a central role, the project really is the centerpiece. Here the project does not get as much of the focus it deserves.

It leaves you wanting.

6.title: Disturbingly downplaying the drama behing the nuclear weapon
6.content:
The movie barely represents the Hiroshima and Nagasaki drama. Being at Hiroshima and visiting the museum I was shocked to see some depictions with the aftermath of such a horrendous act.

Briefly showing the internal struggle in Oppenheimer's head regarding the morality of it and focusing more on the politics and on the romanticized meetings is unacceptable. For sure, Oppenheimer had nightmares about the bombs, but instead we are seeing some flashbacks and a carbonized body. That is it! Nothing else.

Half of the movie is pointless, nobody cares about how Oppenheimer was discredited in the public for being a spy or that his clearance was dropped. Everybody cares about the horror of creating and using of such an absurdly overpowered weapon.

6.title: I've never fast forwarded a movie before this
6.content: Insanely disappointed in a movie that should've captured me from start to finish. The premise of the movie led me to believe that a lot more science and physics would be involved, as opposed to just talking about it. Also don't know how I'm supposed to be interested in a story with 700 characters and be expected to follow along. It was a really bad angle on a something that should've been much more interesting. Silver lining is definitely the acting but overall, I would never watch this again and it is definitely not Christopher Nolan's best work. If you have 3 hours to kill give it a watch, if not don't bother.

6.title: Better watch "Parmanu: The Story of Pokhran" or "Rocketry the Nambi Effect" in IMAX
6.content:
I have been a lover of Nolan's movies since my childhood and have developed feelings that "whatever topic that he touches, converts into a gold". He has proven that, be it Dunkirk, Batman Trio or even Tenet. But this time, he has done a weak job.

Now, don't get me wrong, I have seen many documentries and I understand that this movie is not for everyone, it needs "patience" to watch. I have been with many movies which includes only onversations and are well made... but this... doesn't give the feelings which one would need to "feel" the Oppenhiemer's character. It could have been made much better.

Firstly, we expect in any biographical movie, it would give some background to the character. Here, it doesn't even start from his childhood (even though it is a long 3 hour movie). There are many events that could be told about Robert J. Oppenhiemer. How he got interested in Physics, how his friends bullied him when, how he suffered emotionally when achieved success and many parts of his life would have given a great depth of his character, but back to back to back to back close up shots and him thinking makes not sense most of the time.

The movie mostly is around Oppenhiemer's interrogation with his involvement in the Manhattan project. Many characters have been selected brilliantly, especially Einsten's and Oppnhiemer's himself are well casted.

The way to movie was marketed, the way there was a hype "a perfect cinematic experience", "a perfect IMAX movie" were totally non-sense. This movie can simply be seen in any typical movie theatre. There is the conversation! Except one or two blast sequences, you wouldn't miss a thing that may make you wish that could be seen in IMAX.

If Robert was deeply enchanted by Bhagvad Gita, then it could be some "serious" scene where he is reading Bhagvad Gita and it is deeply impacting him in his hard times or whatever, but instead have shown during a cheap s*x scene! This is not the Nolan whom I knew!

See "Rocketry the nambi effect" or even "Parmanu: The Story of Pokhran", I would say "they are worth watching in IMAX!".

Anyways, the good things are: Acting. It is fabulous. Of each, single, character. The sound design, perfect. It is much much effective, in many scenes. The cinematography, oh my! Just lack in the storytelling and storyline.

Seems like Nolan picked up a story, "tried" to add some tweaks like black and white and IMAX and expected it to be the Nolan level great, but this time it isn't, as far as what I felt.

I tried to give my honest review, even though it is Nolan, it is not he best film of his career, it could have been much better. Hope, next time he would come up with his "originals"!

Seriously missing the 2010-15 times where we were getting his back to back masterpieces!

6.title: Overrated- better history documentaries in YouTube
6.content:
This movie is the perfect example of the Emperor's New Clothes tale made movie... Aside from perfect acting and good editing it lacks the most important thing in art, heart!, it tries so hard to be genius just like the character it's based on, but just like him it does not have any wisdom and more important, it does not prove to be an entertaining movie with a significant and central message, in Other words is not special at least not to be called a masterpiece

save yourself the time sitting in a movie theater and watch it at home by episodes while your are folding clothes, it is war movie without the excitement of the genre and the moral implications of the decisions taken by a few that affect millions

If you want a better and nore shocking bio pic watch the story of Ray Kroc and McDonalds performed by Michael Keaton.

6.title: Great story badly put together
6.content: The overall plot is obviously great and interesting, however that isn't exactly a praise for the film as that is purely owing to the great historical value of the development of the atomic bomb. The delivery of the dialogue is largely mumbled and very quiet in comparison to the over use of the background music. The whole sound of the film varys largely from super quiet to loud thudding background noise making it hard to watch. The nude scences in the movie are completely unnecessary and add absolutely nothing to the plot besides being explicit in a highly unsexy way. Overall an interesting film but could have been a lot better as most characters lack any level of emotion.

6.title: Decent biography movie, but overrated and overhyped.
6.content:
To be honest, i watch this movie yesterday at IMAX cinema. But find it disappointing with the bombing scene only "just like that"? I can have better visualization in Discovery Channel or National Geographic or other in Youtube. It is to much exaggerate the Kodak 70mm feature in this movie, while 4/5 of all movie duration wasting on the discussion, court scene, and talking session. I must be honest, what for the IMAX or Kodak 70mm for this movie?

And most of half duration movie is debating about he is communist of not? So tired. Whilst the bombing in Hiroshima and Nagasaki is not even seen.

This movie is overrated and overhyped. It is decent biography movie, but don't exaggerate it to much.

Special appreciation to Cillian Murphy who try his best to live up the character, and also for the Einstein.

6.title: Overhyped costume drama
6.content:
Film well made. I guess. Costume and acting. Directing too. Music was totally anonymous. More annoying than anything. The rest was ...meh!

I loved Murphy since 28 Days Later and he is always just amazing.

Movie itself is quite boring. I almost fell asleep two times. And I also had two breaks to get some motivation back. I didn't really care of the characters or the plot. Also, it was a little bit confusing at times. Or maybe just uninteresting...

So I'll give this a 6 for it isn't a 5. But certainly NOT over a 6. I just watched The Sinner season 3 on Netflix an was extremely more interesting. So to conclude, I rather watch 4 hours The Sinner then 3 hours of Oppenheimer.

6.title: Overrated. Disappointing and not Nolan's best film.
6.content: Incredibly overrated. Disjointed and was all over the place in my opinion. It's long and boring, the first half more so, the second half picks up but still a movie you'll only ever watch once. I didn't think the casting was great either with some odd choices. I thought Matt Damon was good. Disappointing, but I am sure it's a film critics will love but not so much the general paying public. I'm sure the movie will win many awards but as mentioned I felt some of the roles were miscast. Stylish but at times hard to follow and hard to stay awake if I'm being totally honest. There are many positive reviews but for me this film was too long, too boring and a big let down. Watch a documentary instead as I think it would be far more entertaining and educational.

6.title: I was not entertained
6.content:
I'm sorry to bring the ratings down, but I was not entertained.

I guess if I were only looking at its artistic value, acting & visual beauty, I would have given Oppenheimer a 10. However, movies are supposed to entertain and I had to watch this over 3 separate sittings just to get through it. At times, it was incredibly boring.

The writers tried to get clever by centering the story around an inquiry that occurred after the atom bomb was dropped. I was less interested in this inquiry and for such an expensive production, I would have preferred to see more about the dropping of the bomb. I mean, isn't that what Oppenheimer is famous for, developing a bomb that wiped out an entire city? The actual event itself felt so rushed in the movie, but scenes of mindless dialogue took centre stage.

A great movie can be incredibly simple. Stop trying to be clever. Watch a French or Italian movie. They are incredibly real, to the point where you feel like you're watching your own family interact. Hollywood is becoming devoid of anything real, because they constantly change the formula, away from the winning formula that made it great. I have found myself watching old classics from the 80s and 90s more and more. I struggle to sit through a modern Hollywood production.

Oppenheimer was a decent movie, but not something I would ever watch again.

6.title: A failed chain reaction!
6.content:
Disappointed and surprised that a movie from Nolan could be this poor.


Lot of details crammed in to a movie which lost its focus. These days you can make a series to explore themes, character development etc. If your are making a movie stick to a theme(I know I am nobody compared to a genius like Nolan and thats why it is very surprising that he would make such a terrible movie)


IMO after watching a serious movie it should stay in your psyche for sometime and it should not be easy to shake it off. This failed that test by a huge margin for me.


There were really only 2 good scenes which showed the glimmer of Nolan's true talent. First one, where Oppenheimer makes a speech to the scientists/colleagues after the bombing where his dichotomy is shown. Second one is the final scene, the conversation with Einstein.


Cilian Murphy's acting is really good and Emily Blunt(even though she has very few scenes) is good. The rest of star studded cast(Gary Oldman, Kenneth Branagh, Rami Malek, Florence Pugh) was really un-necessary IMO. It had been better to have had lesser know actors in those roles since they were just 1-dimensional and not meaty enough. Using famous actors just raised my expectations just to be deflated later.


Depiction of Richard Feynman was a big joke and degrading. Why even show him if you are not even having him part of any anectdote. Just him and his bongos seemed like a cheapshot gimmick.


The themes as far as I could perceive was the clash of principles, patriotism, values, a supposed hero seen as a villain(shades of Batman), guilt; how being sensitive, intelligent is very complex in extraordinary situations; ultimately the question of clash of science, human curiosity, fun/search of knowledge vs the realities of misuse of the products of science(which currently has manifested as AI related issues). There was so much potential to explore these themes philosophically, emotionally, morally and as an existential question. But the movie got lost in biographical, historical mini details. It tried to grab too much and failed to hang on to any by the end.


Hope Nolan realises this was a poor movie. He should stop pandering to hollywood superficialities. Go back to his roots of story telling he displayed in movies like memento. All the technical hoo-hah cannot compensate for a good tsory with heart and honesty..

6.title: Biggest Nolan fan, ultimately dissapointed
6.content: After letting the movie marinate in my head for some time, i am dissapointed with it. Plain and simple. I am the biggest Nolan fan (Inception, Interstellar and TDK are in my top 5 all time), and this, plus the fact that almost everyone seems to be putting this movie through the roof, made me go in with more hype than i've had in a long time. Unfortunately, the movie is not what i expected. Not by a long shot. As a big fan of history, plus anything to do with atomic bombs/nuclear power, and everything the trailers led us to believe, i thought Nolan would create a fast paced, time distorted story around some of my favorite topics. Instead, time distorting is what i felt in the last hour of the movie, as it felt as though time was standing still and the movie dragged on until the end. The reason for this is that Nolan focuses 90% of this 3 hour movie on the events outside the creation of the bomb, with long drawn out court/interrogation scenes, making this feel more like a Strauss vs Oppenheimer than about the story of the father of the atomic bomb. For context, i love great dialogue in movies/TV. But this was too much and not interesting enough. The black and white honestly didnt land either. Also, after hearing for months about the explosion scene that Nolan created with no CGI, hearing him say this needed to be seen in Imax, hearing how this movie was gonna be a mindblowing display of sound/visuals, left me all the more dissapointed when the explosion scene lasted no more than 10 minutes. At first when it ended i thought, surely we will see more of it with the bombings of Japan, but no. That was it. Was the point of seeing it in Imax, only for those 10 (albeit great) minutes of the explosion scene? There is no need for Imax for 3 hours of dialogue. I also heard several people in th early screenings talk about a "horror" theme to this movie. Maybe those people had just finished watching Barbie and were not being objective. This movie did not have horror themes at all. It barely explores Oppenheimer's feelings after the bombs are released. Instead we see the final hour with more of Strauss vs Oppie. Let me also give some credit where its due. The cinematography, the sound, and the acting were great. Its what we expect of Nolan. But when you strip away all those things and look at only the story, its not great, instead its quite boring. Looking only at the story, i could have been fooled into thinking this was a documentary movie on netflix. Perhaps its on me, for going in with such high expectations for a Nolan movie. If you haven't seen it yet, lower your expectations.

6.title: Dramatic film, but dissonant backround score very distracting
6.content:
Overly long, dramatic content, excellent make-up artistry, but I was continually distracted and irritated by the almost non-stop, over-dramatic, too often dissonant musical score.

Why??

A solid, non-musical should moves on its own. Music is spice, not the meat. Here, it is over-the-top and only distracts.

As in a great piece of music, no note can be added, or taken away, without affecting the overall quality. Not that this is a masterpiece. But she same concept should apply.

Additionally, and wholly unnecessary, are the sudden depictions of explosions--like cheap scares--when characters are discussing possible nuclear reactions.

6.title: Non popular opinion: its a solid 6
6.content:
If you take out all the hype and all the famous actor. The movie its just a 6. Good sounds, good camera. But the movie itself its not the best Christopher Nolan movie, so my best bet its that the hype its just a popular opinion affected by the hype of everyone and all the actors involed.

As a Christopher Nolan movie, i was waiting some more action or at least a recreation of the bomb at Japan. But not even that.

Also the movie its a bit too long. Probably they can cut like 20 min of the movie and the result would have been the same.

I hope people read this to not go to see the movie with a big hype.

6.title: A movie that falls short of the mark
6.content: Bearing in mind the length of this movie, I was expecting it to be riveting. But I have to admit I only barely got the gist of what was going on for the entire 3 hours. This was I think in part because of the amount of different characters who were inadequately introduced and also due to the continual flipping from one timeline to the next. Also, some insignificant parts of Oppenheiner's life were unnecessarily detailed, while other more major events were inadequately explained or glossed over, making it confusing and difficult for the the viewer to connect emotionally with his story in some way, which might have made this movie more more engaging. Having said that, there were definitely some very good scenes and dialogues which showed glimpses of the blockbuster this movie could have been, but it just didn't quite live up to it's potential and for the most part it was boring, confusing, political, and not really much more than a documentary.

6.title: great acting in general but ultimately gets lost without it a heart called Jonathan Nolan
6.content:
I've read a few reviews on here so far...it seems that no matter what Nolan does they will give 10... and others who hate Nolan films because of the annoying fan boys...the fun is somewhat in between.

I like most of Nolan's films, I enjoyed Interstellar, inception, the dark Knights, momento and the prestige...I'm generally a fan most 8-10/10 movies and on par with Spielberg's, Scorsese's etc. He's very good and up there with the modern greats.

However... his last 3 movies whilst technically great have been so/so...Dunkirk was a borefest done better elsewhere, though technically brilliant...Tenet...I enjoyed more and actually liked the time/dimension flipping etc but ultimately it never welded together as a top movie (the sound was unbearable) and this...Oppenheimer.

Firstly...the good bits...cinematography is stellar as is the score both very accomplished and probably Oscar worthy.

The acting universally is superb, I see Cillian Murphy getting a nomination and Robert Downey Jnr winning most awards ceremonies...the support cast is also very good.

The middle bomb test is very good and I though it was very restrained in truth, I expected a bit more technical wizardry but was happy it was fairly restrained.

There are some wonderful moments of imitate acting at times, in small pockets that really resonate...the Einstein bits with Tom Conti are well done, as is the intimate scenes with Florence Pugh who again is very good.

The bad bits...

It's a logistical mess, the running time wouldn't be such problem if it was sequenced properly...the flow isn't one you can warm to...and for the live of god I actually went back and watched segments again. I think the narrative was just off...it started chatty and slow. I think he jumps here there and everywhere instead of having 3 solid acts as such. Fan boys will say he's pushing the boundaries or something silly but I've watched slow films and enjoyed them massively, tinker Taylor for example.

I don't think Chris Nolan is anywhere near as good without his brother Jonathan pulling the story and script together...and this is the problem with his last 3 films...he's the visionary, his brother is the heart and that's what's missing...the last 3 movies are COLD..technical and visually brilliant, good acting etc but they try to cover over the massive void where the heart should have been.

All of his earlier films with his brother writing interweaved brilliant warmth and heart strings throughout...the love stories in the prestige, the family strings in interstellar, Leo and Marion in inception, Rachael, albert and Lucius in the dark knight...

It's not a bad film no where near but it's not a masterpiece...

Biopics are hard to do well, I watched JFK recently which maybe is comparable, and it's not got the visual brilliance but what it does well is draw you in, it's got emotion...I felt Oppenheimer lacked just that...emotion except Downey Jnr who was really exceptional ...as normal

6/10.

6.title: Perhaps I my hopes were set too high
6.content:
I mean any film that gets an 8.5 (current rating) should be exceptional but I found the movie fell flat. None of the characters really moved me. I really wanted to but didn't care what happened to any of them by the end of the film. I came away caring about as much as Oppie and Kitty cared for their kid. The characters all felt pretty flat.

The only exception might be Matt Damon who played the commanding General. I somewhat liked his character but even in the end didn't feel contributed much to the story.

I suppose you could say Robert Downey Jr. Pulled off the politician and you were not supposed to come away liking him but I thought there was no way he would have put up with his aid chastising him and getting away with it.

I don't think it's s spoiler to say the film is about the effort to develop the nuclear bombs that were dropped on Japan. The film goes a long way to say it wasn't necessary as Japan was all but beaten. But it makes mockery about the decision the president and men who were directing the war. Yes this felt very much like the makers of the film were trying to play into the modern blame game to shame the US for having used the weapon. They went to great lengths to explain why it wasn't necessary and only touched lightly on the arguments for using the bomb.

I really tried to like this film but in the end it just let me indifferent. I am giving it a positive score of 6 for now as it did have it's moments. And perhaps the overall effect they were going for was to show how uncaring these people were. If that was their point, then it is well done. But one would hope you would have some feeling towards the characters in the end. This film didn't make nearly as much impression as I had hoped. I think Oppenheimer was probably much more interesting than this depiction of him.

6.title: Underwhelmingly Lacking in Nolanism
6.content:
This movie failed to captivate me, although it has potential. Nolan was able to justify the long run time, I don't think the movie is stuffed with fillers or unnecessary scenes. The story is rich and it has historical significance. If anything I can easily imagine a miniseries that goes into even more depth, exploring more of the many characters' background or delving into the science more. The pace also was fairly tolerable, I didn't particularly feel bored. I think the main problem, however, is that the movie feels bland. All this buildup, but in the end the climax felt weirdly lacking.

I think there are multiple reasons for this. Firstly, the expectations and the hype for the movie pushed me to expect more than there was. Secondly, the effects felt forced, almost cartoonish. I know Nolan prides himself over the lack of CGI, although I don't think that is inherently a selling point for a good movie. Essentially, I don't care how effects are generated, but whether they are good or not. The swirling circuits, orbits and random shapes that plague Oppenheimer's imagination look kind of stupid most of the time. Compared to Nolan's stunning aesthetics for Interstellar, mind-bending design of Inception and the simple yet haunting use of rewinds and fast forwards in Tenet, this movie is nothing. Thirdly, I think that the focus of the movie is not fully developed. Beyond the individual characters, we don't actually delve fully into the war. We are consistently told what is happening right now in the war or what just happened but we don't even get to experience anything from the Japanese perspective. I understand the reasons for doing this and loyalty to the original text, but this justification is not a solid one. The book never intended to be a global phenomenon, it's simply a biography. This movie, however, is definitely made with an international audience in mind, so it is a perfect opportunity to explore the difficult question of atomic warfare. A discussion of a crime that doesn't include the main victim seems kind of ignorant at best, and an abhorrent injustice at worst.

I did enjoy some scenes, the dialogue, and I think the psychological tone of the movie was satisfying. I also fully support science communication for it can inspire people into STEM careers and education. However, the saving grace of the movie is the acting, particularly Robert Downey Jr. Who might have delivered his best performance so far. Honestly, I just have come to experience more from Nolan. More entertainment, exploration of radical ideas and epic narratives is the currency that this director deals with. In my opinion, I think that this is his most underwhelming work.

6.title: Highly over-rated.
6.content:
Indeed, as the title says, I feel this film is highly over-rated.

The first hour was excessively long and most of it felt useless in the (3 hour) long run. I felt absolutely no attachment to his mistress or his wife, nor did i care about the conflict that caused between any of the characters, because there was absolutely no time spent actually developing those relationships, just exposition followed by a scene with unnecessary music, trying to trick your brain into thinking this is way more epic than it is.

And yes. The music. There are probably less than ten minutes in this entire film without music in the background. I find it laughable that this won best score. The film is a series of short clips with fanciful shots and unnecessary rising and falling music that do ultimately connect to tell a story, but the story is present in a way that never really connects with the audience in any serious manner. There's no real connection to any of the characters- not even really oppenheimer himself.

And downey won best supporting actor for this? Give me a break. It was a hack job that anyone could have done, and he didnt even really do it all that well, for him. Just kind of phoning it in. Yes. I'm downey. I'm here. Im playing a corrupt politician, and I'm excited about it, I guess.

It did start picking up nicely once the espionage elements and los alamos got running, but between an overly long beginning, and a poorly edited, rushed (literally a 3 hour movie and the director and editor managed to make the ending feel slopped together) climax, it's a pretty big letdown. Murphy acted it well, but just like with downey, there wasnt much to it. Stand there. Look off into th distance like youre contemplating the universe. Never press stop on the music box. Give a line or two. Cut scene. Repeat.

Could have been great, but pretty mediocre.

6.title: Ok movie but Christopher Nolan now started cursing God
6.content:
The movie was interesting.. story line mainly rotates around how humans social structure works and how politicians manipulate to get a step forward.

I was not "in" as like watching Blade Runner 2049, where my eyes were wide opened to not miss anything.

It was good, but I doubt I'll watch it again.

It's also said how the military wants to create a bomb out of everything and the American's idea "Destroy first and ask questions later" really comes out.

Unfortunatelly there are also lines cursing God, which were not needed at all. The lines didn't give any new information and it even felt that the lines were forcefully added.. just to push some kind of agenda. It's unfortunate as this shows that even Christopher Nolan started to fall. It's really sad how Hollywood is destroying everything that is good.

6.title: Good premise and strong message, but choppy and strung out..
6.content: Good premise and strong message, but 100 jump cuts and strung out character interviews unfortunately jade the explosive nature of the movie. Great biopic story build-up and general pace for the race against the Nazis and development of the atomic bomb. An allstar cast combined with some great cinematography helped show off modern day movie making capability. However, the last 1/3 of the movie was almost a waste of time, with the exception of the carrot stick Einstein ending. My partner genuinely fell asleep on my shoulder, during the endless questioning of every character in this movie, about what they thought of openhiemer and his connection to communism... Yawn. Many hidden layers and messages in this film which I enjoyed. Many hidden character hidden motives come to light which were mildy interesting. Score was ok.. Although there is no epic tune sticking my head, unlike interstellar or moon for example. Overall I think this movie is a bit overhyped, with people heavily praising Christopher Nolan without justification, definitely not his best work. Cillian Murphy does give a stellar performance... But there's only so many scenes I can take of him staring off-center in conflicting thought. It gets a bit repetitive and 3 hours seemed uneccessary for this story. Overall a good watch if you have interest in the creation of nuclear weapons and particularly the 'opi' man himself. Leave the cinema halfway if you don't enjoy politics and interviews and comi bashing. 6/10.

6.title: Doesn't live upto it's hype
6.content: I watched this movie after so much hype. Realised it's not meant to entertain. It's a typical confusing Nolan movie with good acting and direction, but 30 minutes into the film, you end up wondering when will it all start to make sense. Am I the only one in the room who's too stupid to understand it, or is it not meant to be understood. There are many many characters and you're automatically assumed to know all of them. Most of the footage is spent on reminding the audience that Oppenheimer was a communist supporter. There were reports that the audience cried in a scene. I don't know which scene made people cry, I couldn't find one.

6.title: All over the place.
6.content: Maybe I need to watch this again. But for the life of me, I can't help but fail to understand how so many reviewers gave it a 10 rating and waxed poetic over the incredible brilliance of this film. Being a card-carrying nerd, and a fan of the director, was so looking forward to thus movie. It sounded like something that I would really enjoy. Instead I was, frankly, rather bored and disappointed. The plot jumped around seemingly not knowing how to form any kind of cohesion; the dialogue was rather jumbled and difficult to follow; and three hours of all this got old very fast. The only part that was very spell-binding was the actual detonation of the first bomb, and a movie like this shouldn't depend on blowing things up to be captivating. Well, I'll probably watch it again and give it another chance, if I think I want to try to risk sitting through another only mildly interesting three hours.

6.title: A Michael Bay movie for people with too much self regard.
6.content:
Honestly, Oppenheimer is a bit of a mess. It jumps back and forth between multiple timelines at a frantic pace. It uses constant music and sound effects that could be best described as noise. The visual effects are sometimes a little strange and abstract. The nudity is pretty gratuitous, I guess because a prestige picture can't be rated PG13. All of this might be tolerable in a shorter movie, but Oppenheimer makes you sit around for three whole hours.

It's pretty clear that Christopher Nolan was trying to turn Robert Oppenheimer's life into an intense political/psychological thriller. And I can imagine how a filmmaker might actually do that. But Nolan just uses a bunch of cheap tricks. If his name was Michael Bay, we would laugh at this movie. But people need to feel smart, so we have to pretend that Oppenheimer isn't just three tedious and obnoxious hours of nothing much at all.

6.title: Slow and ponderous
6.content:
Thought this liked like it would be good. However, it wasn't really. I've been quite generous giving it a 6. Mainly for the acting.

The story was slow and jumped about timelines too much.

Lost interest and nodded off halfway through for 10 mins. Don't think I missed much.

I can't really recommend this unless you are a real history geek. That's just about the only reason you would want you watch it.

I though there would be more action and details about the making of the bomb. It just seemed more about how Oppenheimer seems to have initially been blamed for creating the bomb. The detail was very sparse.

Overall a boring film.

6.title: Mediocre misuse of concept for a historical film
6.content:
Dunkirk was such an extraordinary film visually and in the the story telling, so appreciately not overly sentimental or jingoistic. Oppenheimer, in contrast was just not that appealing and certainly less than the sum of its many many parts and ultimately is a disservice to the extraordinary moment which brought together so many extraordinary people together for better or worse in The Manhattan Project. As many others have stated this film was overhyped as something that must be seen on the biggest screen possible, preferably IMAX. For one absent one scene and a few 30 second cuts, there's nothing so requiring that type of scale. It's largely an office drama with an identity crisis. Sadly enough also, just oscar clickbait because this really wastes opportunities to delve into the imaginative scientific minds, the think tanks at Princeton, University of Chicago, UT-Knoxville, Bay area Universities, the strong european tradition that most of Manhattan Projects braintrust came from, or Oppenheimer's own personal upbringing, anything to reveal what made the subject tick and become the leader of such a weighty doomsday project. It also wasted the resource of an amazing amount of acting talent to no point. For despite everything that occurs in three hours the impression you are left with is that somehow the point of all of this is to produce The Richard Strauss Show by way of several minutes of Florence Pugh being provocatively naked and intellectual randomly with great lighting and makeup.

I bought the high art hype long enough to be intrigued at where we may could have traveled cinematically from the 'I am become Death, Destroyer of Worlds' from sanskrit portion of the show. But that happens in a different iteration of time from this, where Pugh's occasional nudity becomes arbitrarily exploitative for it's deliberate randomness, like so many other scenes. I feel sorry for viewers of this movie that know little or nothing of the science and political history of the Manhattan Project. They will be bewildered for no good reason, might just conclude that this was another elitist hollywood film rather just a poorly executed piece of cinematic storytelling.

6.title: It didn't match my expectations.
6.content:
It felt like a very long trailer, not a movie. I don't think there is a conversation in the movie for more than a few minutes. Every scene wants to have you surprised, and honestly, it felt ridiculous after a while. Disappointing storyline. It rather failed to depict Oppenheimer as a real person and scientist. Nolan pictured him as an absolute hero. The conversation around quantum physics and nuclear physics in the movie was a bit shallow and short. There are a lot of great movies and series based on the work of real scientists, such as A beautiful mind, Chernobyl, or Imitation Game which explain their research and achievements with a simplified language for the audience and build the movie around that. The movie was very nationalistic and patriarchal. Just because he's American, there is a notion in the movie that he was the best in his field then. At the time that Einstein, Planck, Schrödinger, and Heisenberg were alive. And the most frustrating part was the representation of women. Drunk, mentally unstable, and angry at all times. It became a pattern in Nolan's movies, I think. All his main characters are men surrounded by dozens of more men. Usually, put one or two women at most in them.

The acting was terrific, and almost all of the cast did a fantastic job. I really enjoyed the music; however, it was three hours of non-stop music.

6.title: disappointing.
6.content: As with all of Nolan's films, it looks gorgeous and has a great caliber of actors on screen. However, i can't help but notice a few things that are getting worse with Nolan's films. The first is his pointless convoluting of the story. Please just give me something more linear. It does not automatically make you look smart treating your story like its an enigma code waiting to be cracked by the viewer. There were many moments in this film where i had no idea what point in the time the scene was set. The second is his preference for the score over the actors dialogue. There were moments in this film where we had intense action music really loud just for people talking. Please Chris just let me hear the actors and appreciate their performance. I really don't get it. It seems like an issue 80% of people have watching his recent films and the guys just doubles down on it. A final issue was the song and dance made about how zero CGI was used for the bomb, yet the most interesting shot of this, which i assume was meant to show the atom splitting, was shown for about 5 seconds right at the start of the film. The bomb test itself did not use any more of this footage and was anti climatic as i really didn't think the shots were that spectacular at all.

6.title: headache
6.content:
Well played by actors, ruined by the constant sound and music, let me tell you that i had a headache after the movie.

Constant jumping between past and future, litterally every 5 minutes is just too much for me.

Good sides:
you can learn something from such movies.


well played by actors


The bad side:






Overall good movie, but the way that is presented can give you headache, especially if you are in the cinema.

6.title: Make sure you get a good night's sleep the night before viewing.
6.content:
Not sure if I was sleep deprived but I found the film somewhat grating. The score was great but relentless and too loud, it was hard to decipher the dialogue. The shots were very short and choppy. There was a lot of dialogue, so much so that it required an exorbitant amount of focus and got tiring very quickly. I understand the reason why they didn't depict the bombings on Japan as the film did not wish to glorify the bombings in any way. Running length was far too long.

The psychological evaluation of Oppenheimer was very astute. The film reads as more of a psychological study of his mind and involves a lot of courtroom drama (he said, she said type of stuff). It is not an action film or even a historical biopic in my opinion.

6.title: Oppenheimer is Overrated
6.content: Christopher Nolan is a great filmmaker, but not many directors are admired as much as Zack Snyder. Nolan, known for working without co-writers, wrote and directed Oppenheimer. The movie explores the life of a complex man seen differently by the public and those close to him. With strong acting from Cillian Murphy, less impressive performance by Emily Blunt, an Oscar-worthy role by Robert Downey Jr, and a solid turn by Matt Damon, Oppenheimer's storytelling is unnecessarily complex, jumping between color and black-and-white scenes. While praised for recreating an atomic bomb test with practical effects, the three-hour film feels distant and not as good as it's hyped to be.

6.title: Technically perfect boring documentary
6.content:
Oppenheimer is about technical perfection, there's no denying it. Visuals are just incredible, acting is great, music, sets, costumes... all magnificent.

But nothing can save long and boring script with endless overly complex debates that add barely anything to the story.

I chose this higher rating only because of the technical perfection and because it is an important story people should know about, but it really doesn't work well as a movie. And the shockingly loud sound effects trying to compensate for the lack of a good script won't save it.

The making of is a different category. It's much better than the movie itself.

6.title: different one from Nolan
6.content:
Unusual biographical drama from the genius director.

Watching it felt very unusual as it didn't feel like watching a biography but more like watching a drama with twists & turns, though most of it is driven through the courtroom drama with some turning elements sprinkled over it, it is really tough to grasp and hard to understanding due to Nolan's usual non-linear screenplay though that's the only way to keep the audience engaged.

Most of the film is just dialogue driven instead of visualizations except the portrayal of what's going on inside the mind of the protagonist and the depiction of the atom bomb test & the politics surrounding it was really good to watch.

I didn't expect the divine Bhagavat Gita book to be described during the intercourse sequence, maybe that should've been avoided.

But, overall, it's a Nolan film, and like usual we might understand its depth only after several years of watching & interpreting & debating.

6.title: Basically a 3 hr trailer
6.content: The pace of the movie is too alert for my taste. Scenes and frames and events changing every 3-5 seconds, the audio goes from 0 to 100 I had to cover my ears. The editing simply made me sick as if I was in a speeding car on a windy road hitting lots of bumps. The acting is 10/10 and the quality is impecable. I kinda wished the movie had shown some insights into the Japanese side as well, like maybe the story of a simple family living in Hiroshima, for example, to get some balance and more nuanced cultural insights and sides to the same story. It felt so unilateral even with Oppenheimer's hallucinating guilt. The main antagonist in this story is some guy playing political tricks I didn't care about which just made the story difficult to understand or get emotionally invested into at times.

6.title: Generally enjoyable... just about!
6.content:
A tough subject, the story of how the biggest bomb in human history was developed and the way our human minds conive and corrupt... I found some of the dialogue creaky - littered with lots of inappropriate phrases and jarring speech mannerisms. The frequent on-screen effects supposed to suggest the interaction of particles like atoms and other physical entities was inevitable I suppose, given the subject matter but didn't bring much benefit. The trademark intercut of time narratives likewise - just made the story harder to follow than a more straightforward story line. Murphy works hard to represent the "hero" but others seem less three dimensional with some of the large collection of supporting scientists reduced to almost cartoon-like performances. Blunt does her usual turn of portraying an angry, snooty and slightly disconnected woman, Conti tries hard to deliver his few lines as the most famous modern physicist ever, Dilan does the tough grumpy soldier pretty well... but over-all, I found it a bit of a bore.

If you want to find out more about the Manhattan project or modern physics theories, there are many and better books. If you want to find out more about the capricious and unreliable political entity that was post-war federal United States, likewise. If you want to find out more about Oppenheimer the man, there are many better ways to carry out your ambition. All-in-all, rather dull and unrewarding film, made worse by its long, long length.

6.title: Triple A movies can be boring too
6.content: There's nothing wrong with Oppenheimer. It's a movie packed with great actors, directed by an amazing director, and has a lot of great one on one dialogues and smart come backs. Objectively this is a great movie that checks all the check boxes, and will likely receive enough awards to make its creators proud. It's a movie that was made to look great on a shelf accompanied by other Nolan films, maybe flipped to the back side to proudly display the 180 minute runtime. But it wasn't the type of movie a lot of people could watch twice. I can see a parallel script for Oppenheimer that better uses the lengthy 3 hour runtime in a way that's, well .. more fun. This version is too padded with the wrong stuffing. Instead of focusing on the scientific aspects of Oppenheimer's work, it delves too far and deep in his romantic and political dramas. The trial setting is simply too boring and bland. Hearing testimonies from every cast member inside a claustrophobic room really killed the enjoyment for me. The romances, doubly so.

6.title: Great cast, great for history buffs but too damned loud!
6.content: Being a student of the history of nuclear weapons development, I was pleased that the film was surprisingly accurate in terms of Oppenheimer's role in the development of the atomic bomb. I was especially interested in the efforts made to destroy Oppenheimer's reputation after the war and applaud Robert Downey's Academy Award level performance. My reason for rating this film lower than I had hoped to rate it is the sound track. Three of us found it difficult to clearly hear the cast members because of either distortion in the recording or masking level ambient noise in the film. The use of "airy" voices that has become so prevalent in todays films is infuriating. It is as if the use of vocal cords in the uttering of speech is now forbidden. I kept wanting to shout out "SPEAK UP". SAY IT SO WE CAN HEAR YOU!" Finally, the use of extreme noise levels in this film was far, far overdone. For an atomic bomb explosion? OK. But the use of room jarring, earth shaking low frequency sound levels over and over again was both gratuitous and ridiculous. I would be very careful in recommending this movies to my friends and relatives.

6.title: VIEWS ON FILM review of Oppenheimer
6.content:
With his numerous films, Christopher Nolan never makes it easy for you the viewer, to gravitate to a smooth landing. I mean he's just not the most focused of storytellers, juggling tons of personas and narratives that enter and leave the screen faster than a speeding bullet. Such is the case with his latest titled Oppenheimer, a three hour biographical flick about J. Robert Oppenheimer (played by a disciplined Cillian Murphy) and his involvement with the Manhattan project (aka the development of the atomic incendiary).

Haunting at times, lumbering at others, and secretly showing Nolan channeling his inner Terrence Malick, Oppenheimer is talky and physicist speak from the get-go. It also adds numerous cut away-s courtesy of Chris, who numbs the audience member with imagery of all things fission. Yup, the best way to embrace Oppenheimer is to hark back to Christopher Nolan's earlier stuff a la Memento and 2002's Insomnia. You just have to think of those pics as longer and much more drawn-out.

Historically, Oppenheimer has a solid sense of time and place (circa 1926-1954) and the musical score by Ludwig Goransson is eerie, glacial beauty. Continuity-wise, the movie sadly wears you out, presenting so many characters (played by known actors) that perform amicably but fade in and out like "slay" insertions. Look there's Emily Blunt as J. Robert's wife. Look there's Casey Affleck as military intelligence officer Boris Pash. Look there's Rami Malek as nuclear expert David L. Hill. And look there's Gary Oldman as president Harry S. Truman. Watching Oppenheimer, you concentrate less on the overall yarn here and more on the spot-the-unrecognizable-celebrity ogle. I mean it almost becomes a drinking game (not that I condone such actions).

Edited lightning-quick but still in need of a cutdown via 30 minutes of runtime, Oppenheimer is the type of vehicle you see once and then proceed to decompress. Based on the huge box office take however, it's safe to say that it could never be a "bomb". Natch.

6.title: Just Not What I was Expecting
6.content: From a technical, filmmaking perspective, it's a very good movie, but that shouldn't be all a movie is about. I realize that the 1950s commie witch hunt was part of Oppenheimer's life, but I really thought I was going to see - and wanted to see, a movie about a genius scientist's thought processes and theories and development of his inventions. This movie barely touched on any of this. It was about 3/4ths commie witch hunt and 1/4th, if that, about his genius. Needless to say, I was very disappointed for this reason. A technically well-made movie will never replace a movie that tells the story you want to hear.

6.title: A bloated, but well made movie
6.content:
This movie has three distinct thirds, two of which I believe are extremely bloated and poorly executed. Don't get me wrong this movie is incredibly well made, well acted, and beautiful to look at, but it's also flawed.

Backstory and slow moving plots are perfectly fine, but it still needs to be engaging. The first third of the movie moves at a snails pace, and it not engaging in the slightest. I love slow moving dramas, but the characters need to be interconnected and the plot needs to move, here it does not.

The second third is pretty great, having a slow build up to a powerful climax. Not much to say here, it's a good hour.

The final third of the movie is stronger than the first but still lacks engagement. Straus's? Moves against Robert come across un-impactful and thus the entire third act just isn't overly fun to watch.

Many have said it, but 3 hours is simply not needed for this film. I would take 30 minutes off of the first third, 40 off of the last, and add 20 to the middle to add more time in the best part of the film.

Overall, it's a well made movie, most likely a good movie; But it's also not an engaging or entertaining movie.

6.title: Minority opinion
6.content:
I'm clearly in a minority here so take my opinion with a grain of salt. Nolan provides here a visually stunning movie with excellent acting performances. Robert Downey jr vanished so well in his role, that it took me 2 hours to recognize him, apof all the performances given, his was the most stellar and i fully expect a nomination for best supporting actor for his portrayal of Strauss. Cillian Murphy was very good but not special.

The jumping around in time was something to get used to, but nothing new for a Nolan movie, I liked the twists towards the end, and of course the historical component was fascinating. But in all honesty the movie inspires me much more to read the Oppenheimer biography "american prometheus" than watching this movie again. 180 minutes was to long for the material presented.

6.title: Balancing Historical Grandeur and Character Introspection
6.content:
The cinematic exposition of Oppenheimer's narrative is characterized by an intricate interplay of endless details pertaining to personal political entanglements and acquisitive power aspirations. This preoccupation with details seemingly engendered a dissipation of the potential emotional impact inherent in a grander narrative centering on Oppenheimer's pivotal choice to lead the Manhattan Project, thus becoming "the destroyer of worlds." Although the film's trajectory was competently executed and aptly elucidated Oppenheimer's intricate interpersonal dynamics, it served as a prelude to the ensuing psychological trauma and moral quandaries that the protagonist grappled with.

Nonetheless, a pivotal juncture within the narrative catalyzed a divergence, culminating in an ostensible abandonment of the overarching thematic thrust. This trajectory redirection appears markedly less compelling in contrast to the broader narrative focal point: the development of the atomic bomb and Oppenheimer's involvement therein. The rationale for maintaining primacy upon this narrative facet is inherently linked to the central quandary faced by storytellers when presented with a comprehensive historical figure. Here, the illustration of "Lincoln" by Spielberg can be seen as an illustrative paradigm. Spielberg's endeavor inherently acknowledges the impossibility of encompassing the entirety of Lincoln's life within the confines of a single cinematic presentation. Instead, the creators discerningly elected to spotlight a crucial epoch - the 13th Amendment - yielding a succinct yet resonant portrayal that, despite potential reservations pertaining to biographical fidelity, effectively encapsulated a significant period within Lincoln's lifetime.

Parallel to this, analogous considerations pervaded my initial engagement with Oppenheimer's cinematic portrayal. As the narrative unfolded, a foretelling climax was discernible, poised to culminate in the anticipated zenith: the essential tests and atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Regrettably, the narrative trajectory was interspersed with a proliferation of peripheral details interwoven into Oppenheimer's life, alongside the role of Lewis Strauss. The cumulative effect of these secondary nuances lead to a dilution of the narrative's climactic focal point, impeding the projected emotional impact of the aftermath of the bombings, particularly upon Oppenheimer. The scene when Oppenheimer gave his speech after the bombings, meticulously crafted to evoke his potential emotional state, emerged as a masterstroke in Nolan's directorial expertise. However, the subsequent course of actions devolved into a profusion of discussions encompassing political machinations, betrayal, and inquisition. It is imperative to note that cinema, while may be rooted in factual events, is not documentary; it exists within the realm of narrative storytelling. Thus, were Nolan's intention to craft a documentary, such a trajectory would have been more suitable.

Moreover, the broader thematic underpinning of the film appears entangled with a conspicuous assertion of Oppenheimer's historical significance. It becomes evident that Nolan endeavors to imbue Oppenheimer with a sense of unparalleled importance, juxtaposing his unblemished honesty against a backdrop of malevolent counterparts consumed by personal ambitions. This portrayal strives to evidence Oppenheimer's innocence, even as he grapples with his culpability in the project's catastrophic aftermath. This endeavor, regrettably, manifests overtly, lacking the persuasive potency required to render it authentic. To fortify this construct, a more palpable exposition of the internal conflict that engulfs Oppenheimer, and an intensified exploration of the character's psychological trauma, would have proven indispensable. Although Nolan does employ astute techniques to convey Oppenheimer's emotional state, the narrative impetus is periodically eclipsed by a superfluity of inessential intricacies and character dynamics, thereby compromising the film's pacing and overarching tension.

With regard to the ethical dimension, it is imperative to acknowledge the susceptibility of any artistic endeavor to being co-opted as a medium of political messaging. In the context of weighty subjects such as the present one, the artist assumes a responsibility to possess a judicious comprehension of the causal dynamics and ramifications of political quandaries, and in "Oppenheimer," potential harnessing of science as an instrument of warfare. Particularly for a cinematic work centered upon a historical epoch of this significance, a pronounced assertion of modernity's shortcomings and affiliations should have been evident. This does not mean to advocate for propagandist inclinations; rather, it is about the necessity to encapsulate the severity of the incident. The film's preoccupation with individual moral dilemmas and political aspirations, while not unwarranted, appears to overshadow the broader contextual resonance, thus weakening a comprehensive understanding of the era's significance.

6.title: Familiarity is a prerequisite
6.content:
Solid performances amid frustrating editing.

I feel historical knowledge of the players and timelines are a must as Nolan does little to help the ignorant.

The timelines (and there are several) jump without informing the audience of just where, relative to the main narrative, we are.

Characters (and they are legion) are introduced without satisfactory backstory or introduction. Again, those very familiar with this period or those of militaristic or scientific backgrounds may at once recognize the speaking parts, but those with only a passing knowledge may find themselves lost at times.

The detonation (test site) of the bomb itself seemed anticlimactic.

Personally, I aim to educate myself further and then rewatch as I feel this film deserves at least that much.

6.title: What a snoozefest
6.content:
I'm an engineer whose loved physics his whole life.

I literally leaned over and took a nap on my wife's lap during the last third of the movie.

A confusing mess. They threw big physics terminology around to sound smart, but it didn't help the narrative. I found myself trying to follow along and kept getting lost.

Anyway, aside from switching between black and white, color, and etc., I felt that this was a huge missed opportunity. I'm not a director or story writer, and I would never in a million years think I can do Christopher Nolan's job - however why on earth was there barely any capturing of the effects of the atomic bomb in Japan!

There was like a few seconds of flashing images of people being bombed, but wtf, literally this whole movie is about the bomb and there was nothing that captured how devastating it was.

The movie is aptly named, since it really is about Oppenheimer, not about the greater effects of his work.

We went home and watched Youtube videos that gave us a better understanding of what the results of dropping the bomb really had.

6.title: Nolan's limitations laid bare
6.content: When a film gets this much praise you wonder whether it'll fall flat on it's face and it does but only after the bomb.... I had no interest in the Communist sub-plot. It wasn't that interesting and if he loses his security clearance...so what? His character became a bit repetitive as well and the dialog just wasn't interesting enough. It started off so well but he couldn't keep it up. I don't believe Nolan is that skilled/nuanced a director to make such a film work. He should stick to more action based movies because if you delve into his films the scripts and sometimes the acting isn't his forte and for Oppenheimer to work the script is rather childish and immature in the second half. It dragged very badly and I couldn't wait for it to finish. I won't want to watch this one again yet I've re-watched many of his previous films. Shame. PS where were the incredible scenes of the bomb which were being quoted. Didn't see anything amazing there.

6.title: Tiw Oppenheimer
6.content:
Today I watched Nolan's Oppenheimer and it was good.

To start off I think that Cillian Murphy and most of the other cast did really great. I think the acting in this film is genuinely very good, most of the actors really transform into their characters, even some smaller role actors have the opportunity to show a lot of range in this film.

The story is definitely my favorite part, I enjoy almost all of it and think this is one of the best tales to be told on the big screen. I think Nolan also did a good job writing a 3 hour long film without to much of it feeling like it needed to be cut out, it's not easy to do. There are a couple moments that are incredibly visceral and really make you question the philosophy of what's happening here.

My huge problem with this film is the technical aspects however and there is a unfortunately a good chunk of it that I do not love. For starters, the cinematography in this film feels like a downgrade from every Nolan I've watched(haven't seen tenet).

Half of this film, no, 75% of this film is just shot reverse shot close ups that are so insanely unimaginative that it really boggles my mind that they didn't just pull the camera back a little bit. Like, your sets are actually pretty neat, can you PLEASE pull the camera back from Oppy and show me the laboratory their in?? Maybe show me a bit more scenery and not a close up shot reverse shot? We did get some genuinely Jaw dropping scenes, however for the most part it just often was so bland.

The cinematography also doesn't help the fact that this movie has some really adhd editing going on. So many different scenes happen and so many different characters come in so quickly that it's actually bordering on bloated. It really felt like there was like 30 cuts on average per minute in this 3 hour long film and that's just eye straining sometimes. Like we're cutting back and forth between areas and times and it's just so much information overload...

Also the mixing, as per Nolan standard, renders certain scenes absolutely unintelligible on a big screen. Maybe it's fine for home video or with subtitles, but, especially near the end, some scenes the vocals are just buried in the mix so badly. I cannot hear over the music that is not normally in the scene why is it so loud...

And uh yeah the music was fine, I really don't have much to say about it. I guess it serviced the film well in some parts but I found it to be generally forgettable. Like I really loved the music in some of Nolan's older works (dunkirk and memento in particular) but this particular soundtrack didn't blow me away or anything. No pun intended.

Overall, I still enjoyed this movie despite what I believe to be pretty annoying flaws. It has a lot of payoffs, it's a good story and writing(barring one kinda cringe scene with Florence Pugh), and it really is fantastically acted by the main actors. I definitely do not regret watching this movie but I do wish that some elements didn't feel kinda phoned in.

Low - Mid 6/10.

6.title: Good, not great.
6.content:
I went into this film very excited, as I had not seen a Christopher Nolan film in the theatre yet. Nolan has become as big a draw as the stories his movies tell, so when he releases a film, it's an event.

That said, I settled in for Oppenheimer. The story of the building of the first atomic bomb, and the man who headed up the team should make for a fascinating morality tale. Can you live with yourself knowing you had a large hand in incinerating thousands of human beings (many of them civilians) what did your genius unleash on the world? Was it the right thing to do even though Germany would have dropped the bomb on us had they had the chance? All valid questions, and unfortunately, not really given a lot of time in this movie.

It's more about the man's life, his mistress, his wife, his colleagues, etc. Which is fine, but the crescendo should have been the bombs themselves. As it turns out, that is just the 2nd hour of this three hour film. The last dealing with Oppenheimers appearance in a kangaroo court set up by his one time boss at the US atomic energy commission, in response to an insult delivered in front of a congressional hearing. Not exactly riveting stuff. It's a shame, this could have been a truly great movie, but what the bombs did, and what they meant for the world on the verge of the Cold War were not given enough screen time. These were truly weapons on a scale that the world had never seen before, but you wouldn't really know it watching the film. If you didn't know the history of WWII, you may feel lost, and if you went into this film wanting to learn about why the atomic bomb was such a historical event, you may also come away less than satisfied.

6.title: The music overwhelms the movie.
6.content: Oppenheimer is a movie that underperformed. It's weaknesses are so in the light that the director felt the need to paint It's shortcomings with an annoying music score. Murphys mono-tone voice is quite weak and his character suffers because of this. The script is rushed and tries too hard to tell Oppenheimers life story with flashcards. Is Oppenheimers story worth making a movie about? Sure. Why not? Was this Oscar winner worthy? Guess that depends on the competition. Oppenheimer is definitely better than Barbie. Let's not forget what happened because of Oppenheimer and his group of scientists. Listen for the nonstop music that drowns out the whispering dialog. I found myself so distracted from the movie mostly because of this. At best a 6.

6.title: A bit of a bomb
6.content:
I had very high expectations of Oppenheimer, all the reviews were positive, the trailers looked great and it sounded like a really interesting story. My hopes were dashed in the first forty five minutes with a story line that just jumped back and forth and frankly never really made sense. The sections of the movie that had some story continuity, were quite good and I enjoyed, but continuity was not a strong point of this story.

On a positive note, the cast was great and their performances were very good.

But in the end, this looked like a move that was made to win awards, not entertain the viewers.

And I'm sure it will win plenty of awards, but one three hour viewing was enough for me.

6.title: One time watch.
6.content:
This time Nolan's narratives of non linearity, a lot of jump cuts and lots of political reality doesn't seem engaging, doesn't fit properly. Oppenheimer's narratives should have been like memento, a serene based linear presentation. Reverse narratives would also been fine but let it be reserved for Memento. This style of presentation tunes well with the non fiction. And also the movie is 3 hours long, with no such interesting themes. Just plain biography that misses the Nolan's spark, as evident from his previous works. The music is average though. The acting is nothing to be mentioned about. Murphy, Blunt, Pugh, Matt, RDJ all acted plain misses the emotions. Acting in Nolan's film is not a spotlight. Generally technical aspects weighs heavy in Nolan's films like intelligent script, lighting's, narratives etc.

There is nothing to mention about Oppenheimer's true biography. There is one thing praiseworthy though in the film, few characters are impressive. Just like pugh as the communist who is irreligious, has sex while reading the Bhagawat Gita. Scientist Oppie is worldly, devoid of social friendly religious traits, inclined towards politics, which still makes nukes a political agenda. His world is also shown as the same. Scientists like Einstein and others favored negatively to Oppie's work and so on. On the other hand a lot of political chitchat with no such emotional appeal, with no interesting subplots makes this film at best boring. Nevertheless Nolan's experimental attempts is good, but not the best example of biographic film. Just average for all the great casts working together.

Some scenes falls flat though. The explosion of A- Bomb is not shown real, even the Indiana Jones showed properly the nuclear blast. But it misses this. Another, When oppie says he feels blood on his hands the president takes out his white handkerchief and says the most boring statement. I thought the president would have told Oppie to rub his hand. So, there are such types of scenes with some dull moments. Really wanted the details of Oppenheimer's personal life, in order to understand the moral qualms but it did only half. Summing up, Nolan's full spark is missing this time. A one time watch. A 64/100.

6.title: Like attending a 3-hour long, heavy college lecture that requires significant mental effort to get through
6.content:
Don't expect to be entertained while watching this movie. This film might inform you on the life of Robert Oppenheimer and might even stimulate you intellectually, but not in a fun or engaging way. It demands careful attention all the way through, with about 80% of the movie being heavy dialogue, the contents of which are hardly discernible without subtitles. Perhaps I went into the theater with the wrong expectations (and after Tenet, I probably should have known better) but I didn't expect to have to absord and retain so much information in order to not get lost at some point in the movie's 180 minutes long runtime.

So why a 6, then? Well, even though the plot represented the epitome of tedium, the acting was top-notch, the dialogue was well-written (even though it requires a C2 proficiency level in English to fully understand), the score was fantastic and the cinematography was amazing. These factors bring the movie to an above-average rating.

6.title: A chaotic storyline
6.content:
The points I felt were well made were 1) The nuclear bomb is an extraordinary example of the powers of the universe and 2) Once people get there hands on it, especially the government, you can bet good sense goes out the window. Oppenheimer himself thought he was facing this dilemma, and its weight upon him was very well portrayed, and his dismay with people. Portrayed well also was the alarming failure of authority to really come to grips with their role in opening Pandora's box. Unfortunately, the movie makes all too clear the inability of mankind to govern itself, and the unlikelihood that we are at all smarter about it today..

So the major themes of this movie are powerfully done, the major actor is splendid. So what's not so good?

In part, what is jarring is not only the idiocy of the men in charge, but the filmmaker's view of the audience as also idiots. It has to be drummed into us that the bomb is dangerous- did you get that? Well let's repeat it again. And maybe again.

The movie does not proceed sequentially, but jumps back and forth over decades. I don't think that actually helps the presentation. The movie "The Day after Trinity" is strictly in time order, and actually more powerful as a result. Also, its filmed clips of the detonation were better chosen.

The soundtrack makes subscripts necessary, but there aren't any.

So my feeling about this movie is it is worth seeing. It makes some excellent points very well. But I feel it could have been better, and would have be been better if the audience were considered more sentient. The importance of the subject is gotten across, but leaves me feeling the movie didn't believe we could get it.

6.title: Really? >8?
6.content: I typically rate movies based on me liking it in general, the writing, of course acting, and maybe above all the rewatch-ability aspect. In some instances, a movie ending may be so great and so "top secret" that after you get that crazy rush you really wouldn't watch again because you know the ultimate climax. Still, you may not desire to re-watch it but you would absolutely LOVE to watch it with others just so they could enjoy it. This, is not any of those scenarios. If you rated this way up there.... would you really watch this over and over? Would you watch it with others just to see their reactions? If you're being honest, you wouldn't. I wouldn't either.

6.title: Inexcusably long Oscar bait
6.content:
I've made it clear in the past that I do not like the direction Christopher's Nolan's career has gone in. He seems desperate to win an Oscar and so every movie (or at best every second movie) is just an attempt to tick every box he can to achieve this. 'Oppenheimer' is no exception. What do the Academy love? Biographical films of course. His talents are far too exceptional to be wasting years on projects like this that any half-talented filmmaker could do.

The film is undoubtedly well made. The story, though still painfully slow and dull, was helped along with the incredible pacing all of his films possess. One scene often runs into another with the audio overlapping. So even though the film is inexcusably long for what it is, it is at least made in a way that tries to make it palatable.

The final hour of the film is the strongest and saves it a point or two. The ending is also exceptionally well done and will leave people exiting the theatre on a high note, exactly like it was planned to do. This was a one time watch for me though and not a film I will remember a week from now. 6/10.

6.title: Too long that I stopped caring!
6.content: Phew, finally watched Oppenheimer and even finished it. I was curious to know if I would like it or not. The movie was too long. At certain points in the first half, I wanted to switch off, but still continued hoping it would get better. The second half was way better and the movie should had ended. But they drag it on for another hour. At this point I just didn't care anymore. I love good cinema and hate mindless stuff. But Oppenheimer was not engaging at all. Don't understand the need to confuse viewers with complex storytelling and back and forth flashbacks. In this case, it didn't work for me. I'm glad though majority have liked the movie, since it does touch upon an important and sensitive subject.

6.title: The Fission Fizzles and never really Explodes
6.content: With all the hype surrounding this movie and all the stellar actors in it, one would expect this to pack quite the impact! I found the opening half of the movie leading up to what turned out to be one of the most Anticlimactic expression of a nuclear bomb ever filmed...You might say How can that be possible?
