Just watch the detonation, cling to ur seat, prepare to be amazed and blown away and then you will see what Im talking about...Cinematography was good,for sure throughout the movie, but nothing memorable nor outstanding..Similiarily with the acting,n as everyone did a decent to excellent job but nothing exceptional..Maybe its the writing,which seemed patchy and inconsistant in engaging interest,especially in the parts after the bomb demo and the final parts with the Hearing going on, I just fastforwarded thru ...This is what I mean that the movie had its moments but could not sustain them and those moments were mixed with long, ,boring, drawn out sequences that could have been left on the cutting room floor..There Should have been More focus on the horrors of the bomb,its devasting effects on the people it was dropped on and the equally devasting effects it had upon oppenheimer's psyche and his soul..Completly avoiding the showing of the dropping of the 2 bombs was just biazzare in a movie that could have shown the Real horror of the use of an atomic bomb and instead,skipped over it and focused on courtroom hearings...Its a good effort,it has that "cinematic" quality all about it especially in the opening half but it Fizzles out and looses its spark and just becomes a tedious and frankly ,uninteresting story twords its end...Decent yes, outstanding masterpiece? No, not at all..missess the mark of greatness and falls short.

6.title: Overly Long and Not Particularly Entertaining
6.content: For all the hype, I was disappointed in "Oppenheimer." It was well done and visually easy on the eyes but the movie was overly long and boring at times, especially the first hour. The second half was somewhat more interesting, but truth be told, the movie focused on a character who was not particularly likeable and really hard pressed to have sympathy for him. There is gratuitous nudity twice and don't undestand why Christoper Nolan felt it necessary to include it in this movie. Honestly, I did not find this movie particularly entertaining and am not likely want to see it again. As far as movies go, I much rather want to spend my time and money to see the likes of "WIcked" or "Gladiator II" or even another showing of a Jurassic Park/World movie.

6.title: $100M Disappointment
6.content:
A supposedly great director with an even greater budget... Producing the greatest embarrassment to film ever put to screen.

I will save you the trouble and the money. The dialogue is pretentious and wants to feel witty by being read very quick. The actors have no range (by direction) and the soundtrack is forgettable. The CGI is cartoonish, I feel like I'm watching looney tunes. The narrative is boring, simple and unimportant, even summed up in one sentence during the mid-point of the movie. The only interesting point was the brief inclusion of Edward Teller observing the atom bomb (who would later invent the hydrogen bomb). The dialogue is so drawn out that it might actually be more enjoyable as a script only.

What is it worth seeing for? The representations of bygone scientists, like Einstein and Godel walking together, Mr. Teller's grand ideas of hydrogen bombs, Richard Feynman playing his bongos.

The movie actually had potential to be important, and to communicate something meaningful, but it didn't. The crew wasn't stopped by 100 million dollars; they were stopped by Christopher Nolan as a director. How one man can waste such an incredible amount of resources is beyond me, considering that he has made incredible movies before.

Is it worth watching? No. Was it the modern classic it was touted to be two years later? No. No one cares about this movie.

Should you save your money? YES. Go watch something else.

6.title: Only one sceen worth watching
6.content: There is only one scene for which this movie is worth watching, and that is the scene when Openheimer sells his vision for the Manhattan Project to the general. The rest, especially all the politics and the personal rivalry, seemed commonplace and boring. I think it's a miss that they did not include more of Richard Feynman in the movie, who is one of the most beloved physicists of all time. Generations of kids have learned physics from his famous lectures. Now that I think of it, physics was probably not a favorite subject of the director in school. 6.title: Context is key
6.content:
Don't go watch it for the explosion, it'll be anticlimactic and you'll have to endure 2 hours of fantastic acting to get there, with another hour of continuous monologue to follow. It's one of the first bombs of its kind, not necessarily the biggest. An opening statement wouldn't go a miss - that it is all based on fact or an artistic representation of events, who the characters are and the role they play, which was muddy water some times.

Definately a different style of film, tense, all the way through and suspenseful. The snippets of conversation that gradually built and built to the formation of the experiment and the path to its creation. Following the bomb test, it was thought a pincle moment had been reached, only for it to be dragged out by the trial, which was good but not much was made of its purpose. The film ended and no one seemed to be reprimanded for anything or any courses of action taken. Good film, but felt like a stab at a world record attempt for longest film for the sakes of it. More isn't necessarily better.

6.title: Meh? Why all the hype? Are movies that bad anymore?
6.content:
6.5 at best. I'm mid-60's in age and grew up with the fear of atomics. I've always been fascinated with this era and at some level, very interested in the technology used to develop and test the device, and the politics and military's demand to use during war-time. This movie did touch on some of the thinking present during that time leading to the decisions. I enjoy learning, reading, and watching anything to do with WWII. My father was in the war, so I have some ties to this. Growing up on the West coast (of CA) I was in close proximity to many of the research areas, such as Stanford, and Lawrence Livermore Labs.

I tried not to fall into the over-hype of this movie prior to its release, but really looked forward to seeing it. The Regal "RPX" theater was maybe a third full (Sunday at 3:00p). The filmography was not necessarily impressive - top notch, but not outstanding or superior. Some of the edits were annoying, constantly flipping between different time lines, and using B&W vs. Color to help show "artistic license", I suppose. It was more annoying. I do like B&W, however and when done well, it's very impressive.

The sound quality was the most annoying part of the movie. It was very, very loud at times. I noticed my 20-something son sitting next to me covering his ears perhaps 3 different times. Several others in the theater were doing the same. The music was unfitting for this movie. It really felt like music that would be used during a two-minute film trailer to advertise a new movie, however the music lasted 3 hours. It did nothing to add ambiance or mood to the scenes. It was a distraction at best. Some dialog was rolled over by the music and was missed.

As a comparison, "Fat Man and Little Boy" (staring Paul Newman) is a much better story - compelling, sufficiently detailed in the technical aspects, and helped to tell the broader narrative of the teams that worked on this project. The scene showing the Trinity test was, frankly, a letdown. Others have commented here, so I'll let that one go.

Matt Damon had some terrific moments early in the movie, but it wasn't sustained. Emily Blunt's character was muted, and somehow lost in some of her impact. The most moving scene was when she "watched" her husband with the other woman. Although the scene told a story, it was unnecessary. Better writing could have brought the audience to resonate with her despise and hate. Cilian Murphy's performance was terrific, but not Oscar worthy. Robert Downey Jr. Did an outstanding job and took me for a bit of a ride early on. I ended up flipping on his character, which at the end of the movie, not so subtly illustrates his motives. Not a good look for the man, but it was finally addressed in the way that the average movie goer could understand. It was refreshing to see Einstein portrayed in this movie, but I'm not sure if that was closer to reality or just the clever inklings of a writer.

Overall, I'm glad I saw it, and it is still drifting around in my head - which is one good sign that it made an impact. I'll probably watch it again when available to stream at home....with sub-titles.

6.title: Visual Grandeur vs. Narrative Depth
6.content:
Despite the anticipation surrounding Christopher Nolan's latest work, the film might not meet all expectations. The grandiosity of the movie, driven partly by Nolan's stellar reputation and the extensive marketing, creates a halo effect that might be misleading.

The casting of Cillian Murphy in the lead role under Nolan's direction is a welcome decision, and his remarkable performance rightly takes center stage. However, the inclusion of over 21 celebrity cameos appears as an unneeded distraction, drawing attention away from the central narrative and undermining Murphy's role.

Concerns also arise around the film's pacing. From the beginning, it plunges into a frantic tempo that continues relentlessly throughout. While this pace might be fitting for certain plot elements-such as racing against the Germans/Russians-the unyielding speed becomes disorienting. Quick scene cuts and often inaudible dialogue further contribute to the confusion.

This incessant pace, though potentially intentional, restricts the artistry's room to breathe. The audience is left with little chance to immerse themselves and "feel" the film. With an expansive budget and a three-hour runtime, the rush to include substantial footage feels more like an attempt to justify the spending rather than letting the narrative unfold organically.

Nevertheless, the movie's merits are undeniable. The visual splendor, combined with a beautiful musical score and Murphy's compelling performance, enriches the film's artistic value. Still, these qualities, as exceptional as they may be, do not suffice to label the work as a masterpiece.

The conclusion to be drawn from Nolan's latest creation is that, while there is much to admire, certain choices undermine its overall impact. It might not connect with everyone, especially those seeking a more cohesive and immersive cinematic journey. The film shines in parts but may disappoint viewers expecting more than a Hollywood spectacle.

Reflecting further, the true core of the story seems lost in the spectacle surrounding it. Nolan's name, the Hollywood cameos, the dominant score, and the grand IMAX visuals all contribute to the narrative receding into the background. The film's indulgence in cinematic glamour, though visually and auditorily thrilling, risks losing storytelling's essence. The intricate weave of characters, emotions, and themes gets overshadowed, tilting the balance towards appearance over depth. The result is a dazzling yet soul-unsatisfying movie that comes across more as a Hollywood extravaganza than a poignant human drama.

6.title: Great Acting Horrid Sound Mixing and Editing
6.content: This film had some truly golden moments especially in the second half of the film, and Cilian Murphy did an incredible job, but the editing and constant overbearing music ruined it for me. The first half of the film felt like a trailer for the film itself, with overly consistent quick edits and a relentless rollercoaster of dramatic music that sounded like it was a score for a different film altogether. I kept thinking something was wrong with my sound system as I couldn't hear the dialogue over the music at times. At around the 2 hour mark, or during the build up of the first bomb test the emotional content of the film started to sync up better with the music and I finally stopped thinking about how off the music was as my suspension of disbelief finally kicked in. At this point I could begin appreciating the film for its historical interpretation, acting, artistic elements etc... but was only able to do so after I was able to forget about the music.

6.title: Couldn't follow it
6.content: The volume in the Imax was set so high i missed half the dialogue, especially the mumbly Oppy. If he had much of importance to say I missed it and it made following the jumping about in time even harder to follow. EXCEPT Matt Damon. His enunciation is clear as a bell. He knows how to speak. Wish other actors had been to the same school. It is probably a much better film than i experienced, the visuals are stunning and ther is some science mingled with the human stories. So, disappointed. It would be so easy for directors to ensure their films are audible and for actors to address their audience.

6.title: Irregular Narration, Fast Paced, Ok Visuals and a Great Camerawork. It's Neither Boring, nor Great.
6.content:
I will keep my review very simple and absolutely honest.

The movie is a biopic in its purest sense. Don't watch this movie if you think the Trinity test will be spectacular with great special effects. Nolan tried to achieve the blast with practical effects and that took a major toll on the seriousness of how violent Nuclear explosion can be. Basically there is only one explosion people go to the watch the movie. If someone is telling me they watched the movie just for the Dr. Oppenheimer's pov of life, I would say they are lying to themselves. Everyone on this planet have some philosophy of their own and a sob story. Oppenheimer's doesn't make him any special or more vulnerable than us. That's the essence of life.

I did not go to the movie expecting it to be an action flick. Also just because I am a long time Nolan fan doesn't mean I can lie to myself convincing that's it's a spectacular movie. The movie is just blant. Over 90% of the movie is distracting with its cutting and showing different timelines while lacking consistency in story telling. Nolan is know to cut scenes and show past and future back to back without giving the audience gap to breath. This style of screenplay will work only for some movies but not all. I totally understand why Nolan had to do what he did, but it simply didn't workout that well.

I am from India, and usually I know when it's a great movie by seeing our Audience reaction. 70% of the seats were full and I thought people would usually blast the theatre with screaming like monkeys do, like we do in all good movies. But this time, I watched a soul-less, exhausted audience. Most of them were not even bothering to stay and give the movie some attention.

The other thing I want to talk about it's the sound track. As gorgeous it can be, it's frustrating and irritating to see Nolan using the same Dunkirk theatrics like the playing the foot stomping rail track sound again and again. To summarise what I saw

1. A loud monotonous eerie sound track.

2. Characters yelling half the time to make the movie look serious.

3. A failed Trinity explosion practical effects.

4. Too much screentime about the protagonist AEC hearing and potential indictment. (Honestly, who in this day and age would give a damn about how the guy who made the atom bomb coped with Govt Committees for a stupidest reason that he could be potential Communist? I mean, how could the director think people who are watching the film know how big of a deal it is to talk communist ideas in a Capitalistic nation during WW2?)

5. An unapologetic scientist in real life, which the movie did a fantastic job to not give a F or care about him and why he had to do what he had to do. Nolan literally failed to make me feel sorry for Oppenheimer. Just, seeing him read a BS sankrit phrase, "Now I become death, destroyer of worlds" is meant to convince he is really sorry for killing 210000 people?

6. A movie which seriously lacks flow of story telling.

7. A 3 hours, loud, serial type of drama.

Atleast to do some justice to the people who are about to watch this movie, I would say, try to learning the names of the characters in Oppenheimer's life and how influential they too are. This movie is not for an Average Joe with zero knowledge about scientists and their respective contributions. And the way Nolan introduced them like a high speed train into the movie is seriously bad.

All in all, it's a good movie, but not spectacular.

6.title: Watched a good movie and Disappointed
6.content:
I went to the movie with an expectation to see a Nolan movie. In Memento, he stimulated our brains to ask questions about human memory, in Interstellar about the dimensions of the universe, time and gravity, in Tenet about time, in Prestige electricity and teleportation, in Inception... you got my point. Even on Batman series, his touch was able to make it the most grounded comic movie and achieve intellectual stimulation.

Oppenheimer, could make us think about the structure of the universe, time, space etc... no it's just a good US history and politics movie. The PR to watch it at a IMAX saloon is totally fallacious. IMO, just wait to watch at home on Netflix.

6.title: Complete Disappointment
6.content:
I used to love Nolan movies, but I was very disappointed in Tenet and the movies he made afterwards. I had great expectations for Oppenheimer, but except for the Trinity test scene, none of the scenes impressed me. They even bored me.

In a movie about the person who invented the atomic bomb, I wish the effects of this bomb were shown better. I don't think this message can be given by just putting a model made of ashes. Watching how the life of the person who invented the atomic bomb deteriorates seems to me like a cover-up of the damage that the atomic bomb caused to people.

Apart from that, when I listened to the soundtrack playlist before watching the movie, I was fascinated, but I think they didn't use the music well in the movie as well. It was another disappointment for me that they composed such beautiful music and couldn't use it effectively.

I also couldn't figure out the meaning of the meaningless and disturbing sex scene in the movie. Since I knew that there were no such scenes in any Nolan movie before, I thought, "If Nolan shows us this, he must be up to something, it has to mean something." However, I still couldn't figure out the meaning and I just felt uncomfortable watching the movie for nothing.

I was sad to leave the movie, which I watched with great hopes, saying "thank God it's over".

Emily Blunt, Robert Downey Jr and Murphy are really great. Other than that, it's a waste.

6.title: painful truth
6.content:
Where do I start? Oh, yeah, it's 3 ****** hours long. T h r e e. I don't know about you, but 3 hours of bombs tired me. Cinematography was top tier and Cristopher Nolan delivered as he always does, as did Cillian Murphy. They are all expectational at their jobs, and as much as I was wowed by the effects and other camera choices, I was greatly disappointed overall. I could not enjoy the visuals, for I felt like I had been condemned to watch one of those documentaries you must write an essay about for history class.

And yes I am aware of the irony that I am complaining about that as if I don't rate music books and movies as a hobby, but really, try to understand.

A movie should make you want to express yourself - even if its bad or good or great or terrible. The problem with Oppenheimer was that I have nothing that makes me want to talk about it. Nothing unique to itself anyways. Sure, we could *all* converse of the great visuals and the acting, but these are not unique to this movie. Nolan's direction exists outside of Oppenheimer and Murphy's acting is arguably even more expectational in other projects.

So why would I want to talk about this one? The plot is like it has been taken out of a history textbook and sprinkled atop with a flimsy romantic interest. Truly disappointing!!

And again - I can somewhat see how writing this can be contrary to the point I'm making but I am not writing about this movie because I want to, I'm writing because this evoked not a single sentiment as I watched it and that shouldn't be the case for such a beloved movie.

6.title: Can't understand half the dialogue
6.content: Christopher Nolan really screwed up here. He joined the scores of other Hollywood movies where you can understand what the actors are saying only half the time. I didn't think it made any sense to switch between black and white and color. I think the sex scenes were gratuitous and unnecessary. They were more of a distraction. Don't get me wrong, I love watching naked women in movies, but this takes away from the storyline of this nonfiction film. I wish there had been some scenes from World War II in Europe. Yes, this movie was about only Oppenheimer, but to add a few scenes from the major events of the world at the time, the setting would've been better. The time period would've been more apparent. This is where the lack of clear dialogue makes the movie a failure. If you're not gonna show some scenes of Europe at war in WWII during this time, period, at least make the actors enunciate and sound clear.

6.title: TikTok like scenes
6.content:
For me this film felt like a disappointment in comparison to the trailer. I understand that trailers often show a glimpse of the film, and it is difficult to say whether it will actually actually meet the trailer expectations.

One of the main things that stood out to me, was that all scenes were very short. They jumped from one place to another, within a matter of 30 seconds or less, without giving some time to the audience to fully immerse themselves into the experience of each scene. This experience reminded me of watching some Tik Tok short videos (too many transitions and scene cuts), and giving users a little shot of high stimulation. For me, this also created some difficulty to follow the storey along during the film, since every little scene was somehow created to be "relevant" on its own and made it distracting.

It is a bit sad for me to reflect on this, because I felt that by bringing some high stimulation and short scenes to a film does not help our society to come down and relax, but instead to feed our society with more high stimulation, which already exist in so many places and I find to bring that forth even more to films is unnecessary.

In terms of the duration of the film, I felt that it was very long, and some parts could have been cut out and still convey the same message.

However, there were definitely some positive attributes, such as arriving at the period, when this actually took place, really good actors, amazing costume design and beautiful sense of aesthetics and cleanness. :)

6.title: Bring pillows and a blanket.
6.content: There's a reason this movie has been kept super under wraps-it's a biography most of all and not even an interesting one. I don't want to spoil but it centers on an event where they don't leave the room. Yes flashbacks and other things happen but this is not epic Christopher Nolan. Extremely disappointing. It's hard to Go on about a movie that really wasn't good but what was most disappointing was the waste of talent. There's a certain oscar winner that is basically a glorified extra until his big moment at the end. It almost felt like Nolan asked his friends to be in a movie and came up with a script after. Don't rush to a theater. Do not recommend.

6.title: Not nearly as good as I had expected
6.content:
As "Oppenheimer" (2023 release; 180 min.) opens, we are introduced to Robert Oppenheimer, generally known as the "father of the atomic bomb". Oppenheimer is being interrogated by some congressional subcommittee in 1954, at the peak of McCartyism, for his alleged links to communist people and causes. We then go to Cambridge, England where Oppenheimer is doing his graduate studies... At this point we are 10 minutes into the movie.

Couple of comments: this is the latest oeuvre (don't call it just a film from writer-producer-director Christopher Nolan. Let me state upfront that I am a huge fan of his works, and that surely he is one of the leading filmmakers of this generation. I absolutely loved Tenet, Dunkirk and Inception, just to name those. As you can imagine, with all of the critical acclaim and box office success this movie has been getting, I came to the theater with pretty high expectations. What I saw on the big screen did not match my expectations, I'm sorry to say. I never felt truly engaged by the movie. I never felt emotionally invested in Oppenheimer the man. On top of that, the movie seemingly went on forever. This negates the fine leaf performance from Cillian Murphy, and several others. I had hoped to see this in XD (the biggest screen at Cinemark), but alas by this weekend (the 3rd weekend of its release), "Oppenheimer" was relegated to a regular screen, unfortunately. Bottom line: is Oppenheimer a 'bad' movie? Of course not. But I can only tell you that my high expectations were not met, and that this wasn't nearly as enjoyable as Nolan's other recent releases.

"Oppenheimer" was released several weeks ago on the same day as "Barbie", creating a "Barbenheimer" effect that benefitted both movies. "Oppenheimer" has received nearly universal critical acclaim and I expect that it will be in the running for many awards when the awards season rolls along. If you are a fan of Christopher Nolan's earlier works, I'd readily suggest you check this out, and draw your own conclusion.

6.title: too long
6.content: Somehow it didn't impress me, It was too long for my taste and I watched it four times, watching it in one piece in the cinema would probably knock me out. I didn't even know about the politics, so I didn't even know the figures, but Strauss was kind of an idiot that you might wonder if he didn't have fingers in the assassination of jfk after all. . I would only be interested in the development of the bomb, not the politics around it, and there wasn't much of it, at least not from my point of view, and if it was, it was so uninspiring. 6.title: Overall a decent movie but not worth the hype
6.content:
The kind of movie which peaked at the moments leading to the main event rather than the main event. Honestly, was a bit disappointed considering the hype it got . The politics , which is there substantially in the film was kind of boring and lengthy . Not a fan of the explosion or the sound effects considering the hype the film got in that part

Cinematography was next level , just as what to expect from a Christopher Nolan movie .

Acting was outstanding. Suprised by how well Emily blunt did the scenes and instilled a whole new wow factor to the movie . Also the Black and white IMAX shots were also beautiful which gave a different feel to the movie . Also , try to understand basics of atomic reactions and bombs to grasp the scientific aspects of the movie better before you watch it .

6.title: Disappointed, boring politics
6.content:
I expected much more from this film, I found it too long and, unfortunately, quite boring.

All the actors are exceptional, don't get me wrong, but too little space is given to the technique of building the bomb compared to the politics. As an Italian, I believe that Enrico Fermi's role deserves more space, considering his contribution to the Manhattan project.

In the explosion scene I would have expected to perceive the true power of the bomb, making the most of the impressive acoustics of a cinema hall... instead I got two minutes of muted scenes, with beautiful vivid flames yes, but ending in a mushroom cloud barely visible on the dark background.

The political intrigue organized by Strauss for the Cabinet job was as engaging as reading an old calendar... it could (should) have been replaced by a written epilogue.

6.title: Full of fillers
6.content: The hype was real. I was very excited to watch this movie, only to be disappointed. The screenplay was poor, and some of the dialogues were vague, attempting to appear important. There seems to be a challenge in translating that complex timeline onto the screen from a director's perspective, and unfortunately, Nolan did not succeed in doing so. The scenes failed to capture the gravity or urgency of the situation-the task at hand. By the end of the movie, it remains unclear who truly invented the atomic bomb; however, Oppenheimer's directorial skills seemed more influential than his scientific expertise. The drama of affairs, communism, and excessive smoking was overplayed scene after scene. The only redeeming aspect of the film, in my opinion, was the quantum world CGI effects depicting atoms-a visual element Nolan should consider emphasizing in modern films.

6.title: This is an objectively mediocre movie
6.content:
Unexceptional film making. I found it to be both anxious and oppressive as it relentlessly jumps continuously through what can only be described as long and exhausting. It's 3 hour runtime is taxing, fragmented and crawls by. This movie could be an hour less without having any real effect on the story. It is challenging to watch and will easily get away from the viewer.

We are introduced to the father of the atomic bomb and the question of whether he was a communist or not. Theoretical physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer is recruited by the United States government to oversee a top secret operation intended to develop the world's first atomic bomb. The film attempts to convey the complexities of World War 2, cold war history, and to bring a quick end to the war. These are truly some of the most important events and questions of the 20th century and how it still affects everyone decades later.

I'm left with the feeling that Oppenheimer just doesn't deliver. I certainly don't feel the need to rush out and see it again anytime soon. In fact, I'm sure I won't ever endure the painful 3 hour experience again. I guess I was expecting something a little more entertaining.

6.title: Worst movie from Nolan
6.content:
I am huge Nolan fan and usually I love biography movies (and books). Also I love history, so my expectations were high - maybe too high. I also read how well Nolan's team planned and executed that big bang. But I felt it wasn't real nuclear explosion, so illusion was broken. Also the pace and event to focus - I would have chosen different route. Lewis Strauss character had too big role in movie, of course because of courtroom part of movie. But no, I don't think that Lewis Strauss is important at all. Not important as historian character and not interesting character.

Also, It was surprising how much sex this movie contained. To make it less boring? Nolan explains "the aspect of his sexuality, his way with women, the charm that he exuded, it's an essential part of his story." Do I wanted to see this? No. The only feeling this movie left - was emptiness. Still, there were some interesting history bits that I didn't remember or know, like that hypothetical chain reaction after detonation. And actors were great.

6.title: If it was shorter it would be better
6.content:
This film is long. Too long.

In the first two hours not much happened, at least it felt like not a lot happened. It was lacking the personal struggle that Oppenheimer probably felt with making the bomb and the other scientists. It felt like it was almost a Wikipedia page with no real emotions, about the struggle that it was. The music that was used through out the film felt not fitting and badly timed, which made it harder to get immersed into the film.

Oppenheimer is a film about a scientist who was the inventor of the first atomic bomb, the bombs that were used on Hiroshima and Nagasaki. It follows the life of Oppenheimer from his years in university to the time more than 10 years after the bomb.

The last hour was the best it finally starts to get interesting with things happening and not it just dragging on. The acting was also great it made it believable that it was set in that time and that the actors were the actual people they portrayed.

I would say it is not worth it to watch it. If it was an hour shorter or so I would recommend it, but it isn't worth it to waste 3 hours of your life on it.

Side note: There is no Dutch in this film although they claim it is spoken.

6.title: Badly needed editing
6.content:
I have several issues with the film: it is too long, too many characters introduced without context, the time jumps made it difficult to follow, the real issues the film addresses needed more exposition (which scenes could have replaced the numerous metaphorical displays intended to represent Oppenheimer's genius, thinking and emotions).

The first half is very choppy with cuts every few seconds and countless angle and perspective jumps on each scene. I guess the director, cinematographer and editor felt the subject matter involved so many simple conversations that the audience would get bored.

It's too bad they didn't pick an issue and explore it fully rather than give many storylines haphazard coverage. The betrayal was obvious but the second half focused on a complicated structure to allow a big reveal.

Finally, the actual bomb construction, how it worked, and the tests were barely presented (the first test of a nuclear detonation has been done better in nany other films) and the destruction and death from its use in Japan needed a graphic depiction.

6.title: Not as good as they say. Bad start. Great ending. Makes you think. Very Watchable.
6.content:
I really love all of Christopher Nolan films and he's always been one of my favourites in film.

With almost 500 000 votes after only some months after being released, "Oppenheimer" is one of the biggest films in some time. I wanted too see this since it got released. I felt it should be a must watch and i finally got the chance to watch it.

The very deep manuscript is really well written!

You can early notice its a strongly visual and beautiful piece!

Editing, acting and soundtrack is very good!

I really enjoy deep questions about physics and the universe. I really wish i ccould say i really enjoyed this film. But i cant unfortunately. Yes, its a good film. But not more then that.

Its very confusing and abit difficult to fully understand unless you have a degree in physics. Its very difficult put together, which makes it difficult for the viewer to follow the line in the film. But it gets much better after an hour or so into the film.

Great last hour! And great last line of the script!

Pretty difficult to decide which rating it deserves. The start was pretty bad. But i definitely think the last 2 hours alone deserves a 7/10.

Nolan puts a interesting psychological, moral and ethical perspective on the use of weapons. And it makes you think that final question: Was Robert Oppenheimer good or bad?

Great! But Not Nolans best!

Not as good as they say. A very watchable and a good film, but don't expect too much.

6.title: Very disappointed
6.content: Just came back from the cinema. I'm feeling very disappointed about this movie. Best director and great actors&actresses, but the movie is way worse than other Nolan's works. I didn't have even one psychological fluctuation during this 3-hour period and almost fell in asleep for a few times. Please excuse my personal opinion. No disrespect to anyone. I didn't have even one psychological fluctuation during this 3-hour period and almost fell in asleep for a few times. Please excuse my personal opinion. No disrespect to anyone.

6.title: Compelling, but lacks substance. A movie for the TikTok generation.
6.content:
The first hour of the movie screams "afraid of losing my audience". At points it's almost like a trailer, with random lines thrown one after the other. It gets better from the bomb test onward, then the last half an hour is completely unnecessary, just like the entire character of Downey Jr, despite his great acting.

The lead was truly inspiring acting, but had little to work with, and there's close to no character development, it's a 3 hour puddle that's afraid to go into any depth, very fast paced and compellingly directed. He's feeling sorry, then he's not feeling sorry, then he's feeling sorry again. Confusing af.

The movie is made for people with ADHD and Tiktok addiction, jumping back and forth between 1000 timelines, that they had to make one black and white just to not lose the audience. Why make a drama if you're so afraid of it?

The sound and music make me think Nolan has a hearing problem. It's so loud it's distracting. I guess he wants to reproduce the feeling of attending a concert, or cover all the possible people getting bored and talking during the movie. Who knows?

The script has a lot of cheap Hollywood tropes sprinkled throughout. Definitely not a masterpiece, albeit an entertaining movie. You gain nothing by watching it. No substance. Might have watched a Nolan movie about drying paint and would have been just as good, and just as hollow.

Conclusion: it's compelling and you won't get bored, but don't expect any substance or character depth.

6.title: Disappointing
6.content: This movie watches like a three hour trailer. The actors are good and the cinematography is great, but the movie itself is a fragmented mess without any real dynamics. All scenes seem to have the same intensity. Lots of dialogue and uninteresting sidestories. The director failed to make choices about leaving some stuff out of the movie and tried to cram too many story lines into the script. The result is that some story lines are quite superficial while others linger way to long on particular topics. And thats what makes this movie quite boring. What happened to the art of telling a good story?

6.title: Focus of the story is wrong
6.content:
The main focus of this film is on the political story after making the bomb. There's not enough detail on how Oppenheimer lead a group of Nobel prize winning scientists to overcome various challenges in the Manhattan project (e.g. How they extracted enough uranium, design choices of the bomb). The success of the Manhattan project overall the biggest achievement in his lifetime and what people should know more about, not the intrigue with politicians and such detailed security trial.

70mm film is quite clear most of the time, especially ommersive when the black edges disappear on imax screen, but there're occasional defects (big black dots last for a few seconds, or flashing white background). Sound track is good, though not as great as Zimmer's sound tracks. Sound effects sometimes felt too sudden and loud.

6.title: It's a good film but a little boring and doesn't focus on the most interesting parts of the story
6.content:
The film is more about personal vendattas and attempts to grab political benefits than about the discovery itself.

Much of the film is about hearings to damage Oppenheimer's reputation and career and the downfall of the person who did it.

I hate to say it but it was a little boring. It's beautifully shot and superbly acted and not a bad film at all but for me it was a bit cowardly.

I disagree with the reviews that say it brought up important ethical dilemmas and issues. The film only ever so briefly touches upon them. In fact the damage the bomb did is barely mentioned and the ethics are given a cursory glance at best. The only ethics I think it did quite well was to question if Oppenheimer really had an issue with continued and developed nuclear bombs for moral reasons or if it was about him retaining power.

6.title: Oppenheimer: An Ambitious Yet Disappointing Biopic
6.content:
*Context:* "Oppenheimer," directed by Christopher Nolan, promised a riveting biography of Robert Oppenheimer and the creation of the atomic bomb, but unfortunately, it veered off course and left viewers wanting more. The film focused primarily on discussions surrounding Oppenheimer's security clearance and Strauss' confirmation hearing, failing to deliver on its marketed premise.

*Negative aspects:* The negative aspects of "Oppenheimer" are quite pronounced. Running for nearly three hours, the film was heavily laden with discussions, ego clashes, and court room drama, rather than exploring the intriguing world of atomic bomb creation and the scientific brilliance that shaped history. Although the discussions and courtroom drama were needed but at the cost of A-bomb development process, was something not anticipated at all. The Trinity test bomb scene, while boasting great sound design, suffered from inefficient visuals that did not live up to expectations (as promised before release).

Complexities & non linear narrative again: Adding to the film's complexity, a non-linear storytelling approach left many viewers perplexed and struggling to grasp the sequence of events and the significance of certain conversations. The omission of pivotal moments, such as Oppenheimer's childhood years and the aftermath of World War II, hindered the film's ability to provide a holistic portrait of the brilliant scientist and visionary.

*Few positive aspects:* On a positive note, the film's sound design and soundtrack deserve acclaim for its flawless execution. Additionally, the performances of the cast were commendable, with RDJ delivering a noteworthy portrayal.

*Conclusion:* In conclusion, "Oppenheimer" embarked on a bold journey to depict one of the most significant periods in history, yet it ultimately fell short of achieving its full potential. The film's preoccupation with discussions and courtroom drama overshadowed the opportunity to delve deeper into the fascinating world of atomic science.

*Final words:* "Oppenheimer" falls short as a biopic, failing to showcase the crucial A-bomb development process and attacks. While the sound design is impressive, the film left me unsatisfied, yearning for a deeper exploration of historical events. A missed opportunity to deliver a compelling narrative on a pivotal figure in history. It was marketed a "biopic thriller" but ended up being "biopic courtroom drama thriller".

6.title: I expected lots of things - certainly not what i got
6.content:
Christopher Nolans Filmography is one of the most respected of all time. And I think it´s deserved. But this time Nolan did not nearly reach the level of his previous movies. Oppenheimer starts so confusing you can not grasp what is going on. The timelines switch almost randomly and scenes that feel important are stopped just to pick them up again at a random point later on.

In addition to that, Robert Oppenheimer ist portrayed as a maniac-like man, who is obsessed with atoms and quantom-physics, which is shown through trip-like sequences. This man shown in the movie is nothing like the man I know from the interviews he gave post bombing. I do not see the man who spoke with tears in his eyes, regretting what he did.

And to add to all of that, Nolan (of course) has to build in a twist. But this twist is so useless, it actually bothered me. Not every great movie has to have a twist but seemingly Nolan thinks otherwise.

The movie does get better after the first one and a half hours. The skipping between the timezones declines a bit by then. But towards the end, when all the times finally come together, for me all hope was already lost. The end for me almost feels like a teaser for the cold war. The building of the rockets is seen and Oppenheimer constantly tries to prevent a arms race. That is not how Nolan used to work. And I know Nolan can do better. But he didn´t this time.

Sadly, this movie was not was I expected. But you can´t always get what you want, right? And atleast all the actors did a great job, especially Cilian Murphy.

6.title: slow and rather boring
6.content:
Maybe if you really love the style you will like it, but 3 hours is too much for this script, it is just too slow, like its intention is to be long. At times it is enjoyable, but if you are the kind who likes action movies (I am not, and still find it boring), you will most probably have problems enjoying this movie.

Cillian Murphy is rather the same as in 'Peaky Blinders', I do not see him getting out of that role, the same facial expressions, tone...and smoking. I would have imagined Oppenheimer a bit different, not so 'british' as he is.

It is not a bad movie, but rather a boring movie. It is also predictable, at least for me it was.

Also, I am not a fan of black and white films, and I do not see the reason for doing it as such. Maybe if you are, you will understand it better. It all comes to personal taste in the end.

6.title: 3 hours with 90% dialogue and confusing time jumps
6.content: After 2 and a half hours, you realize that it all revolves around the conflict between Oppenheimer and Strauss, who originally hired him to create the Atom Bomb. Strauss later tried to undermine him simply because he didn't want to give Oppenheimer so much credit. Other topics such as competition with the Nazis, how the bomb was made, Oppenheimer's relationship with Eisenstein, and his love life are only briefly touched upon. There is a continuous musical score accompanied by overwhelming sound effects to alleviate the boredom. You are relieved when things become slightly clearer at the end what is the focus of the movie and especially that the film is finely over.

6.title: The Hearing of Levi Strauss
6.content:
Oppenheimer Review (that absolutely nobody asked for):

Acting 10/10 Directing 8/10 Script 3/10 Pacing 8/10 Structure 4/10 Emotion 3/10 Story 2/10

Wonderfully acted out piece of propaganda.

Matt Damon & Benny Safdie really stood out to me amongst the all star cast. Stellar performances.

Cillian Murphy was hypnotizing to watch as always.

RDJ will almost certainly get an Oscar nod.

The talent in front and behind the screen did a fantastic job of drawing in the audience, I was on the edge of my seat half the movie!

How did almost no other character in this entire film have any sort of negative feelings about the bombs dropping in Hiroshima & Nagasaki whatsoever, except for Oppenheimer. Nobody blinked an eye when they mentioned Pearl Harbor, and when news hit that Hitler invaded Poland all they said was "You've been upstaged." No emotion. Pathetically unrealistic.

David Kromholtz had one of the only characters who felt true this whole movie.

The movie painted Oppenheimer out as a martyr, and Truman (Gary Oldman) as the button man, which is just historically wrong. They literally brought Oldman in just to sell the biggest lie of the whole film.

"It wasn't you, it was me."

Not a single mention of his occult involvement nor his influence and decision to drop those bombs.

Lastly, because of what this movie both opened and closed with, the black & white narration of the film, it would seem be more pertinent to title this film: The Hearing of Levi Strauss or something similar.

A few masterful scenes cannot make up for this intentional catastrophe. Very disappointing.

6/10.

6.title: Good, but not that good
6.content: While Christopher Nolan is a superb director, the film did little for me. That may be because of my age. I found the 1980 BBC miniseries "Oppenheimer" starring Sam Waterston as the famous scientist better written, better acted, and much more informative than the current film. Having said that, Nolan's film, no doubt, will be popular and informative for the younger generations which have shorter attention spans, aversions to a TV series produced four decades ago, and probably little knowledge of what it was like to grow up under the threat of nuclear annihilation. The current film tries to cover three segments of Oppenheimer's life: his younger years, the Los Alamos/Trinity segment of the Manhattan Project, and his persecution after WWII because of his communist ties. All three segments are sort of shuffled together like a poker deck between hands. The intercutting, while done well, is often jarring and confusing, but that is the hand dealt to feature film producers since they must stuff their work into the time slots allotted to them by theater owners. The miniseries, like a novel, allows the story to be stretched out in more lifelike proportions. Much has been said about the use of 70mm film, and even the producers suggested this large format added to the majestic nature of the subject matter, which by any standard is epic. However, the technical aspects of the film, while adding eye candy to the production, did little for the Oppenheimer story, which is epic in its own right. Large parts of the dialogue were difficult to decipher, a common problem with today's motion picture and television productions. Diction is no longer an essential aspect of the art form, having fallen to the god of realism rather than articulation. And the music was nothing short of banal, with an overpowering mix that got in the way of the story and the film. In short it was unimaginative and too loud, like Dick Wolf's more recent television productions such as his "Chicago" franchise. Oppenheimer tells an important story to new generations, and that may be its saving grace. For my taste, give me the BBC and it's 1980 miniseries with Waterston.

6.title: Not so good
6.content: Unnecessarily timelines (that in memento were reasonable), too much presence of scientists (should have subtitles scientists name in their appearances)i think most viewers were from science background, they could have been comfortable if scientists name appeared as subtitles , background music was as expected, enjoyed it to fullest,cillian murphy is at his best. I expected Hiroshima scene ,should have been in to add some emotions, christopher need to learn a lot from Rajamouli in adding emotions,frankly speaking those who are admiring the movie are not rating honestly, half of viewers were leaving out in half time.

6.title: fooled
6.content:
This film left me with a slight hangover. I went there expecting to see a film about the development of the first atomic bomb by Oppenheimer.

Nothing could be further from the truth, more than 80% of it was about his private life and his subsequent persecution about his alleged communist sympathies.

This was not what I went to the cinema for and I felt a bit fooled.

I had hope that it would have been interesting, but I should have known better, Nolan has never really been my favorite director.

The actors and actresses are all doing fine, but the excess of drama started to irritate me at a certain point.

6.title: Brilliant cast, boring film
6.content:
I love Christopher Nolan, one of my favourite directors. But he seems now to just be doing complicated difficult to follow films just for the sake of it, because he has to. People might say I'm stupid for not "Getting it" I did get it, he just took the long way round to explain it all. There was just no need for this. It should have been a 10/10 film. A man was snoring on the same row as me in the cinema, people talking getting agitated with it, because there was no need for this 3 hour slog of a film.

Saying that what saved the film was brilliant acting. The story was brilliant but like I said just too drawn out and annoying to follow dialogue, especially in the last hour or so. There's some Oscar's in this film though for sure. Cillian Murphy and Robert Downey Jr excellent.

6.title: Watchable, interesting, beautiful but not particularly entertaining
6.content: It's a good movie, some have called it a 'masterpiece' and 'an important movie in our history'. It's watchable, the filming is beautiful and filmed in the Nolan style that most people love, it's a good story and the amount of famous actors is insane, clearly they fall over themselves these days to be in a Nolan movie. The film is long and although we'll written with some great performances I felt it lacks any real entertainment and tension with the exception of the test scenes, it feels a very political story. For me Nolan has clearly peaked, Batman, inception and interstellar where up there in most peoples top 5 of all time, Dunkirk, Tenet and now this are nowhere near that standard, it's worth a watch but don't expect an IMBD top 25 movie.

6.title: Not in the least extraordinary
6.content:
I saw no extraordinary directional skills watching Oppenheimer that have not been seen in any other movies in the past 100 years.

The two hours I watched out of a three-hour movie was okay. At the two-hour mark after Oppenheimer and Truman meeting in the Oval Office, I stopped watching, turned the sound off, and continued teleworking. In the third hour, the movie went into endless black-and-white scenes of Washington hearings or meetings regarding Oppenheimer's Communist affiliation, which I did not care to listen to.

The movie began with too much switching from B&W to color scene; what was the purpose? The abrupt switching from one scene to another was also annoying; l reviewed another movie with the same issues. Why do directors or editors do that? I've never seen that issue in older films, only in the past 20 years.

In older movies, each scene has a lingering ending on the actor's face, subject, or scene.

Why did the scene during the Washington hearing on Capital Hill in B&W? Did Nolan have a not-so-kind hidden message toward Washington politics?

The woman Oppenheimer met at the party 'Jean' storyline was severely underwritten. We never saw scenes of civilized build-up relationships; all we got were disconnect scenes, a slam-bam-thank-you-mam, an unnecessary 'F' scene, Oppenheimer informing her of his pending wedding scene, an argument by trash cans scene, and Jean's suicide scene.

Why was Jean mad when she first appeared in the movie? It seems like she didn't like Oppenheimer, then in the next scene, in the blink of an eye, they were half naked, sexing each other. It was the most outrageous scene-to-scene I have ever seen in a movie.

As for the wife, what was her problem, why did she drink, and where were we, the audience, supposed to guess?

The naked sexual simulation scene at a hearing or meeting was from out of left field. Does Nolan do this in all his films?

If you like horseback riding, there are three or four scenes; I guess Oppenheimer loved riding horses in the desert.

As for the acting, Cillian Murphy was good, but nothing spectacular. The question is, should he win best actor for his eyes?

Robert Downey Jr., Emily Blunt, and Matt Damon, we're all good.

Out of a 10 rating, I subtracted 4, leaving a 6 rating. The four were removed because of the atrocious storyline of Jean, the girl Oppenheimer met at the party.

6.title: it was like vanilla ice cream: not too bad and never too good
6.content:
It was like vanilla ice cream: not too bad and never too good. A very interesting topic, one of the biggest historical event but there was never a great moment in the movie. A very boring take on a larger than life topic. This could have been a movie that could inspire millions.

There was potential for several goosebump moment at many different points but it turned out to be a very okayish. Guy on my next sleep was sleeping. I never thought that a movie about bomb can be so bland. I wanted to like this movie but there was never a moment that i would take home.

Nolan is just taking significants world war event and turning them into forgettable average movies. After Dunkirk this is strike2.

6.title: Overrated by a long shot
6.content:
Quite disappointed. Story and timeline were all over the place. If you have never hear of Oppenheimer, you are still quite lost because the story line missed connecting to the audience. Really felt like I wasted 3.5 hours on a nice Sunday afternoon.

I'm really surprised that the story was missed so badly. I Mt feels like the writers strike had something to do with this but sadly it doesn't.

What a great opportunity it was that was missed to bring some important history to those that have forgotten or were just unaware.

Movie was 3 hours + the previews. It made it feel like I watched an old baseball game before the pitch clock.

6.title: Truly disappointed
6.content: It's the first time I have this thought about Nolan' a movie . This movie I just feel disappointed. The movie wants to make like a combination of documentary and story. But it just don't go . Einstein is not an old retired old man walking around the river to tell u what it's right . And I don't get any point about those two naked scenes. Literally it doesn't help anything but make the film level to R . Oppenheimer is one of the greatest scientists ever . And he doesn't know if he made this the government wouldn't throw it out ?it's so joke when they said cuz culture they don't throw it to Kyoto. Like peoples life are nothing than culture.

6.title: Didn't quite deliver
6.content:
This was an exhausting movie. While Nolan shows respect to his audience by providing a challenging plot to keep up with, viewers must actively listen to all the dialogue to follow along, a task which lasts the entire 3 hours. While the music and some of the visuals are great, the characters were not likable. Their complexity was evident but somehow non of them were relatable. The plot was detailed but seemed somewhat revisionist. The communists, the Japanese, and the protagonist himself were shown to be unjustly victimized. The movie is full of tension but never quite delivers. The payoff was entirely un-atomic. I don't see myself re-watching this movie.

My ears are still ringing the day after. Perhaps that was the point.

6.title: Worthy but overlong biopic
6.content:
Very detailed lengthy profile of Oppenheimer, in charge of America's race to develop the Atomic bomb by assembling a team of nuclear scientists.. Cillian Murphy must be a shoo in already as the next Oscar best actor winner. Strong support from Matt Damon and an unrecognisable Robert Downey junior.

Several members of the team had certain Communist leanings before WW2 and this continued throughout the project. As usual in Hollywood the contribution of British physicists was minimised, especially that of James Chadwick who was awarded a Nobel prize.

The nuclear tests in the desert are undeniably powerful and awe inspiring. The dropping of bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki certainly curtailed the was in the east. However, Nolan missed a trick by omitting archival footage of the explosions and their aftermath e.g. Pictures of damaged survivors suffering long term effects. The Hiroshima Peace Park should also be includes as a final scene.

6.title: Not What You are Expecting
6.content:
This movie has great actors and acting.

The problem is most people are going to expect a focus on the bomb as I did. There is not much focus on this.

One thing that annoys me when watching a movie is jumping back and forth through time. The story should be linear. An occasional flashback is ok, but this movie constantly jumps back and forth and it's irritating.

So what is this movie? It mainly focuses on communist intrigue and it is more like a courtroom drama than a movie about the first atomic bomb.

Part of the fault as mine as my expectations were different than what the movie provides, however if I knew it was more courtroom drama then A-bomb I would have skipped it.

6.title: A ok movie
6.content:
Yes there were some good scenes, especially the test in the desert. The rest is a bit confusing and rough, but I got it, it's Nolan's style. I can feel that this movie was shot in 57days. I would have preferred Ron Howard or Oliver Stone as director. Nolan's movie is for sure 1hour too long. The last hour is not necessary. Since Interstellar I start really doubting Nolan's skill. He is for sure light years behind a real genius Stanley Kubrick. He should not even try.

Dunkirk was ok but Tenet was a complete loss of my time. Of course this is my opinion. But this movie confirms that I don't like this director's new style.

6.title: A great movie is somewhere in the editing room
6.content:
Cons: impacient and overbearing, way too often feels like a trailer rather than a movie, it feels desperate and rushed despite being 3 hours long. The music is constantly loud and innapropiate, putting it plainly it ruins most scenes, big time. The scenes are short and constantly changing, rarely leaving any room for the characters to breathe and play out. It constantly has cuts to related physics footage in the middle of conversations, which is also super distracting.

The dialogue is weirdly witty in a self-indulgent thinks too highly of itself kinda way. It could also be often described as dumb/pretentious, that last part might sometimes just be a reflection of the egos of the characters of the movie, but at times it simply cannot be because it misrepresents the science that the characters would know, because they did it themselves.

The cinematography ain't nothing special but its not bad, serviceable

Pros:

despite being 3 hours long it isn't that boring at any point

The narrative flow of this movie is actually sensible and fluid, it only does not feel that way because of the editing, a better movie is there on the editing room, I wonder if they f it up on purpose so they can sell a director's cut later. Another reason why the pacing is kinda odd is that its fast but feels rushed, thats because the scope is too big, they wanted to portray the bomb investigation, the life of oppenheimer, the trial and the philosophy of the bomb. So even though the movie feels worse because of it, with it being as bad as it is its good that it covers a lot! If the film had the weird pacing covering what a normal film covers it would be much worse! The ambitious scope makes it way more interesting.

Despite it not being to my taste, the fast paced adhd vibe it offers can be what some people prefer, one of my friends loved it despite normaly having a hard time watching movies, not everything must be smart to be enjoyable, with the correct perspective this movie might be right for you.

It's genuinely beautiful, has its own style.

The acting is great, specially by cillian murphy.

It's hilarious how out of place remi malek feels in the movie in his small chr until the important scene and how oppenheimer treats him like s every singly appearance he sees it.

There are moments when a montage does fit, the music is not disrupting the scene and the fast editing fits. In those moments all thats left are the immaculate visuals and productor value. Also the music ain't bad, its just used awfully.

The sequence of the young oppenheimer back in germany has some great enjoyable creative presentation even if the problems are still felt. There are other parts that take the same creative freedoms and deliver, its great, at times it feels like a movie that truly pushes film-making.

Conclusion: some elements are used innapropiately in a great ammount of scenes, but the story is interesting and nearly every aspect of the film is handled, on practical sense at least, impecably. Amazing film on a technical level.

6.title: Disappointment from Nolan
6.content: I am a big fan of Christopher Nolan and my favorite films are Batman trilogy, Interstellar, and Inception in that order. I went in to see this movie with huge expectations. However, I came out disappointed. The movie started off well and I was looking forward to the second and third acts. First of all, I expected a lot more insights into various challenges or hurdles these scientists have faced while trying to come up with the atom bomb and how they overcame those. None of that was shown. Given that this movie is being made in 2023, there is huge scope for showing the trinity test in a much more impactful and fear-inducing way. What we instead see is a silent explosion that is not even close to the scale I was expecting on an IMAX screen. Yes, it is close to reality as all the scientists were witnessing this from 20 miles away, so they wouldn't hear the sound first but I didn't go in there to see a documentary. And the whole third act tested my patience. It is continuous rambling and talk from various characters without any emotional connect or impact. Waiting for the next movie of Nolan and hope he returns to the larger than life stories again.

6.title: just seen not madly impressed
6.content:
Finally got to see the great Oppenheimer but unfortunately on a laptop screen so I guess a lot of the effect was lost. Nevertheless, I still found it long and confusing. 6.content:
It was ok... I learnt some history, however, with the hype and Nolan I expected more. This movie felt lacking in cinematic creativity. The scenes of Oppenheimer experiencing internal turmoil whilst holding a tough exterior were great. I really liked the editing and effects during this speech scene and was wanting much more of it. 6.title: A Mix of Quality Ingredients and Missed Opportunities
6.content:
Oppenheimer is a very typical Christopher film in that it features many of his routine trademarks, strengths, and weaknesses. It has the loud, intense score and sound design that he is known for, which I found effective here. It has beautiful production design and cinematography. It has a wonderful and very deep cast. Cillian Murphy is fantastic. However, that wonderful and very deep cast includes very few women, and Emily Blunt and Florence Pugh are largely wasted.

Oppenheimer isn't so much a history lesson as it is a portrait of the man. Yet in that regard, it still feels incomplete. Some aspects of his life seem quite clear: we can see that he is an engaging teacher and leader. However, the film doesn't really explore his personal relationships. Throughout the film, we are told that Oppenheimer's important personal relationships include Jean (Florence Pugh), Kitty (Emily Blunt), and his brother Frank (Dylan Arnold), but we are never really shown anything meaningful about them. In particular, we are never shown anything that illustrates why Oppenheimer is in love with Jean and Kitty. They were two very intelligent, complex, and interesting women, and it's disappointing that they are given so little to do. Additionally, you never see him actually interact with either of his children.

In part, this movie is about the internal conflict caused by creating such a powerful weapon. In one sequence, Oppenheimer has a vision of people affected by the atomic bombs. Christopher Nolan's daughter has a cameo as a young woman whose skin is peeling off her face. Nolan explained the casting decision saying "...if you create the ultimate destructive power it will also destroy those who are near and dear to you. I suppose this was my way of expressing that in what, to me, were the strongest possible terms." However, Oppenheimer never seems to have that moment for himself. This destruction is never reflected back onto the people he loves. The people he sees in his visions are strangers.

The film has so many really wonderful elements and some powerful sequences, but I found that the avoidance of his personal life left a gaping hole. Even though it's a three-hour movie (with good pacing), it still only scratches the surface.

I do feel like this is a movie best seen in a theatre, largely due to the sound design. It's hard to recreate those big rumbling sounds and powerful silences at home.

6.title: Unnecesarily confusing and complicated
6.content:
I would not watch it again and I wouldn't recoomend the movie.

It's complicated, has too many characters I can't keep track of, it's too long, too focused on politics, and too many jumps in time.

Too many characters. I can't remember who is who or better said what they are and why are they relevant. Combined with time jumps it's confusing.

It's too long. Combined with time cuts and character numbers and the story it self, it's hard to keep attention. It became boring on top of confusiong.

Too many jumps in time. It's like Memento squared. Maybe I'm getting old. I loved memento. It was so different then. But compared to this one, Memento was *linear*. Memento went backwards in time but it was linear, you went back and each time you were explained the clip you just previusly watched and presented with some questions that would be answered in the next clip. Oppenheimer was all over the place.

I watched it at home with couple of friends and we were constantly asking each other when are we now? I know somthing about physics, technology and history and was still struggling to keep up because of all the time jumps. If I went to fetch a drink or went to the bathroom for a minute I would have to ask "what just happened" every time. ONe of the friends didn't know where the bombs were dropped in the war or when, how confusing the movie was for her?

It's so much focused on politics and Oppenheimer views. This in it self might be historically significant and impotant for the story, but the way the movie presents this is so convoluted that I couldn't make up my mind what Oppenheimer actually wanted. Just like Oppenheimer's opponents in the movie couldn't grasp where he stood politically and even if he is political or scientific. Just like Oppenheimer himself didn't know if he wanted to be political or scientific or in the middle? At the end of all that big movie part that is politics I'm not sure what I learned about it, what Oppenheimer was or what his enemies thought he was. It's confusion on all levels all arround multiplied by many characters time jumps which I know I keep repeating a lot.

Maybe I would watch it again if someone took the movie and made it linear time cut. I would be interested to see if that would be a better movie.

It's watchable. Not a "skip" recommendation, but not much more.

6.content:
I'm not an action junkie, i said Schindler's list was good. But i asked once again? What is the real struggle in oppenheimer's life? Because he made the trouble himself. His womanizer behaviour, he makes fun of strauss making strauss framed Him. He's making a bomb that could kill millions of life but then regret doing so?
