5.title: I have become hype, the average of biopics
5.content:
No human on the planet has a bigger cult of personality than Christopher Nolan. Not Trump, not Musk, not Messi, not Putin. No one.

His fans see everything he has done as a masterpiece. It's not just that he can't do no wrong, but that he can't do no average.

Yet that's exactly what this movie is. An average biopic.

Advertised as a visual masterpiece, it actually makes no difference whether you watch it in IMAX or not. Facial close ups and office meetings make up for 90% of the movie. Few desert shots and a very, very brief explosion scene don't warrant the price. Nor the hype.

Additionally, I'd say that the Terminator franchise presented the dangers of nuclear war far better and visually more stunning. Maybe even Stargate too.

Everything presented can be expected, many common character clichés are present. The runtime is another decision driven by Nolan's ego. The score was clever at times.

The spectacle is somewhat created by having a great actor fill every role, yet few are given any jobs that an average drama student couldn't fulfill.

I enjoy Nolan's work, bar Tenet, which was at least ambitious. Yet Oppenheimer is just coasting on reputation.

5.title: A disappointment
5.content:
A disappointment. Three wasted hours. What's the point of such a talented cast, excellent cinematography, make up etc., for a long, tiresome, and poorly told story?

The impression left is that this story should have been told in an 40-episode series, each episode lasting an hour, over 5 seasons. Instead, everything was condensed into a frenetic pace within 3 hours. Names and events were rushed, dozens of characters thrown in the audience's face, without adequate character development, cuts and transitions were too quick and too frequent, there was an overload of information, everything happened too fast.

Nolan has incredible talent and knows how to make cinema at a very high level, he has proven that before. But unfortunately he lost his touch here, in my limited perception as a layperson who loves good stories that are well told.

5.title: A Nolan miss for me, but make your own judgement.
5.content:
I find Christopher Nolan's films very hit and miss, nevertheless I'm still drawn to the cinema in the hope the latest release will be akin to one of my Nolan favourites.

Oppenheimer unfortunately for me was a bit of a miss.

I could appreciate this was a good biopic to cast on the big screen, however my thinking throughout was this could be better served over a longer series format. Multiple sections of the movie seem skirted over for me and would have been better served going into greater depth, that's even with this being a 3 hours in length.

There was a number of characters that were lost in the dialogue, which can be tricky to stick with if you don't have a predisposition to quantum physics. Many character names were quoted and I was scrambling on many occasion to remember which man in the suit and glasses they were referring to, there seemed to be so many of them!

Acting performances were solid, which I would expect with the stellar cast on show in this movie.

I'd say give it a watch and make your own judgement, but what was one of my more anticipated movies of 2023, I can confidently say won't be one of the standout releases of the year for me.

5.title: Tedious on several levels
5.content:
What has been negatively written before is mostly accurate, so I will concentrate on my greatest annoyances.

Sound editing. When the background music is so loud and obnoxious (drum beats especially) that you can't hear the actors speak, the sound editor must not have been paying attention. An occasional scene like this is okay, but a movie full of scenes where the dialogue is overshadowed is not. Almost the entire movie had the music volume way too high during quiet dialogue. This is a trend in movies and tv and needs to stop. The actors and dialogue are the stars; music is an enhancement. Or, in this case, a very serious distraction.

Film editing. At its most basic, this is a linear story, easy to understand. But the director opts for continuous cuts to the past or future, destroying the current scene and losing the audience's concentration. Why should I have to work so hard to keep all the pieces together due to the unrelenting flashbacks and flash forwards? It end up being a mess. Tedious. It is a straight forward story. Keep it simple. Why did Nolan make it so complicated to follow?

Length. The actual film is about 2 hours and 45 minutes, followed by about 15 minutes of credits. The length didn't bother me, but I felt tighter editing would have helped. The film felt a little sloppy.

Performances were great. Story was great. Costumes and period pieces were super too.

5.title: YAWN
5.content:
Christopher Nolan's incessant use of suspenseful music is a crutch heavily leaned on in Oppenheimer. It seems as though the filmaker believes that bombarding the audience with intense musical cues will create an illusion of tension and excitement. However it becomes evident that the music is attempting to compensate for what is simply a very boring story line!

Its an uninspired plot, which struggles to maintain even the faintest glimmer of interest. The runtime feels painfully stretched, leading to an inexplicable endurance test for viewers. I found myself counting the minutes until the credits mercifully rolled!!!

5.title: Bore fest
5.content:
I mean I don't know what most people saw here, but this was a bore fest. Amazing cast, great acting , superb cinematography and sound. But that's about it. Except few moments in the movie, rest was complete borefest. Half my theater was sleeping after 45 minutes. Werner Brothers might buy some reviewers to give great reviews and Nolan fan boys might go ga ga over it,.but that's usual with most of his movies. Box office, it won't last over few days.

I mean majority history of the atomic bomb was left put. The challenges with the actual science, material, building up those towns , the race for the bomb . Nothing. All interesting things were left put and the movie focuses on boring tale of oppenheimers trial. Seriously. You missed the most interesting part of that history.

5.title: Nolan relies on telling rather than showing.
5.content:
As I settled in to watch Oppenheimer, it quickly became apparent that the film suffered from what I like to call: "The Nolan Syndrome", three hours is an excessive runtime for a film that fails to hold the viewer's attention. By the time I reached the one-hour mark, I was already feeling weary and disengaged.

What struck me most was the lack of visual interest or excitement throughout the film. It felt as though you could simply listen to the audio and have virtually the same experience, as nothing was captivating or visually stimulating to hold one's attention. Nolan keeps insisting on Oppenheimer's brilliance without any meaningful demonstration of it.

Furthermore, characters were introduced in a rather lackluster manner, primarily through other characters talking about them or mentioning them by name, rather than being introduced organically through the progression of the story. Instead of experiencing richly crafted characters with depth and complexity, it felt like I was watching mere shadows of individuals, barely fleshed out enough to hold my interest. When you add the continuous barrage of loud background music. It felt as though Nolan was desperately trying to compensate for the film's shortcomings by bombarding us with noise, making it difficult to focus on the narrative. The constant flipping between timelines only adds to the confusion, distracting from any potential depth the story might have had.

Oppenheimer left me feeling profoundly underwhelmed and dissatisfied. The film's saving grace undoubtedly lies in the exceptional performances delivered by its cast but Christopher Nolan's reliance on telling rather than showing, coupled with the film's lack of visual intrigue and character development, ultimately resulted in a viewing experience that fell far short of expectations.

5.title: Good marketing caused the only IMAX 70mm theater in EU to be sold out for many weeks
5.content:
Brief summary: it wasn't worth it. Much better experience in IMAX 2D was e.g. Oblivion (including a soundtrack by M83). A much better WWII related story was e.g. The movie Enigma. A much better biopic story with flashbacks was e.g. Professor Marston & the Wonder Women

But if you're interested in American politics and intrigue, go for it. Pay attention to all the characters (and there are a lot of them), many will prove to be very important after another hour or two...

The only humor was for the initiated (Kurt Godel appreciating trees :-) to mention one instance).

One more metric: I categorize movies into several groups, the best ones I would go to the cinema again and again (and often do), the ones that impress me I want to see again in the cinema, and the others I have no interest in seeing repeatedly. Oppenheimer, unfortunately, I had to put in the latter group.

5.title: My heart feels nothing
5.content: Okay we all know who Nolan is and his style, I was also lucky enough to watch movies like Interstellar, Dark Knight and they were all great experiences, but unfortunately I'm not lying, not this time. No. Nolan tried very hard to get the Oscar he deserved. I'm happy for him. With this film, it's hard for the Academy to refuse to give Nolan an Oscar. Nolan has always been very fastidious about selecting information and putting it as accurately and scientifically as possible into his films. With this movie, the amount of information expressed in the dialogue is too much, the characters are like robots appearing and reading lines, the scenes change continuously, it is really difficult for some ordinary people to receive it all. Nolan tried to bring the filmmaking style of the 50s and 60s into Oppenheimer while still maintaining his own style. But with stories about superheroes or space exploration, we have something to wait for, a battle of wits, a door to outer space. As for a biographical film, Nolan's weakness appeared here, the emotional development of the character, love, hatred, sympathy? They are too few in this movie. I don't feel anything. Of course the top-notch music and scientific experiment sequences are impressive, but even with Murphy's good performance, Oppenheimer is still just an underwhelming character for me. Of course, this movie can satisfy those who love politics and science, but from an emotional perspective for the viewer, I am quite hesitant if I intend to watch it again. The questioning and response scenes are too long and have a lot of dialogue, while important scenes such as Oppenheimer's childhood, the motivation for his decision to participate in bomb making, the clearness in the marks of Oppenheimer's life, especially the connection between the main character and his two women, Jean and Kitty, even his brother Frank, is very weak and lacking. Even Robert's somewhat eccentric personality has not been expressed specifically. His conflict with Strauss, the story with Einstein, President Truman, are just like cameo scenes. Maybe I was waiting too much for a movie with less dialogue and important characters that brought more emotions. With this movie, "I will leave my clothes on the clothesline"

5.title: Nolan's "Kitchen Sink" Approach Makes This Long-Winded Biopic Hard to Follow
5.content:
Christopher Nolan's ambitious "Kitchen Sink" approach proves to be both a strength and a hindrance in his latest film, "Oppenheimer," a sprawling biopic that delves into the complex life of J. Robert Oppenheimer, the controversial figure behind the atomic bomb. While Nolan's decision to write the screenplay adds a personal touch, it also leads to an overwhelming narrative that can be hard to follow across its three-hour runtime.

Nolan's attempt to humanize Oppenheimer walks a fine line between insightful character study and hagiography. The film presents Oppenheimer as a multi-dimensional figure with sympathetic qualities, highlighting his humanitarian efforts during the Spanish Civil War, his pivotal role in developing the atomic bomb that ended World War II, and his subsequent guilt over the devastating civilian casualties in Hiroshima and Nagasaki. The portrayal, however, veers into portraying him as a liberal icon, occasionally overshadowing his complexities.

Although Nolan takes a fleeting stab at revealing Oppenheimer's darker side, these glimpses are limited. References to his almost-lethal apple poisoning incident during his student days and his questionable associations with the Communist party are a good start along with touching on his tumultuous affair that ends in tragedy and ethical lapse looking the other way when a colleague suggests sharing secrets with the Soviets. Nolan could have delved deeper into these and additional flaws to provide a more nuanced depiction of his character.

Critics have rightfully pointed out Nolan's missed opportunity to visually capture the catastrophic aftermath of the nuclear explosions in Japan. While he includes a scene exploring the decision-making process behind the bomb's target, the film falls short in conveying the true horrors of the aftermath, which diminishes the weight of Oppenheimer's responsibility.

Chronological jumps and an abundance of characters and events, particularly focused on Oppenheimer's closed-door hearings before the Atomic Energy Commission in 1954 and the 1959 Congressional Hearings involving Lewis Strauss, the former AEC chairman who championed the end to Oppenheimer's security clearance, contribute to the film's disjointed feeling. The hearings often come across as dramatized public transcripts, lacking depth and character development. However, these segments do succeed in offering a historical lesson on Oppenheimer's life and the pressures he faced.

Nolan shines in his portrayal of the Manhattan Project and the lead-up to the first atomic bomb test. By delaying the explosion's sound and emphasizing the participants' reactions, he creates a compelling and suspenseful scene.

The performances of Cillian Murphy as Oppenheimer, Robert Downey Jr. As Lewis Strauss, and Matt Damon as General Leslie Groves add authenticity to the film, while Emily Blunt and Florence Pugh's roles as Oppenheimer's wife and mistress lack impact.

Perhaps the film's most glaring misstep is the inclusion of a gratuitous nude fantasy lovemaking scene between Murphy and Pugh during the AEC hearing, which detracts from the serious tone and narrative flow. In addition, the constant obtrusive musical score does little to enhance the drama.

As an educational history lesson, "Oppenheimer" succeeds in providing insight into the key events of Oppenheimer's life and the historical context of the atomic bomb. Nevertheless, Nolan's narrative choices occasionally hinder the film's potential by overwhelming it with details and characters, leaving the viewer longing for a more focused exploration of its central figure. Rather than attempting to cover every facet of Oppenheimer's life, a more nuanced and restrained approach would have allowed the film to truly shine.

5.title: A Fissil Film
5.content: We came away from watching Oppenheimer with mixed reviews and everyone agreed the movie was confusing. First, the narrative about a famous, soft spoken American is masked by "mood-music" throughout most of the film. As a result, the viewer is forced to read lips in order to understand the plot. Second and typical of Nolan's films, the plot skips around to the point where it becomes difficult to follow. This Hollywood "Hop-Scotching" produces audio & visual enhancements, but it also shrouds the spinal message of the movie. Additionally, the film also contains dozens of actors making it impossible to track who is who and what their positions are. Oppenheimer is technically accurate but not smooth in its presentation. I would recommend to those who have't seen it to read up about Robert Oppenheimer beforehand so you can gain an appreciation of his controversial biography. Oppenheimer is worth seeing, but it'll be awhile before I'll view the film again, perhaps with captions, so I can digest what message Nolan is trying to portray. Non-fictional movies about a major historical event shouldn't be fragmented in its message, as the Trinity test suggests.

5.title: Not a film for everyone
5.content:
I tried to like this movie, really I did, but I just could not bring myself to do it. While the movie does speak about it's theme in great lenght it just does it in the most monotonous and uninteresting possible way there is. Not only does watching this movie feel like a chore, it feels like the actors themselves forced to play in this most and just weren't enthusiastic about it at all.

The first 2 hours or so, up until the detonation of the first bomb, it was still okay, you are still compelled to keep on watching as the film slowly builds up to the moment of the detonation. Too many times there seem to be scenes where nothing important happens and they are just fillers of some sort. There is also a lot of scene transitions that happen in such rapid succession and out of order that sometimes it's hard to even know what story and narration you are supposed to follow. Unfortunately, the detonation of the bomb was for me the culmination of this whole film, and everything that comes after that regarding Oppenheimer's security status and his guilt feels way too stretched out and way too unnecessary, barring this meeting with President Truman.

Ultimately, despite my interest in history, I might not have had sufficent information to really immerse myself in the film, however as far as the film itself goes, the aspect are quite weak.

5.title: Oppenheimer is not a very enjoyable movie to watch
5.content:
I will start this review by stating that I have yet to compare the movie to the "true story" of Oppenheimer. I think that is a good thing as I do not want my review to be based solely on whether or not the movie is historically accurate, but whether or not I enjoyed the movie overall.

It is 3 hours long. It feels like it is 3 hours long. From a strictly movie perspective, I would advise against thinking this movie will be as riveting as the trailers make it. It is not.

Most of the problem regarding this movie centers around the understory, which by the end becomes rather long and boring. I wonder how historically accurate it is too?

I cannot go any further other than to state that Oppenheimer is to documentary movies what the movie, JFK, was to documentary movies. The entire time watching it I felt it was Hollywood script and not reality.

The one thing I did like about the movie was the overall message that you arrive at. In today's world, I thought it was an important message. But if you are looking for a great Christopher Nolan film, watch, The Dark Knight. It was far better than Oppenheimer in terms of enjoyability.

Even great directors need to realize that historical cinema needs to be told with a level of actual human emotion that is accurate and to the point. It works much better for real life events than to try to come up with something you think will work as Hollywood "based on a true story" movie making. The acting is great, but the film is not.

But there is no doubt that for whatever reason people seem to really like this film based on the current review ratings. Overall, I thought it had a good moral message, but was otherwise incredibly long and boring with a questionable amount of historical accuracy.

5.title: Loud, noisy and false
5.content:
A biopic drenched in fiction which ended in a plot if which you can't tell what's based on facts and what isn't.

The first hour is just a chaotic ensemble of pieces of moving images put together by the same person who edited Elvis, so it seems. When Matt Damon enters the movie calms down for a short period after which it ends in chapters if loudness alternating (ear shattering) with chapters of complete silence. Reminds me of the way my teacher in 6th grade tried to silence the classroom. Everyone despises him until today.

The idea is excellent, cinematic speaking it's outstanding, albeit not on the same level as Inception, but the plot is so chaotic and so many things are missing which results in a somewhat unrealistic and lacking plot.

Nolan seems so fond of pulling big shot actors out of his hat, that it distracts from the plot itself.

5.content: Up until trinity I would say the movie was done really well. The last hour felt too long and unnecessary. Although I will say the last 15 minutes captivated me again. I just felt like it was hard to stay focused. I don't think they needed to go on that long about Strauss. I also didn't think the deposition needed that much time either. I think the movie needed to expand on what happened in Japan, because maybe for the people who don't know much about the history of Hiroshima and Nagasaki it could have been more understandable why Oppie struggled with his creation of the bomb. Anyway I just thought it got rough to keep watching. My bf said he almost fell asleep during the last part too.

5.title: Self-conflicting and futile
5.content:
The biopic of Oppenheimer, the inventor of atomic bomb, is depicted in a weird fashion. The movie starts from his early career days at university and follows his transfer to the Manhattan Project. The movie is too long and made bitty with a non-linear narrative which I found completely unnecessary. The viewer is usually distracted with scenes from the future showing his trial against some people. Those distractions are too long and very annoying. There are too many characters and they are all underdeveloped. I didn't understand what the point is in deliberately confusing the viewer.

Also it is not possible to understand the viewpoint of the filmmakers. Are they heroizing or disparaging Oppenheimer for developing an atomic bomb? I think they are undecided and this is why they created such a mess. Last but not least, trying to depict Oppenheimer as having a bad conscience is utterly ridiculous.

5.title: Maximalist, spectacular, uneven
5.content:
Nolan tries his luck at the biography genre for the first time, but still treats it as a blockbuster. One could blame the overambitious scope of the project, which tries to fit too much even for a running time of 3 hours. That includes the brilliance of his scientific work, the urgency of the atomic race during WWII, the struggles in his personal life, the consequences of his connections to the communist party that he couldn't shake off, the aftermath of Hiroshima/Nagasaki among others. As a result, Oppenheimer is extremely heavy in dialogue - even though the nuclear physics parts are kept to a reasonable length and depth, all these scientists' names that are being brought up without said person being present in that scene can be confusing to the viewer - uses epic, bombastic music - which is somewhat overused and could have been even more effective if it wasn't constantly attacking the audience - and aggressive editing along with a non linear narrative in order to keep a blistering pace while building suspense and momentum. This maximalist approach takes its toll on the viewer and creates an exhausting watching experience that hardly leaves any room to breathe.

Another complaint would be that the movie is rather uneven. On the one hand, The Manhattan Project / Los Alamos Laboratory / Trinity part was the clear highlight. On the other hand, the juxtaposition of Oppenheimer being trapped by Lewis Strauss to a hopeless hearing with Strauss suffering the same fate himself was a nice touch, but it wasn't really necessary for such a large part of the movie to turn into courtroom drama.

Still, it can't be denied that Oppenheimer is a cinematic spectacle. It does a commendable job at showing the events from Oppenheimer's point of view - unlike a typical biopic, he isn't presented as a hero or a villain, the movie takes no side in that debate - in no small part thanks to Murphy's excellent performance. A great example would be the scene where he delivers the victory speech and the full scale of his "achievement" becomes clear to him. Even the fancy visuals such as the visions of the atoms, the universe or the nuclear reactions are a welcome addition.

5.title: My expectation was to high
5.content:
Firstly, there was absolutely no need for the sex and nude scenes. They did NOTHING to improve the movie but actually detracted from the movie. All the actors,for the most part, are good actors and actress's, so I lay the blame on the director and the screen writer. This movie did nothing to increase the historicity of the era or the desire to know more about how "the bomb" came into being.

My recommendation is the movie "Fat Man, Little Boy". Paul Newman, as General Groves, makes that movie great. Laura Dern and John Cusack add all the love interest to make this a great movie.

Oppenheimer amplifies too much imaginative psychological characterizations and not enough history. Where as Fat Man, Little Boy covers the why's, and how's to fill in many historical gaps.

I found myself looking at my watch 15 minutes after Oppenheimer started, wondering how much longer the movie was going to run.

5.title: A LONG movie to sit through to be disappointed
5.content: 3 hours long and it felt EVERY bit that long. First, I want to say that the sound design and sound editing was atrocious, much of the dialogue was lost through low volume by actors and the musical score overpowering it. Second, the first 30 minutes was difficult to follow as the timeline kept bouncing around (to be fair, I missed the very opening so maybe there was something there that may have helped explain it). The ensemble cast was so large that keeping all the names straight was also hard. I realize this movie was more about Oppenheimer but previous movies on the subject were better (IMO).

5.title: Wanted to love this
5.content: There's not a single moment without background score, except for the bomb explosion. It always bothers me when a film requires background music for everything, even quiet conversations, that nothing is good enough to survive without musical support. Also bleach bypassing IMAX seems a real waste - why use a lab process that increases grain and reduces contract ratio on the highest resolution film medium available? It all feels pretty one note, style over substance. Dry. Given Nolan's limitless resources it should be much more rounded. I didn't care about anyone, or even really get to know anyone, including Oppenheimer. Overall really disappointing and all the glowing reviews to me feel like everyone has drunk the Kool Aid. The emperor has no clothes. Not sure how much I'm influenced by having read the biography it's based on. Dr George Miller used to say that a film should feel like a great piece of music with highs, lows, quiet, crescendos, pacing. This feels like one very long chorus, and not a great one at that.

5.title: All surface but no feeling
5.content: Nolan rarely does empathy well but this is a soulless three hours of men mumbling at one another. Florence Pugh and Emily Blunt are wasted and portrayed as damaged souls. Scenes come and go barely registering on your conscience. Watching this movie is a bit like thinking back to you time in school where you were forced by your teachers to watch educational videos which were kind of okay but you'd rather be playing Lego or riding your bike. That's what watching Oppenheimer is like. It's like a three hour lecture with a bit of sex thrown in. Yes, it's a competent artistic film but that doesn't mean it's that good.

5.title: Overrated
5.content:
Too many goofs. L8ke the Einstein meeting. From the biographical point of view, this is disastrous. Either they were too lazy to research or just found it looks better, which it doesn't improve anything.

The movie is definitely too long amd often extremely boring.

The sex scenes were absolutely not needed, typical for Hollywood to add useless sex scenes in a film like that. It is sufficient to show there was a relationship.

Too many goofs. L8ke the Einstein meeting. From the biographical point of view, this is disastrous. Either they were too lazy to research or just found it looks better, which it doesn't improve anything.

The movie is definitely too long amd often extremely boring.

The sex scenes were absolutely not needed, typical for Hollywood to add useless sex scenes in a film like that. It is sufficient to show there was a relationship.

5.title: OK, but not a Classic
5.content:
Plusses

The production values are excellent.

Generally depicts the period accurately.

Good special effects, especially the recreation of the Trinity shot.

Shows that like everyone else, scientists have sex lives.

Occasionally asks some profound questions.

Minuses

Quickly jumps from scene to scene.

Excessive use of flashbacks.

Fair amount of overacting, especially by Robert Downey jr,,

The music and sound effects often drown out the dialog.

At times tends to ramble on and on with no end in sight.

Distracting surrealistic sequences.

My general conclusion- OK, but not a classic.

By comparison, " Fat Man and Little Boy" is overall a better film on the subject.

It pretty much mirrors my view of the recent remake of "All Quiet on the Western Front".

Generally good but can't compare to the original.

5.title: Totally shocked... This film will put some people to sleep... seriously!
5.content:
I am a HUGE Nolan fan. I love his films so you can imagine my excitement to have seen press reviews and booked to see this movie. I avoided trailers cos I wanted to be blown away.

But... I was hugely disappointed! And I mean CATACLYSMIICALLY!!

Acting is great, no doubt.

The score is great, definitely.

Cillian Murphy and Robert Downey junior deserve oscar nominations, absolutely!

That's it. This film is almost like watching a documentary, that you've committed to (cos you want to learn something, and you like the subject matter) but then get bored halfway through, but still persevere hoping there's a huge payoff for your investment in time.

Sorry folks but there really, really isn't. It's very fragmented, jumps around in time far too much..... but you'll still stay until the end in the hope that this Nolan film will blow your mind with some incredible last hour.... and you'll say '"Masterpiece"... but it doesn't.

I left the cinema, texted my mate (I'd already arranged to see it in IMAX with him in a few days) and cancelled. Luckily he hadn't bought the tickets cos, even if he had, I'd have sent him the money but not gone. Huuuuge disappointement. For me anyway, and the two people I watched it with. They felt the same.

And from what we witnessed, quite a few other people too.

Make up your own mind tho.

If you enjoy watching senate hearings, or study 20th century American history, then go see it. If you want to see an exciting Nolan movie then stay at home and watch any of his other films.

I almost wish I'd have gone and, watched Barbie instead...... almost....

5.title: Oppenhyped
5.content:
Oppenheimer is Nolan's latest and on the top of my must see list this year (there aren't many) needless to say it's not what I wanted.

The movies boring plain and simple, there are only a handful of moments that Nolan actually captured what I was wanting to see and in a 3hr movie it's few and far between.

I'd be singing a different tune had the movie ended when Oppe was giving his speech and imagining them being nuked it seemed like the perfect ending to it...but no it drags for another what seemed like an hour of court room but not court room drama it wasn't interesting.

Didn't like any of the characters which makes it difficult to watch and the writing/acting was pretty subpar. So much trying to get an Oscar overacting. Cillian was good in the role nothing too memorable to rave though.

It just got to the point of what's the point? Would've been a better movie had it been more focused on the building of the nuke, Hiroshima, the aftermath and moral dilemma but it focuses more on the issues with Strauss, the government, his wives and sabotaging one's career and reputation just got boring.

The movie also gets loud at random points as if it's trying to make the movie more engaging than it is or to wake the audience from its slumber.

The nuke scene was poorly shot. Didn't seem like much of an explosion either could've been better.

Overall Oppenheimer is Oppenhyped it doesn't live up.

5.title: Nolan - The Depeche Mode of the film world
5.content:
So in the electronic / synth music world, its a sin to criticise anything the Mode do.

I definitely feel the same can be said about Nolans films. He has made some great films, The Prestige, Interstellar & Memento. But on the other hand, has has made some stinkers, Tennent was appallingly stupid.

This looks absolutely beautiful, the cinematography is sensational. The performances are very good, Murphy plays the lead perfectly and Emily Blunt plays a brilliant drunk. However there are some terrible accents, is Kenneth Branagh meant to be South African?

Problem with this movie is, it's very confusing, its also very, very boring, it doesn't pack any kind of emotion, we are talking about the most shameful moment in history, yet, somehow it clearly manages to avoid any of that.

Very boring.

5.title: Aggressively "okay"
5.content:
Well, it is definetly the most capable Nolan has been writing-wise without the help of his brother.

The more abstract sequences, such as Oppenheimer's recurring visions and Kitty's struggle with his affair are also welcome additions, even though they make up very little of the runtime. Actually got me wondering how Nolan would handle an erotic thriller.

Unfortunately, the rest is still typical Nolan.

Cold, unevenly paced with no sense of where to let the narrative breathe, dumping exposition at every opportunity, matter-of-fact filmmaking with little interest to go beyond the surface and above all, needlessly muddling with timelines so as to appear more complex. Shooting in black and white for "Strauss's point of view" was also completely unnecessary, as there is no other point of view or playing with an unreliable narrator, it's just the factual retelling of events, but in black and white.

It is very much just a biography transferred into the medium of film, keeping focus on events instead of people, missing a lot of opportunities to emotionally engage the viewer.

This might be enough for a lot of people who just like to learn about someone's life, but it absolutely isn't for me.

At least the final act somewhat manages to convey a very important lesson:

The line between hero and villain is always ambiguous. It all depends on where powerful people decide to put their blind spots.

5.title: Ordinary
5.content:
2 negative things which i felt : 1) Background music is a strong tool to use to increase the impact of a scene. A fast chaotic BGM signifies that a scene or a sequence of scene is moving towards a crescendo.

Every scene, even the most normal conversation had a fast paced bgm. V annoying. Right from the start.

2) too much of politics shown & hardly any physics shown. The explanation of the bomb etc.

For eg, look at the mini series "Chernobyl" They showed the science behind the making of a nuclear reactor, the sci behind the accident, sci behind the containment & damage control of the accident.

The scientific genius of opp was hardly documented. The movie was all about the political juggling done by him during his lifetime.

Also, 3) when the movie is about history, it is good to atleast mention the names with their titles in a small box at the bottom when you introduce them 1st.

5.title: Dramatically disappointing documentary
5.content: This movie is a rather fractured and way too long inaccurate biopic about a 'not so nice guy' in conflict with his own ego, suffering from selective morality at the expense of his family and friends. Oh, yeah, the story is set against the backdrop of the development of the A-bomb in the later part of the Second World War. Proving once again that Americans can't be trusted to explore their own cultural history with any real subjectivity. Kitty seemed to be the only character with any backbone and a grip on reality. Frankly the second half is a really boring exploration into the dirty hypocritical backroom politics that the US is famous for. Truth be told, largely a waste of good 70mm film stock.

5.title: Disappointing
5.content:
A bit tedious and IMO very disjointed. The 1st part gave a reasonable insight into the race to develop the bomb, highlighting the multinational collaboration of scientists, but it skirted over the race against the Nazi's which could have added to tension. I think the tv documentary was far better as an expose and had more drama.

The 2nd part was poorly linked to the 1st, with insufficient explanation and it became a fairly standard courtroom drama.

There were some interesting bits, although more could have been made of them, especially the possible chain reaction to the 1st test. Cillian Murphy was good, but not as good or believable as he was in Peaky Blinders. Robert Downey Jnr was excellent, although the storyline about his character warranted more development & explanation.

5.title: Lacked Impact.
5.content:
Taking on a movie exploring the life of Oppenheimer would always be a complex and intense situation to develop and portray on screen.

There's a lot to unpack with regard to what aspects to explore, but ultimately it would always culminate on the development and deployment of the atom bomb.

And here's the problem, Nolan delves deep into Oppenheimer's life but (as usual) chooses to mix & match and jump around in time to show multiple points in Oppenheimer's life, in and out of context, some in colour, some in black and white (and random conceptual visuals) which unfortunately slowly degrades from the focus of the movie.

And when it comes down to what is one of the most important and scary moments in history, it's just neatly tucked away (in a belated phone call) to focus on the final act which seems to be more like the Lewis Strauss Show.

It gets messy and unnecessary and at a runtime of 3hrs becomes a bit of a chore. Cillian Murphy is exceptional (and well deserving of the Oscar - not sure why RDJ got one for what was a pretty generic portrayal) but for what should be an explosive movie just drops the ball (or bomb).

5.title: TL;DR: Big LOUD noises!!!!
5.content:
Oppenheimer might be a decent movie somewhere under all that noise but I put in earplugs (I came prepared: it's a Christopher Nolan movie) and often put my hands over my ears as well. Nevertheless, with the cranked-up volume in movie theaters these days, I had no problem following the dialog.

There's a terrible soundtrack of melodramatic music to make sure you know how you're supposed to feel, frequent random booming and rumbling to make your liver quiver, and screen-filling explosions that come out of nowhere and seem designed only to startle - sort of a science equivalent of jump scares.

Nolan seems so determined to force us to feel - literally viscerally - that THIS IS REALLY IMPORTANT STUFF!!!! That character development and to some extent the plot suffer. It's a convoluted timeline, though use of black and white for flashbacks helps. The postwar period quiets down somewhat: fewer rumblings and explosions, but the strident, manipulative music continues.

The real Oppenheimer was a far more interesting and complex person than the character in this movie, though Cillian Murphy is, as always, excellent. They do indulge some of the real Oppenheimer's reservations about the implications of atomic weapons. But they portray him as pretty much a hapless victim of postwar McCarthyism, while leaving out much of the real Oppenheimer's affiliations with the communist movement and his willingness to name names when he was under pressure.

I would have liked to have seen a more thoughtful movie. There is some character development for Oppenheimer, Robert Downey Jr does a very fine job as Lewis Strauss, and Rami Malek does well with a brief though substantial part.

Overall, disappointing given the hype. Maybe I would have liked it better if it weren't so loud, and so focused on making sure that we never forget that it's about the ATOMIC BOMB, which is a REALLY BIG DEAL.

5.title: The least entertaining Nolan film
5.content:
Massive Nolan fan, TDK, inception and interstellar among my top 10 films, with others not far behind.

Oppenheimer is well acted, looks great, but my god it's boring.

I've rewatched all of Nolan's film over an over, but I will only put myself through Oppenheimer once.

It's just does nothing to pull you in, the subject matter is obviously significant and important, I just think it would be better served as a documentary than a 3 hour film. The characters and story in this film are just not that interesting. I didn't care about anyone.

It's a real disappointment, and no one is more upset about this than me.

5.title: A let-down
5.content:
The story of J. Robert Oppenheimer is an extraordinary one and this much-acclaimed film is not without merit, but I have to say, I was let down by it. I'm happy that Christopher Nolan paid tribute and brought visibility to Oppenheimer, and one gets the gist of his life, but I found it a rather shallow and under-developed treatment, which is ironic considering the film's length.

Oppenheimer was a tremendous intellect whose life went through incredible transitions - from apolitical intellectual to radical, anti-fascist leftist, to leader of thousands of people to create the first WMD, to trying desperately (and unsuccessfully) to control the proliferation of atomic weapons via involvement in Washington DC, to a disgrace of sorts in the revoking of his security clearance. Cillian Murphy does well in this role, revealing the brooding, often contradictory ways Oppenheimer acted, as well as his naivete in thinking the demonstration of power in the bomb being dropped would end all future war, and that he could put the genie back in the bottle once it happened.

Unfortunately, Nolan's storytelling got too much in the way of this compelling bit of history. I don't think the decision to tell the story out-of-order, interleaving events before and after the war, was a good one, as it led to a pace that was too brisk under a barrage of names and facts. I think it would have been more powerful had he told the story linearly, saving the fall from grace until after the bomb had been deployed. Either way, there was far too much emphasis on Lewis Strauss (Robert Downey Jr.), the Atomic Energy Commission chairman who engineered his downfall behind the scenes.

Nolan tries to provide historical context but he does so by trying to ram things into the viewer through dialogue which feels forced (and certainly not of the period), and then flitting around too rapidly. The pacing is terrible and it often seemed like each scene was a trailer, complete with overdone, intrusive music. The invented conversations Oppenheimer has with Einstein here were frankly ridiculous, and the one with Truman wasn't much better. Meanwhile, the women characters seem like an afterthought, and Florence Pugh present just to show her body.

The film doesn't want to touch the scientific or engineering challenges the Manhattan Project team faced with a 10-foot-pole; nor does it want to really show the horror of the bombing of innocent civilians, or to truly immerse itself into the debate as to whether dropping the bombs on Japan was necessary. All of these things are unfortunately just given lip service, and instead, the film leans heavily into the politics in Washington, with the security hearing of Oppenheimer, and the Senate confirmation hearing of Strauss. Those things obviously had their place in a biopic of the man, but should not have been the overwhelming focus.

My recommendation is to watch the 89 minute film The Day After Trinity (1981) instead of the 'Hollywood treatment' that Nolan created here, which isn't much more elevated than the plethora of MCU films these days.

5.title: Boringheimer
5.content: At an hour and twenty minutes in and realizing that the film lasted for three, I was pretty sure I would never get through to the end. After a while I simply lost interest. The film is well crafted but the back and forth between the characters and all their possible communist leaning associations that lead to congressional investigations just flat out became tedious. The sequence of events relative to the the Big O's development of the bomb and development into the babes didn't seem to have any coherent sequence in terms of where we were in terms of historical chronology. Somber music drones in the background in an effort to convince us of the seriousness of the entire matter. A lot of high quality actors and crew made an ostensible historical motion picture that may have won a lot of awards because audiences are simply growing tired of super heroes. As far as our relationship with the Russians go, the film implies that we've made no real progress since WW2. Overall, an O K movie that narrowly avoided being a bomb.

5.title: Such a great story but...
5.content:
How on earth could they release such a great story that was held captive by an overwhelming sound track...

You can't hear the dialogue over the god awful drone overlay ... whoever did this needs hearing aides and someone to teach them that less is more.

Totally unacceptable and disappointing ~ nearly as abysmal as a vangelis caricature ...

The character development was short, and the speed at which things hurled into the fray was breathtaking, perhaps adderall is not the best drug for someone trying to direct a story so utterly important... The bright spot is perhaps someone will see this train wreck and make a better version.

5.title: Chamber drama with loud music
5.content:
Not bad, but could've been more captivating. Incorporating elements of espionage, a country rivalry in bomb development, and similar plotlines could've enhanced it. As it stands, it's a chamber drama with numerous characters and insufficient intrigue for its 180-minute runtime.

The characters are fine, but I didn't see a reason for IMAX. Even the highly praised explosion didn't impress me.

In other words, the film is worth watching, but it wouldn't make a difference if I watched it at home, and I certainly don't need to see it a second time.

I expect more entertainment from a movie theater, especially considering all the hype, something that enriches me. But I didn't learn anything new. 5 out of 10.

5.title: Good, but not so good
5.content:
One must assume that this is going to be fantastic given the credits' list of names. Your anticipation builds as you begin to watch it. Then you understand that it is unnecessarily dramatized, extremely long, and uninteresting.

Like, every 10 seconds of his life, Oppenheimer saw electrons crashing together? Come onnnn!!! I failed to understand if this was a movie about his love life, relationships or and his work.

This film is stretched out like a piece of gum you chewed for three hours, and I'm sure the filmmaker would have liked it to last another six if he could have shown how Oppenheimer ate his food and went to the toilet, in details.

5.title: Oppenheimer
5.content:
Rating a movie based on the hype it initially received is unfair, short-sighted and does not do any justice to the movie.

While this movie does feel like Oscar-bait it was still a worthwhile watch for most of the time in my opinion. Cillian Murphy delivers as he almost always does. He truly is single-handedly the best thing about this movie. The acting, set pieces, sound design and cinematography were all on point. The sequence leading up to the first successful detonation were really good and intense.

However I have a few problems with this movie. The nuke detonation itself is kinda underwhelming with all that intense buildup, however I still would like it more than a cheap CGI explosion.

The side story of the second love interest was not necessary and did nothing to move the plot forward. The nudity in these scenes also felt overdone. The I am become death line is also wasted in these scenes.

The dialogue between Oppenheimer and his love interests feel awkward and it just looks like two smart people talking about smart things.

I feel the runtime of the movie could have been shorter by at least half an hour.

The non-linear story telling is a Nolan trope, but it makes the movie which is already hard to follow even more confusing. It is just a biopic and not a mystery like Memento.

In summary, I think its good to watch once and never again.

5.title: What a disappointment
5.content:
After having seen the high ratings, the interviews with the cast and the trailer, I was looking forward to see an accurate depiction of an important part of history, still shaping our world today.

But the actual movie has nothing to do with the trailer; 2/3 of it deals with endless interrogations after the war about Oppenheimer's possible old communist links and his refusal to cooperate with the H-bomb development, so to find an excuses to revoke his security clearance and side-line him. And this in endless time-jumps back and forth.

The actual 1/3 of the movie that deals with the development of the "gadget", the theory behind it and the practical problems to turn various theories into reality was only lightly addressed, barely scratching the surface of the development, the technical difficulties, the logistics, the organisation and the timeline.

True, the film is called "Oppenheimer" and not "Trinity", "the Bomb", etc, but I felt that for 2 out of the 3 hours I was attending some courtroom interrogation about Oppenheimer, not a movie about the man and his team developing the technology while admitting various levels of doubt, guilt, conscience, etc.

Yes the acting was very good, Cillian Murphy, but also, to my surprise, Matt Damon.

But overall, this movie does not at all represent, in my humble opinion, what it is being sold to be.

5.title: Oppenheimer
5.content:
Let me start by saying that I am a huge Christopher Nolan fan. I love everything he has done... up until now.

I walked out of the cinema feeling nothing but disappointment.

At its core, this is a film about J. Robert Oppenheimer - "The father of the atomic bomb" and the role Oppenheimer played in history.

How can you truly tell Oppenheimer's story without first admitting to the audience that his discovery lead the United States to drop two atomic bombs, within three days, on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, and the impact and fallout of these decisions? How can you possibly tell a story about the birth of atomic weaponry without a certain focus on the 129,000 to 226,000 people that were killed by this decision, in addition to the many people who continued to die from the effects of burns, radiation sickness, and injuries? The majority of the people who suffered and were killed were civilians, and the fact that this remains the only use of nuclear weapons in an armed conflict?

Remember, this is sold as a film that is about history, and it is meant to be a biopic.

The film touches on Oppenheimer's inner turmoil with unleashing such weaponry, this kind of power, and who can be trusted with it, but it is fleeting.

Oppenheimer will forever be linked, through history, to these events. This alone is a huge part of Oppenheimer's story, and I believe Oppenheimer himself struggled terribly with the knowledge of what he had created and the devastating impact it would have.

The cast is great. The acting is great. The sound and soundtrack does not compare to The Dark Knight (2008), Inception (2010), Dunkirk (2017), Tenet (2020), or, dare I mention the "I" word, Interstellar (2014).

Perhaps the production companies did not let Nolan do what he does best, and some of his creative control over this project was minimised?

Ultimately, it almost feels like this was a film about politics and climate change, using Oppenheimer as the vehicle rather than truly telling Oppenheimer's story. This is most present in the concluding dialogue of the film:

Oppenheimer: When I came to you with those calculations, we thought we might start a chain reaction that would destroy the entire world... Albert Einstein: I remember it well. What of it?

Oppenheimer: I believe we did.

Simplifying the incredible complex history of Oppenheimer and these events seems unjust and pointless.

5.title: I did not expect to not love this film
5.content:
Oppenheimer while a solid film is not what I expected.

I'll start with the great. The performances especially Robert Downey Jr are off the chart. Emily Blunt has an absolute masterful scene. Cillian Murphy is very good as Oppie.

The good. It's an interesting film that FEELS important. It's shot well of course. Many of the scenes hold your interest.

The rest: it's too long... and for no reason. It's 3 separate films poorly edited into a mismatched formal outfit. Additionally, the sound mix fails miserably. The big moments are big; however, the dialogue is often missed at crucial moments of the film making the through line difficult to follow.

It feels like a film that wants to be Oliver Stone's JFK; but, fails to have an underlying story interesting enough to justify the black and white and odd cut backs. The atom bomb is a sideline to the story unlike every ad campaign which makes it the primary focus. By the time we TEST the bomb (considering we don't see anything of Hiroshima or Nagasaki) we are left with another hour of the same beat over and over and over in a claustrophobic coat closet of a conference room with 2 dimensional characters including Oppenheimer himself for every single scene in the room or similar 2 dimensional congressional hearing members droning on about whether Downey (who is brilliant) should be confirmed for a cabinet position.

I wanted to love this film but it's just another big budget effort that fails to meet expectations.

5.title: Over hyped and Bad Imagery
5.content:
The movie jumps from the past to present trying to be clever and come off like inception. Instead, it's just unnecessarily disorganized. I guess it's to makeup for the lack of material, they had written. Very loud and incoherent at points. There's art to sounds and tones and it was used ineffectively. There's really no development of the characters. In one instance, Kitty Oppenheimer, Emily blunt, is seen with booze and ignoring the house hold, and just unkept. Which applause to Emily blunt for her acting, she did a great job given the lack of material she was handed for the role. Then in the end, we are supposed to be applauding her in the final scene when she doesn't shake the other scientist's hand? Same goes for every other character.

Also what about Oppenheimer poisoning his teacher and then considered a hero? What is this movie trying to say? I never got the importance of the isotopes sold to Norway. I had to watch a C-Span video to figure out the relevance.

What I looked forward to with this film was for it covering how they developed and designed the nuclear bomb and the implications of it, but that was never covered. They do no justice to the science or imagery of the bomb. You do not have to see it in imax for the bomb scene. They also don't have a clear message of where they stand for on the premise of the bomb, since the last hour is convoluted on it's message with Oppenheimer trying to keep his secret clearance. I feel it was overhyped. Terrible writing/story telling, film cutting, visual effects, and sounds, but great acting.

5.title: You'll need a history lesson
5.content:
First, the buzz around this movie is very overblown. 15 years ago this movie wouldn't have been anywhere but the History Channel. And why was this film in imax. There's nothing special about it.

Secondly before you watch the film, brush up, heck do some research. I feel pretty educated and felt lost AF in how this story was told. I know no more about Oppenheimer now than I did having watched this movie.

Thirdly, the film is chaotic and all over the place. Back and forth and quick edits and time blurring. I was aggravated with the flow. I kept having questions, I would have stopped and googled the film to figure things out. But...

Forth. It's way too long. This would have been a great HBO miniseries. Like Chernobyl.

Look I like Nolan's movies. And yes the acting is very good. Set design is good. This movie's story telling just wasn't for me.

5.title: Interesting but overdrawn - not one you'd watch twice
5.content: The story fascinates me and I knew nothing about the title character coming into this, but it is a very slow and drawn out film. The first hour and a half or so could probably have been condensed into 30 minutes, considering most of it is told through flashbacks anyway. Cillian Murphy and Robert Downey Jr played their roles well and deserve the praise, but this is not a film you'd watch twice: it is far too long in length and there's too many nuances going on that, quite frankly, aren't necessary - or at least not to the extent of that they are shown on screen. I would classify this more as a biopic than anything - you walk away with a lot of information about Robert Oppenheimer but not much else.

5.title: Average , if you watch it properly
5.content:
This is another film made for the people that made it to show off , not for the viewer to enjoy it's has a lot of unneeded dialogue , a lot of stupid dream sequences , cillian Murphy is not engaging enough ,

This is s film everyone tells you they love because other people have told them they love it , all hype no execution

Like the Irishman , and banshees of innisheran it will be forgotten once watched , I would bet my house no one will be re watching this is a few years despite the unbelievable amount of waffle surrounding it

And why do I have to type minimum amount of characters , waste of time , reviews on here should be allowed to be more succinct instead of these wanna be semi pro film critics.

5.title: Loud, Overscored and Soulless
5.content:
It's a shame this film was criminally overscored, it threw me off almost every scene because the music was so overpowering, especially when you DON'T need it if you have great acting.

The music in the first act was too cheeky and inspirational. When Oppenheimer was recruiting the scientists it honestly felt like the Avengers were assembling.

Big, loud and expensive is not a synonym of good storytelling either, particularly when they deviate the focus from the very disturbing weapon they're creating and decide to dwell on the defamation case against Mr. Oppenheimer. More than 200,000 people lost their lives instantly, I think it's safe to assume that having Strauss holding a grudge against Oppenheimer as the central point is very disappointing and superficial.

Cinematically, all throughout the movie it seemed like everything was SO GRAND, everything was the next big thing. WE know the Avengers scientist team are going to invent the holy grail of destruction, THEY don't know that, so why act like they're changing history already.

Ultimately, it's not a bad film but I resent the fact that the subject matter was not treated with the seriousness it deserves. The film almost feels like a light hearted feel good movie about a nuclear BOMB.

5.title: Overrated
5.content: I tried to watch this movie originally and only got into about 15 or 20 minutes before I turned it off. After seeing how many Oscars it was nominated for and how many it ultimately won. I decided to give it another try, and was underwhelmed to say the least. It was mentally daring to watch with little reward. It was long (3 hours to be exact) and drawn out with little climax during the whole movie. I HATED the switching between color and black and white. I get it was seperating the present from the past events of the movie, but it was beyond unnecessary. The only reason so gave it as high of a rating as aid is is because of its studded cast. A waste of 3 hours I'll never get back. IM SHOCKED it won so many awards.

5.title: well-made but simply not greatness
5.content: Oppenheimer is an ambitious movie, a well-made movie, but simply put, it's not a great movie. Historically, science and politics have always been a rough mix, and this biographical movie covers all the bases. Oppenheimer is a complex person with a unique intelligence that, during wartime, makes him a hot property. But his politics come back into play throughout the story, especially post-bomb. The acting is solid, but not exactly living up to the raves I've read and heard. The casting is pretty good, except for the bizarre Harry Truman scene. Overall, it's good, dialogue-heavy, three hours of biographical drama that probably would work just as well on Netflix as the big screen. It did not quite fulfill my expectations.

5.title: Beyond yawn
5.content: Don't see what all the commotion is about. The film is erratic, messy and incoherent. Too many characters and lots of scientific jargon make it challenging to follow and not in an "Inception" or "Interstellar" way. Top name actors give great performances and there's some great cinematography but that's not enough to redeem Nolan's dry, boring script and droll subject matter. And with a 3 hour running time, I really wish I hadn't spent the money to stream it. I certainly wouldn't have watched beyond the first half hour had I not paid $6. Perhaps those in the scientific community will appreciate this film.

5.title: Great craftsmanship but boring
5.content: Great actors and acting, great visual and sound, great editing, great dialogues - but still I didn't like it. 3 hours is too long. It should have been shortened to 2 hours. The interrogation scenes were just too stretched out. And the subject of this interrogation was not even that interesting. I understand that Nolan didn't just want to make a movie how Oppenheimer built the bomb but wanted to add something else which allowed flashbacks. But at the end of the movie I was like "This is it?". I also didn't understand why sometimes scenes were in color and sometimes in black and white. I'm sure Nolan used this to tell us something but I must have totally missed it. There are a number of Nolan movies that should be watched twice or even three times to understand them better, such as TENET, Inception, Dunkirk. And if you watch these again, you will find parts that you have overlooked and you can enjoy the movie with a different perspective. But I have absolutely no desire to watch Oppenheimer again. It would simply be too boring.

5.title: Dull and mumbling
5.content:
I bought this for husband for Christmas as we were desperate to see it. Omg so disappointing. Mumbling their lines, we had to have the volume high it vibrated lol so put subtitles on, we're not deaf. Literally don't they teach actors diction any more.

The music was too loud and drowned out their lines any way. The story is slow, the characters just come on, say a line and leave like some stage production that does not inspire character feeling. I wasn't with any character, I didn't feel for any of them.

I had high hopes for this but wish I hadnt bothered as Nolan is a good director ie Batman, inception etc. They play old mumbling men and it could have been a lot better.

Not going to re watch it.

5.title: Too annoying to be enjoyable
5.content: An intriguing character, an historic time, a chance to show what made the man whose name the film bears, squandered on an overbearing visual and audio production. Loud, building, ever-present music, probably to make up for the lack of dramatic dialogue in the script. No family back-story, none of the quirks of his character as a young man, just a series of short episodes in labs while music plays incessantly and too loudly. Jumping back and forth in time, to create a sense of mystery to demonstrate a great man taken down by pettiness. You can't make this movie without hitting some high notes and the test scene brilliant, and the sense of moral regret is well delivered. But the overall production, especially the editing, and the focus on the 'trial' and the decision to omit the early back-story years, creates a gap that is never quite filled, despite the brilliance of Cillian Murphy portraying a man struggling with the impact of what he has unleashed on the world, not to mention a host of fabulous cameos.

5.title: Monotonous
5.content:
I try to be honest and consistent with my opinions. I believe in critical thinking and I hope it is not a dying skill.

This film is a grandiose homage to some of the greatest minds our civilization ever produced. Nolan's effort here is sincere but quite lacking in real drama. There is little to separate this from a docu-drama that felt a trifle exasperating.

I have an engineering background and was familiar with the basic history of the Manhattan project and the prominent characters. I left the theater slightly disoriented with all of the names and actions of the subsequent political players who dominate over half of the film. That's over 90 minutes.

I know this is a story about profound philosophical concepts, but I don't feel they were addressed adequately. The opportunity was missed. Instead we are shown a slightly confusing story of jealousy and persecution. The dawn of the Nuclear age is ultimately something we will always have to deal with. I don't feel this film emphasized that enough.

Overall I was disappointed, slightly confused, and fatigued.

5.title: That Was Hard To Watch
5.content: Seriously, that movie was hard to watch. The constant switching back and forth among multiple scenes for 10 seconds at a time got really annoying. It didn't add anything of value to the film and came off as trying too hard to be a novel approach. Add to that the music score that was mostly mismatched with each scene and it often drowned out the dialogue. The story itself was so weak. If you halfway paid attention you alread knew who the bad guy was way before the end and even then so what, the main event was long past. The only reason why I gave it 5 stars was because of the cast. Had there been a better director and intriguing plot it might have been a great film. I'm almost ashamed I watched it and feel like I have to take a shower.

5.title: Not Up to the Mark
5.content: One thing I don't like about this movie, there is a scene in this movie when oppenheimer was doing sex with his gf and using Hindu scripture Geeta phrase. If Christopher Nolan known for reality instead of VFX why doesn't he used real video reference and create separate scene for that movie. Before releasing, there was a hype about this movie because of Oppenheimer use the Geeta phrase after dropping the bomb by US army that was a reason, I was curious about to watch this movie but if you are not aware about physics & history, my suggestion for you do some RND first then you can watch this movie otherwise you will going to sleep on the chair. I think director doesn't explain movie so well.

5.title: Overrated
5.content:
Ok film, too long. Dragged out the non important stuff to make it dreary. Main characters were good as far as they were allowed but to give this movie a rating that it has is ridiculous.

Far better films languish at a lower level and it seems the newer the film the better the rating.

It's a great but unsettling story that needs to be told but the over complication with personal struggles gets to be boring. Marital difficulties when laid against the backdrop of potential ending the world kind of pale into insignificance.

New is not necessarily better, personally I can think of a large number of films that entertain me far more than this basically average offering.

5.title: Historically questionable
5.content:
While it's a good film in many aspects, such as acting quality, imagination, and technical prowess, it failed to captivate me.

Oppenheimer is a historical biopic that uses a non-linear format to create a more interesting storytelling format. Yet, this also makes the film harder to comprehend, especially with dozens of characters over a long run time. Being of historical interest, I would have preferred a chronological format that helped me to understand the events better.

One must also question the emphasis given to certain events and characters over others. Many American films emphasise American involvement at the expense of British or say Canadian involvement. However, it was more surprising here to see the British scientist contingent as a mere footnote in the film when the British started the world's first nuclear weapons research project and helped initiate the Manhattan Project alongside the Americans. More than simply being downplayed, the British are even shown in a negative light.

As with many biopics, Oppenheimer verges on idolisation of the central figure. While it certainly touches upon some negative attributes of Oppenheimer, there is a clear hero and villain in the film, which is always dangerous in non-fiction settings. Scenes repeatedly show crowds giving undivided attention to Oppenheimer as if he were a God. It felt over-the-top.

I'm fine with a long run time, but I didn't feel the film justified it. Despite an interest in physics, history, and war, I found my attention waning. With history so interesting (it was one of the great 'what ifs' and turning points in history), I think this is unforgivable. I appreciate that, based on the many positive reviews on this site, this may be a contrarian opinion.

5.title: Somber
5.content:
I'm glad I didn't pay to see this. If I wanted to watch a political court room drama I'd watch C-SPAN, not a 3-hour film. The trailer promised a visual spectacle about science, and the invention of the bomb. Instead, as mentioned before, this is a long drawn out political court room drama where the majority of "visuals" is watching a bunch of white guys sit around tables and talk at each other.

I think I've seen all of Nolan's films, and liked all of them, so all I can guess is the studio trusted him, and he went on a drug binge in some foreign country, came back, still hungover, and slapped together what he thought would be his opus...while still on drugs. The studio got their copy of the film, panicked, wondering how they'd salvage this expensive monstrosity, and so cut together a trailer that didn't remotely depict the actual film, and campaigned best film of the year in hopes everyone would see it...even though most everyone was hard pressed to find anyone who'd actually seen it.

The costumes and set design was good, it was shot well, but that's about it. The acting was lifeless. Having the variety of stars was pointless, as for some reason they were all directed to have no sense of character or humanity, like robots. Emily Blunt was the only one who managed to have an essence of humanity. Honestly, as crass as it sounds, Florence Pugh's completely gratuitous shot was the highlight of the film. I mean, congrats.

This seems to be some long, drawn out film about finger pointing who's at fault for historical genocide. They're all guilty. They paint Oppenheimer as a man who is vaguely sociopathic, kind of a Communist, who builds a bomb for no other reason than he can...then we're made to believe he has some sense of humanity, remorse...and is a victim. He killed a bunch of people, didn't think twice about it, and no one twisted his arm. He's not a hero, he's not a victim, and not even a genius. He's just a self-involved smart guy with a bunch of resources, that for some reason they're suddenly trying to justify his actions. So, in 50 years is there going to be a film justifying Harvey Weinstein? Putin? Probably. Gives them an excuse to employ a bunch of white men and tell their skewed perspective, like most of history.

5.title: middling biopic rescued by Murphy and Pugh
5.content:
Of the three biopics I saw recently, _Oppenheimer_ ranks somewhere between the excellent _Simone: A Woman of the Century_ and the amateurish _Maestro_. To its credit, _Oppenheimer_ does OK with the science aspect of the bomb-making (although the over-emphasis on matter-wave duality and "black-holes" -- which has nothing to do with atomic bombs -- is par for the course in today's commercial media). The large-engineering-team aspect of the Manhattan project is somewhat well-represented. It is an improvement over _Interstellar_, in which two people writing equations on a blackboard magically translates into mature technology. (Even if one of the two is the beloved Jessica Chastain, accustomed to saving the world by herself in _Zero Dark Thirty_, _The Tree of Life_ ...)

Both _Oppenheimer_ and _Simone_ are effective on conveying the anti-semitism that is a large part of their protagonists' lives. Neither film manages to make the case that their protagonists are exceptional leaders. Being smart or passionate is not enough; you must have that elusive quality for others to follow you. Why is Oppenheimer picked to lead the entire project?

Is Nolan pro-science or ani-science? The words "Manhattan Project" has been evoked for other breakthroughs many times (think climate change, or solving quantum gravity in _Interstellar_). It seems intellectually lazy not to put that in context. Equally strange is the way the film omits both the Japanese citizens incinerated by the atomic bombs, and the Asian victims conquered and brutalized by Japanese occupation and "liberated" by those bombs ...

Instead, the last hour plus is devoted internal US politics. I have never figured out what director Christopher Nolan's politics or ideology is. His most famous films are the Batman trilogy, with the protagonist being progressively violent and proto-Fascist (especially the last installment, siding with the boys in blue against the anarchists). However, _Oppenheimer_ is openly pro-communist. I must confess I tuned out before the end -- the endless last hour, with its endless procession of colorless back-stabbing politicians, is too much for me. Nolan seems more interested in the scientist's reputation and public standing than the work he actually did. Which perhaps tell you something about Nolan's approach to his place in cinematic art.

In terms of the filmmaking, _Oppenheimer_ is effective during its sustained passages (partly thanks to Cillian Murphy's inspired work), and poor during the overly directed and edited segments (the feet-stomping sound effect is particularly unsubtle). Apart from Murphy, Florence Pugh is memorable as the intense, sweaty left-leaning lover who commits suicide. (Right at the halfway point of the film too; if Nolan has any consistency, it is his mania for killing off female characters, especially in the first half of his films.) Emily Blunt, once again, proves very good at playing herself, which is unfortunately considering she doesn't have the charm of a Charlotte Gainsbourg or Sandrine Kiberlain. Once upon a time she was a promising indie actress ... The rest of the cast is poorly served by the sheer number of cast members. Surely this is a film that would have benefited from condensing/omitting some real life players.

5.title: Bloated and Ridiculously Overrated
5.content:
There is absolutely no reason for this movie to be three hours long. It is loud, "talky", and filled with a number of extraneous characters. We are subjected to WAY too much back story for minor characters who get screen time because they are "major Hollywood actors" making cameos.

Quite frankly, OPPENHEIMER is two separate movies: the first 90 minutes prior to dropping the bomb, followed by another 90 minutes after dropping the bomb. The second half works far better than the first, but it's still WAY too much filler and too many "jump cuts". More is rarely better.

And the soundtrack is distractingly obnoxious.

Great acting all around (especially by Cillian Murphy)...great costumes and makeup...very close to being historically accurate...and an ambitious bio-pic of an important figure in history.

But - overall - a bloated, self-indulgent work that really just panders to the Oscar committee.

5.title: A tiring collage of three very different and disconnected works
5.content:
It's a stretch to call this work a film. The lack of coherence and creative vision is obvious from the start. Nolan's "Oppenheimer" feels like a pile of material produced to fulfill an obligation.

And this comes from someone who actually loves some of the filmmaker's works.

Watching this is a pain, worse than listening to an orchestra without a director. Even in that case, the musicians would be bound to find a minimum of harmony by themselves, just by hearing each other play. This is more akin to someone recording each instrument separately, without any specific rhythm and instructions, and then just mixing all of the recordings together, believing that a symphony will be forced to emerge into existence, simply because each musician was a virtuoso.

During the plain collection of disconnected scenes that is the first out of three (unintentional) parts of this audiovisual work, apart from the exhausting overuse of too loud soundtrack, you have to cope with the feeling that you are binge-watching season one of a history-themed TV series without a clear main story. The second part is quite different, but it's more of a dramatized documentary about the creation of the atomic bomb than a biopic. And then, you are suddenly transferred into watching a courtroom drama without a courtroom.

The relief moments, reminding you that you are watching something cinema-related, are those highlighted by Robert Downey Jr.'s exceptional performance in the role of the antagonist. Cillian Murphy, on the other hand, is shockingly flat; this lack of acting is also painfully evident in all other roles, which is another piece of strong evidence supporting the theory that this three-hours-long video was made without any direction.

Regarding other aspects of filmmaking, there's little-to-none artistic value in this work. I would recommend to avoid watching it. Even if you are prepared for a mediocrity, you will be surprised at how underwhelming the result is.

5.title: No plot, Einstein and the bomb is better
5.content:
I preferred the documentary Einstein and the Bomb. Dialogue was much better. Einstein is also a far more interesting character than Oppenheimer.

I found the film long and overworked. Really it was 30 minutes too long. What were they even debating about in the end I have no idea because it was not really made clear. Security clearances. What precisely was the impact of not having them. Didn't really get the significance.

If you know already the story which I did then thats really all there is to it. I can imagine why it got lots of Oscars because it's set in American and talks a lot about politics which they love.

5.title: More TV movie/docudrama than IMAX epic
5.content:
I find Nolan films falling into the 'trying too hard to be clever' category. He tries to be cinematic but I cannot think of a scene in all his films that is really cinematic except the gliding Spitfire at end of Dunkirk.

Is this because, fundamentally, Nolan's a writer, not a director? He thinks in terms of dialog and narrative not visual.
