I wouldn't go as far as saying Oppenheimer was a mess but chopping the chronological narrative so much when it's a story of event and consequences felt like it did a disservice to that period of history in general and his life in particular.

When you left the screening what message did you take home with you? Was it a sense of pity for Oppenheimer because he was misunderstood, persecuted, responsible, or that this moment was the dawning of the nuclear age -something that was only realised by Oppenheimer? If the latter, why bother with the whole AEC chapter? That could have been 'Oppenheimer Part 2' but, let's face it, no-one would've been interested in that story.

5.title: An Hour Too Long
5.content:
Though I am a big fan of Christopher Nolan, I believe that this film has a number of issues going against it.

First off, it runs far too long and could have probably been whittled down to a couple of hours.

Then there's the unnecessary use of nudity where the point made could have easily been done without the use of it.

The music score is continuous and ramps up in parts where it overshadows much of the dialog.

I have no idea why this film has garnered so many rave reviews but I found it to be mediocre at best, if not boring in much of it.

I'm just glad I didn't shell out the bucks to see it at the theater and instead got the chance to see it for free.

5.title: Wait for it on TV - Dreary take on momentous project
5.content:
The cinema was full, properly full for the first time in at least 3 years, everyone eagerly anticipating this major Hollywood take on the world shaping events of the Manhattan Project.

Within a half hour my wife was asleep, I was still hopeful that the film would step up a gear and start to build, only it never really does, it ambles along for well over an hour before we really hear anything about the project itself. Even then it remains pretty dull.

Do not pay to see this film ! Its a sad fact that, along with the bomb test itself, the other major highlights involve Florence Pugh, playing girlfriend Jean Tatlock, and her most impressive breasts.

The focus of the film is really the, largely irrelevant, aspects of Oppenheimers life before and after, his friendship with some left wing and communist party members.

5.title: Just my opinion, a bit overrated to be honest.
5.content: Sure cinematography and acting were excellent, however I think i hyped myself up for a bit more action than 1 single scene of action in a 3 hour movie and I honestly don't think the build up to that was impressive at all. The score for the movie is way too intrusive even over scenes where they are just sitting in a room chatting lol it reminded me of when youtubers put dubstep music over a clip of them camping out in nature... like trying to force dramatic feelings. This is definitely just a politics as usual drama so don't expect much else to do with the war. I enjoyed the documentary that recently came out, over this big budget hype train.

5.title: Historical Inaccuracies
5.content:
From a cinematic standpoint, Nolan's directorial skills are unmatched.

My issue with the film comes from its highly sympathetic view of Oppenheimer. Nolan makes Oppenheimer into a martyr, which was the same thing that happened in the book this movie is based on. However, the man had heavy communist sympathies. They touch on his belief that the Americans should have been collaborating with the Soviets; however, that's as far as it goes in the movie. There is compelling evidence to suggest that he (or one of his proxies) was leaking secrets to the Soviets. When Truman arrived at Potsdam and told Stalin about the bomb, Stalin already knew about it, meaning this info would likely have come from high up in the chain of command. This movie displayed a sympathetic view of Oppenheimer when in fact he likely was giving info to the USSR.

It is a shame now because we are currently seeing the fruits of the communist infiltration of the 50s and 60s manifesting in the country today. The subversion of America has taken multiple generations, and although Oppenheimer may have been unjustly harassed (I believe justly), the Americans of the 50s were right to be petrified by communist infiltration. If only we would heed their warnings now.

5.title: Tik Tok Anyone?
5.content:
I felt like I was watching hours of Tik Tok videos!

Why so much back and forth? And way too many 2 minute scenes. My head was spinning!

I guess this is the only way to get Gen Z to watch a historical pic?

Don't get me wrong, Cillian Murphy was incredible (no doubts there), and Robert Downey Jr. Stole the movie, in my opinion, but this movie was missing something and I'm not sure what.

Maybe it was the fact that the actor who played Einstein barely looked like him? Maybe it was the dragging of the story because, in all honesty, how interesting could this story be in actual real life? Although it was an incredible story about intellectuals making incredible discoveries that destroyed thousands of lives, it was longer than it should have been and no "Apocalypse Now."

5.title: A miss of a movie that could have been great
5.content: I'm not sure what master piece people watched as this movie did a great job of the lead character, but not much else. The whole point of the bomb was missed and the audience never really understood why it was so needed. The technical aspects could have been skipped and the trial as well. If you are going to make a movie about the A bomb and H bomb then the audience should understand the devastation they cause. The Japan A bomb has never been forgotten and is the very reason no nuclear weapons have been used ever since. The change in Japan from this was massive. This A bomb changed the world of war and prevented a much worse nuclear war between Russia and US. To this day nuclear weapons are not used as Japan is still remembered. This A bomb on Japan is the single biggest impact on the world in regards to war and weapons the world ever saw. And somehow Nolan reduced it to this boring, slow, uninteresting slug of a movie. I guess we can't be great every time.

5.title: Not the best work from Nolan
5.content:
Had always been a fan of Nolan's works, but Oppenheimer certainly is not one of them. Here are my reasons.

First of all, the editing is a huge mess. Unnecessarily overcomplicated and rushed. The movie brushes through scenes like it's browsing on Tiktok, and jumps around different timelines like it has ADHD. What's worse is that a lot of these mini scenes are pretty much pointless fillers, serving no purpose whatsoever.

Second, they throw in new characters every few minutes and fail to develop almost any of them. Despite the great acting, they still feel dull and abundant. By the end of the movie, I couldn't recognize half of the cast nor do I care much about them.

Most importantly, does it have to be THIS LONG? The first half of the events are simply unnecessary and uninteresting. The length could have been cut down by an hour and nothing will be lost. I understand Nolan wants to include Oppenheimer's private life as well as events that impacted him prior/post the Manhattan project. However most of these are at very surface level, as the movie tries to run through so many different storylines and yet didn't really focus on and dive into any of them. It wasn't as thought provoking or emotion evoking as it tries to be, instead it becomes a tedious mess with so much happening but nothing much to take away from.

I have to make it clear though, despite my rant, I don't think this is a bad movie. I think the scenes are well shot and directed. The cinematography and acting is undoubtedly top tier. I like the visuals and sound effects, and certainly enjoyed the second half way more than the first.

That being said, this is still quite a let down as I had a lot of expectation for this one. Although this could be the type of movie that you'd enjoy more on a second watch (given more context), I 100% will not spend another 3hrs on this ever again.

5.title: Easily Nolans worst work
5.content:
The problem with Christopher Nolan movies is, that no matter the premise, people will always enter the theatre with incredibly (and sometimes unrealistically) high expectations. I don´t think, many people would get overly excited about watching a 3 hour biopic about Robert Oppenheimer, but put Christopher Nolans name on it and it becomes one of the biggest blockbusters of the year. I am a huge Nolan fan as well but tried to limit my excitement as much as possible, remembering very well that in 2020, I left Tenet kind of disappointed because of my unrealitstically high expectations - even though it was overall a very good movie (after the second viewing that is). For Oppenheimer, it didn´t make it easier, that movie theatres were immediately sold out for days and initial critics (even the ones that were not generated by Chat GPT) were showering it with praise. I finally managed to get a seat in a rather small theatre tonight and have to say: Even with neutral expectations, this movie was a disappointment.

Don´t get me wrong, with a 100 Million dollar budget, it will obviously still provide you with incredible imagery, flawless acting, a great soundtrack (there is a BUT! Though) and an original story that still manages to give you a blockbuster feeling, something that has become very rare in Hollywood these days. But I will still not watch it again. Here´s why:

Christopher Nolan movies have often stood out from the crowd, due to 1. Big spectacle, that was held together by 2. An emotional story at its core, with 3. Some kind of twist considering the narrative structure. Oppenheimer completely neglects the emotional part and tries but fails to deliver on both the spectacle (with one obvious exception) and the narrative complexity. The narrative device of telling the story over three different timelines delivers one (maybe two) exciting twists at the very end but otherwise almost feels like Christopher Nolan just HAD to use different time periods because...that´s his thing. Telling the story through retrospective court hearings is not new and most of the scenes do not really add anything. The Social Network for example did a much better job of incorporating this narrative device. If you are expecting big spectacle, you have to be aware that 95% of this movie is pure dialogue. There´s nothing wrong with that per se, but Nolan has never been famous for his great dialogue writing skills (except for some memeable Joker quotes I guess) and this movie is no exception in that regard. There are like 5 witty one-liners (most of which already given away in the trailer), the rest is basically characters explaining the different plot points to each other (minor exceptions apply). The spectacle is provided by the Nuclear bomb explosion scene and I am not gonna lie, this scene is spectacular and very satisfying to watch, amplified by the fact that the almost 120 minutes leading up to it have been very underwhelming (more about that in a second). Nolan reportedly was very proud of this scene, being shot completely without CGI, which is undeniably an incredible cinematic achievement, but if you are expecting to be blown away (pun intended) by a 150 minutes visual, action-packed extravaganza ala Inception, the dark knight, or Tenet, be aware that this is a completely different movie. The emotional component is completely absent, the relationship between Oppenheimer and his wife is reduced to maybe 10 minutes of shared screentime, with Kitty Oppenheimer being a voice of reason and concern about Mr. Oppenheimers scientific, political and romantic endeavours, and him barely reacting to it. Oppenheimers affair and the rather unfortunate ending to it is also not given enough screen time to have any emotional impact on the viewer. All of the other characters (except Lewis Strauss) are mainly reduced to Cameos anyway, without any insight into their emotional site whatsoever. Which brings me to the main point, why this movie fails:

For the first 120 minutes, up until the nuclear explosion, the movie has NO ACTUAL SCENES. I´m sure I´m not the only one, who occasionally gets stuck on youtube, browsing multiple, 3-4 minutes long clipped out scenes of my favorite movies. I dare you to try clipping out memorable scenes of the first two hours of Oppenheimer. It is an impossible task. No scene can actually breathe, it is a just constant cutaway of Oppenheimer meeting a certain character, sharing 10 seconds of dialogue, moving on to the next location, the next character, the next scenery, the next "plotpoint", with dramatic music CONSTANTLY playing in the background, trying to create an artificial sense of urgency. In the beginning, I thought this would be just to get through the first stations of Oppenheimers life quickly before the actual plot can kick off, until it dawned on me, that the whole movie is cut that way. What doesn´t help is the neverending CAMEO parade of A-list Hollywood actors, that makes you wonder "oh wow, what are they going to do with this character?", before you realize that you will most likely never see him again. In that sense, the atomic bomb explosion scene is a huge relief, because the movie finally STOPS. Takes its time to develop a scene. Shows characters emotions. When the music stops for these couple of seconds, I even breathed out a sigh of relief. And after this scene, the movie actually takes a turn for the better. The scene of Oppenheimer mentally checking out in front of a cheering crowd is great. The meeting with Truman scene is great. Even the final congressional hearing scenes and a few of the final court testimonies are great. Because Nolan finally takes some time to develop some actual character interactions, instead of just rushing over them. The ending scene is great. But if the first two hours of the movie are rushed, a good (but also not perfect) last hour can´t really save it. At least not for me. For me, this is by far Nolans most disappointing film, but even if it had been done by a different director, I still would not consider it to be a good film. So if you are craving a blockbuster, that does not contain superheroes, video game characters or toys, jump onto the hypetrain and watch it, but if someone asked me for a list of 200 movie reccommendations, Oppenheimer would probably not be on it. 5/10.

5.title: Everyone's talking about the good, so I'm gonna talk about the bad
5.content:
What I have against this movie :
in the beginning you as a spectator are just abandoned in the middle of a story without any introduction or exposition, like you're expected to do your homework at home and just after go to see the movie
for a good majority of time the movie is dragging, in some points is has pointless dialogue and drama
too many characters and names you don't know nothing about and are too hard to keep counting
the sex scene was awkward and the nudity seemed really unnecessary
it seemed like the movie followed to many narrative threads for the majority of time and then struggled to connect them in the last half an hour - thus connecting the loose ends seemed forced at times and since there was little to no character development or study to the majority of the characters, at times they acted, guess what, "out of character". For real, there were like a hundred characters introduced to us only for them to appear for like 1 and a half minutes.

5.title: McCarthy witch-hunt of 1949, little else. Hard pass
5.content: Turgid boredom that managed to suck the life out of the awe and brilliance of quantum discovery, portraying seminal theoretical psychists as lowly clerks, and focusing on U. S. commy paranoia. No soundtrack, just a wall of bass. Nolan utterly failed in script. Lighting too dark. No build of tension - you will forget you are there to see the inception of atomic bombs. Not even a courtroom thriller - just endless questioning of Oppenheimer in a room, and a complete fizzle of an atomic explosion. Acting fine, but I'm in the presence of Einstein and checking my watch!?! This should have had huge tension as Nazi's vs. Allies race - you'd hardly know it was WW2. As a warning about A. I., as Christopher Nolan said he had intended, then we are all doomed.

5.title: Irrelevant
5.content:
Boring story about the questionable persecution of supposed communists in the McCarthy era.

The history of the development of the atomic bomb is treated only marginally. The military Manhattan project with its enormous human, industrial and financial expenditure is mentioned but not presented or questioned. There is no processing of moral questions, historical backgrounds, the actions of individuals or scientific backgrounds.

The film as a whole is irrelevant. If you are interested in the topic, you should read a book or simply read a few Wikipedia artists. If you are more into visuals, the graphic novel THE BOMB The Weapon That Changed the World is recommended.

5.title: Bad men giving a genius a hard time
5.content:
"Very rarely go to the cinema these days - rip off candy bar, can't pause it to take a break to stretch, pee, or a smoke for smokers.

But sometimes a film comes along that I believe would be worth watching on the big screen. Unfortunately, I should have waited for the reviews because when it was explained by some reviewers to be boring because it wasn't about the science but some bad men giving a genius a hard time with hearings and backroom dealings, I would have waited for the digital releases online, and then be dissappointed.

Nolan also threw in some obligatory sex in there and a bit of ineffective heartstring pulling. My God, I couldn't believe how bored I was. I get that some viewers are into politics and conspiracy theories but there are thousands of people in history that could have been chosen for that type of story but Oppie had a much bigger place in history than some bad men giving him a hard time, they may as well make a film about me always being given a hard time by controlling types, but I didn't organise men to split the atom, and if I did, I would want that story told.

So glad my sister and niece declined my invitation to see it, because I would have been apologising for weeks. Why Nolan thought the politics of that time and the human backstory of Oppie would be more interesting than the academic interactions of the scientists and the science problems being conquered is beyond me to understand. If I ever meet Nolan, I will just ask him, "Oppenheimer, WTF?""

5.title: Not what I expected from a film so highly touted but a big disappointment
5.content:
Usually within the first fifteen (15) to thirty (30) minutes of a film I can usually determine if a film will stir that movie excitement within me we all long to feel. Unfortunately in the case of Oppenheimer I started to get that uneasy feeling which sometimes happens when I feel I have been bamboozled by the Hollywood hype and by a well laid out marketing campaign.

Approximately at the thirty (30) minute mark Mrs Shullivan and I both simultaneously shared our disappointment in what we were watching was very disappointing from what we were expecting and experiencing.

The film Oppenheimer was turning into a biography turned into a movie in which the film stars were almost reading their lines over top of one another if you listened closely. Also seriously competing for film cred was the irritating and non stop music score in a poor attempt at maintaining some semblance of drama and urgency within the moment of screen time when in fact Mrs Shullivan and I just found the music score was almost a continuous five (5) sequence musical note which worked much better in the original 1970s "JAWS" franchise films than it does in Oppenheimer.

All in all we both found the film a big disappointment so I can only provide an IMDb rating of 5 out of 10.

5.title: Nolan forgot that not everyone knows the story already. Missed opp.
5.content:
Like many here, I was excited to see this movie and learn more about Oppenheimer. Nolan sadly jumped back and forth through the decades that it was pissing me off. Too many characters and Nolan definitely made the assumption that all movie goers would fully know the story, know all of the characters/scientists, etc. For a story about Oppenheimer, Strauss (Downey, Jr.) seems to have more screen time...and really why? I was lost and this film, while visually great looking, fails to tell the story of this person so we walk away knowing his full story, especially since it dragged on for 3 hours! No summary at the end, like how many of these people at Los Alamos later died of cancer, like Oppenheimer, would have been educational and helpful. Wikipedia will be more helpful and that's a shame. Head scratcher.

#Disappointed and yet it will likely win Best Movie Oscar as those voters won't want to admit they didn't understand it either.

5.title: Overhyped
5.content:
This movie is really not worth your time. Poor story, great actors with nothing to do. Definitely one of the worst Christopher Nolan movies.

It just does nothing. There is no suspense. There is no interesting politics. Basically no character development. Not even some suspense of the hard scientific problems solved, the hard moral and ethical dilemmas. Even the big finale is just the bomb test, not dropping them on Japan.

The could have gone deeper into the science like with Interstellar. They could've have had the global geopolitics like with Ambassador. Really none of this is done. We don't even really learn about Openhimer as a person. His womanising is glossed over. The weekend it was released, the Barbie movie also came out. Wish we saw that instead....

5.title: Overdone
5.content:
I thoroughly disliked the directing of this movie. It was way too long, had a confusing, pinball timeline. There was unnecessarily tense music throughout, turning every mundane interaction into a high stakes anxiety fest. The dialogue is awkwardly terse. Overall, it's an unenjoyable experience. What ever happened to just telling a story?? This feels like an over-produced caricature of a Hollywood movie.

Like all movies, the dialogue is too quiet, and the music and explosions are too loud.

I'm sure this just sounds like a rant to many of you. Feel free to ignore it you disagree. I just wanted to share my opinion.

5.title: Movie was a bomb...
5.content: Biggest disappointment of the year. Not Oscar worthy of best picture. The movie is called Oppenheimer which is the main focus of the story. You will be disappointed if you expect to see more about the bomb. The movie trailer used sensational and tense images about the bomb which were only a small part of the actual movie. There was nothing intense or attention getting about this movie. It was boring, political and way, way too long. So many better choices if your interested about the bomb story. I suggest the 1989 movie "Fat and Little Boy" If you want entertaining TV drama the 2014 series Manhattan is worth watching the show is fiction, but the major elements that the show is based on are true.

5.title: I must be missing something.
5.content:
Not sure the hype around Oppenheimer. I am a fan of Nolan but his storytelling is somewhat strange. Timeline never flows properly and the movie likes to jump all around.

I like Dunkirk, I love Batman Dark Knight Trilogy, I thought Inception was thought provoking as well as Interstellar but his last film Tenet and this one was just utterly bad storytelling.

There are many parts to like, the great music the odd and weird way we get to feel inside Oppenheimer's head but for the most part the movie was just too long and narrative was all over the place.

There is story about his youth, story about his Manhattan project, story about his politics, story about his trial to remove his status and finally a story about a political rival ann maybe even a story about his lover. If you could of rearrange and stop jumping around this movie would of been better for me.

5.title: 6 stars is pretty disappointing for Nolan's movie.
5.content: Christopher Nolan's latest directorial effort left me with mixed feelings. The screenplay and scriptwriters fell short, resulting in a convoluted and confusing narrative. Despite Nolan's attempts to overdo things, the weak foundation couldn't support the complexity. The music lacked a thematic connection to the storyline, leaving the overall experience underwhelming. While the film showcased impressive visuals and cinematography, it couldn't compensate for its flaws. A five-star rating for technical prowess, but the execution fell flat, leaving me wanting more from this talented director. Hoping for a better show next time around.

5.title: Overrated
5.content:
I don't really get the hype. I find Nolan's movies to be unnecessarily complicated without a coherent plot to produce enough build up of any emotion. Movies that are not linear in timeline are for some reason perceived as smarter???

And although the movie attempted to show Oppenheimer as a man with moral remorse, it never showed us a glimpse of the Japanese who experienced this tragedy. I did show a total lack of empathy from Americans at the time however, which I believe is accurate to a large extent.

The production and cinematography are on point and on that level- well done as always. Personally though, i need a more linear plot. The movie seemed to switch from one point to another thing without logical smooth transition ...

5.title: Great topic but too long, too complex
5.content:
Topic is very good as it takes the viewers through the development of the atomic bomb.

Casting is very good.

However, I found the back and forth in time quite confusing at times. It's not an easy movie to watch, you really need to concentrate .

Also, found it too heavy and way too long.

The Director obviously did an impressive amount of research and at times felt I was watching almost a documentary.

However, I would have liked to see this movie lasting maximum 2 hours. Way too long.

Can't fault the actors and actresses especially Downey Jr, I wouldn't be surprised that he would win an Oscar for his interpretation.

5.title: Watch a documentary
5.content: Too long and disjointed tale of a brilliant yet disturbed lonely man. Just read about him and learn more. This movie did not do justice to this momentous event of physics, science, and the creation of an atomic bomb. If Germany or even Russia had built a weapon so destructive, they would now be ruling this already troubled world. Just imagine Hitler living another 20 or 30 years with the Nazis controlling this Planet. I wish these bombs, any nuclear bombs did not exist. However, I sure am grateful to the brilliant men collectively in America who got there first. However, just skip this twisted and disjointed attempt to inform the public of this complex and momentous era in world History.

5.title: emperor's new clothes ☹
5.content:
Christopher Nolan is about to release a new movie!! Wahay!!

Its a no brainer!!!

You are guaranteed to expect a story hidden inside an ever elaborate riddle with the occasional paradox thrown in to keep you on the edge of the seat, and the whole thing..You can bet your bottom dollar..will be expertly delivered by a cast with exquisite passion.

You won't understand much of what was before your eye first time so you'll have to watch the film over a dozen times, without an atom of reduction in your enthusiasm your attention never fluctuating, the reward, a revelation of the beautiful complexity.

So when the story of one of the most important achievements of humanity was Nolans new project one can be forgiven for becoming just a tad overjoyed.

The anticipation was overwhelming the cast was A list but I'm afraid Oppenheimer was a HUGE disappointment. Can someone explain why Cillian Murphy won an Oscar?

The acting was fine and that's all it was just fine nothing exceptional.

Maybe documentary style genre is not for Christopher Nolan.

Non linear presentation just feels broken, many different bits and pieces just put together didn't make much sense.

There are similarities to the lives of Oppenheimer and Alan turing, biopic of the latter told brilliantly in The Imitation games.

I'm assuming the high rating is due to Christopher Nolans die hard disciples.

Im certain if this film was directed by somebody else the rating will be below 5.

Anyway looking forward to Christopher Nolans next project with overwhelming anticipation.

5.title: missed the mark
5.content:
The last hour of this movie is soooo much better than the first 2 hours. I would imagine most people know the general story of the atomic bomb but the story of all the after math isn't often taught in an overview of american history.

The story is told beginning to middle and end to middle so for the last hour they meet and we get to the good part. For me, this isn't very effective story telling since we are getting important parts of the end of the story at the very beginning of the movie. I think it's a lazy way to "elevate" the movie and the jaw dropping surprises would've been more impactful if told chronologically.

The beginning is too fast and introduced the viewer to 30+ characters so vaguely that by the time each deposition comes around, it doesn't have the weight it should because we don't know these people and their relationships very well (apart from groves, rabi, and strauss).

For how big this movie was and the high rating, i was shockingly disappointed! 3 hours and i had to take 2 breaks until the last hour really grabbed me.

5.title: Disappointing, but not for a lack of effort.
5.content:
This was a tough one to get through for me. The pacing and score of the film were unrelenting, and scenes were cut together with the same mentality of one who thinks music would sound better if we played the notes as fast as possible. Scenes of over dramatic intensity felt used to divert the viewer from something lacking in the film. To me certain scenes were so saturated with drama I wanted to pantomime the puking gesture.

My suspension of disbelief dropped every time I saw Albert Einstein. All of the Hollywood-ized science talk was also particularly cringeworthy. I understand most audience members probably wouldn't get hung up on this as much, but for scientists I think this is a difficult hurdle to leap over.

This felt like a Frankenstein of a movie for me, seeing Nolan's excellent style plastered onto a nonfictional story seemed like something an AI might create. Ultimately it felt jarring and lacked the conviction it was striving so desperately to portray. I'm glad so many people enjoyed it, but this was a total flop for me.

5.title: Average
5.content:
So, I saw this this one after seeing many previews for it & had a feeling it would be good with an interesting story to tell, that & of course it was either this or Barbie (shudders), of course I went for this & thought it was average but only just that.

During World War II, Lt. Gen. Leslie Groves Jr. Appoints physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer to work on the Top-Secret Manhattan Project. Oppenheimer & a team of scientists spend years developing & designing the Atomic Bomb.

I found the film to be average, it's actually not bad & I'd have to say, the first Christopher Nolan Film I liked, if not the only. Though not nearly amazing, it's good & at least whipped the floor with that Barbie Film. But that's another rant for another time in regards to that flick, but anyhow, this film was enjoyable, but a chore to sit through. It's overly long & drawn being the main 2 issues I had when watching. The dialogue & the characters were the other 2 things, the former being too confusing & hard to get, though I did just about get what they were saying with the story & the latter, well, was in itself like the story of the film, a bit hard to follow & understand.

The action in the film is good, but too few & far between. The runtime is a whopping 2 hours & 55 minutes, too long, way too long & that doesn't help with the dialogue & multiple characters being thrown in, not to mention the poor pacing issues this film had. But in comparison to Tenet & Inception, this was good & at least was mildly coherent, even though I did still find this flick hard to get, but it's Christopher Nolan innit? Rolls eyes...

The eye candy & effects were good not to mention the visuals which were pretty impressive. Cillian Murphy done a great job at portraying Robert Oppenhiemer, so there's that at least.

Overall, it's an overbloated film with poor pacing & a 175 minute runtime that could've used a load of work to it to make it snappier & more to the point, why it had to be stretched beyond breaking point is beyond me. The effects were good as with the eye candy, effects & the acting from Cillian & the others, but aside from that, it was average & at least better than Tenet, Inception & most importantly, Barbie...

5/10.

5.title: Flashy and overly long
5.content: One of the more critically successful films released last year, sees a large cast in Christopher Nolan's long awaited blockbuster. This film features a cast full of award winners and critically acclaimed veterans. The acting isn't the problem from a film standpoint. As a whole the budget is big which shows its great visuals and overall scenery. However the story is rather boring to a degree and it drags on quite a bit. The first hour feels somewhat like a filler while it does pick up but even so, the story is something that you must be truly invested in to have a great enjoyment. Overall, it's simply not as compelling as praised to be.

5.title: Disappointing.
5.content:
First time I've ever nodded off in a cinema. Firstly, the film is WAY too long. The characters are pretty much universally unlikeable and it is chock full of meandering wramblings from the McCarthy era mascinations.

There is no edge of the seat narrative, and I know that this is not the subject for that. However, there should be some entertainment in a feature film that long.

Overpowering musical score basically drowning out everything else didn't help.

The Prestige is one of my favourite films that stands up to repeated viewing time and time again. Oppenheimer though visually spectacular in some aspects had me longing for the end. Disappointing.

5.title: Despite a 1 mile Blast radius, this film still misses.
5.content:
As a die hard Nolan fan this film missed hard.

It's way too long for starters. It's basically two separate movies. The token time twist Nolan uses was nothing more than a flashback which really didn't do much other than let us watch two movies simultaneously.

The soundtrack was eh. There was only one stunning visuals scene, so IMAX is wasted. The story/characters didn't really have any emotional pull for me. Not like Interstellar, Inception, Prestige, Dark Knight. No real twist at the end that makes you think. Whoa!

RDJ did great and was thr standout for me. Especially seeing him get away from being Tony Stark.

Emily Blunt also had an amazing scene near the end but unfortunately her role was minimal in the story.

The trailers made this out to be more of a thriller espionage style film, instead we get a lot of science talk no where near as cool as Interstellar and a lawyer hearing interrogation that isn't a trial with no tension.

Bummer since I was really looking forward to this one. Just wait and rent it.

5.title: Too Hollywoodized Up
5.content:
It's not a terrible movie. I was very excited to watch, being a fan of history and the sciences. It just seemed... poorly executed. A great idea that fell sort of flat, running along some cinematic cliches.

One of the things that kind of got me was the gratuitous sex scenes. Don't get me wrong, I like boobies just as much as the next guy/gal, just... seemed out of place. It seemed like someone was checking off the bingo card of Hollywood notions needed in a good movie.

A lot of the acting too was just... flat. Which is weird with the ensemble they had. There are a few emotions that come across in there, but nothing ever explored. Every time someone begins to get into an idea, whether it's about communism, patriotism, morality or pragmatism, they've already moved onto the next scene. There is one point where Oppenheimer is riding a horse through a desert, stumbles on a notice of meeting being held about the morality of deploying the "gadget". He walks in during a heated debate, speaks a handful of words, people clap, then it's onto the next thing.

It's like there was a disagreement between directors, producers, and story tellers. I felt like I was following a schizophrenic through high paced imaginings... and that's coming from a schizophrenic. They wanted to shove decades worth into five minute increments.

In the end, I couldn't even finish the movie. Think I got to the last 30 minutes, but was just frustrated with the piss-poor linear then non-linear story telling. Again, seemed like a great idea that just was not executed properly.

5.title: This well-made film lacks rewatchability
5.content:
While this film is enjoyable, it might not be one that viewers come out loving. The majority of the entertainment value of this film is in the beginning leading to the creation of the atomic bomb. Once the bomb is created and tested the rest of the film becomes a bit underwhelming. The aftermath of the attacks on Japan were shared through dialogue and a bit of quirky visuals but nothing truly showing how those people were affected by the bomb. It would have been emotionally gripping to have those visuals or even real news reports from when the attacks took place.

The events of the film do not follow a linear path and the use of greyscale and color help to distinguish those events. The use of sound in this film was also utilized very well to create tension and to set the mood. The acting by the entire cast was top notch which was elevated by the strong dialogue.

However, the role played by Florence Pugh was unnecessary and served more as a distraction to the overall film. The story could have been told without it which would have decreased the runtime that dragged at times.

Rami Malek's character was underdeveloped and it only becomes more apparent when his importance is revealed and one is left wondering why he only had two silly scenes.

Other small roles such as the one played by Casey Affleck's provided just enough context to understand his role and significance in the story.

Robert Downey Jr. Does a great job at his role but the motives for his character seem silly. While these motives might have been true to the real-life person it just took away from the character and weakened the story. Cillian Murphy delivers a well-acted performance but his character's personality is bland. Thus, making the film less interesting.

In the end, this well-made film lacks rewatchability. It tells the story it wants to tell but it doesn't make it compelling enough. A well-made film doesn't make for a great story.

5.title: "Your reproductive system is more exposed them mine, presumably." Lilli Horning
5.content:
I was pretty disappointed from the beginning. They spend more time on sparkling pictures of sub atomics then facts or story. Then it only gets worse from there. We get flashbacks in flashbacks in flashbacks. To help in the confusion sometime it is in black and white, and other times it is in full color without any relations as to why. Then there is that awful tinkling music that permeates but does not enhance the experience. The birthday suit scenes were fun to watch, but they were gratuitous. Can you say soap opera?

On the positive side it was fun to see all the different major actors and think, " Now where have I seen him/her before?" It looked like everyone wanted to get into the act. This was not a venue for out of work, over the hill actors. In the middle of the soap opera there were some real personalities and facts that gave the production some value.

The whole thing turns into a shallow conspiracy story. Or is it?

A side note is that it was interesting to see that Leslie Groves: Matt Damon wore the same shoulder patch that I did while I was in the Army Map Service.

5.title: Misses the Mark...
5.content:
The expectations that go into a Nolan film have obviously affected the end product of most of his more recent efforts, so much so that the great potential story of one of the most significant technological events in history becomes poorly told.

From a historical perspective, so many significant events from the development of atomic weapons are left out, such as Heisenberg (Germany) almost killing himself during his own experiments, the exodus of great scientists to the US preceding the Nazi uprising, the Demon Core incidents after the War, and the celebrity status Oppenheimer achieved after the War. Zero historical footage is used in this film, which is worse for it as so much amazing stuff could be repurposed here. We aren't even allowed to feel anything about the atrocities of Germany, Japan, or the USSR at the time. In fact, a key reason Truman wanted to end the war with the bomb quickly was to keep the Soviets from making a mess of post-war Japan by claiming lands by invasion, which would have led to a partly communist Japan to this day.

From a science perspective, little is told about the development of the bombs themselves, including the obstacles the scientists really faced and the achievements they made. No mention of the idea that the technology could also be used to save the world (nuclear power), being reason enough to push forward with the research, aside from keeping it out of Germany's hands, which was a real concern of the government.

As such, this isn't a documentary. Not at all. Any of the aforementioned stuff would have made for a brilliant Nolan film...but I don't see him capable of makes a film with real science and history.

Neither is it a character study, as the biopic title suggests. Rather it's a vehicle for Nolan to edit together trailer-type cuts across changing timelines for 3 hours. I found it tiresome and frenetic. While the acting is good, none of it makes us feel anything for the characters. While there was an opportunity to work on the morality angle for Oppenheimer, which was very much what the real man was about, the film glosses over this to focus only on the politics of the time, where the McCarthy era witch-hunts ended Oppenheimer's career as a quantum physicist. Even then, Nolan misses an opportunity to vilify those actions by the government, making no real statements there.

The result of the 3 hours is the simple message that the genie cannot be put back in the bottle, and in Oppenheimer's mind, would end in our destruction.

That said, all the high grades for this film come from Nolan fanboys, who write pretentious reviews for pretentious films.

5.title: High expectations not met
5.content:
I went to the theater with very high expectations, but sadly enough they were not met. Especially from Christopher Nolan I would have expected something better.

The choice of telling the story out of order made it very difficult to follow especially if you do not know anything about Openheimer in advance. So I would really recommend to do a small research in advance to enjoy the movie more, since I had more questions in the end than answers.

This movie also introduces so many people and names, which makes it almost impossible to remember them all and follow the story easily. In this story they could have easily left some people out that had no sufficiently large role. This movie would have been better for a series, to flesh out the characters that are there better. Or I would have removed everything about Strauss, because it made this movie way too long and did not really add anything to the story of Oppenheimer.

The score and cinematography on the other hand were fantastic. Also the actors on screen are doing all an amazing job.

5.title: Loud, hectic and confusing
5.content:
The film was, similar to TENET before, so overloaded with the soundtrack that one was permanently under tension, although 90% of the film consisted only of dialogues that didn't need any sound background. There was jumping back and forth between characters and temporal events without further explanation and a chronological order, so that one lost the connection at some point. The film couldn't decide which story to tell: the life story of Oppenheimer, the anti-communist movements in the U. S. government, or the development of the atomic bomb.

Nolan applies the familiar method of telling several stories in parallel at the same time. He and many of his fans think this is ingenious; I think it is unnecessarily confusing. In films where multiple stories at the same time make sense, like Inception, Interstellar, or Tenet, it's a legitimate means of storytelling because they are fictional stories. In films like Oppenheimer, however, it has no place because the story is in the past and consequently could and should be told chronologically.

This is another Nolan film where he celebrates himself as a genius. However, genius here is confused with overconfidence. Movies should be for the audience, not to celebrate one's ego.

It feels like going to a five-star chef who has created a few outstanding dishes in the past and now thinks he has to continue offering the same dishes with a different recipe, and they would still be outstanding. The zenith of genius has been passed and the chef lives off his reputation, which many still celebrate.

5.title: Superficial pseudo-epic and unwarranted showmanship
5.content:
When I walked out of the theater after watching 'Oppenheimer' my soul was profoundly shaken, shaken by such a touching theme, such profound characters, and the fact that such a muddy period in history could be portrayed so shallow and contrived by Nolan.

What kind of century was the 20th century? If I were to ask you this question like in a game of 'rapid-fire questions,' what vocabulary would you use? Personally, I might say that the 20th century was a divisive century. Two wars of apocalyptic scale and brutality, numerous new ideologies leading to various actions, the rapid development of new technologies, and the impact of new social movements on each other. Therefore, the 20th century signifies not only physical division but also spiritual division. People were torn apart not only in times of war but also in times of peace.

So how should we describe Oppenheimer who greatly molded the 20th century and was greatly shaped by it? An American? A Jew? A patriot? A sympathizer of the left? A savior? A destroyer? A fanatic? A penitent? A brave man? A coward? A passionate individual? A libertine? He is all of the above, and yet he denies all of the above. Thus, he is the most perfect and painful symbol of his century - a divider. His century further tore apart the already torn him, and vice versa.

Compared to the original biography, Nolan's film completely fails to capture the profound individual psyche of Oppenheimer and the tragic spirit that resonates from the shared history of the 20th century's fatal divisions. There is no denying the fact that this film, in its emotional intensity and narrative structure, lacks the depth and diligence necessary to honor Oppenheimer himself.

In Nolan's work, there is a glaring absence of the director's exploration into Oppenheimer's terrifying paranoia and how his shattered self evolved. The film fails to depict Oppenheimer's multiple identity crises, his peculiar hunger and coldness within intimate relationships. It also fails to portray how this interdisciplinary genius conveyed to the world that mysticism and rational scientific pursuits ultimately converge in both purpose and spiritual experience. Furthermore, the film overlooks Oppenheimer's exhaustion and greatness as a mediator between the military and scientists during the Manhattan Project. It neglects to showcase the hellish frustrations he encountered throughout the atomic bomb development process, and the even more hellish determination belonging to both genius and madness. The film does not reveal how Oppenheimer's soul was fiercely contested by a sense of omnipotence and guilt after the bomb's detonation. It also fails to capture Oppenheimer's fluctuation between immense grief and anger during the McCarthy era, as well as his occasional temptation by a saintly mentality.

If we approach "Oppenheimer" from an epic perspective, it is undoubtedly a completely hollow film. In this movie, the masses are absent, heroes are suspended, men are marionettes, women are blow-up dolls, eras are fashion shows, individuals are mere tourists ticking off their checklist. Everything is superficial and fleeting, barely scratching the surface. The ensemble-style script should have meant that by turning each participant on the historical stage into a single path, a nerve, a dice, viewers would be amazed at the perfect yet cruel interplay of the web of destiny and the brain of God, as well as the infinite possibilities and a series of blind, sober, inevitable, and accidental moments when they observe the unstoppable giant called history. Such an experience would make us feel the same awe as our predecessors did when contemplating quantum mechanics: light is both a wave and a particle, and we exist as individuals and as history. However, "Oppenheimer" is a counterfeit epic. Nolan mistakenly believes that a large number of people can embody the clamor and grandeur of heroism, but unfortunately, it lacks care and profound exploration.

The editing is also a major flaw of this film. It feels so chaotic, lacking emotional and historical logic in its editing, as if I can hear Nolan shouting at me across the big screen, "Look, so many temporal and spatial inter weavings! Is my editing grand enough? Is it epic enough?"

5.title: Bewilderingly Overly-ambitious Story Arc
5.content:
I'll begin by saying Oppenheimer is technically very impressive (cinematography, acting, sound, etc.). Absolutely top notch Nolan on display as always. Where the movie distinctly falls short, however, is the sheer uncompromising amount of *stuff* the movie wants to tell you.

The film is about Oppenheimer's initial days as a physicist, and the early discovery of nuclear fission, and Oppenheimer's role setting up Los Alamos, and the preparation for/execution of the trinity test, and the infiltration of Los Alamos by soviet spies, and Oppenheimer's personal ethical considerations over the bomb's use, and Oppenheimer's personal shortcomings with regards to womanising/arrogance, and Oppenheimer's investigation post-WW2 regarding possible communist links, and Robert Downer Jr.'s character's dislike of Oppenheimer and attempts to get himself instated on the board of some form of senate comittee at the expense of Oppenheimer's career (yeah I also thought that was a little shoe-horned in there). There's just sooo much content; everything's rushed to cut down the runtime, and no moments get time to breathe.

If you're dead-set on telling the Oppenheimer story then maybe focus on part of it and give it time to shine. Either tell the 'what Oppenheimer did' story (the setting up of Los Alamos and the creation of the atomic bomb) or the 'how Oppenheimer felt' story (his reactions to the bomb, ethical conundrums, and how those things affected his life after WW2).

Or, I dunno, maybe just focus on the actual Manhattan Project? To somewhat paraphrase the old scriptwriting adage - 'Is this the most interesting part of your war-bomb story? If not, why aren't you focusing us that?'

5.title: Great acting, boring movie
5.content:
I know I'm in the significant minority here on this review, but I was honestly not impressed with Oppenheimer. I went in not knowing what to expect from it other than the few snippets of previews I had seen and obviously what I knew from my American history lessons in college.

The casting was great and I have to say that they all did a wonderful job, but to me, this biographical movie was too long for me to find it enjoyable. With a nearly 3-hour run time, it was 99% talking and about .5% of a bomb explosion, which was really the highlight of the movie for me.

I wish movie directors would realize that longer runtimes are not always better. Had this movie been closer to about 2 hours, maybe 2 hours and 15 minutes, it would have been much more enjoyable due to the faster pace of storytelling.

The runtime is really my only complaint about the movie, everything else was great, but unfortunately, the excessive runtime impacted my enjoyment of the movie as a whole.

5.title: More Perfunctory Masturbation
5.content: The pretension overwhelms within the first minutes, creating an almost impenetrable barrier to genuine engagement. This movie is essentially a three-hour-long trailer as are so many of Nolan's films. Oppenheimer is filled with flashy sequences, over thought quotables, and dramatic cuts that substitute for substantive storytelling. Cliché after cliché is deployed with precision, each one meticulously designed to elicit a nod of approval from viewers who profess a love for classic films they've never seen. The movie's attempts at profundity often feel forced and insincere, a trademark of a Nolan feature, and little room is left for nuanced exploration of its themes. Instead of offering a compelling narrative, it relies heavily on visual spectacle, foley artistry, and grandiose dialogue that feels entirely hollow. The result is a cinematic experience that is yet again mostly concerned with winning awards and praise by those no longer concerned with wanting new experiences. Nolan caters to a superficial appreciation of cinema rather than delivering truly impactful or memorable myths. From my point of view, it appears as if the only person Christopher Nolan is incapable of boring is himself.

5.title: Disappointed
5.content: I admit, I had high expectations. Maybe too high. And don't get me wrong, the movie is perfect in sense of pictures, acting, scenery and everything but it's just boring. Every YouTube episode of Kyle Hill's HalfLife series is more entertaining than this movie, and that's the disappointment for me, personally. There were so much more (real) stories of, for example, accidents involved in the Manhatten project that could have been part of the movie. A great chance, sadly missed out on. Based on the current ratings I'm the minority here, I know. But I talked to quite some people about that film and I am by far not the only one thinking there should have been more going on. In the end it was to less science and too much soap opera for me.

5.title: It's a typical Oscar movie - boring!
5.content:
The movie is okay. Wasted in IMAX. The music production is at best, oppressive, intrusive and a distraction from what are great actors doing their thing. The script might have multiple layers but it lacks conflict, an inciting incident and a meaningful resolution. It's linear, which biopics tend to be, but it's not a 'story'. Flawed genius? Perhaps or just an unfaithful man - not ground breaking and it lacked a real reason to 'be'. It might have been better if Heisenberg and Oppenheimer were enemies instead of friends or some personal conflict existed that resulted in a winner. Here the movie falls flat and tries to use over bearing music to fill a void left by a lifeless underdramatic script.

Murphy is great but too many cameos by so many stars became distracting with characters lacking depth or development.

You will glance at your watch more than once.

A shame.

5.title: Poorly woven mess that denies revelation
5.content:
Oppenheimer consists of a very many scenes crisscrossing time and space, that knits together a disarray of thoughts presenting the title character as having an essentially successful career based on unlikable ambition, using what he knows to bring better scientists under his control, engaging in regular adultery with their wives while commanding the fruits of their success. He has to attend a bad meeting for a day or three, but basically walks away from it unharmed. He engages in some public waffling about the benefits of continued nuclear research, to virtually no effect and long after it matters. There's a bad guy because there has to be a bad guy, and Robert Downey plays him very well, but his subplot has no real place in the main one, so his comeuppance doesn't do much to exculpate 220,000 dead Japanese and a lifetime of Cold War nightmares for the viewer. There are some terribly trite scenes involving Einstein, or fusing quantum mechanics with romance, that are blech.

I don't understand why this movie got such broad aplomb. Nolan is, for cinema, the true destroyer of worlds.

5.title: The R Rating Downgraded Oppenheimer
5.content:
Overall, I liked Oppenheimer. But the length and 'Adult Themed' rating brought if from a near 10 to a 6. You're captivated by a complicated genius. He ended WW II earlier with the nuke, yet he knew the international stage could end the World. He was top-notch physistist, but he cheated on his wife.

Watching two former movies heroes play aging bureaucrats was worth the watch. Robert Downey Jr is this wrinkled balding guy now. Matt Damon is now a retiring general who looks like a stuffed sausage. I still think of them in Saving Private Ryan and Ironman. So seeing two swashbucklers get old was cool.

Long. This 3 hour movie could have been cut down to 2 hours or a bit more and it would have made the same point.

Mostly, why is this rated "R"??? Oppenheimer definitely could have left out the nude scenes and some cursing. So now a high school physics class can't go.

5.title: A Star-Studded Spectacle Overshadows Substance in Nolan's Latest Cinematic Odyssey
5.content:
"Oppenheimer," a film more dazzling in spectacle than rich in substance, unfolds like a cinematic odyssey, akin to a three-hour montage or an elaborate music video.

The film's narrative core feels absent, overshadowed by its reliance on an impressive but overwhelming ensemble of star actors. Rather than delving into character development or a cohesive story, it revels in an auditory and visual feast, where the music and celebrities take center stage. The anticipated climax, the unveiling of the atomic bomb, is eclipsed by the film's ambitious attempt to squeeze an array of famous faces into its runtime.

The result is bewildering. One can't help but wonder about the creative process behind this project. Was Christopher Nolan coerced into a direction that strays from his known mastery? The film, though visually striking, seems to bear the marks of a struggle, a tug-of-war between Nolan's vision and Hollywood's commercial cravings. It emerges as an eclectic mix, a blend of Marvel-esque spectacle over story, thriller elements, and arthouse sensibilities, all wrapped in a star-studded package that somehow loses the essence of what might have been a more focused and impactful narrative.

5.title: Epic dud
5.content:
This is a three hour movie that feels constantly in a hurry. Someone could have made a good movie about just the Manhattan Project, or just the political intrigue, or even Oppenheimer's early years. Instead, Nolan tried to tick every box and ended up ticking most of them badly. The science, the politics, and the people are all dumbed down to Hollywood boilerplate. Somehow it's both boring and melodramatic, and every point it's trying to make is an obvious sentiment made in an obvious way.

The music is too loud, the pacing is like a washboard road, and it's completely humorless. Some of the acting is very good, and clearly a lot of technical skill went into getting at least a fizzle yield from this clunky script. But the only edge-of-your-seat moments are the detonation of the bomb, and Gary Oldman's performance as Truman.

5.title: Oppenheimer: A Monumental Misfire in Nolan's Oeuvre
5.content:
"Oppenheimer," Christopher Nolan's ambitious adaptation of "American Prometheus," disappointingly falls short of expectations set by his previous cinematic marvels. The film is certainly monumental, but its expansive 3-hour length proves testing for the audience's patience. We anticipate a compelling narrative around scientific discovery, atomic theory, and the birth of the atomic bomb. Instead, Nolan swerves into a labyrinth of political intrigue, painting a shadowy picture of Oppenheimer as a communist.

The film often feels more like a detached documentary than a stirring cinematic experience. There's no central plot to anchor us, and an unsettling absence of critical historical moments, such as the horrific bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Instead, we wade through a tiresome mire of legal drama, which, while probably accurate, lends little to the cinematic spectacle we seek.

Furthermore, the depiction of Oppenheimer is contentious at best. Nolan seems to lionize a figure whose scientific breakthroughs ultimately led to devastating loss of life. This tension between Oppenheimer's humanity and the grim aftermath of his work is a complex issue that the film fails to convincingly navigate.

The film left a void where I expected the brilliance of Nolan's past works like "The Dark Knight Trilogy" or "Inception". After "Tenet" and "Dunkirk," this film lands as another unexciting addition to Nolan's recent oeuvre.

In conclusion, Nolan's "Oppenheimer" is a colossal yet uneven historical drama. It stumbles in its storytelling and character portrayal, failing to fully grasp the enormity and gravity of its subject. Though well-intentioned, it ultimately fails to captivate or provoke thought in the way a film of this caliber should.

5.title: It is not that good
5.content:
I expected better movie of christopher nolan after masterpieces like Batman or interstellar!

It was so boring i really don't know how it ranked 8.4 !! It doesn't worth more than 5 . It was somehow documentary so it couldn't be more interesting than this . I really prefer Christopher nolan work on science fiction movies . His movies in that genre are very interesting but this was according to the biography of A murderer scientist (dr. Oppenheimer)

I really don't know how japanese feel after watching that movie. About the biography of the person who made such a disaster in Japan .

At least i know a murdere scientist better after watching that.

5.title: Long winded and over rated
5.content: I am a big fan of Christopher Nolan's work, but this just didn't do it for me at all. Dialogue heavy and plain boring in parts, it was a very long winded and laboured journey. Frankly, I'm also starting to get fed up with the lack of female representation in his films.... I saw Barbie and that was much more enjoyable! I'm not saying the film isn't well shot, well acted, or has gravitas, but it was way, way overdone and so very long. When I went to the loo, I thought about having a coffee and going back to my partner when the film was further along. I hope his next film is better - I usually love his style, but not this!

5.title: Don't fall for the 'Nolan hype', this isn't nearly his best.
5.content:
Spoiler-free breakdown (not that you CAN actually spoil it since you probably read about Manhattan Project by now).

So I went to the theater not expecting a new Batman or Interstellar since this is drama/biography first and foremost. Here's what's good and what's not.

GOOD:
great introduction of many important scientists since pre WW2 era
the actual development of the bomb
great casting


NOT so GOOD:


CONCLUSION: Had first and especially last hour of the movie had shorter runtime/focus and more focus was put on the actual development of the bomb and it's consequences it would have been a way better movie. This way last hour felt like a boring political gathering where Nolan tried to (unsuccessfully) enforce some kind of tension with some great music score and people were generically talking in a room. Seriously, it was like watching a parliament discussion on TV but with epic music. He grabs you, the viewer, by the hand "see, THIS is what I think is important" and it just isn't. Instead, I'm yet to see him do some drama where things just happen and we create our own feel on it without being fed.

Long runtime in BR2049 ex. Was justified, but here, what was to be done in 15min was stretched into an hour.

It's a good movie, but not nearly a masterpiece with all the hype around it suggesting so.

5.title: Nolan's Timing Fiasco: Biopic or Blooper Reel?
5.content:
Within the initial two hours of the film, we find ourselves navigating through a labyrinth of superfluous character introductions that seem to yield scant significance to the overarching narrative. A judicious recalibration of the storytelling, discerningly excising extraneous segments, could have undoubtedly remedied the pacing predicament, allowing for a more enthralling cinematic experience. Nolan's virtuosity in crafting intricate timing events is a testament to his filmmaking prowess, yet it's evident that his acumen encounters limitations when attempting to encapsulate the essence of a compelling biopic.

Instead of delving unreservedly into the profound moral repercussions stemming from the creation of the atomic bomb, the movie tends to become a socio-political commentary, emblematic of the McCarthy era, inadvertently diluting the gravity of the historical subject matter. One aspect that leaves audiences yearning for a deeper resonance is the film's prevailing fixation on Oppenheimer's reputation and alleged political affiliations.

Regrettably, the film unwaveringly adheres to Oppenheimer's and the US military's vantage point, effectively occluding the multifaceted Japanese perspective. This lamentable omission imparts an inescapable sense of incompleteness to the cinematic opus, denying it the full breadth of narrative depth and complexity it could have otherwise attained. While Nolan's cinematic endeavor ostensibly assumes the role of a scrutinizing lens, delving into the post-WWII American witch hunt for communists, it veers into a convolution that subtly sidetracks from the weightier inquiry: the transformation of the US-government into an unwittingly monstrous entity while grappling with the malevolent Nazi threat.

It remains perplexing that, even with the presence of dignitaries like Obama, Trump, and Biden at Hiroshima, a formal apology for the cataclysmic atomic bombings remains conspicuously absent, perpetuating the enduring reverberations of history's annals.

5.title: Strauss
5.content:
How one can make a 3 hour movie about the man running the Manhattan Project, about the brilliant complex physics, technology and the earth-shattering moral dilemmas entailed in putting it to use; and end up mostly making a political soap-opera is at least surprising and at best a missed opportunity.

How about not making yet another movie about McCartyism and the plight of the persecuted left? Of what comparative relevance is there in centering the movie around the petty politics of a political nobody like Strauss?

Where were the Germans and the Russians? What about the Japanese? And how about trying not to dumb down the physics, but meet the challenge and enlighten the viewer? This could have been a riveting complex story about one of the most deciding periods in modern history and an opportunity to make use of Nolan's uncanny ability to visualise conceptual ideas; as he did to great effect in movies like Inception, Interstellar and Tenet. There is ample opportunity for cinematic brilliance in all the physics discussed in this move, but all we get is scribbled numbers on blackboards and slo-mo explosions. Would this be very much different if made by Michael Bay?

5.title: High quality snooze fest + Botox
5.content: This movie is very well done and the actors are top notch. Excellent soundtrack! However, it is rather boring. Like an unnecessarily long, overly complicated, theatrical documentary. Beforehand I was concerned that I might have to go for a toilet break during the THREE HOURS. Turns out I didn't, but I could have gone anytime between minute 30-90 and basically in the whole last hour. Also, Emily Blunt's obvious Botox/fillers really disturbed the experience for me - it made me very aware of the fact that I was watching an actress and not the character. I get the whole "double punishment" debate but don't think it has a place in the movie industry without context. It only messes with the absurd beauty standards even more to normalise it.

5.title: Long and a Bit Boring
5.content:
I've just finished watching this, I've been looking forward to seeing it as the cast list is great and I'm a fan of Cillian Murphy.

I can see why this film won so many awards but its not a film I would personally watch more than once. Firstly the film is way too long, the jumping back and forth in time is a little confusing and gets a bit tedious after a while.

I agree with others that the music is overly intrusive and gets in the way of some of the dialogue at times.

I stuck with the film as I wanted to see what happened but I won't be revisiting it again.

I've seen other films dozens of times and still enjoy them, this isn't one of those, it's a bit of a slow slog.

5.title: OPP-IE, you don't know me
5.content:
A self-important movie, you'd be a social outcast if you diss it. But it deserves dissing. What is with filmmakers these days that they forget we need people to root for in a movie, even one based on the winners' version of history. Technical filmmaking is okay but people need people to connect to a piece of film.

Cillian Murphy is an excellent actor but is wasted in this dreary, droning 3-hour indulgence. Save for maybe the fat Jewish friend who's always feeding Oppie, the rest of the cast may look like historical folks but there's ZERO character development here. Emily Blunt has one note - a scowl on her face for most parts. RDJ was probably roped in to lend his name in return for a sure Oscar nomination.

This is not Nolan territory.

I'd like to think he had his arm-twisted by the Jewish lobby to make this...have to bag the generational director for the cause. Good for him coz the same lobby will do everything to declare this movie a success and an important film in his canon.

It isn't.

When Titanic was released, it was accompanied by documentaries of the sunken ship as well. Docus for pondering, the movie for pleasure.

Oppenheimer docus would probably serve us well. The movie not so much. So choose to spend your 3 hours wisely.

5.title: Murphy is great but Nolan is not
5.content:
There is a famous Einstein quote: "If you can't explain it simply, you don't understand it well enough." In my opinion Nolan failed to explain it simply. Oh don't get me wrong I loved Inception, Interstellar and Dunkirk even though TBH I didn't understand Interstellar fully.

I had great expectations from Oppenheimer, I wanted to watch it first day as it is about Manhattan project and Nolan made it. But I am disappointed as the move is all over the place. It fails to catch audiences' attention throughout the film, even I wanted to focus and try to understand but the movie was all over place. There is no doubt Cillian , RDJ, Emily and others were great in the movie, they are all great actors, but according to me the movie the fell short of what we expect of Nolan. From Nolan we expect our intellect joy and mind blown but nothing happened as such instead I got bored in few scenes.

5.title: Good Enough
5.content:
Oppenheimer is a historical drama delivered by one of the best directors of his times, Christopher Nolan.

The movie is a spot on drama, with a difficult story to handle, especially in an age when a nuclear threat isn't that far fetched. Hence, the movie's topic often gets uncomfortable to watch, especially when you watch everyone in an ectatic mood over their success, when you know the outcome of that success. And yet, the movie often opts to turn into a courtroom drama, with the timelines overlaping and everything coming together in the end.

Hence, the movie often gets confusing as to what timeline you are on and its not easy to follow. It is also way too long, neary three hours running time, which isn't easy to commit to, especially during summer, which is the movie's release date.

On the other hand, Cillian Murphy finally gets the lead in a Nolan movie and proves once again how talented he is. But, Robert Downey Jr is simply excellent in this one, nearly unrecognizable! The rest of the stellar cast did a good job as well.

5.title: Bump in the road for Nolan
5.content:
Over produced, but I'm sure people will love it anyway because they think they should. I love Nolan's work, so just disappointed.

This could have been shot on 35mm and still been the same film from certain vantage points. I went into this with expectations quite high granted, but from shot composition to narrative structure there was nothing new here, a loud score with moments of sheer jump factor doesn't keep me entertained, when the film itself just felt completely lacklustre. I didn't feel any emotion translated across and considering the gravitas of the atomic bomb, it felt small, even in imax. Nolan is better than this.

5.title: Great cast. Good acting. Editing and soundtrack was horrendous.
5.content:
Overall I think this was a good film.

The cast and their performance was by far the best part of this movie. Cillian Murphy and Robert Downey Jr. Had by far the best performances out of this entire roster of new and budding stars. I was a little disappointed with Matt Damon's performance as it was tough for me to believe he was a general, he just didn't convince me. My last gripe with the cast was that Rami Malek had three scenes and the first two he spoke a singular word. The last scene he was in he stole screen as was the intent but I digress.

The most annoying thing to me was the pacing being inconsistent and jumping too much from timeline to timeline with each cut. If the amount of cuts were halved I feel this movie would be soooo much better. Just imagine having twice as much time with these characters and maybe getting to see some actual depth with them before jumping back and forth in the TL.

Lastly, the music was horrendous. Simply put, there was no reason for the music to get so intense and loud during the interrogation at the end. I feel as if the raw emotion from those two actors would've been plenty for tension.

5.title: 'Oppenheimer' failed to create a spark
5.content:
While we may all be acquainted with the storyline of J. Robert Oppenheimer, the film attempts an audacious feat by splicing and reordering multiple periods of his life, attempting to craft a fragmented mosaic that, alas, falls short of coherence. The ill-conceived endeavour leaves audiences grappling to piece together the historical segments in a meaningful way, leading to a frustrating lack of understanding of their significance to the overarching narrative.

Throughout the cinematic journey, the incessant splicing proves to be the Achilles' heel, preventing the film from delving deeper into the various storylines that shaped Oppenheimer's destiny. A lamentable example lies in the scant attention given to the conception of the H-bomb, which is relegated to a mere fleeting mention during a debate at Los Alamos. One can't help but yearn for a more profound exploration of this pivotal moment, a crucial juncture in the annals of scientific history that cries out for greater elucidation.

Perhaps most vexing is the film's reluctance to shed light on one of the most critical questions surrounding Oppenheimer - his alleged association with communism. The shadow of uncertainty looms large, leaving audiences grasping for answers that never come. The denial of a deeper understanding of Oppenheimer's political leanings robs the narrative of the nuance it so desperately requires, and by extension, diminishes the potency of the central conflict surrounding the withdrawal of his AEC security clearance.

Ironically, a troubling revelation arises for those who sought to glean insights into Oppenheimer's life from this film. It becomes painfully apparent that one might have been better served perusing his Wikipedia entry or watching the documentary 'The Day after Trinity.' In those mediums, Oppenheimer's life unfolds chronologically, granting a sense of coherence and a true appreciation of the man and his profound impact on history.

In the end, 'Oppenheimer' fails to achieve the lofty aspirations it set for itself. It meanders through its own ambitious convolution, leaving audiences perplexed and disheartened by a missed opportunity to illuminate one of history's most intriguing minds. With a more focused and chronological approach, the film might have risen to greatness, but alas, it remains a lamentable casualty of its own artistic experimentation.

5.title: Messy
5.content:
My wife and I had to watch this film in three sittings as it's rather tiring. It jumps all over the place and generally lacks cohesion. The dialogue is generally very mumbled, and seems to lack passion bar Matt Damon's character. However, the cast and acting in general were pleasing. Far more emphasis needed placing on the fact that Russia were perfectly prepared to finish off Japan in the traditional war manner, but it was the USA wanting to flex their muscle by unnecessarily deploying their new weapon.

I feel I am being quite generous giving it a 6 considering the incredibly interesting subject matter and world changing events they had to work with.

Shan't be putting myself through watching this again.

5.title: Ugh
5.content: I was already very familiar with the story of Oppenheimer and the project, but I was anxious to see it get the big screen treatment it deserves. However, I was sorely disappointed. Yes, it's long but Ghandi was long too and much better. The music is too loud and incessant, the constant flashbacks are confusing and annoying, and the story plods along. The director obviously wanted to create a "work of art" with this film. He may have done that, but he ruined a great opportunity to tell the story right. On second thought, this would have been better done as a mini-series. I want those three hours of my life back.

5.title: Imitation Game Gone Wrong
5.content:
"Oppenheimer" endeavors to shed light on the fascinating life of J. Robert Oppenheimer and his involvement in the creation of the atomic bomb. While the film does have its informative moments, it falls short in various aspects, leaving audiences with mixed feelings and a sense of missed potential.

One of the film's strengths lies in its exceptional cast and great acting performances. Cillian Murphy, who portrays J. Robert Oppenheimer, delivers a commendable performance, capturing the complexities and inner conflicts of the renowned physicist. The supporting cast also shines in their respective roles, bringing life to the historical figures they portray.

Furthermore, the film's documentary-like approach provides historical context and insights into Oppenheimer's life and achievements. The incorporation of real archival footage and interviews with experts adds credibility to the narrative, making it an informative experience for those interested in the historical events and the people involved.

However, "Oppenheimer" struggles to find a balanced narrative between its documentary style and a conventional biopic format. The constant shifts between these two approaches create a disjointed viewing experience, making it difficult for the audience to fully engage with the story and its characters.

The dialogue is another critical aspect that hindered the film's potential.
