The high-paced, technical jargon-heavy conversations about scientific concepts might have worked for an academic audience, but for the general moviegoer, it often felt overwhelming and alienating. This made it challenging to relate to the characters, as their personal interactions and relationships were overshadowed by these technical aspects.

As a result, the character development in "Oppenheimer" suffered. Moments that were meant to be personal and emotionally impactful felt rushed and underdeveloped. The film's tendency to focus on the highlights of Oppenheimer's life rather than providing a more nuanced portrayal prevented the audience from connecting with him and other characters on a deeper level.

Furthermore, the film's soundtrack became more of a hindrance than an asset. The attempt to create tension through overwhelming and deafening noise was not worth sacrificing the viewers' comfort. Instead of enhancing the viewing experience, the excessive use of the soundtrack became a distraction that took away from the film's potential emotional impact.

Regarding the plot and historical context, "Oppenheimer" suffers from a lack of clear focus. The inclusion of both the bomb story and the persecution initiated by Strauss creates an unnecessarily lengthy and convoluted narrative. The prolonged subplot takes up a significant portion of the film, further detracting from the emotional resonance and leaving the audience wondering about the film's core message.

Additionally, the movie's handling of the aftermath of the nuclear bombs dropped on Japan is problematic. The lack of empathy and portrayal of the devastating consequences of these weapons of mass destruction is deeply disappointing. One brief, imaginary image of a burnt corpse falls short of capturing the immense human tragedy, and the film misses an opportunity to explore the ethical implications of these events.

In many ways, "Oppenheimer" feels like a missed opportunity, resembling a flawed version of "The Imitation Game." While both films deal with complex historical figures and their contributions, "Oppenheimer" struggles to strike the right balance, resulting in a fragmented and unsatisfying narrative.

In conclusion, "Oppenheimer" offers valuable historical information and, at times, feels like an educational documentary. The great cast and commendable acting performances are notable highlights. However, its failure to maintain a consistent narrative style, coupled with the overwhelming technical dialogue, underdeveloped character arcs, and problematic handling of historical events, hinder its potential to be a truly engaging and emotionally resonant biopic. For those seeking a comprehensive and immersive depiction of J. Robert Oppenheimer's life, "Oppenheimer" might leave them wanting more.

5.title: Unpopular opinion: good but boring
5.content:
I was pretty eager to see this film, despite its 3 hour length, and just went today to see it. For about half of it, I have to say, I was so bored. The acting was amazing don't get me wrong, and the bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki have always been interesting subjects to me, but this was just boring..

It moved kinda slow at first for me and I found myself daydreaming to stop myself from falling asleep. I know that it's long, and I get why it's long: I'd rather sit through 3 hours of one film than 1 hour 30 mins of one and have to wait 3 years for a sequel. I get it. But I am a person who doesn't really like science, it's my least favourite school subject and I'm not very good at it, especially physics. So I was so uninterested in all of the science-y talk and equations or whatever Oppenheimer was doing. It made the film feel a lot longer. Again, I get that we have to understand how he made the bombs or whatever but I felt like I was watching a step-by-step tutorial on how to make one instead.

I didn't feel any emotion really throughout the film (except from the sexual scenes because I was with my parents so I was embarrassed) and I was even about to check the time at some points, which is something I don't really do during films.

I do have some positive notes though: the acting was really good, as expected from people like Cillian Murphy and Rami Malek. The music was also good too, even if it was just quietly playing in the background. I also like how we see how making the bomb later affected Oppenheimer; like him saying that he felt like he had blood on his hands, and him seeing bright lights (representing the atomic bomb) twice. I thought that was cool too.

So while I do think it was kinda boring and didn't fully live up to my expectations, I can also tell that a lot of effort was put into it. There were a lot of good actors here too like Robert Downey Jr, Cillian Murphy and Rami Malek (who I was really happy to see lol). If you're into movies about true events (so historic movies) then I'd say definitely go and see it. If you can't handle the 3 hours though, or you think you'd get bored, maybe don't bother with this then. However, would I watch this again? Probably not. But it's not a bad movie at all.

5.title: Jarring! Distracting! Disorienting! Loud
5.content:
This movie was like cooking a 5 course meal masterpiece and adding too much salt thus ruining the experience.

I really want to agree with everyone else on the brilliance . There's so much to love and so much detail, hard work, brilliant acting, set design, costume design, and love that went into this movie, but I can't even finish it. So disappointing.

Music is too loud. The exhausting camera shots, jumping from angle to angle, camera movements, scene to scene jumping constantly, flashes of nuclear reactions depictions all over the place, and all of the jumping from past to present. I can't do it. It's disorienting.

I completely agree with other reviewers regarding criticisms of the overall experience.

5.title: I had high hopes...
5.content: It turned into 2.95 hours of nothing much at all, and 5 mins of boom. No Enola Gay or Boxcar, no evidence of any harm it did, only related in conversation. The whole film past by, pretty much in a blur, I can honestly say, I was totally underwhelmed. I will not be watching it again at any future date. It will go down in my memory as completely forgettable. Some have called it complicated, how? When we left the cinema, my husband said, wow! At what I asked him? Really and truly I had looked forward to this film for a while, and while there is no doubt, there was some really good acting, I mean Robert Downey Jr not playing himself, who knew? All in all, I think I may have enjoyed Barbie more and I worked in science.

5.title: A Redundant Biography without Focus
5.content:
It's a redundant biography without focus, rather than a movie. It includes so many details that I don't know what's the point. Or perhaps Biography movie is not my type. And it is way too long!

I care story and insights most, but this film is overly worn make up. The music is overused, creating continuous tension by music results in opposite effects: the movie is not well structured, it is loose. The funny thing is, despite with abundant details I couldn't understand many parts. The dramatic visual effects prevents audiences from understanding the conversation and physical theory. If the purpose is to impress people with fantastic genius and fancy theories, it's a success though. But on the other hand, people don't need to watch a movie to learn that physics is obscure.

I'm not impressed by Oppenheimer in this movie. I don't see clear characters of him. It even doesn't present transformations of his life stages and minds, for example how he agreed to manage the project, any struggling? Or this is just the fact that he accepted without hesitation? After I read a paper about Oppenheimer, did I realize that this is such a complex and legendary figure. Nolan is fascinated by Oppenheimer's dramatic life and personality. No wonder Nolan wants to show everything, with 3 hours long. But in this sene, it's a complete failure, it doesn't make sense to show a series of snapshots.

In general, the movie is not handled well. Absolutely the material has a great potential. Either tell an exciting story of quantum physics, which is so fascinating, or create a charming, complex figure. It failed to fulfill either.

5.title: Visually good, but...
5.content:
I don't see how this movie could have possibly gotten such a high average score.

I am neither a big fan of Nolan, although I've watched and appreciated the Inception, nor a movie geek in general, but the topic and hype around Oppenheimer have lured me into a cinema.

I've seen a beautiful picture, great work of actors, but that's pretty much it. The storyline was constituted of patches of dialogues that were sometimes very difficult to combine into a continuous plot, distinguishing what goes where.

The character of Oppenheimer is many times named as a "genius", but there are literally no proofs of that in the movie. How do I actually get to know that he is a genius? Through the dialogues like "oh, I've seen you work about quantum mechanics, it's impressive"? It's not very believable, even if in IRL it was indeed like that. I need to SEE it, that's what it's a film, a movie.

Also, if the movie was so much focused on the speech and talking - I did not get at all who Robert Downey's Jr. Character was, and what relation did he have to Oppenheimer or the plot. Since I'm not a native English speaker I couldn't get almost a word of what he was saying because of his spelling and complicated bureaucratic terms combined (even with the subtitles), thus, it made me hate the character and had discouraged me from following up until the end of movie, since the 2nd half was dedicated solely to the process, which was full of Downey Jr.

I left the cinema some 30 minutes before the end. And I have never done this before. I was seriously trying to keep myself engaged and interested, although I would just not manage to do so due to the confusing cuts in between the timelines, gibberish talking od Downey Jr. And general pace of the last third of the movie post-explosion.

I believe it could have been executed better, especially the second part, that has lost me completely. Also, I was not connected to the character of Oppenheimer enough to actually care about all the persecution and the results of it.

Will not watch the movie again, and don't regret leaving the cinema.

As for me - the topic is interesting, the picture and the play are on a high level. The plot, the editing and the relationship links between the characters are weak, the storytelling is not believable and weak.

Overall it's overrated, deserves a 5/10. Sorry for you, Nolan fans. Don't make it a cult, please.

5.title: A director who insists upon himself
5.content:
This is a great production. Note that I say production, not film or a piece of art, because essentially it's just a production. A very polished product created by a well-oiled machine - Hollywood. But it feels hollow somehow, despite the serious subject matter, great acting, and well-crafted elements. Why? There could be several reasons, but ultimately the reason is just that Nolan is a producer, not an artist.

First, the production, it's full of clichés, from the swelling but predictable music, the jam-in-as-much-as-we-can pacing (especially the first third of the movie), the stylized colored/black-and-white scenes (to denote different eras, of course), over-the-top close-ups, etc. And then there are illogical scenes, which discount all the scientific research homework that it's done. For example, Oppenheimer walks into a conference then starts to fire questions right away; then the scene where Einstein looks at a complicated set of calculations, then understands/agrees with it immediately. Even Einstein needs time, buddy...

As for Nolan himself, he seems like an ultra serious kid that we all have met back in high school. That kid is obsessed about an art form, reads up on it, practices it, dresses as that kind of artist to a T. He will look down upon anyone who tries to veer away from the conventions. What he believes to be the classics. Later on, due to his diligence and the seriousness that he gives off, he will start winning prizes and gaining power. He wants to be taken seriously, just because he claims to be a serious guy. But at the end of the day, he is still not a true artist, just someone who insists upon himself.

5.title: Doesn't work for me!
5.content:
I respect Nolan's craft but I am not a fan.

I was left a bit bemused with the decisions that Nolan has taken as a director for this film. The entire first half the audience is made to invest emotionally in the making of the A-bomb. Because of the nature of the storytelling showing the film from the point of view of Oppenheimer, it is a natural way of making the audience root for the main character. Understood. Accepted.

The second half goes in establishing that Oppenheimer was a true patriot. He is even decorated for his contribution.

But what about the aftermath?

Yes there are mentions here and there. But there is no visible remorse. Nor in his actions it is clear. It is as if there is no accountability in the man. That is what baffled me the most. Was it the plan to hang it in the middle and allow the audience to choose how they see it fit? If yes then why tell the story from Oppenheimer's pov? Why make the audience connect with the man? The emotional investment in the main character only to be left wondering in the end as to why Nolan chose to leave it this way?

This may have worked for every other person but sadly it has not worked for me.

There is nothing great that we have not already seen in a Nolan film. The acting overall is good. Clearly the studio backed Nolan very well, so well that the film has prominent actors even in short cameos.

It's 5/10 for me as the movie, for me, fails at a human level. The film has no soul.

5.title: Wish I could get these 3 hours of my life back
5.content: I'm a movie buff. I love quality storytelling and Character development. This movie had none of these qualities. It was laden with music & sounds that were way too loud and completely distracting. Even to the point where, when you wanted to care about a character, you couldn't because the constant noise distracts. The acting and cinematography was good but if you don't know the story of Oppenheimer you will not understand. I recommend watching a biography of his life first so you can get a sense of what happened. This movie only touches on what actually happened. It's more of a courtroom drama..

5.title: Most excruciating three hours on cinema
5.content:
Excruciatingly long, slow and *gasp* dare I say it, boring. It's boring. The only good thing was the stacked cast of actors, it get to a point while I almost doze off, Casey affleck's voice woke me up and then yeah there he is, a surprise appearance by casey affleck yayyy. That's how bored I am.

This is a passion project of Nolan, only it felt like he made it for himself and that's fine actually. Too bad I dont enjoy this movie, though another thing I do enjoy however was the score. It is mighty cinematic & beautiful, it also enhances some of the boring dialogue which otherwise would be rather bland. I've been a fan of Ludwig Goransson since Tenet & Wakanda forever.

I think Nolan's name alone could made this a box office hits, however in this day where our attentions were divided upon so many things, it could prove to be detrimental for our enjoyment of the movie, maybe I couldn't enjoy this movie because my brain was used to shorter & compact contents (Tiktok is a pandora box for me) BUT in my defense, comparing this movie to Nolan's previous works, I cannot say this was superior in any means. Inception, Interstellar, Batmans, Tenet were all feast for my eyes & brain. But I pushed through to the end and I pat myself in the shoulder as I walked out of cinema.

Cinematography is sub par, strory's not really engaging, the back and forth in timeline feels messy, performances was nothing special, all the actors did their job okay, and also the much hyped no cgi for the bomb sequences felt underwhelming. I agree that they dont need CGI because this is not an action movie, it's a historical biography movie whom also focuses a lot on political tension during wartime. And it wont matter much anyway, the bomb scene was just a short scene. So I guess the much hyped marketing tactic which spread around saying all of the effects was practical was actually inconsequential.

Feel free to skip this one as I felt the regular nolan fans will be dissapointed. Its a historical biography drama but less emphasis on the drama.

5.title: Interesting historical story. Over elaborate cinematography
5.content:
I find myself in a bizarre situation having watched the movie.

I was very interested and engaged in the history of the story. I thought the acting was brilliant.

However, I felt that they tried to be too clever with it. They constantly chopped and changed through the timeline which left me having to Wikipedia it to check what happened and when.

Sometimes doing this adds to the watch but not with this movie.

This doesn't mean that I think people shouldn't watch it. RDJ is very good in it in particular but others were too.

Directors and writers just need to calm down sometimes. Not every movie has to be a total work of art. Sometimes when the story is good you can just let it flow.

5.title: Very boring
5.content: In this movie you will learn nothing about history or science. Nothing about emotions. Nothing about geo politics. It looks quite nice. Maybe it could have been ok if edited to 2 hours. 3 hours implies an epic. But this movie was just not epic in scale. To be an epic, it would have had to go outside Oppenheimer's bubble. About 1 hours was dedicated to his trial of "security clearance", who honestly cares about that. The Albert Einstein character was kind of like a Santa Claus type figure, not an actual person. It was just boring. I feel like an idiot spending money to see this, encouraging this false intellectual movie. Let's face it, all biography movies are not actually good movies, except Walk Hard (a parody), and I'm Not Here ( didn't use the typical biography format).

5.title: A movie twisted by the duality of it's being. Parts are great. Parts are unnecessary.
5.content:
Nolan needs to be reeled in by the people around him.

While parts of this film were interesting, beautifully shot and thought provoking, others were honestly very boring and felt like filler out of an anime. The whole movie is 3 hours and could be cut to 1.5 hours and could the use an extra half hour about how the atomic bomb works, what the build up to it was (showing the people that warned about Germany's development and the attricities Germany was commiting), and fleshing out Oppenheimers relationships more and himself as a person.

The whole part about the trial and some scenes in middle part movie contained some scenes that made me sleepy and had people in the theater (quite rude I have to say but still) yawning loudly and sitting leaning forward to keep themselves awake, sometimes rubbing themselves in the eyes. It's a shame, because this movie certainly has some amazing parts, such as the development of the atomic bomb in New Mexico and the colleges at Berkely leading up to it. Also the communist gatherings in the early parts of the movie were relavant for the small part of the trial that I would keep in and also gave an interesting view into the zeitgeist of facism and communism in the years leading up to WW2.

The movie is very hard to rate due to variance in it's quality. However, I simply cannot recommend to watch it in cinema's becuase you would not have the option the fast forward through the sleep inducing parts. Therefore, I have to give the movie a 5/10. Were the movie to be severely cutted so that te good parts remain it would be a 7.2/10.

5.title: Meh
5.content: A very technically proficient telling of an ultimately bland story. I got about half of an hour into it and it would be unfair to say that nothing happened, rather a bunch of pieces of stuff was happening but it was all out of context. The narration kept hopping back and forth between a statement that Oppenheimer was giving to some committee and what I'm assuming was a Senate confirmation hearing regarding one of the POTUS cabinet member choices. I had began to read a fictionalized account of the making of the atomic bomb and got fired up to read something else and when I came back to it, forgot where I'd left off, but one thing that struck me about that book was the observation that splitting atoms was almost purely a theoretical concept and the US govt was essentially racing against time to turn the theoretical into a reality. This movie gives a little more detail on that aspect of things, but it just seems like it spent at least a tad too much time detailing his political dabblings, which I don't begrudge him for, but I just really don't care and the only people that I can see caring are people that want some validation for their own like-minded political leanings. Ultimately, as much debt as history owes to Dr. Oppenheimer, I don't think a biopic of his life is worth 3 hours of my time. It's a very stylish and competently directed film. I probably should have known a film titled Oppenheimer wasn't going to be anything more than a film about the man himself.

5.title: Lazy effort all around
5.content: Arguably one of Christopher Nolan's worst films. It amazes me that the person who wrote Interstellar and Inception could be so lazy in writing a biopic. The dialogue is atrocious. Character introductions were cliche. The subjective black and white story line was unnecessary. It's tough to make a three hour movie feel rushed and empty but Christopher Nolan managed to pull it off in Oppenheimer. Sadly, it seems as though this Barbie/Oppenheimer scheme Hollywood pulled to get us all back in the theater to see these movies (at least from my perspective) failed. Oppenheimer's only shred of decency is it's use of sound and some scenes cinematography. Outside of that this movie is not worth seeing in theaters.

5.title: Slow down Nolan!
5.content:
This movie cramped too much story, even it's 3 hour run time is still not enough. It rushed every single scene with dialogues, dialoges, boom, moved on to the next scene, dialogues, next scene, boom, next scene, without letting the audience absorb or process the scene.

It's like doing a marathon while holding an explosive diarrhea. This movie can't wait to see the finish line.

Nolan should just focus the story about Oppenheimer and the bomb, leave the story about his communist past, his messy love life, his trial and that strauss rdj story. This is a movie not a documentary. Focus!

Imagine if better filmmaker made this, like Paul Thomas Anderson, Scorsese, Coen bros or Dennis Villeneuve. They would focus the story and let the scenes breathe. Nolan is technically brilliant but he's just an artsy Michael bay. A noobie film snob favourite. People love to sniff his farts because it made them think they are snobby film connoisseurs.

5.title: Subatomic
5.content:
This film is, at least, 30 minutes too long and suffers from a Writer/Director who is in love with his project so he can't bear to get out the pinking shears. But, unfortunately, a shorter film could not save this one. Structurally it is a mess, with its flashback, within flashbacks, within flashbacks, like a Russian Matryoshka doll!

The most interesting aspect was the films' throwback to those films of the 1960's that had huge casts of top British, German and American actors. In that regard, let's take a look at the cast: Cillian Murphy is outstanding and perfectly suited to the role. I kept thinking that, if this were a different era, this role would be played Montgomery Clift, of whom Murphy reminded me. Matt Damon: ever since Damon became a 'star,' I have found him to be highly overrated. His early work was much better. It was good to see Robert Downey, Jr. Out of those silly Super Hero movies and doing interesting work again. It was good to see Josh Hartnett back in a big movie. Kenneth Branagh is always good and always interesting. Casey Affleck is a good actor who is always better when he is playing sarcastic, or slightly sinister. Also, good to see James Remar ('Dexter'), Tom Conti, Greg Jbara (away from 'Blue Bloods'), Trond Fausa (who was so good in 'Lilyhammer') and Gary Oldman, who nailed Winston Churchill, and now nails Harry Truman.

Someday, someone, may have the courage to make a film that doesn't toe the tired, thread-bare, diktat that the post-war Communist threat was just the fantasy of some right-wing kooks. The post-war Communist threat was very real indeed. Ask Great Britain, France, Italy and Germany. It remains sheer folly to think the USA was not also endangered.

5.title: Why is Oppenheimer overated, arrogantly long, mediocre and unnecessary?
5.content:
Nolan's depiction of the life of Dr. Oppenheimer is very unoriginal. The rise and fall of successful person, has been told a million times over. The background or field of the subject seems inherently irrelevant. From Scarface over I,Tonya to Nixon, the story is as old as our society.

Backroom politics are necessary because everybody has an agenda and you are going attract haters.


Being praised, spit out and praised again (by the same people).




Surely, loads of people achieved extraordinary results and they deserve a tribute. That's where the storyteller comes in. Or should come in. Minute 10 to 100 are easily skippable. The pace stays the same, the dialogue is blunt, we don't learn anything, it's not entertaining, ... A part of any production process often is knowing what to leave out. I am sure Oppenheimer lead a fascinating life but Nolan's infatuation clearly clouded his judgement. Three hours is simply too much for what he has to tell and what he does tell is done so poorly.

Of course, that is Nolan's director's trademark: blending and slicing in the editing room to make an standard script seem interesting. It's basically the Memento-trick a bit dimmed down. Although, he didn't use his space/fantasy inserts scarcely. The so called sound evocations missed their goal as well. Frankly, I am not convinced that he used movie-medium very wisely. He just told the story with images. Xavier Dolan in Mommy, now that is using the media to convey emotions. The stomping of the feet for example, oh my every boxing-movie did it and better too.

That could be forgiven but the dramatization of the test-launch was truly ridicules. Count-down of two minutes and he already inserted a close-up of a trembling hand hovering above the launch button? Grotesque. I agree, after 100 minutes of bla-bla he needed to do something but this seemed like candid camera to me. Someone would appear and say hahaha: this was an experiment: we showed you a over-the-top remake to test you. It feels like very little has changed since Griffith's silent age. Brainfart.

If you are 15 and haven't seen or read a lot, I can understand that this had somewhat of an impact but I hope you keep inhaling culture so that 15 years from now you can look at this movie again and say: "mind you, did we actually think this was good? How far we have come. Kudos to us."

I still struggle to believe that the general consensus leads to an 8,5 on imdb. Acting, photography, sound, locations, ... that's all outstanding on its own but how? How can you still take people along on a journey with such old, old directing tricks? My fate in mankind takes a huge dive.

5.title: Like an Endless Trailer
5.content: The character assassination of Julius Robert Oppenheimer is a much described and debated subject, and it's basically also what this film is about, I think, and little about nuclear bomb making. Nevertheless, though it's nearly three hours long, director Christopher Nolan still tries to fill the plot with more than is possible, and the results is that it stylistically appears like an endless trailer, where the editing and the jumping in time looks more like a long music video than an epic film. At times it becomes distressing to watch, and it's a great relief when this cannonade of pictures takes breaks in a few longer and slower sequences. If the intention has been to illustrate the main character's inner life during the process, it's perhaps reasonable, but this great topic would probably fit better as a mini series. However, Cillian Murphy makes the very best out of it as Oppenheimer, and despite the aggressive editing he manages to build a credible character. Sadly it doesn't work too well for several other characters, who also are more or less miscasted.

5.title: Quite overrated.
5.content:
Personally, I found this movie quite boring. Mostly because of its long lastness of three hours.

Have it won seven Academy Awards? I'm not surprised, it could have given it ten Oscars, and why not all of them - those academics adore awarding boring and meaningless movies, especially for the last dozen years...

I admit, this one was not among the meaningless, but on the other hand, it was one of the most boring I have watched in my life. Even if I did not know in detail the personality of Oppenheimer, and did not know about his achievements - I was still not particularly impressed.

The only thing I liked was the acting. Robert Downey Jr. Was exceptional in his role, unrecognizable as a vision and as voice - I was impressed, really.

Cillian Murphy was the usual actor - always serious and absorbed in his character.

A movie that would be gathered in two hours was stretched out to three hours... At times, I fast-forward it because three hours are too much time in our busy daily routine, and I do not like to watch movies in parts.

In general, I would say that I only liked the acting, nothing else, I wasn't impressed at all. So that's why it's hard for me to give it more than 5/10.

5.title: torn on this
5.content:
One one side i can appreciate the gravity behind the movie, detailing the back story behind one of the most pivotal points in the evolution of human science and history, the moral conflicts behind those who spearheaded the project, and the internal political battles between the US government and the scientists whose own ideologies made them suspected against america

on the other side, it was seriously dragged out, with little in the way of any impact aside from the scene immediately after the bombs were used and oppenheimer imagines their effects on people it was more like 6 half hour episodes of a documentary show end to end, it told an important story but it was painful to sit through.

5.title: Tedious
5.content:
I found this film tedious. Flash forward and backward tend to be cumbersome in most visual media. In this it was awkward and complex.

The lack of brutally stringent security measures reveals how the USSR became party to mutually assured destruction. And the hubris of powerful men led to the development of atomic power and the determined humiliation of Oppenheimer. Given the impact in real life, time should have been devoted to showing the massive devastation actually effected by the bombs in Japan. By revisiting the magnitude of power wielded, the horror is made manifest. The shame of the victor would be more comprehensible.

It is an important movie. I, however, was disappointed and will not suffer through it again.

5.title: Boring and misses the point
5.content:
Would have been a 6 if it wasn't because of the wasted potential.

This is not the story of Oppenheimer and the bomb, this is the story of Oppenheimer feared being a communist and being ousted notwithstanding his achievements. Felt sorry for the guy, but the movie didn't really manage to make really care.

Storytelling is long-winded, disconnected and frankly just plainly boring, it is a Nolan movie with a really non-Nolan plot. It's a one hour buildup, one hour actual movie and after that I was looking at my watch thinking "I don't think I can withstand another hour or this".

I think the most ridiculous part is trying to build up tension and suspense when they try the prototype - you know it is going to blow up because it's an historic movie so I guess it is trying to build suspense in the actors?

5.title: Great acting but Zzzzzz
5.content: This is a well directed and well acted movie but man is it ever tedious and boring. It's three hours you kind of want to end about twenty minutes into the film. Perhaps I'm just shallow and don't fully appreciate the depth and this "epic" nature of this Nolan work of art but I know I'm not alone in that department. It seems most of the people who took this time to review this film are of intellect that gets this film on another level but most of the people who watched it and didn't review it, didn't review it because they turned it off after about twenty minutes. I mean go ahead and ignore me and watch it but don't blame me for not warning you should have spent the three hours you wasted in more productive fashion.

5.title: Could have been good... too much music, too long. Bored. Gave up.
5.content:
Found the amount of background music in virtually every scene an irritating and distraction. Why is this necessary? I'm sure we could understand how to feel about a scene based on the acting and the script without being told how to feel by the music. If this could be removed, together with lopping an hour off the running time, it might have made a decent film. Gave up with 40 minutes to go as I was bored.

Am I surprised this was such a success at the Oscars? Not really. The acting was pretty good. It was well shot. It could have been a classic. Instead it just feels like an overlong, overblown, noisy disappointment.

5.title: 90 minutes too long...
5.content:
Oppenheimer is a long, slow-burning film that is not for everyone. The film is over three hours long, and it can be quite dull at times. However, the soundtrack is excellent, and the film's middle section is particularly well-done.

The film tells the story of J. Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the Manhattan Project to develop the atomic bomb. The film is well-acted, with Cillian Murphy giving a standout performance as Oppenheimer. However, the film's length and slow pace can be a major drawback.

If you are a fan of Christopher Nolan's films, you may enjoy Oppenheimer. However, if you are looking for a more exciting or fast-paced film, you may be disappointed.

Here is a more detailed review of the film:

Pros: Excellent acting, especially by Cillian Murphy Beautiful cinematography Excellent soundtrack Thought-provoking themes Cons: Too long Slow pace Mind-numbingly dull at times

Overall, Oppenheimer is a well-made film with some excellent performances. However, the film's length and slow pace may be a major drawback for some viewers. I would recommend the film to fans of Christopher Nolan's films, but others may want to wait for it to be released on streaming.

5.title: Life of oppenheimer or politics of oppenheimer
5.content:
I had high hopes But it was over. I think it doesn't give much about Oppenheimer's personal life, but a lot about his political life. For which I find the movie boring. And it would have been better if the movie had ended sooner rather than having an episode about politics at the end of the movie.

Moreover, the acting of the movie was very good, the casting was very good, but I did not like the story very much. I feel boring because of the repetition of one incident in the movie. And the time of the movie is too much. It would have been better if the movie ended sooner.

So It's my Opinion.

Thank you.

5.title: I am a Nolan fan but .....
5.content:
The movie's main issue is that it didn't need to be so complicated. Movies can be engaging without being confusing, like "The Godfather," "Shawshank Redemption," or "Million Dollar Baby." Another problem is that the movie drags on because it's too long and some parts feel slow.

I was expecting a movie about an atomic bomb and science, but there's hardly any science in it, well that is an individual perspective. They only show the explosion briefly, and then the movie focuses on something else.

Then they tried to make Oppenheimer a hero, but if you think about it, he wasn't perfect. He cheated on his partner, had affairs, and had connections with communists, even helping them. Considering the time and the situation in the US back then, he could easily have looked suspicious. They could have focused more on the science and used good effects like in "Interstellar," which in itself is a good combination.

The only good thing about the movie is the actors. All of them did a great job, which is a positive aspect. This is the first time I'm so disappointed with a movie from Christopher Nolan.

5.title: Slow and dumbed down
5.content:
I had such high expectations for Oppenheimer - the film set off well enough, but soon I was exhausted from the lack of information relevant to the development of the atomic bomb - it would've been fun to learn how scientists actually came up with the math and theories - especially if there was a slight risk of blowing up the universe.

This film simply feels dumbed down - to the point that Oppenheimer appears as more as a manager than a scientist.

To make matters worse, the pacing is painfully slow and runtime about an hour longer than it needs to be.

But make no mistake - the core story is a fascinating one and worth a look. But Academy Award material? Not sure about that.

5.title: They were bad boys and scientists. Nothing else matters.
5.content:
This movie is OK but has a terrible script of people overstating their opinions, feelings and scientific opinions. I am interested in the progress of the bomb. I am not interested in his private life. There is over focus on the committee investigations which is for the reason of????

For me we know this bunch were not interested in women or anyone. So let's just go with their sexist opinions as a fact. This is a white guys movie. Let them stand. Boys behaving badly is a huge part of the whole era. They messed up the world. Their US based investigations that they thought were fun were not.

Let's have a boys behaving badly movie and admit it.

5.title: True movie buffs know this was a 1 time watch film and NOT IMAX WORTHY!! please read why
5.content:
First off great acting phenomenal cast but a MASSIVE missed opportunity to make it a 10 . This was filled with dialog which in 2023 makes it a film you can watch at home we have an 85 inch OLED TV and watched the 4k version. Here is the problem Oppenheimer is basically Doctor Frankenstein we See IN DETAIL him create his but when it's time to finally see the monster we DONT we hear how devastating he is how he killed all these people but we NEED TO see the monster. This was the RARE time a block buster DIDNT use special effects. It could have show what Hiroshima saw felt. 5.title: Story upstaged by style
5.content: I saw OPPENHEIMER in 70-millimeter format. I wish I had liked it better, but I didn't. What I disliked most about it was the soundtrack. There was INCESSANT background noise that rumbled and roared and thudded (with a lot of Sensurround-style vibration) throughout the film. Sometimes it drowned out the actors, several of whom were hard for me to understand in the first place. The style of the photography was also off-putting. To make it seem like a documentary or a period-piece, sections of it were filmed in black-and-white or used filters to deaden the colors. I think all these gimmicks were there to disguise the fact that the script wasn't really very focused and was 3 hours long. The script is based on true historical events, and reality isn't easily shoehorned into a coherent plot. It was never clear to me exactly what the point was. There are a lot of good actors in this movie, but I didn't know who they were until I saw the credits! I still think of Matt Damon and Robert Downey Junior as young men, and they're NOT! I thought Downey gave the best performance in the film, though. The art direction and costume design seemed to accurately depict the period, although thanks to the cinematography, we'll never know what the true colors of anything were. (I wonder if the film-maker told these people that he was going to use stylized cinematography beforehand, or whether they found out when they saw the film.) I admire the film's ambition, and I think the issues it raises are things that people should think about, but I wonder if it would have been better if they had just told the story.

5.title: A Visual Masterclass But A Not so GoodStory
5.content:
I personally did not like the non-linear structure of the film. The way that Nolan tried to spin Strauss's betrayal as suspense was lackluster and off-putting . Firstly, the structure really just made the trial lack build-up. Practically, the last ten minutes or so is where things unfold haphazardly. Almost trying to piece together a cop-out climactic surprise villain ending. Then 'thematic' suspense is just off-putting for what it was trying to do, create a complex view of Oppenheimer. By the end, he was just doing Spielberg's school of Heroes vs Villain. Strauss, very bad man. Oppenheimer, complex but mostly good. Its too simplified for comfort. The use of time could have been more effective in showing the change that the film aims to show with Oppenheimer's view of the bomb to be honest.

It had more success in telling the pre-trial Oppenheimer. I think its much more successful in creating the enigma of Oppenheimer. You could see him weak, uncompromising, a bit psychotic, and just a tad bit hypocritical. I felt that some portion can be edited down clearly, especially the Communist period or the pre-Alamo days, which was while important in the trial, does not really hold any weight once told verbally. It is what it is, people he had knew. The relationship between his wife and him could have been the better choice to focus on. The three hours is not entirely necessary for the film to be honest.

Otherwise, the film is marvelous and well-crafted. I think Cillian, Emily Blunt, Matt Damon and Safdie were noteworthy in the film. The story could definitely had be tweaked. 3/5.

5.title: Not worth a second visit
5.content:
We are not Americans, so we had the advantage of not being familiar with the political intrigue surrounding the A-bomb story. We went in with high expectations, stimulated by the the M&M-frenzy (Media and Marketing).

We came out a little confused. Was this what we hoped to get?

We had seen some excellent acting, fine photography and a sometimes gripping story. I learned a bit about American politics.

Unfortunately, a mediocre script, chopped up by dreadful editing kept us on our toes the whole time, trying to figure out who was who, what was this persons' relevance and what happened when.

There was no subtlety. Once every two minute we were jolted out of our seats by sudden heavy sounds, presumably aimed at waking us up. Yes, they got our attention. Also, some characters were given parts to play that left nothing to be imagined. Strauss, for instance, came across as untrustworthy from the first glance he gave the camera. The president, in his brief encounter with Oppenheimer, was clearly pictured as a man without any doubts or pity,

I would call this movie an excellent superficial story. With shortcomings.

A bit of a disappointment.

5.title: Feels like watching a three-hour-long film trailer
5.content:
Capturing a wide array of historic events, characters and themes into one all-encompassing movie proves to be a difficult challenge for any director, and this one is no different.

The audiovisual spectacle and certain performances (Robert Downey jr. In example) aside, the majority of scenes felt chaotic, sudden, and lacked length, leaving you with a constant sense of getting outpaced and needing to catch up. It's not necessarily the complexity of the chosen themes, but directional choices in how to portray them, that makes Oppenheimer feel like an overextended film trailer. Watching this is a Sisyphean task if you ask me.

5.title: Pretty boring movie, could've just been an audiobook
5.content:
Start off by saying before watching the movie, I didn't even know the movie title was of the main character,, and I didn't even know who Christopher Nolan was or his work until after watching the movie and looking it up. Instead I had heard it's about a movie about war and supposedly a 'masterpiece'.

After watching the movie, here's what I did/not enjoy...

PROS Some amazing acting from the cast, Cillian Murphy, Matt Damon and Emily Blunt were particular standouts for me.

I did enjoy the dialogue content, but I hated its delivery (see below).

CONS Rapid fire edits throughout the entire movie made it very difficult to follow the storyline, I don't think more than 3 or 4 mins was spent on each scene - which was not enjoyable for a 3hr long movie.

VERY dialogue heavy - combined with the fast edits above, it felt like they were trying to cram too much into 3 hrs. And it's okay to have fast conversations in each scene, but then it jump to the next fast-paced conversation scene, and the next and so forth. There was no time to digest the weight of what just happened!

Poor visual storytelling - the fast edits + dialogue heavy script combined made it feel like the cinema format was not properly delivered, and it felt like I was being 'told' what was happening, not 'shown'. Based on this, I probably could've just listened to this movie like an audiobook, and had the same experience.

No emotive storytelling either - when I finally figured out Oppenheimer was a person (and the main character) I thought this would become an emotional story about his life, relationships, aspirations and fears. Instead, it felt more like a rapid-fire roll call of his personal and work resume - almost like a documentary.

Strange sound design in some parts - there were some parts when the actors were speaking (eg Emily Blunt) and I had no idea what she saying, so much so it made me wish the cinema had included subtitles!! Surely I could expect more for a $100M movie?

I'm struggling to understand how on earth this movie is considered a 'masterpiece'? Not a movie I'd watch again...

5.title: Much Ado About Nolan's Ego
5.content:
"Oppenheimer" is about nebulous men struggling with identity. We're told that the problem is morality, but the finished film - the sum total of Christopher Nolan's vision, script, direction, and ego (so much ego) - has little to say about the catastrophic technology it supposedly chronicles. It barely registers as a biopic, and it certainly isn't a meditation on history or even the bomb. Instead, it's three hours of a director insisting that he has something important to say, but that you should be smart enough to understand what that is without him having to accomplish it.

And that is a problem that no one seems to be mentioning in their rapturous reviews of "Oppenheimer". What exactly is it all about?

The entire film is so monotone and self-serious that one often forgets why any of the talking heads are important. They all speak and act like the same character. And honestly, they aren't particularly important. Edited linearly, "Oppenheimer" would be a quite simple, drab film. The performances are great, the roles thankless. So much so that when the only characters that suggest real people are not on screen - Downey's frustrated Lewis Strauss and Damon's General Groves - we feel their absence. Murphy does admirable work, as does Krumholtz as Isador Rabi, but really, these are flat, rote characters that gain empathy through persistence, not necessarily precision. In fact, that's the game that "Oppenheimer" plays: it only ever manages to emphasize the grey areas of it's central ethical dilemma.

To that end, the bomb really doesn't matter. The devastating after effects of the device are measured in terms of its function as science and as a scientific albatross around Oppie's neck. The human cost - and the cost on Oppenheimer himself - are given passing glances, leaving us to the real meat of the film, which is, in fact, conference rooms. "Oppenheimer" is about men talking. Make no mistake.

This makes for a tortuously obtuse and often offensively glib first hour. With the intrusive, often silly Tangerine Dream-esque score highlighting every petty argument and special-effects-imagining-the-cosmos scene and the spot-the-celebrity platforming, the only sign of humanity we get is literally writhing human flesh. Female nudity is a plot point for "Oppenheimer", though as in most Nolan productions, women barely exist. Here are two of Nolan's three female types: tragic trollop and tragic nag. Really, these could be any two actresses. They don't matter. Make no mistake, this is a film about men talking.

The second hour is genius. Cross cutting between the genesis of the bomb and the political machinations surrounding it, you get the sense that Nolan has really found a moment of true excitement. That sets up an incredibly disappointing third act which reveals exactly how weak Nolan's script is once it literally loses the power of nuclear annihilation. Everything, in fact, comes together over a very famous meeting that, historically, never happened. Poetic license? That's a problem when you waste 3 hours browbeating the audience with conference room minutiae and a script lifting from actual government documents.

"Oppenheimer" - in an ironic note that I've seen leveled against "Barbie" - is a film that wants to have it's cake and eat it too. We're told that the bomb is loathsome and dreadful and unethical pornography, and so Nolan knows that we have to see it. And we want it big and messy and full of ejaculate. Never mind that 300,000 human lives were what Oppie saw every time he closed his eyes - no - Nolan returns us again and again to the conference room, where petty insults manifest in conspiracies and smirking. Lots of smirking.

So what has Nolan accomplished here? The same end that he arrives at in each of his films: stolid detachment, pseudo-intellectualism, and stunning cinematic craftsmanship. Unfortunately, the movie is only worth an 90 minutes of inspired filmmaking. The rest is simply pretentious fat. Or rather, the rest is Nolan's insistence that he has something so important to say, but never gets around to it in 3 hours. Oppenheimer may be an infinitely interesting human being, but as a film character, he's cardboard, no matter how hard Murphy works to give him wrinkles.

Defenders of Nolan (and they are Legion) will explain to you that this is a great anti-war film, but it tells a lot more than it shows. It's not a satire and as a history lesson, it certainly omits large sections of the timeline that may have provided some drama, like say, the fates of Daghlin and Slotin. Frankly, this is the same tiresome walk and talk that weighs down the typical Aaron Sorkin history lesson, somehow rendering all of the characters and all of the audience to the same level of "look at how smart we are just for having experienced this."

None of this matters if the film moves you emotionally. I felt nothing during these 180 minutes. Certainly, I didn't come away with a greater understanding of the scope of the bomb, nor did I learn much about Oppenheimer. I learned a lot, however, about how meticulously exhausting Nolan is when Downey Jr isn't on screen.

5.title: Fragmented Storytelling
5.content:
The story of J. Robert Oppenheimer is very worthy of telling. He was a deep, fascinating man of sparkling intelligence and I was delighted to hear that this movie was being made. And even better with one of my favorite actors. With his eyes like sapphires set in crystal paperweights & a sublime acting talent to rival the greats, the fantastic Cillian Murphy in the lead role, well I just HAD to see this. Yet I am sorry to say the result of the movie iteslf was something of a let down.

I shall start by saying this movie requires 110% of your attention, if you are to enjoy it in any way. I gave it this & I did enjoy the superb acting from all the cast. The cast give it their all & my 5 stars is mostly for this reason. But the movie itself is let down by bloated, yet fragmented storytelling. Distracting flash back scenes, & a soundtrack that on one hand makes your ears bleed & on the other you can not hear character dialouge. This movie really needs subtitles. Also insulting the Sacred Hindu texts of the Bhagavad Gita is absolutely not on. I am a British woman who has lived & worked in India & I have deep respect for the Hindu faith, so why on earth was this included?

Now onto the story itself. We are missing such a lot here. Oppenheimer was known as the father of the atomic bomb, but there is scant storytelling about said bomb beyond badly done CGI of rather limp explosions. Where is the "Tickling the Dragons Tail"? Or explanations about the "Demon Core" as these are missing. You can't really tell a story about Oppenheimer if you exclude what he actually invented. In fact in 1989 a much better film was released called "Fat man & little boy" which is far more superior & explains these things better, so I suggest people watch this instead. However in Oppenheimer 2023 their is barely anything about the science & its horrific effects, as well as the horrilbe deaths & endeless suffering his invention caused. There are some mentions of his horrible dilemma of actually dropping the bomb, but these are scant & rather superficial.

All in all Oppenheimer tries too hard to be epic & it is about an hour longer than it needs to be, which is why some people are calling it boring. Personally I do not think it is boring as the acting in this movie is so good. The acting carries it! But to tell a real story of its subject, it would need a complet rewrite & a cut of all the nonsensical, long drawn out scenes that mean nothing. Basically if you are going to watch this, give it your full attention, make sure you have subtitles & enjoy the acting as it is excellent.

5 stars for all the cast as you did a terrific job!

5.title: The score is the only thing keeping the attention
5.content:
Oppenheimer, the man, felt not the least sympathetic or dramatic to me and was therefore very hard to stay engaged with. Dialogues aplenty but none of the dialogues get really delved into, rather they all feel rushed. The score then, is a brilliant work, until you realise that it was what kept your attention all along and would be more fitting to a psychological thriller- you know, with dialogues that are not rushed.

I couldn't finish it for the film could not decide whether it wanted to be an epic flick like the ones Nolan is known for or a drama.

5/10 for the score and cinematography nonetheless.

5.title: Too long, too talky, yet interesting
5.content:
I just saw this late this afternoon in Astoria Queens, NY. Here are some observations:

1) It goes into incredible detail about Oppenheimer's leadership and engagement with the group creating the atomic bomb, his troubled relationship with a woman named Jackie, and then after it was discovered that a Russian spy had infiltrated the project, the subsequent way in which he was mistreated as a communist sympathizer, which he wasn't.

2) The acting by both Celian Murphy and Emily Blunt (not to mention others) was top notch.

3) The film had way too much dialogue, especially of cerebral and technical natures, for the average moviegoer to follow. This slowed the pace down quite a bit, making the first hour, in particular, interminable! There could have been much less of it and put across in layman's terms.

4) The soundtrack seemed to overpower what was going on on the screen at times.

5) I believe the entire story could have been paired down and told in two hours, making it a more enjoyable experience for the audience.

6) And the whole film seemed overly slick, almost as if the way it was made was meant to overshadow the story.

5.title: Will watch again
5.content:
To be fair I had a bad seat stuck in the corner. Also, there was something with the audio in the film or theater. I couldn't make out parts of the dialog over the background/scene noise.

Too much time spent on Oppenheimer himself, wanted to know more about the other scientists. Political intrigue bores me. Should have spent more time on the women in his life or don't cover it at all.

Could have watch a 3-hr movie of scientists in a room talking the theory and math of quantum physics even if it was just the surface level stuff I already know.

I took Matt Damon's advice and left after the trinity event.

5.title: 3 hours watching white men with different graded of gray talking
5.content:
If the press would have just been honest I would have saved 3 hours of my life.

Not even Barbie can counter such completely liveless 3 hours solely white men with different grades of black to white hair. Yea, there was a woman for sex and another to stand besides him.

Don't do this to your spouse, Barbie can't make up for this.

Despite spending 2 hours with courtroom style talking out never makes clear what exactly Oppenheimer contributed, how he was genius (I can't tell after watching this movie).

It is possible to make talking interesting, for example the scenes in JFK sitting at the pond. But Nolan simply failed to make it any interesting.

Not even any of the displaced people of the first American nations which were displaced were shown. This movie shows how boring a world would be if only white men existed.

Of course what it also did not show was the effect of the bombs. Basically anything else besides Oppenheimer.

I want 3 hours of my life back.

5.title: Well Made Propaganda
5.content: Hard to judge this one-obviously very well made as are all Nolan films-however the problem is that the ignorant public often interprets these historical movies as fact not fiction. Every Hollywood movie including this one that portrays Communists always shows them as caring wonderful people basically saints that would not hurt a fly-30 million Christians were murdered in the Soviet Union by these Communists-we never ever here about this because it doesn't fit the Hollywood narrative. So that is the issue-not how well done this film is but the actual intent of the producers-which is to distort history.

5.title: Typically bad science movie
5.content:
I've spent a lot of time reading about the history of science from this period and this movie was a huge let down. It's a romance wrapped in a nerd plot. Very little attention is given to the vast array of characters and thinkers that went into this effort and instead we are presented the myth of Oppenheimer as an on steroid. I've read Stan Ulam's book, Godels personal writings and many other scientists from this period. None of them give a picture even remotely close to what is drawn here. Oppenheimer was not that big a deal. I'm sorry but he just wasn't thought of as all that much by most these people. He came from an exceptionally wealthy family, and though he was a very intelligent child, many thinkers seem to have the opinion his family connections were more important than his mind. Feynman has some funny stories of Oppenheimer being not only wrong but cruel and willfully ignorant and almost sabotaging a whole conference due to his fixation on a bad proof.

Anyway, it's just a romance story. There's nothing here beyond feeling intense from big sounds bad sweeping images. But, your mind will take nothing from this ultimately except mythology.

5.title: Overrated - Barbi is better!
5.content:
I don't understand how this movie got so many awards? It's not even close to being worth nomination, and I have to say - Barbi was much better!

As a lover of films centered around scientific discoveries and the lives of great minds, I was really looking forward to watch Oppenheimer hoping for a cinematic experience like the Imitation Game or the Theory of everything. Unfortunately, Oppenheimer fell short of expectations, failing to deliver a compelling narrative or engage with its themes effectively.

One of the biggest issues with this movies is its lack of a clear purpose or thematic direction. While Barbi raised thought-provoking points about women's equality (I loved the speech of America Ferrera, even Ken's song raised some good points), Oppenheimer struggles to find its footing, feeling more like a documentary reciting cold facts. There is no central theme or purpose so I still don'tget it - why did Nolan make this movie? What is the message?

Pacing is another big issue, especially the first half of the movie - it's boooring, i had to force myself to watch till the end. The simultaneous presentation of different events like two court hearings +discussions on hydrogen bomb and the actual story of making the bomb without proper context only confused me, detracting from the overall narrative flow.

All those hearings and discussions in the beginning lost its meaning because of zero context provided on the purpose of those hearings until the end of the movie. That 1st was actually security clearance hearing - so what? What is the importance of that hearing I couldn't get it. He didn't go to jail, just got his access revoked. Why was it so important for this movie to waste viewer's time?

There are too many characters all men dressed in grey with zero added value leaving audiences struggling to connect with or even distinguish between them.

His relationships with women also suffer from a lack of emotional depth or meaningful interaction. Zero dialogue or expressions of affection only leave me wondering if he loved them or not? Was it his character that he has no emotions or was it just the fault of the movie script?

One of the biggest missed opportunities and disappointment is its failure to address the ethical implications of the atomic bomb. With no meaningful exploration of the moral dilemmas surrounding its creation or the devastation wrought by its use, the film feels shallow and devoid of substance. The absence of any critique of the US government's decision to drop the bomb on Japan or the absence of actual horrifying videos of the explosion or it's impact on people not even saying the impact of radiation after the explosion is particularly disappointing, leaving a significant thematic void in the narrative.

Despite these shortcomings, the acting performances are fine. However, even stellar performances cannot compensate for the lack of character development or meaningful engagement with the film's themes.

In conclusion, it is just a huge disappointment. In comparison Barbi, which effectively tackle important social issues, Oppenheimer falls short. I bet if Barbi was about men, it could have won all the awards.

5.title: The film's message resonates Fermi's legacy demands recognition.
5.content: The film proves engaging on a global level, even though some parts are tedious. However, it's truly senseless that the remarkable Enrico Fermi has received inadequate visibility. He embodies the crucial figure who provided fundamental guidance to all other characters, playing an essential role in the project's realization. For those who might not know, it's important to underline that Fermi is the inventor of the reactor, a contribution without which the achievement of atomic energy would have remained an unattainable goal, significantly altering the course of history. The film's message resonates-Fermi's legacy demands recognition.

5.title: Cool music video
5.content:
Oppenheimer was a really cool music video! A bit long though. Maybe it just needed an intermission or something.

In all seriousness, the sound mixing was just unbearable. I'm sure it was a great movie, but I quite literally could not hear 80% of the dialog over the constant explosively-loud music. That's fine in an action movie I suppose, but Oppenheimer was primarily composed of what I gathered to be meaningful dialog.

According to interviews, Nolan thinks his sound mixing is a revolutionary artistic choice and that other directors are too conservative with their sound. I think having music playing the entire time, including during dialog, is an artistic choice and I'll give him that. Making the music louder than the dialog, however, is not an artistic choice; it's amateurs using Windows Movie Maker who don't know how to use the sound level features. It made an otherwise grade A movie feel B-rate.

Maybe he just forgets that not everyone knows the dialog by heart like he does so we can't guess at what's being said while he blasts his music like a college frat party. Amazing how one single decision can detriment an entire film. Maybe if he had listened to anyone other than his own ego and all his "10-stars just for breathing" simps, things would have been different.

Well, I suppose I'll have to rewatch with subtitles when it comes out on demand. The theater was three hours I can't get back.

5.title: Boring and confusing
5.content: I really wanted to love this movie because I am a history buff and I wanted to see the story behind the bomb, and in a way I did get the story behind the bomb, but in a very confusing and boring way. The movie kept jumping around between time periods before the war and after the war, showing all kinds of scenes out of sequence, which if done right can be very effective, but in this movie it was done wrong, very wrong. A simple "1939" on the screen would've made things clear, but I guess we're just supposed to know. Even at the end of this three hour long marathon I was still confused about many of the scenes, and it wasn't just about the time periods, but the dialogue itself was confusing. Half the time I didn't know what or who they were talking about, and the last hour, after the bomb exploded, was not only boring and confusing, but also entirely pointless and the movie would've been better without it. In addition, they added in these scenes, presumably for dramatic effect, that were intended to show the character's emotions or thought process at the time, showing us what he was feeling but was not actually happening, and that too missed the mark for me. Much of it was just awkward and annoying. It wasn't all bad. The acting was very good, and some of the scenes were very powerful, but overall I'm still very disappointed in this movie. It could've been so much more entertaining.

5.title: one of the best
5.content:
The movie was quite good. One of the best in biography, of course, after Lawrence of Arabia. I just didn't like the flirting that happened in the court, it was completely out of the movie, the games were great. It was very good that the movie was divided into three parts. And that part of the explosion of Trinity was great and I think it was not computerized and it was a real explosion that shows how much importance was given to the movie. And the narration of the film was very masterful and it seems that Nolan knew when the actors should talk and when they should walk while talking and when they should turn their backs to the camera, which conveys this extremely masterful look of Christopher Nolan.

And overall it was a very good movie.

5.title: Great acting but challenging to sit through
5.content:
I discovered this film to be excessively intricate, unnecessarily lengthy, and somewhat challenging to sit through. The acting, notably from Robert Downey Jr. And Cillian Murphy, is commendable, however, the relentless and simplistic portrayal of the American perspective becomes rather wearisome. Moreover, it missed a chance to delve deeper into illustrating the profound impact of the bomb on Japan.

Not sure why this movie is/was shown at IMAX but I'm glad I watched it at home over two days because I almost fell asleep twice.

This movie is an hour too long and probably one of Christopher Nolan's worst films.

5.title: If you're looking for thought provoking cinema, this isn't it.
5.content: This film has everything laid out. I have been looking forward to it for months. Like others, Nolan is one of my favorite directors, nay, probably my favorite director of all time. All the critics raved about this film. The trailer made it look like something that I could take my kids to for the discussion I expected we would have afterward - even if I had to cover their eyes during the nude scenes. I was expecting to come out of this picture blown away and I even paid $25 to see it with a friend in IMAX first just to double check it was tween friendly enough. Well, I am sorry to say it was an enormous let down. Was it a decent flick? Sure. The cinematography was good, the story is interesting kind of, but let's be real here, Oppenheimer himself is not the interesting part of the story, the bomb is. The fact that you have to murder tens of thousands of people in order to save tens of thousands more. What the bomb does to people who aren't vaporized when it goes off. This was just barely touched on in the film. There are no scenes of mathematicians working feverishly, no real feeling of how large of a project this must have really been. There are snippets of things here and there about the project, but this really is JUST A BIOPIC of Oppenheimer. And somewhat of this Strauss guy that history pretty much has forgotten. And truth be told, none of it was really that interesting to me. Feynman would have made a much more interesting film, IMO. So, was it OK? Yeah, it was OK. Am I glad I spent $25 to see this in the theater? Nope. This is a rental, if you have nothing better to watch. But do yourself a favor, go get The Dark Knight or Interstellar and watch that again - you'll be happier in the end. If you want something kind of along the same vein that's a better movie, see The Imitation Game. If you are looking for.a thought provoking movie, watch The Fog of War.

5.title: Pinch me I'm dying
5.content: I was so very bored. They should have made 2 movies the making and detonation of the bomb and the persecution of Oppenheimer I would not see either. A plethora of dialogue that really did not interest me, however there was obviously much research done on this story so if you are a fan of government conspiracy, physics, math and endless discussions then maybe it's for you. The character of Kitty was just annoying, her 4th marriage, drank like a fish, couldn't handle being a parent almost giving up her child and then proceeded to have another, allowed her husband to cheat I just wanted to slap some sense into her. I definitely would have rather watched this at home so I could fall asleep in the comfort of my own house.

5.title: Just ok. Graphic sex scenes
5.content: I was disappointed in this Nolan movie because it's such a departure from his string of intense and cerebral movies. It's Mostly about politics during the time period. Great acting by all the cast but it has completely unnecessary soft porn that ruins the story line. Don't bring young kids! Good stuff includes the history of the creation of the bomb and how Oppy struggled with the consequences once it was built. The story line about how Strauss was involved was very interesting. I would bet that very few people know about his struggles after the WWII ended. This is a long one so get comfortable.

5.title: Turgid and full of cliché
5.content: The first hour of this film in particular has every cliché you've ever seen in a biographical movie come up again and again. What I found most annoying is this assumption that the audience can never understand any of the science involved in the story, so the makers substitute writing frantically on blackboards, cutting to sparks on a black screen, and the character being described as "brilliant genius", presumably because he can see the sparks whereas other people can't. Without any sort of context, the science is a meaningless abstract reference and the real story is lost. As for Cillian Murphy, he could have had a great career as a half forward for Nemo Rangers if he'd played his cards right and now look at him- sitting on an armchair stark naked in front of millions of people like an eejit.

5.title: It's Not Really About The Bomb
5.content:
Finally saw Oppie a couple of weeks back, I'm so sorry I don't understand the hype. It was just okay, my son who was too excited to see it also a bit disappointed. He's expecting more into the science of the bomb, but it's' just a subplot and we get more about his trial (inquiry) instead. I honestly was expecting the same.

That's actually okay, I like a good biographical drama it's just that we went in expecting something else, probably our fault. But that story itself wasn't that good, that's the problem when the subplot is more exciting. The atomic test was the climax and then for the next hour it got tedious.

But that "climax" wasn't even that exciting. I was amazed and somewhat disbelieved when I read about how they used practical effects for the atomic bomb test, and after seeing it I absolutely had no doubt that it was practical. It was so underwhelming, you see splashes of fireballs, if I didn't know it was a nuclear bomb explosion I would think that it was napalm. Even the sound fell short, the stomping scene room gave my subwoofer more workout.

As of now our favorite film from Nolan is still Interstellar.

5.title: It's all relative, isn't it....
5.content:
..but at 180 minutes this is definitely a long film but after watching the veiwer is non the wiser. I remember a TV series years ago on the race to create the atom bomb which was far more informative especially regarding the technical issues.

Nolan's effort is squarely focused on Oppenheimer as a man, however even after three hours I didn't get much insight into him. He is shown as a communist adulterer but his brilliance as a scientist is strictly a tell not show afair.

The movie is certainly very well made, has an inch thick gloss coat and there are plenty of familiar faces yet it's style overshadowed the substance. For example several sex scenes get more screen time than the bombing of Hiroshima and Nagasaki which would be considered the money shot in other genres but here comes an hour before the closing credits.

5.title: A glorified documentary
5.content:
Well I guess if you're a person that just hates documentaries and will never watch them on tv (like my wife) this film is an excellent opportunity to learn a thing or two about the origins of the A-bomb. The film is long(about 3 hours), slow paced and filled with political jargon but visual effects and great acting will keep you awake.

On the other hand if you're a history buff , just avoid it. It'll be like watching a rerun of the last Oppenheimer documentary you've seen just way noisier. You'll feel the film lacks drama, suspense and emotion. The director mr. Nolan atempts to correct this by using never ending flash-backs and flash-forwards. It doesn't work mr. Nolan. If anything it just annoys the viewers James Cameron got it right when he added the story of Jack and Rose to Titanic. Or the countkess other directors that have added fiction to their historical films to spice em up a bit.

All said I still believe Oppenheimer will probably sweep the Oscar's. Mainly due to publicity this film got and to the fact most films been released since covid have been subpar.

5.title: Boring and deceiving, stay away from Biopic's Nolan.
5.content:
The trailers for this film leaned way too much into Robert Oppenheimer's atomic bomb phase, where as this film actually only focuses on it for about an hour or so. Despite being a well acted, well visualized, and well adapted or faithfully adapted story; this is still a movie!! And you need to give the audience a reason to care. Oppenheimer as an individual is a boring and immoral lead, and his supporting characters aren't any better, or interesting for that matter. I feel like this should be a glorified documentary instead of a film, slap biopic on it if you want but unless your a science or history whiz this is a hard film to get invested in.

The middle of this film is where I really got bored, the last hour was ok, and the beginning was eh; but by the end I was just asking myself, and I should care about this why? I didn't even get to see the atomic bomb drop and kill people! How could you not include that? At least a brief scene would've sufficed.

Historical films in my opinion need a balance of education and entertainment, and this film has none of that. It's just slow, slog fested history with no effort into connecting audiences with the characters. Next time Mr Nolan, stick with what your good at, because this isn't it.

5.title: A disappointment
5.content:
I simply can't like this movie. It wants to say way too much and says way too little about way too many things. It can't decide what it wants to be, so it's not really anything - not just for the viewer, but for the creator. And that's a problem. It's not good as a biopic: there are serious historical flaws in the story, which irritated me. I'm a huge fan of John von Neumann... anyone, who knows who he was understands why I mention him. As a drama? The movie can't decide the centre of the drama. It's too weak as a spy-story, too weak as a political drama, too weak as a personal drama. Not one aspect is worked out to carry the film. The strongest aspect was how many times in american history the "what you did 20 years ago is more important than who you become and what your expertese is" ruined people's lives. Or at least was used as a political rethoric against opponents. And I appreciated that, hence the 5 points. As a moral/personal evolution the moral conflict isn't built up, the "evolution of a scientist" dies away halfway and doesn't really connect with the "organizer scientist". The "science should or should not have moral boundaries" isn't worked out and built up, just comes and goes without a purpose. The only detactable personal evolution is the "man of future becomes the man of past", but somehow that remains too weak in the end, too. So the movie falls apart and not even the brilliant actors and the massively impressive explosion scene can hold it together.

I couldn't help feeling how Nolan this time couldn't feel the fine line of balance... that "sometimes less is more".

5.title: Okayheimer
5.content:
I have mixed feelings.

First here is what I liked

The acting is really good especially Cillian Murphy and Matt Damon. Their scenes together were my favourites.

The subject is very sad but it is an undeniably interesting part of history

The film is really well made in terms of costumes, location, and effects etc Christopher Nolan is a great filmmaker. Not every movie he makes is a masterpiece like The Dark Knight or Interstellar but they are always at least quite good (except Tenet)

now here is the stuff I did not like

Women. I'm not trying to be sexist. Emily Blunt is a really great actress but I did not get anything at all out of the scenes with his wife or his mistress. I know people argue that you need that stuff to show him as a well rounded human being so he was not just a scientist but also a man with a family it grounds him makes him relatable blah blah blah shut up! No. He was a genius physicist from 80 years ago, I don't have to relate to him, all I'm really interested in seeing how he got the job, how they made the bomb, and if he felt any remorse afterwards for opening the gates of hell and slaughtering thousands of innocent people.
