Furthermore, the film's positive reviews seem almost surreal, as if Nolan's reputation alone is enough to earn acclaim. However, "Oppenheimer" suggests a concerning shift in Nolan's filmmaking, seemingly influenced by Hollywood's elite. The movie comes across more as a platform to showcase a roster of famous actors than a thoughtfully crafted biopic. The charm and depth expected from a Nolan project seem lost in this latest endeavor, replaced by what feels like a superficial display of star power.

3.title: What a HYPE!!!
3.content:
What a HYPE!!!

Is this a documentary or a movie? Seems it failed in both categories.

If it's documentary, If you haven't learnt about this man before, then you still don't know much about his family history, how he grew up and what really inspired him to do what he did.

If it's a movie, the way the story was told was like a documentary, a bland one. The sex scene and nudity didn't seem necessary. It didn't seem to add or make his character more interesting (when in real life, he was known as a womanizer).

3 stars go to: Cillian Murphy, Robert Downey Jr. And Original Score (although, it seems intrusive, sometime)

3.title: Nolan is not Sorkin
3.content:
This was one of the most boring movies I've ever seen.

I truly do not understand the hype - I have loved ALL of Nolan's previous works but he's stepped far away from his comfort zone in this feature. It's a style of movie that I would enjoy if I was heading in knowing it was written by Aaron Sorkin - a movie of this pace requires such a talent in order to survive. However, as Nolan is not Sorkin, the script and pace are equally interminable to the point where I had to walk out after 2 hours just to save time in my life.

Honestly by the time I left, I didn't even know what was happening in the story or, quite frankly, why Nolan thought it would be interesting enough to tell - I can now understand why this story hasn't been told before.

3.title: like watching a Jackson Pollock painting being made
3.content:
This movie was deeply disappointing. If you want to see a good movie about a WW2 STEM project leader, see The Imitation Game instead.

I think if someone else took all the raw footage from this movie and completely re-edited it, and re-did everything else, like the music/soundtrack, etc, there is a really great movie that COULD be made...the acting was fantastic, and historically this is a fascinating topic...but this movie isn't it.

This felt like watching a Jackson Pollock painting being made... like paint randomly and chaotically splattered againt a canvas with little rhyme or reason, and no discernable forms or shapes. It felt like the makers of this movie cared solely about proving they were "arTISTEs", and what suffered was actual storytelling.

The first 30 to 45 minutes were a mess. The whole movie suffered from absurdly short scenes that jump all over in time through out of context events that assault you like a random spray of shotgun pellets. Scene changes are jarring, and have no flow.

I expected something more to do with the Manhattan project and scientists, but instead got something that was a muddled mess of unspecified time periods, with the maker of the movie trying way too hard to be mysterious in order to confuse the audience for 2.5 hours before allowing them to realize that the movie was really mostly about a beef between Oppenheimer and one senator, with a little bit of Oppenheimer's introspection and Monday morning quarterbacking whether he had made the world a better or worse place thrown in. Again, Oppenheimer's introspection was so random, and chaotically scattered that it has no flow. You couldn't feel him changing over time, instead it bounced disjointedly all over the place. One scene he seems to have no regrets, the next he does, the next he doesn't, the next he does. His love life was similarly revealed in scatter shot, and seemed irrelevant to anything else. The movie seemed to be trying to tell too many stories: his love life, his college life, his professional life, his politics, his blacklisting after the Manhattan project, his beef with that 1 senator, all as separate stories that didn't tie together at all. It would have been better to pick 1 or 2 of those stories and gone deeper into them than to try to tell all of them in 1 movie. Way too many time periods shown, in way too confusing of a method. Again, terrible storytelling of a story that had so much potential.

Visual and audio representations of Oppenheimer's psychological state, essentially delivered to the audience as hallucinations, were randomly thrust upon us, so the movie bounced violently between seemingly more documentary to suddenly dreamworld fantasy. Unlike the tv show Scrubs where JD's daydreams felt like a natural extension of his character, the fantasy world here felt unnatural, and like the director was grinding the flow of the movie, what little flow there was, to a halt to make a public service announcement of how the character was feeling.

Music was over the top. Everything had music. It was annoying. It was noticable how the music was trying to manipulate my emotions, to make up for the poor storytelling being too impotent to do that on its own.

Note to all directors: Don't be afraid to use title cards indicationg time and location when you suddenly change time or location. There's a reason why movies do that.

3.title: Historically correct, but fail as a movie.
3.content: This movie may serve as a good biography or documentary, but as a movie it fails, the script and dialogues were plain dull and uninteresting. Not much of acting were actually needed as the whole movie were just conversations all over, there wasn't much plot twists or dramas in it, nor was there any character developments. A good movie involves an interesting script with good twists and turns that draws the audiences attentions, good character developments or actions etc but oppenheimer is a disappointment without these integrity, it only plainly play through the story of the a bomb invention. Well as the direction to chop into bits and pieces which were actually hard to follow and rather a pain long watch. Nolan is a great director but certainly not all of his movies were great, history films didn't work well like tenet, dunkirk and oppenheimer, perhaps he should stick with fantasy/super hero flicks that were more enjoyable.

3.title: Overhyping is counterproductive as it raises expectations to unrealistic levels that leads to disappointment
3.content:
Sorry but it just doesn't live up to the pre-game hype! And it's certainly not worth the extra for an IMAX viewing of bland desert landscapes, meetings and chalkboards full of maths symbols!

Yes it tells a story of a complicated man, in a complicated time in history but too many stories jumping around back and forth with a music score so overbearing in places it was starting to give me a headache (earplugs stopped me walking out for a break)

Strange though, as with nearly three hours runtime, Nolan chose not to use a single Japanese actor for a few scenes from their perspective in the aftermath?

For me Downey Jr gave a standout performance even in support as did Matt Damon. Blunt's low amount of screen time was noticeable, as the wife in support of a brilliant contrarian, but boring cerebral genius, who fared little better than Churchill in the post war years! (They had both served their purpose in war)

Will watch again on a TV screen to go back over details missed, in all that loud music & scene jumping. Perhaps Nolan will do a directors cut to add in the Japanese perspective, he could cut the completely unnecessary Florence Pugh nude scenes and keep the same runtime.

3.title: Too long and bad writing
3.content: The good parts? The acting, top notch. The story itself is also very important and interesting, but it was told in an awfully bad way and very slow progression of main storyline. It is NOT worth watching in the cinema, there is very poor usage of sound effects. It's just loud for no reason. Only the bomb effect was great, but rest is just very loud noise for no good reason and you just don't want to hear at it full blast when people are clapping or similar loud noises. It provides absolutely no effect other than you want to close your ears. Also bad cinematography, random use of white/black coloring for no good reason. It's not used as flashback there is no consistency of using white/black here and there it's just random and doesn't make the film anymore interesting, completely unnecessary. IMO the worst film Christopher Nolan has produced so far. If not for amazing acting, I would've left the cinema. 3 hours used to tell a story that could EASILY have been boiled down to 1,5 hours. 30-40% of the movie is about an interrogation that has real consequense or impact to the audience, it just seems like an awful long waste of time because. Some guy felt leftout so he decided to run a cross examination of Oppenheimer, which leads to nothing except he can't have his security clearance re-approved. Why would you Nolan spent 40% of the film on this utterly boring part? I honestly beats me how people can enjoy this movie. I would rather watch a black and white documentary on the manhatten project then my hearing would be intact and I would be more informed and less filled with nonsense.

3.title: Disappointing
3.content: I was so excited about Oppenheimer. My favourite director, many of my favourite actors (Cillian Murphy, Emily Blunt, Gary Oldman), but this was a 3 hour snorefest. It is historically accurate and looks good, but it didn't take long for any interest or care I had in the story or characters to disappear. Sure this movie is about a key moment in history, but it is very, very boring. So disappointing from such a genius as Nolan who has made so many brilliant movies. Even the hyped up detonation scene is massively underwhelming. I just can't understand the hype around this movie. Do yourself a favour and go outside for a walk.

3.title: You can't have dramatic scenes if all scenes are dramatic
3.content: Hate to say it, but the movie is quite bad. I usually really enjoy Nolan's work but this one is lacking any redeemable characteristics. The main issue is that it is boring. The story itself is interesting but the way it is presented is dull. It felt like 3 hour long trailer. Every scene had to be dramatic with over the top dramatic music and dialog. And when you have only dramatic scenes you don't have any dramatic scenes. Even the explosion lacked any actual effect. The only dramatic thing about it was that we had some 30 seconds of quietness. The movie had that stupid dramatic music non-stop. NON-STOP! The actors were fine, put the script was lackluster and I think the cast, the music, all the drama and the way the story was presented was because they knew the scrips was bad. Also I don't know who that movie targets. I feel like years ago history movies targeted people who would appreciate them and because they were done with a lot of love to the story, attention to details and made interesting they were appealing not only to history buffs. Nowadays historical movies target everybody so they are no longer historical but exaggerated dramas that are only inspired loosely by history. The movie really sucks.

3.title: Need my money back. People leaving the theatre
3.content:
How in the world this is close to a 9 I don't understand.

They need to have a University Class on the subject and characters and the reward of graduating the class with 80% or higher is going to see the movie. What happened to entertainment - my brain was tired in the first hour. First of all - TURN DOWN THE SOUNDTRACK! I would highly recommend that you skip the theatre and wait until it comes out on a device you can get close captioning on as the soundtrack overwhelms all of the dialogue and you can't hear what they are saying which might have helped understand it. I was begging for CC. I think there was one chuckle in the movie - so dark and depressing and muddled. I truly hated this movie even after reading up on the material. Just don't get the high ratings. Maybe people don't want to admit they don't get what is going on? SKIP IT. SERIOUSLY.

3.title: Unsurprisingly, Nolan fans are already overpraising this film.
3.content:
My son just described Oppenheimer as one hour of physics, one hour of building a bomb, and one hour of courtroom drama. That it is, but he neglected to mention that it's a full 181 minutes of bum-numbing Oscar-bait that will be a test of patience for all but dedicated Nolanites (or nuclear physicists, but I don't think there were many of those at the screening I attended).

I don't care how urgent and emotional the music gets, it's still people talking about quantum mechanics, communism and legal stuff that I didn't quite understand. It's not exactly a fun watch, nor a particularly profound one: we all know that the creation of atomic bombs ended WWII but ushered in an age of nuclear threat that still hangs over us today. I think most sane people would happily put the genie back in the bottle if they could. The film says nothing new - it merely emphasises how most of us feel about war, and nuclear weapons in general. Nolan could have done that in a lot less time, but the film wouldn't feel as important then, would it?

The performances are undeniably good, with Murphy putting in a strong turn as the titular scientist, Nolan delivers some fairly impressive visuals (although the long awaited detonation of the test bomb is underwhelming - I doubt seeing it in IMAX would have helped), and I now know what Florence Pugh looks like naked (now that I would liked to have seen in IMAX!), but I feel that mankind needs a three hour biopic about J. Robert Oppenheimer about as much as it needs a destructive force capable of destroying the planet many times over.

3/10. It's like Oliver Stone's JFK for science nerds - long, boring, and destined to win awards (they'll give an Oscar to any old tripe these days - **cough** Everything, Everywhere All At Once **cough**).

3.title: Snoozenheimer
3.content: This movie could have had the whole first half cut from it and it wouldn't have hurt the film. In fact, it might have made it better because, for being about the man who is the "father of the atomic bomb," it was really boring. The movie didn't really start picking up until Trinity Site was picked. Also, while I understand the director made artistic choices to show how Oppenheimer felt, many just felt forced and overly long. The nudity wasn't necessary and detracted from the scenes. The communism hearings were exceedingly boring- the movie could have gotten the importance of security across in much less time. The movie honestly felt over after he spoke to Truman about the bombs dropping in Japan, but then it went back to the hearings. The movie should have been half as long with half the characters.

3.title: Boring movie that seems more profound than it is
3.content:
Every so often, a movie comes along that everyone seems to praises on the surface; and yet deep down, everyone also knows it's boring and pretentious. That's what Oppenheimer is. It's one of those movies you go into knowing you're supposed to like- and then when you inevitably don't like it, you feel like your taste is too juvenile or you're not smart enough. But none of that is true- it really just is a boring, dull, and kind of pretentious movie.

In short, it's really just a bunch of dialogue and stuff for three hours. Nothing particularly emotional, exciting, or eventful. Some interesting stuff, but not enough to justify a three hour runtime. I fully believe this movie only got the recognition and awards it did because of a high budget and famous director/cast. Keep the storylines and dialogue but use unknown (but equally talented) actors, and nobody would care about this.

This is a movie you watch once to say you did it, then never watch again. Thank goodness.

3.title: Unremitting snore fest !
3.content:
I think this is a massively overhyped, seriously underwhelming film which I am afraid I gave up on halfway through! Watching it was such a slog, I struggled to stay awake - and that doesn't happen to me!

It's unrelenting documentary style is not easy to engage with and there are very few lighter moments to entice the viewer to keep watching or to become emotionally involved.

The story jumps from one era to another, dialogue is so heavy and the whole film just drags incessantly on and on like a tedious school history lesson, where you can't help checking your watch again and again!

Avoid at all costs is my advice!

3.title: Watch at home
3.content: The acting was great, but the story was disappointing. The first two hours covered nothing. We didn't learn anything about how they invented and created the bomb. The 3rd hour was good with the story of the politics and the hearings. Nothing has changed our government is just as corrupt as it was back then. Could have left out the sex and nudity as it served nothing to the story. People that gave this a high rating is questionable. And the directer advising people to see it on the biggest screan they can is also questionable. Why.. they showed one expolsion and I don't need to see boobs bigger than my hole body lol. The last hour is the only worthy part of this movie. Wait and watch it at home those 3 hours are LONG...

3.title: A mix of terrible movies
3.content: A bad court room drama movie. A bad war movie. A bad political movie. A bad innovation movie. Put them all together and you get Oppenheimer. This movie just goes on forever with its multiple layers. Right at the end, I was still waiting for the final reveal or the big twist. The only saving grace was good acting by A-list actors and actresses. Such a waste of 3 hours. Not a movie you will want to watch multiple times. A bad court room drama movie. A bad war movie. A bad political movie. A bad innovation movie. Put them all together and you get Oppenheimer. This movie just goes on forever with its multiple layers. Right at the end, I was still waiting for the final reveal or the big twist. The only saving grace was good acting by A-list actors and actresses. Such a waste of 3 hours. Not a movie you will want to watch multiple times.

3.title: Oppenheimer
3.content:
Honestly don't understand why this movie is rated so high, clearly alot of nolan fanboys praising him like a movie god. 3hrs of bland dialogue and no action.

The main moment, the nuke explosion is the most fake underwhelming nuke I've ever seen, Nolan's fetish for "no cgi'' and practical effects totally ruined the whole authenticity of the explosion when it's basically just a fuel explosion, no real mushroom cloud, no real shockwave, wrong lighting. Just bland fake explosion of fuel. Surely they have the budget to make a real explosion with real explosives to get a real shockwave and add in a cgi mushroom cloud. Would have looked way better.

3.title: Great actors kept this relevant to see
3.content: Unfortunate snore fest. Just a sausage fest of dialogue. Same ol story of how men make useless wars and play the victim card after the fact. Definitely Nolan's slowest film. Idk how to make this lengthy besides stating that barbie lived up to the hype and this film did not. Once the atomic bomb set off my bowels we're ready to go. Did not stay for the last 15 minutes and I have zero interest. Nolan is great and of course I'll see future works but this was a history channel flop. So I'm sure it'll get lots of Oscar's. Gave me something to talk about (or b*tch about). I'm so glad I didn't drag my girl to this. Men go see barbie with your girl. It's less of a waste of time.

3.title: Boring
3.content:
This movie should have been right in my wheelhouse. I knew the story beforehand. I am a retired Marine LtCol. Visited Hiroshima. But this movie was punitive to watch. I like Cillian Murphy. He was great in Peaky Blinders. It's not that he is miscast, it's that he's having to carry a 3 hour movie when 2 hours would have been fine.

The weird flash forward, flash back, really strange starlight scenes were annoying. As were the hearing scenes. I get it. He had leftist ties. I knew that beforehand. But those hearing scenes were tedious, at best, punishing at worst.

It's poor editing. You could have told the story in 2 two hours.

It's a bad movie.

3.title: Overrated and BORING.
3.content:
I don't hate Nolan,He is a talented filmmaker and good storyteller sometimes.

This wasn't his best shot though.

There is no character development whatsoever,I didn't care about any of the characters and shoving a famous face into camera doesn't make the audience feel connected to them.

It was a lengthy,boring movie which left me disappointed and dissatisfied.

Tho whole personal aspect of His life was pointless and badly written.

The acting was also affected by the poorly written story,Blunt is usually a good actress but in this movie she was so out of place.

The only reason i gave 5 starts is because it brought up the name of a scientist who many may not known and now they can go and read about him themselves,as this movie didn't serve him well.

3.title: Left the Theater
3.content: I had been waiting to see this for a month and finally was able to have time to see it. I have just enough knowledge to know who Oppenheimer was but didnt know the full story behind him. There was constant time hopping and so many substories within the main story I couldn't keep track of what and why all these were relevant. Not to mention tons of characters and no idea how they were related to what was happening or their importance. As someone who is interested in learning about history I really tried to hang with it and just couldn't. Maybe different editing would help, definitely less time hopping and more information on the characters. Hoping someone remakes this with clearer overall definition.

3.title: Clunky and violently boring
3.content: This movie jumped all over the place. And it was boring. All the rave reviews seem to be more about society demanding that you love the film. I was so excited to rent the film. When I did, I had to stop watching from boredom. Then I told myself that it was just my mood. So I started it up again. Same thing. Then I thought my wife watching with me was a bad influence. So I tried again after she was away. Same thing. I love history films. This was the worst ever. I wanted this film to be OK. But it sucked. In 1987, I met Edward Teller when a professor brought him to a small class at West Point. He was such a fascinating man. Again the movie's portrayal of him was just boring.

3.title: Boring
3.content:
I thought this movie might make me cry and instead it made me yawn.

This movie was definitely not what I expected and It was too long. I thought it would never end and I had to force myself to finish it. I would not have bothered except that I had to buy the movie and it has been hyped to the skies. Either the acting was insufficient or the characters that were portrayed were simply not interesting enough for a movie. I couldn't relate to any of them. I don't see why anyone would want to see this in a big screen format because most of the action took place in interiors. The security hearing was perhaps not the best frame for this story.

Oppenheimer himself (if this is an accurate representation) was a huge disappointment to me. I expected that he would have had many profound thoughts on the Bomb. A man who read the Gita in the original should have been a sophisticated philosopher and ethicist. This movie portrayed him as merely confused and doing his duty by a country he loved. To me, it sounded eerily like the responses of the Nazis at the Nuremberg Trials. Only difference being that he FELT bad. I'm not sure what he really thought about anything. I confess I knew little about him so I did not have any reference point to inform my viewing. But a movie about a great man should not need a reference point.

At least I will try to find out more about him.

3.title: Which gets worse, Nolan's films or the hype?
3.content:
People describing this as a masterpeice obviously know nothing of the history of the subject or the science.

The first clue as to the tone of the quality of the film is the scene where someone bursts into the room saying 'they've split the atom' (meaning Hahn & Co). No, they've discovered the process of nuclear fission, the atom was split 6 years earlier by an Englishman and an Irishman, John Cockroft and Ernest Walton. Said person then runs off to another room to replicate the experiment and comes back half an hour later and says 'yeah they were right'. Utterly absurd.

Later, after much bluster and a pointlessly loud soundtrack interrupting the flow of non-science and mainly politics there is one can only describe as a non CGI (yes I know he doesn't do CGI) nuclear explosion of such underwhelming proportions that it would have made Stanley Kubrick blush in 1969.

Most hilarious of all is the scene after this when 'the army' comes along and carts off what is supposed to be 2 complete nuclear devices in crates on the back of trucks to drop over Japan. 'We'll take it from here' says the General. Absurd when you know what actually happened but hey, the film is already 14 hours long.

My misgivings about this film are the same ones I had for Interstellar namely the science is suedo-science, the facts are suedo-facts. That along with the irritating soundtrack, plot gaffs and omissions overcoming any chance of gaining empathy with the characters.

The film is well cast and acted, that is all.

3.title: Not sure why 70MM IMAX was needed for this slugfest?
3.content:
Let's start with the positives:
Main Cast was great - Cillian, Emily, Matt, RDJ were absolutely great and it was good to see Josh Hartnett who is a very under rated actor.


Good screenplay, dialogues, sets of of 1940s.


Negatives:
Absolute slugfest of a story. Hard to believe this was a Nolan's movie. It's waaay too overhyped because of his name. Personally I think he has lost that touch. The story kept flip flopping from characters personal life to the main project then into 2 different hearings at two different timelines. There were no indications of the timelines at all, you just keep floating around in different timelines where all of them look the same pretty much. So it was confusing to keep up. It doesn't talk about the World War in proper context. Doesn't show anything on Hiroshima, just a few mentions of it and that's pretty much it.


-Why did this need 70MM IMAX cameras? 95% of this movie is person to person dialogues in a normal room setting. There's no action sequence of any kind. Only one small explosion scene that lasts like 30 seconds tops. So why is Nolan making all the fuss about taking up all of the IMAX screens. Personally I feel IMAX should've remained for Mission Impossible Dead Reckoning. It was a faaar superior movie for IMAX than this.



Overall, you can wait to stream it when it comes out or can skip it. Not much you're missing out.

3.title: Sadly , NOT what we expected...
3.content: I've got bad news for ya..." Oppenheimer " is not an epic or deep Christopher Nolan film about a controversial figure and an influential moment in human history...nope...it's like your average political drama with Robert Oppenheimer being the protagonist ! ( and Lewis Strauss being the villain lol )...and on the side we got a superficial documentary like style approach towards the whole nuclear weapons thing ...The only thing that adds glamor or makes it a little fancy is Nolan's style of directing and the star studded cast of course...most of them were committed and gave solid performances ...and then you have Gary Oldman who comes in for like two minutes and steals the show lol ...so ,there you have it ...Oppenheimer is super disappointing to say the least...it's a big fancy movie about nothing ...Even comes out as pretentious and trying too hard at times...there's even a scene that I just can't stop thinking about how awkward it must have been to shoot !( you guessed it ,it has Florence Pugh in it lol )...tbh it feels like this was very a personal project for Christopher Nolan...like he read the biography and thought why not make a huge hollywood blockbuster about it !...if you ask me the only reason to watch this movie is probably the fear of missing out that's all ...* sigh *

3.title: A 3-Hour stone-dead movie
3.content:
A 3 hour stone-dead movie. Its about as boring as watching paint dry.

There wold be NO problem to cut the length of the film in half and still have a surplus of material to tell the plot, which would be a blessing for the viewers.

1. The use of ´weird music soundtrack in every scene is a sign that without the dramatic music interest would fade away and the whole movie would fall apart just because its so nonsensical constructed

2. The use of nudity in the most awkward way has just one specific purpose : To awaken the audience and keep them from nodding away. Its so obvious and to my mind never used before in this over--explicit way. You could say its manipulative to just throw in some nudity here and there ...

The cast are all wooden puppets , the saucy love story´´s are beyond ridiculousness , the drama is non existent and the script is bit and pieces back and forth in time. In three hours nothing happen. Weird music soundtrack in every scene leaving nothing left to imagination, and without the music it would be unbearable to watch this disaster of movie with a myriad of stone-faced non descriptive actors . Nolans worst one so far. Greatly disappointing. Grossly overrated.

3.title: Bloated. Boring. Good luck staying awake
3.content:
So this movie is 3 hours long. You know how Director's Cuts include stuff that was edited out of the theatrical version? In this case the Director's Cut needs to remove an hour.

Just for background I studied both Astro and Sub-Nuclear Physics in college, and even I was bored to tears. I looked over at my girlfriend, whose excited idea it was to go and even insisted on paying for the tickets. Yep, she was fast asleep for at least half the movie, and this was the 6pm to 9pm showing, not the past her bed time timeslot.

So much of this movie is just plain unnecessary, like the director was trying to vamp and pad for time, when instead he should've gone crazy w/the digital snips and dumped about half of it. The side thread w/the Commie gf was so inane, it was obvious her only role in the film was as a pair of b**bs, her character was otherwise 98% irrelevant. I think even the director knew there'd have to be some T&A to keep the audience from sleeping all the way through.

Another example of unnecessary padding. Special effects meant to convey how Oppenheimer thought about quantum mechanics and the universe. References to String Theory and other nerd science stuff I'm sure would be lost on 99 out of 100 people watching it. Worse, they don't do this just once, for 30 long seconds, but 3 or 4 times. To quote Cinema Sins. "Movie has time for this?"

RDJ and Cillian Murphy were perfectly cast, as were the myriad of famous Physicists of the early 20th century. Otherwise though this is a story about a man whose one lifetime achievement, incredible as it was, took up 3 years of his life, and what we got was a biopic of that plus 33 more years of his life that's only mildly interesting.

3.title: Boring even with the intense music
3.content:
Nolan has really fallen off in his ability to deliver compelling films.

Perhaps the last legitimately good film he made was Inception, with his best being The Prestige, Memento and The Dark Knight.

Yes people like Interstellar, but even that strays into Shyamalan silliness territory, and also relies heavily on its overbearing booming soundtrack just like Oppenheimer.

Oppenheimer requires subtitles even for native English speakers, as most of the dialogue is so mumbled and inaudible without it, and even more-so with the intense music laid over the top of it, music which is used to try to keep the movie afloat due to it being so boring as it is.

The film isn't bad up until they explode the bomb, but everything after that point (over half of the runtime) had me falling asleep and needing to go back and listen to the dialogue multiple times.

The film is by far Nolan's most pompous and self-aggrandising, like Nolan has come to enjoy the smell of his own farts way too much. But also that the movie feels barely stitched together, and the overbearing non-stop intense music throughout is used as an attempted cure-all for the movie just being very boring, and without even one definitive story beat.

For more compelling movies about the bomb and WW2, watch Barefoot Gen, Dr. Strangelove, Grave of the Fireflies, Letters From Iwo Jima.

3.title: Disappointed
3.content: The acting was amazing, the cinematography was also amazing, but thats where the good ends and the bad starts. 3 hours are you kidding me? This story could have been done in an hour forty-five with credits. There was too much filler garbage i was immediately annoyed. Glorifying the smartest people creating the biggest bomb after the worlds best scientific discovery was sickening. I know that was true, but it made me sick. Showing how twisted and demented our government is was a great idea. There is literally too many things i want to say but don't know how to word them. I highly recommend everyone see something else and save a lot of time. Watch this at home after it hits netflix.

3.title: What a bizarre and shockingly boring experience
3.content: I would've been good money that this was going to be one of the best movies I'd ever watch. But wow. First, the soundtrack plays *constantly* throughout the entire 3 hours. It never stops, and it's very loud, a true assault of the senses. Second, its pacing is crazy-making slow. Even 20 minutes into it, I was thinking 'this has got to get better, right?' Only it never does. The dialog is difficult to hear (largely over the loud music that never stops), and the storyline is not easy to follow. But besides all this, it's just a shockingly boring movie. I'm a big movie fan, and this will go down as one of the worst movies I've ever seen.

3.title: Beyond dull... from what I saw
3.content: I was so excited for this film. We had to walk out after an hour, which felt like two. Every scene was about 20 seconds, you had no time to digest what was happening or why and who any of the smaller characters were. One minute he's in a classroom the, next he's in the desert on a horse. Parties, classroom, back on a horse. WHY!?! It did seem like the film was slowing down when he was recruited for the Manhattan Project but by that point I'd lost all faith in the film. Maybe when it finally hits Netflix or something I'll start it again from where I left but that was one of the worst hours of cinema I've ever witnessed. Even the dialogue felt rushed like they knew it was pointless so they just wanted to get through it. How about just not including it?

3.title: As Men on Film would say...
3.content:
HATED IT!

This film was so convoluted as to be a mess. It was difficult to follow and frankly, boring. If the plot isn't somewhat linear I'm probably going to have trouble with it.

One good thing about it was an ensemble cast that included Robert Downey Jr. , Emily Blunt, and Matt Damen. As a result it is well acted and one of the only things that could keep me mildly interested for 3 bloody hours. Take that away and I would have left 10 minutes in.

The best part of the story came after the bombing of Japan where the powers that be relentlessly crucified him. All because he expressed regret and compassion for all affected.

Just because a movie gets repeated accolades has nothing to do with whether it's good or not.

3.title: Inappropriately loud and fast paced for what should have been a quiet boardroom drama
3.content:
So I'll take the contrarian view here and say Oppenheimer is basically kind of bad. I don't think we'd be seeing these sorts of reviews if the movie was promoted or hyped up less. Very sad but true. I did my best to conceal my serious disappointment while I was at the theatre, didn't want to seem a party pooper. I went to the theater hoping I was going to be watching a genuine revival of Hollywood or something along those lines- that I would lean away from speed, colour, and volume, just a little bit back towards pacing, character, narrative. I understand it is a blockbuster film, I was just hoping the needle would move somewhat in the other direction of the general trend in a film such as this. No such luck.

What we do in fact get is a basically relentless exposition dump scored to the Inception soundtrack. The main character doesn't have much character, the supporting characters don't have enough air to breathe after all the rapid-fire delivery of exposition and information about what's going on to develop personalities of their own on screen, for the most part. The soundtrack is indeed relentless and I began to suspect that it was so constant in order to cover up the fact that there's not really much of any narrative tension in the movie.

If you go watch this in theatres you will find yourself occasionally buffeted by explosive walls of sub-bass at peculiar times (the actual detonation of the bomb is actually one of the quieter explosions in the movie).

I think what bothers me the most is that there is so much budget, so much acting talent, loaded into this movie. And for all the resources allocated to this project, the result is basically uninspiring, emotionally flat, basically attempting to buffet you into having a reaction through momentum. It shouldn't be like this considering the movie's subject matter ie, people talking in labs, boardrooms, over glasses of wine, in lecture halls. It's just not the right way to film this sort of plot.

You've already seen it, I'm sure you liked it, but for me, it's a sore disappointment and shows that Hollywood cannot really do it anymore.

Final gripe: seeing Oppenheimer reclining in his La -Z-Boy in the nude after smoking hot sex is extremely stupid, but also funny. So perhaps not a gripe.

3.title: Not at all what it was cracked up to be
3.content:
I get the drama of this story. However, the movie is convoluted, confusing and vague throughout. This could have easily been done in less than 3 hours with a lot more drama, intent and clarity. It meanders for 3 hours without really creating the intensity of the process and what that process led up to which is the atomic bombing of two cities in Japan and the killing of over 200,000 innocent civilians.

Cillian Murphy, a great actor, I do not believe lives up to it in this movie. Not his fault as I think the movie underwrote his character. He barely does more than sit at tables and makes almost too soft spoken comments. I hung in there for the whole movie but was not rewarded with any insight I did not already have or great and powerful scenes that were moving about a very potentially moving time...

3.title: Didn't find this movie compelling...
3.content:
What's wonderful about art and movies is that it's subjective... I couldn't wait to leave the theater... I just wasn't feeling this movie and I'm sure I'm the one percent... I find Christopher Nolan hit or miss... After you read about the history of Oppenheimer and the atomic bomb, it's a very sad history what followed the Manhattan project for the local people; tragic. Look it up...

Anyways, I felt as though the tone and pitch of the movie was quite shrieking & elevated! The tone of did not change much for the three hours... I personally did not find it compelling nor dynamic. Oh well, that's how I experienced it and I couldn't wait to leave!

I don't know just didn't do it for me... I could think of a lot of better ways to spend three hours of my time for the future... but all movies and art is a gamble, so you never know! That's just my opinion :-)

3.title: disappointing
3.content:
"A Masterpiece?" Not for me. I'm glad I didn't buy it. Years ago I concluded that I should read what the critics say and believe the opposite. The same goes for a highly rated movie. If you are already familiar with the story and history, as I am, you may be able to follow it, but it takes some effort. There is too much jumping back and forth in time, so there is no real chronology, which makes it hard to follow, nor is there continuity. Critics might praise it but they are not looking at it as a general viewer. Rather than portray him as a physicist and tell you how he developed his theories, the film goes more into his private life than necessary. Very little time is devoted to the actual physics side, which would have made it more interesting.

The biggest let-down, as with so many U. S. movies, is the endless, unnecessary background music; mumbling actors; semi-whispered dialogue and at times, irritating foul language.

3.title: He Has Become as Nolan, Destroyer of Narrative Sense
3.content:
This is a bloated, grandiose, pretentious cluster of half-anecdotes and impressions. Nolan whips it and whips it bad. I have read a little about these events but pity the 99.99% of humanity that has not, if they come to Nolan's movie hoping to learn. How would the unschooled have a prayer of understanding these events if their only source is this overpriced Jackson Pollock? Nolan is an obscurantist.

He goes non-linear because it's cool. Deep down, Nolan wants to ride Michael Mann into Tarantinismo, prettified with a veneer of ideas that makes him seem Something Better--than he really is. Nolan already brought in the anti-communist grilling in his unnecessary time skips, so after the big fat dud of the Trinity scene it's anti-climax time. He trudges onward, swinging his whip of exposition over the assembled worthies for another 50 minutes of verbiage.

Cillian Murphy doesn't deserve the praise he's getting, though I salute him for keeping a straight face while reciting Nolan's Cliff Notes. Watching Murphy's stupefied, bedazzled gape you can almost see him calculating: 'I might win an Oscar.' So he'll get rich. Hooray for show-biz.

The music! Horribly overbearing and overbearingly horrible. It sounds like Arvo Part trying to play Motown on a Moog. If it were actually good music of course it would be too distracting and we wouldn't get to hear whatever fragment of an idea the actor bandies about. It drowns out the dialogue and it's electronic tone is anachronistic. No doubt Nolan was trying to make it the sound of prophecy. In the late 40s Hollywood had a period when overbearing symphonic soundtracks were the thing (Portrait of Jennie). It's beyond excessive--an impediment to understanding, more obscurantism. Quite early on I caught myself asking: When is this tedious irrelevant music going to stop? It never did.

So the feature film staggers onward, deeper into artistic irrelevance, consoled by financial accumulating. There is so much hero-worship in movie culture and appreciation. You become a celebrity director like this guy and it gets to be like "The Aristocrats" joke. And you make millions. People will pay good money to worship what ever god happens to be at the top of the charts.

Nolan wants so much to be profound, like a god. But a cluster of artistic flourishes does not profundity make. We have all seen false modesty gushers in red-carpetland. Nolan should try the real thing.

3.title: Tedious and self important.
3.content: It is difficult for me to understand how a movie about such a monumental period in world history could be quite so dull. It's full of endless dialogue that the director trusts so little that he covers it all with bombastic orchestral music. He also has so little trust in the audience's intelligence that to demonstrate that Oppenheimer's mind is in turmoil or indeed to demonstrate the potential power of nuclear fission we are presented with short visual clips of explosions and flashes. The actors, as has become the fashion, whisper their lines in order, presumably, to signify the importance of what they are saying. It doesn't work. It sounds phoney. I've already mentioned the music but when it isn't obliterating the possibly important dialogue it is telling us what to feel. Oh please! And why bother having Emily Blunt in the movie. She's given nothing to work with. There is no connection between Kitty and Oppenheimer in this movie. They don't even look at each other in their scenes together. But perhaps my greatest criticism of this movie is that after three hours I learned nothing of the man or the Manhattan Project. I was just told one more time that America was paranoid about communism in the fifties.

3.title: Subtitles required!
3.content:
Nolan has become synonymous with overdoing the background "tension" music but it was so prominent in this, it's the first time we've actually had to put subtitles on to understand the dialogue.

Ridiculous.

Otherwise It was an engaging and tense telling of a story I knew relatively little about. It's definitely overlong at 3 hours and could easily have been edited down a little. The constant jumping forward and back in time, with little to indicate where in the chronological order the current scene is (other than the grey dye in Cillian Murphy's hair) was a bit tiresome.

Still worth a watch, although I won't be revisiting it in a hurry.

3.title: Brilliant acting but three hours??
3.content: Back and forwards colour then black and white, was confusing . I streamed it but my sound was awful. 3 hours was too long and not enough science. Cillian Murphy was super outstanding. Also some other of my favourite actors were excellent but overall it didn't work for me despite the concept. Cinematography was great. I got bored more than the impressive moments of genius. Not enough of some actors and not enough of others. Despite winning all those awards I would have definitely given Clllian Murphy one and another for Peaky Blinders. Overhyped. Story progression too slow. More historical facts and context would have been better.

3.title: Simply could not make it through..
3.content: The movie had a visceral tense background score throughout overlayed with a string of cliched conversational widgets that completely betrayed any of implied suspense. It was flat out boring.. repetitive period references that ran out of originality before the first hour was up. The bomb scene was disappointing, a fireworks scene to portray what is a truly stunning phenomenon when viewing any number of existing films of actual nuclear bombs. I learned very little about Oppenheimer the person, as I had hoped. By contrast I found Christopher Nolan's other films like Interstellar to be incredible, because the film style matched the 'epicness' of the subject. There was nothing epic or enthralling here..

3.title: Oppenheim-meh
3.content:
After all the hype I was pretty much underwhelmed by this mess of a movie.

Unfortunately Nolan seemed to have forgotten this is a biopic and directed it like it was one of his 'puzzle' movies, like Inception or Memento, or god help us, Tenet.

So, rather than telling us what should have been a fascinating story, he jumps backwards and forwards relentlessly, never give us time to learn much at all.

I think now Nolan's time-hopping gimmick is an attempt to hide that he can't tell a coherent story.

In fact, in 3 hours what do we learn ?

Do we learn why Oppenheimer was anxious all the time? Why his wife was angry and despairing all the time? How he could charm people (utterly absent from Murphy's portrayal)? Why he was chosen to lead the nuclear programme (in spite of his potential communist sympathies) ? Why he accepted the job? What his feelings were about creating the bomb? Whether he was actually a communist?

No. We learn none of the above. What we get is a jumpy string of scenes like an overlong advert.

The sex scene is porn-level ludicrous . The nude scene during the hearing is painfully heavy-handed.

His part was so disjointed I really can't tell if Cillian Murphy played it well or not.

Robert Downey Jr played a great part, but in a boring & inconsequential sub-plot (which actually becomes the main plot)

No one else got much of a look-in

What should have been the significant core of the story - I.e. How they created the bomb - is breezed over. The science is negligible ( I contrast this with how effectively and engagingly the complex science was handled in the TV series 'Chernobyl' ).

The tension leading up to the first detonation is genuinely exciting... but the explosion itself is pitiful. And then without further ado we're back to the boring security clearance hearing.

We're supposed to feel anxiety about the nuclear bomb, but we don't see its effects.

Was Oppenheimer, the man, genuinely such an enigma? Or did Nolan simply make an unnecessarily confused movie?

3.title: Don't do it!
3.content: If you must watch it then wait for streaming at home. Extremely long and boring. One of the worst musical scores in the history of film. The editing was poor. Truly a lame and uninteresting film. Basically as lame as the fact that I have to continue to type words so this review will have enough characters to post. If you must watch it then wait for streaming at home. Extremely long and boring. One of the worst musical scores in the history of film. The editing was poor. Truly a lame and uninteresting film. Basically as lame as the fact that I have to continue to type words so this review will have enough characters to post.

3.title: Long, boring and full of itself
3.content:
Oppenheimer is a story of a flawed protagonist that undergos no redemption arch. He is portrayed as 'above' regular human morality and at no stage shows any remorse for his many horrid acts that span decades of his life.

There are no character throughout the film in which you root for nor empathise with. And some of the direction in this regard is questionable.

Being a biopic it is to be commended that very little has been altered however this doesn't make the movie any more engaging and the few changes that have been made are bizarre choices in my opinion.

Epicly acted and beautifully shot. RDJ is a particular stand out and Damon is as good as ever. As with every Nolan film there is enough art and audio to keep true cinefiles engaged.

But this is the first cinema experience I've had in over a decade where multiple parties walked out. And I also witnessed people sleeping in the last hour.

Somehow even the A-Bomb test is underwhelming. Although the tension in the build up is masterful.

But Oppenheimers biggest crime is feeling so arrogant in its own awesomeness that to dislike it feels as though it's a problem with and that you're wrong. It is pompous. And extremely boring.

I felt every minute of its 3 hour run time.

Oppenheimer would serve as a great mini series or a factual documentary with dramatisation throughout.

But as a standalone film I was far from blown away.

I would give it 1 star except for that being disrespectful to the amazing acting and technological feats throughout.

3.title: Too loud too long too much
3.content:
We have talking, more talking, again talking, then a bomb and then again talking talking talking.

Plus confusing time zone mix-ups, women characters who are next to nothing (kind of a trademark of CN), a soundtrack which is waaaay to much for this kind of biopic, a try to take all of his live into the movie and delivering next to nothing at all, a character study which isn't really one (since you don't know nothing about Oppenheimer by the end and what it did to him on a personal level) and you need to be prepared with his live before the movie otherwise you are missing to much.

So in short: Not his best, not the masterpiece everyone wants it to be and the hype suggest. But please go and see it for yourself.

3.title: Why the needless exploitation?
3.content: I tried to get through this twice but it was too flat. The music was too loud. The acting seemed good, but how can you tell when the story is listless and the dialogue muddled? I found the role of Florence Pugh so gross; I couldn't go on. It was little more than exploitation for shock value. It's offensive. Why take a talented actress and use her as a secks object? It's no wonder she always looks like she's had the life drained from her. I used to admire that Nolan could make good movies without having to resort to the oversaturated use of secks currently in the entertainment industry. But now I've lost all respect for him. I hope they all enjoy the awards. I'm gonna ask God to forgive me for watching it and pray He gives Florence hope and healing and assurance that she's worth more than that.

3.title: Did anyone read the book?
3.content:
Didn't like the flashback style. Didn't like the Murphy, too short, no demanding style, not enough sarcasm, mumbles when he speaks.

Just a chore to watch, I was expecting so much more.

The sex was unnecessary, but she looked nice naked, him no so much! His breakdown was glossed over, it did last much longer than a night behind a rock.

Oppie was a chain smoker, but to be politically correct, lets gloss over that too, an occasional cigarette and a pipe now and then. He had diseased lungs,TB and died from throat cancer.

The Day after Trinity was a superior movie, IMO, I would suggest spending time seeing that.

3.title: Film is mostly hype, won't age well, Nolan sells his soul to get Oscars. He might have lost it. Murphy isn't even that good.
3.content:
I reckon that time will tell that even With the Barbenheimer craze this movie was hyped up, cleaning up in Oscars season and receiving heaps of plaudits and a box office hit this movie, actually wasn't that good.

Sure, it looks beautiful, the backing music is great (still too loud) and has that Nolan energy that always keeps the movie going with quite jump cuts and witty dialogue. But this is his most disappointing work. It's too long and indulgent, played more for the academic awards and film reviewer types rather than the audience, which is not something I'd ever say about a Nolan film, even if they're always long and complex.

Downey jnr and Matt Damon are very good. Cillian Murphy does all the right things, and he's obviously working hard. But his accent, and the way he portays the character it - it's just obvious he's acting to me, which is not good acting.

One other thing to comment on is the completely unnecessary and badly done sex scenes. They jump at you, meant to shock you and sear into your brain, heightening your adrenalin and interest, which I think even makes some people think the film is better than it is. Another thing I respected about Nolan thrown out here. It's nearly evil the way it's done. It sounds crazy but once you see what is being done you can't miss it.

To me this film is an obvious play for awards and greatness, Hollywood loves ww2 and nazis. Oppenheimer isn't even presented as interesting here. Nolan will probably get more free reign to do what he wants now, I hope this is a bump on the road to more great films rather than the decline which hardly any can see.

3.title: Choppy and exhausting to watch
3.content:
"Oppenheimer" took me on a bit of a cinematic rollercoaster. The editing style felt like an unending trailer, which, frankly, left me a tad weary. I was hopeful for strong character connections, but unfortunately, the film fell short in the depth department. The storytelling approach chosen for the main character was, to put it mildly, peculiar. It aimed for profoundness, but the narrative barely scratched the surface.

As I settled into the film, I found myself yearning for more substance and a smoother narrative flow. The characters lacked the development needed to truly engage the audience, and the odd storytelling choices left me a bit perplexed. While "Oppenheimer" had moments of potential, it ultimately failed to deliver the cohesive and immersive experience I had hoped for. I left the viewing experience with a sense of unfulfillment, craving a deeper connection to the characters and a more seamless storytelling rhythm. In the end, the film's ambitions fell short, leaving me with a desire for more substance and a smoother cinematic journey.

3.title: Mishmash of film
3.content:
Technically the sound quality of dialogue was terrible!

The film then is bit of a mishmash of bits of quantum physics politics and the man himself and mainly whether he is a communist or not driven by the paranoia of the time.

The man did not get the appreciation he deserved the film didn't show this really. The bits of quantum physics did not explain properly why they suddenly announced that Germany had gone down the wrong path to a bomb. They also could have included the near catastrophic episode by putting to much fissile material together.

Also the spies weren't totally shown up until the end. I think they did try but failed somewhat on how much back stabbing went on with physicists.

Why it got all these awards is beyond me it's not a film I would rush to watch again.

3.title: A lot of buzz for nothing...
3.content:
At best, the film is average, falling into the non-lineal narrative, filled with flashbacks and flash-forwards, only to say nothing... except for Strauss "misunderstanding" Oppenheimer's chat with Einstein!

And all that plot intercut with all of those unneeded images of stars and explosions!

And talking of explosions, the Trinity was disappointing: the build up was overexaggerated, and plenty of physics gibberish, only to show a regular (not to say, insignificant) blast, someone did with some fuel, on their backyard.

The acting was overall "fine", despite the feeling of Emily Blunt's and Florence Pugh's typecasting: the former as the unmotherly alcoholic (the "Quiet Place" saga and "The girl on the train"), and the latter as the psychologically unstable scorned girlfriend ("Midsommar" and "Don't worry darling"). Also, Cyllian Murphy only has one facial expression through out the film, thus making it hard to feel anything with the title character.

At least, it was pleasing to see Tom Conty as Einstein, and Gary Oldman as Truman, as their performances were great... even if it was for a couple of seconds!

Not my cup of tea, but the film can be entertaining on the telly.

3.title: Big disappointment
3.content:
The good: excellent performances by Murphy, Damon and especially Downey. A couple of powerful scenes, especially of the first test of the atom bomb - literally mind blowing .

The bad: disjointed and confusing storytelling. Characters are plopped in and we have no idea who they are or their significance. Bombastic score that never lets up. At 3 hours way overlong.

I was so looking forward to seeing this film, especially after the critical huzzahs for it and I'm a fan of all the talent involved. Well, folks, we've been misled by the critics yet again. Quite a few walkouts at the screening that I attended.

3.title: Talk... Talk... And more talk....
3.content:
I love Nolan but with this disaster? Why so much chatter and so many characters introduced and it's like a brainstorming for the audience to keep up with the memorization of names. In the end I could only remember a couple of names the rest was washed down the drain. Murphy did really well as did Downing Jr. So many big names in the movie doesn't make the movie great. Brilliant performance by all the actors. My only gripe is the storyline, it doesn't borde well with me. This movie should have been a documentary instead. It had a boring storyline to begin with. It was only because of Nolan's skills that made the movie how it is now.

Sorry this movie is not a movie, it's more like a 3 hours documentary.

3.title: Endurance
3.content:
There's some films I've appreciated, if not enjoyed, that are similar, Enigma, Beautiful Mind, Imitation Game, but this is a real endurance test. 3 hours long is an hour too long, in my view. The story is told well, but it's just too much. Less is definitely more at times in filmmaking.

As for the film itself, the music is horrifically intrusive, the back and forth story telling was arty for arty sake and didn't add anything much. It's certainly a story that needs telling, but this didn't honour the story, in my view. As for the film being best movie, often the best movie seems to be given to a film that professional critics like, but I wonder if ordinary film watchers are taken into consideration?

A director's cut is needed, to shorten it and lose the black and white political scenes and change the music. Then I'd give it a much better rating.

3.title: Thermonuclear fart
3.content: I was expecting an interesting and exciting story from Nolan, I was looking forward to the release of the film, but in the end I was disappointed. From the very beginning, instead of a strong story, a patchwork quilt of multi-colored patches awaited me. The director jumped through the chronology, without in any way indicating the transitions between various episodes of Oppenheimer's life, which gave the feeling that you were watching the creation of a drug addict who had caught the onset. Yes, the actors are great, but watching them is boring. Yes, the event is epoch-making, but in the film it is depicted with a loud fart. This is not a movie, but a salad into which the creator puked while stirring and served it to loyal fans under the guise of a gourmet dish. The fans are delighted, covered in mud and demanding more. The rest of the audience stifles a yawn, is bored and perplexed. After this film I completely lost faith in Nolan. Let him continue to make his "masterpieces". I'm no longer interested in him as a director.

3.title: I don't get the hype.
3.content:
I really cannot see the appeal of this movie. Sure it's an important history lesson and the quality of cast cannot be criticized.

However the vision of the movie, the presentation, is all wrong.

It is presented to us like an extended trailer, with dramatic music playing throughout the dialogue.

This is off putting to say the least as we struggle to hear the conversations. Dialogue to music balance is way off. Music too loud, dialogue too soft.

Sorry guys, it's boring.

This should have been so much better than it is. Everything is wrong, but my biggest complaint is the music constantly played over dialogue.

3.title: Huge dissappointment
3.content: This movie really sucks. Script, dialoges, editing, directing, music, everything but the acting for which I gave the three stars. It's like watching a 3-hour trailer that makes no sence, full of pointless supposedly smart sayings, and jump scare loud sounds. Time was in the quantum realm, never really knowing when each scene took place, in which I really wondered what did I miss to interpret the punch line.. I really wonder how it passed production after editing. I hope Christopher Nolan comes back with Sci-fi action film, where he seems to thrive. Best part was Albert Einstein who looked like a 1800's Ottoman pasha.

3.title: No subtlety, no empathy, far too long
3.content:
Christopher Nolan continues to make films in which the characters evoke no empathy. The form is elaborate, with hysterical editing that chops up scenes from different periods in the life of Cillian Murphy (who plays the character whose surname gives the film its title) in staccato mode: the film is practically a permanent sequence montage.

We get the impression that it was designed to be unviewable on an iPhone. Which in itself is commendable. And we also have the feeling that this 3-hours film is just the cinema version of a TV series of, say, ten one-hour episodes. This format would be more appropriate to tell such a story.

The film covers a small part of American history, where Communists, Nazis, Americans and Europeans live side by side. The film seems to want to denounce many things, but fails to be credible on any of them: the creation of the atomic bomb, its use for attack, its use for deterrence (the passages where the characters discuss these aspects are the most interesting), the persecution of communists, the hysteria of McCarthyism, the corruption of politicians.

The film indicates that it was a project and a collective of scientists who created the bomb, and not Oppenheimer, known as the father of the atomic bomb. Which is commendable.

The character of his wife, played by Emily Blunt, is non-existent and contributes nothing.

3.title: Here to tell you the truth because nobody seems to
3.content:
Even though this film is about developing the atomic bomb, the only thing bombastic about this movie is the lack of substance for a 3 hour sit.

Throughout the movie you'll hear suspenseful music that leads only to anti-climaxes. The dialogues were mediocre at best. Visually, this movie has nothing to offer. (The moment you see the atomic bomb explode in a test you see the faces of the actors instead of the bomb, extremely disappointing after watching minutes of counting down to that moment, and hours before the countdown starts)

As far as Nolan goes, as usual the movie is unnecessary complicated. Skipping through time with flashbacks had no place it this film. It could have easily been told chronologically. But, like I said, there wasn't enough of a story to begin with.

Making you feel like there is any substance, comes from skipping through time and suspenseful music. Though this film probably tries to portray an image of a man who morally questions his own invention, it was too much of another war criminal glorification to me. If I had to describe all of it I would say: too American.

Another movie about communists and corrupt informal lawsuits.

This is definitely one to skip. Could have been a movie made for cable tv broadcasted on a weekday.

The stars are for the actors who had to carry this monstrosity. Plus, as a Dutchie I'm also getting quit tired of filmmakers making the same mistakes over and over again. Confusing the German language for the Dutch language.

Minor details, but if you are going to spend millions on making a movie, get your facts straight.

3.title: Boring long movie with no action Do not believe the10 star reviews.
3.content:
Boring long movie with no action. Actors whisper for no reason. Lots un-interesting controversy among the scientists. If you do not know the story of how the war against Japan in WW2 was won then it may be interesting. Although, I have seen better and more gripping documentaries re-enacting this subject. They do not show the problems of their project. And the final act does not include the one thing that the thousands of people in WW2 were working to do. I think Nolan is living on his past reputation from his Batman movies. At three hours it is tedious for teenagers or anyone who likes action movies to watch.

Whoever is making fake 9 and 10 star reviews should be ashamed of themselves.

3.title: Boring, too long, confusing and too loud.
3.content:
Boring, too long, confusing and too loud. I was looking forward to this but it's such a mess. How could you make a film about developing the first atom bomb and not only make it so boring but set the bomb off with an hour still to go.

The story with its confusing and pointless non linear telling along with incredibly loud music where none was needed make it a complete mess.

Acting is ok but nothing special and some characters seem to be there because people have heard of them, like Einstein but add nothing to the story.

And I'm not being prurient when I say that Oppenheimer's mistress with her kit off was about the best thing in the whole film .

3.title: Possibly the most 2 plus boring hours...
3.content:
I was looking forward to this..... but my goodness, what a long drawn out boring load of old tosh... the characters are pretty well drawn, but it's all so so dull... The diminutive lead man, tiny as he is, just doesn't fit the suits he's dressed in nor the part.

He just never really seems to own the character like he did in PB..... some of the most boring parts are the small room long drawn out scenes with boring dialogue.. is this a documentary best suited to Netflix or a drama based on historical record, a record that seems to be the most boring hearings ever recorded, and recreated semi verbatim....... all in all a huge let down.

3.title: Lot of internal US politics than science
3.content: I was expecting something like Interstellar, but not 15 minutes of Quantum Mechanics, Nuclear Physics, or any sort of Physics throughout the entire 180 minutes of the film. Instead, there were lots of internal politics and spying investigations of the US Government at that time. As I am not North American, I couldn't relate to all these backstories regarding what went wrong with Oppenheimer back then. I will surely accept that it was my mistake not to check the genre of the movie. Apart from that, I didn't like the usage of the Sri Bhagavad Gita in the movie. They could have shown him reading it in the lab or something. Also, when Jean Tatlock asks him 2nd time to speak Sanskrit script, again Murphy just translated it.

3.title: A poor attempt at filmmaking
3.content:
The main issue I have with this film is that it fails to resonate emotionally. I am non sympathetic to Oppenheimer past his development of the bomb. I think everything else is window dressing and quite frankly, ultimately proved boring. There's nothing at stake - it would've been better had Nolan made this into a documentary.

You know a film is bad when the story is so thin that the director manipulates the canvas to add "texture" to an otherwise mundane story. I think the screenplay is very poorly written as it fails to connect emotionally with its audience. Both attempts result in a poor showing.

Lastly, I think Oppenheimer's love life, though pertinent to his character presentation, leaves little to be desired and alienates us with gratuitous sex for sex sake.

Nolan missed the mark and Oppenheimer is unworthy of a Best Picture nomination, let alone, Academy Award.

3.title: Didn't expect this low from Nolan
3.content:
This was so bad.

To the point: Didn't you guys had a historian on the team?

What is going on with "Pity russians" we didn't shared the nuclear schematics with them, didn't you know Russians were allies with Nazi Germany??? Didn't you know they held a German-Soviet military parade in Brest-Litovsk on 22 of september 1939??? And then in 1941 in Moscow???

The script is so bad, most of the actors barely acting.

What a dissapointment. Romance line was laughable. She just showed arabic language words to him and got horny? From whom did this assomption comes from?

There are so many better autobiography documentaries out there, like: A beautifull mind; The immitation game; even Hawking: Can You Hear Me?.

This was so bad and inaccurate, "sucked out of thumb", bad play, bad script. The worst autobiography documentary i ever watched, didn't expect this low from Kristopher Nolaner watched, didn't expect this low from Kristopher Nolan.

Also we heard this compositions many times already.

3.title: BORRRRING!
3.content: The science was interesting, but as soon as the topic switched to ninety five percent politics, five percent science, (about an hour in), I was fully checked out. I could not care any less about what happens in this story beyond 1:45:00, when I switched it off, because I couldn't tolerate another second of listening to a bunch of self important men winge on and on about why everyone else was wrong and they were right. This movie could have been about half its duration and been more succinct and to the point. This movie is the most "beating a dead horse" movie I've ever had the displeasure of seeing.

3.title: Oppenheimer is A bomb
3.content: Awful. Nolan is LOST. 2 hours and 40 minutes of meaningless dialogue, abrupt cutaways, nameless, empty characters and 20 minutes of real movie making/story telling. Robert Oppenheimer is an interesting, impactful figure in history, but clearly not worthy of a movie about his life if this is what we get. I cannot believe a master like Nolan can take such a juicy subject and turn it into the most tedious endurance tests one will ever face in a movie theatre. If you're interested in the Manhattan project you'll get a glimpse of it. If you're interested in seeing a two and a half hour interrogation into whether or not Robert Oppenheimer had communist ties whooo boy are you in for a treat. Cillian Murphy was fine. Nolan needs to find himself ASAP.

3.title: Don't waste your money don't believe the hype
3.content:
The only reason I saw this movie is because I belong to a movie club.

I didn't want to see this movie because of Christopher Nolan. I hate his movies (except Batman).

I walked out of this movie with 30 minutes left. It's a 3 hour movie that drags and drags and drags near the end.

There were so many scientists and characters I couldn't keep them straight.

The inquisition by the Senate dragged and dragged and dragged.

Did I mention I hate Christopher Nolan movies?

The music score was horrible. I couldn't understand the dialogue between characters because the music was so distracting and when it crescendo'd, I couldn't hear what was being said.

Did I mention I hate Christopher nolan movies?

Did I mention the movie is 3 hours long? If it's a fast paced 3 hour movie and I don't "feel" the time length, I'm alright with it. Sometimes you go into a movie and you're so engaged you don't notice the time. But I kept looking at my watch at the 2:30 point. And then I had to leave.

The only reason I'm giving it 3 stars is because of Emily Blunt. She was the only character I cared about.

Wait for this movie to come on streaming. I wish I had seen the Barbie movie instead.

3.title: A great story told, unfortunately, in a not so great manner...
3.content:
The story of J. Robert Oppenheimer is one for the ages. Unfortunately, the filmmakers here seem to make choices that interfere with the aesthetic experience. To begin with, the balance between the various elements of the soundtrack are way out of whack. The spoken dialogue is usually kept at a dim low level, and is frequently drowned out by the music score and other background sounds. Secondly, I find the constantly shifting timelines annoying and not helpful for viewer comprehension.

Further, the constant shifting between black/white and color, while at times interesting, ultimately contributes to the discombobulated effect of the film. On the plus side, I found the acting to be very good, especially Matt Damon as General Groves. To those interested, I would suggest checking out other films/books on the topic.

3.title: Not good
3.content: I really wonder if some other unknown producer made it, it would've gotten the same praise as now, people knowing it was a Nolan's production. The subject seems very interesting, but it falls very short. The visuals are great, but for example I don't understand the black white theme going on every now and then, seemed unnecessary to the story. And there were more things like that, that seemed made to impress but did not make sense or add to the story. Also the music is so annoying, it's a constant in the background of ALMOST EVERY dialogue, who does that. I want to focus on the dialogue, but it was there in almost every scene. Storytelling wise it just could not captivate me, it was a lot of back an forth, which made it a bit chaotic. It just was not done well. I felt it tried to hard to impress with the chaotic music, the flashy back and forth, the visuals that the actual storytelling was supressed. Even Cillian could not save it, the actors were all great btw.

3.title: Historical Drivel...
3.content: Went on and on and on and on...poor story telling. Tedious to watch. Better movies out there that tell the story better. No continuity. Struggled to stay awake throughout the ordeal. The old Hollywood is gone. No writers anymore apparently. Sad that movie making has come to this. The only part of the movie worth watching is the cinematography. It is visually striking. Other than that it isn't worth the time. The acting is ok. Nothing special. Sad to see so many reviews stating that this is an award winning film. It is not that in so many ways. Use your time wisely and not bother with this film.

3.title: Booooooring!!!!
3.content: The movie left me with mixed feelings as it attempted to explore the theme of regret and redemption. While the star-studded cast was impressive, it wasn't enough to salvage the film's weak execution. The plot felt disconnected from the intended message, leading to a lack of engagement. Additionally, the movie suffered from being overly long, with some scenes dragging on and loud, distracting elements. Regrettably, the film relied too heavily on the fame of its cast, neglecting to invest in a compelling story or well-developed characters. As a result, it failed to captivate and left me feeling disappointed.

3.title: Bait and Switch
3.content:
With the film being available in IMAX and 70 mm formats, there is a promise of large-scale action of some sort. Instead, most of the activity occurs in small rooms, with the most expansive scenes being some of he New Mexico desert.

There are too many characters, as Oppenheimer is shown starting from his student days. I can accept the scientists he meets only once, as they are introduced and can be forgotten. However, people like the scientists on his team tend to blur, as they are not given enough screen time each, nor played by big enough stars to meld their faces and characters.

At 3 hours, this is a long film. However, the main theme running thru it is a rival scientist who felt humiliated by Oppenheimer, and got revenge by later denying him a continuation of his security clearance, and destroying his reputation. As the U. S. moved into a "red scare" period after the Soviet Union detonated its 1st atomic bomb, Oppenheimer's humanism was used against him - his earlier social justice associations with American Communists, and his pacifism after he developed the bomb. The film would have been a lot better if this was greatly abbreviated or eliminated.

3.title: One Time watch on OTT
3.content:
The trailer and promotions of the movie seem to be about Manhattan project but on contrary it has too many sub plots pre and post Manhattan project. The political drama aspect explored in the movie remain very superficial and don't really grip the viewer.

The viewer need to have knowledge of the political environment of 1950s in the USA. The movie doesn't give background before describing the events that occur during McCarthy era.

There was also not much in the movie for big screens and iMax. The movie is more an abstract autobiography of Dr Oppenheimer.

It is one time watch movie on the OTT and fell short of movies associated with Christopher Nolan.

3.title: Overly edited, too many scenes, music too loud, poor narrative
3.content:
I am shocked that this film has received so much positive attention; perhaps the hype raised my expectations too high, but urghhh.

I seriously worry that either the audiences have become dumber, or the review and promotion system has become corrupted; I expect the latter, perhaps through AI?

As a filmmaker myself, I echo the other critical reviews that for me, make this film almost unwatchable.

Way too many scenes, with inaudible dialogue, and unnecessarily dominant music; distractingly dominant music. Chaotic storyline.

God knows how much money was wasted upon the endless filming setups that didn't contribute to the story.
