The fundamental filmmaking rule is to create a simple strong narrative that the audience can follow, then ensure the audio is clear, and then finally create some nice cinematography (not essential with a film like this). This definitely didn't happen.

This is probably not a review, it's therapy for audiences that are questioning if there is something wrong with them that they didn't enjoy Oppenheimer; don't worry you are not wrong.

...also, never before have I noticed bad make-up... immediately saw this on the opening scene, should have turned off then.

3.title: Eight point five question mark exclamation mark
3.content:
I can't believe this movie scored an 8.5! More like 5.8. The producers and distributors must have paid people to vote as high as they did.

This movie scored and 8.5? How?! 4 would be plenty. So bad. I cannot believe this movie scored an 8.5. Hello? Are you hearing me? 8.5! This movie. You must be joking.

3.title: Nolan's worst film by far.
3.content:
Pathetic jump scares. Unnecessary nudity. An hour too long.

I have nothing against jump scares and nudity - I just don't see the relevance.

The first twenty minutes or so the film jumps around abruptly, some parts in black and white, and I thought it was gonna be awful.

It was okay for about an hour after that. After we're done with anything bomb related the film turns back into a boring mess of timeline jumping and poor acting. Metaphors of guilt, and grandiose expressions.

The "nuclear" explosion looks nothing like a real one. Also, he's put a lot of nudity and jump scares in it, so I can only imagine he must've known how boring it was.

3.title: Don't believe the hype
3.content:
Aside from the sound design which was good, nothing here was really revolutionary. The mere length and drawn out dialogue made this film a snooze fest; the last time I wanted to leave the theater or just close my eyes was at the showing of the latest Matrix.

Additionally, complex details of insignificance and multiple characters/ name dropping make it hard to follow for the average viewer unless you are already well versed on the backstory.

Lastly, many scenes, in particular of the non-PG variety could have been cut out as they did not add to the story and wasted time.

I would not suggest going out of your way to see this film. With 3 hours of a viewer's attention, you should walk away with something.

3.title: Oppenheimer
3.content:
Those who enjoy abstract art, or cubism, would probably digest Oppenheimer better than I did. For me watching the film was like listening to disjointed techno music and bagpipes, or an orchestra playing Chopin and Beethoven at the same time, and never really hearing a clear note. As always Christopher Nolan doesn't disappoint in the set design department. It is a feast for the eyes. The scope of the film and the generosity of detail and movement in every scene is breathtaking. The use of sound and silence from Oppenheimer's perspective was also very impacting. But as with so many films I've seen in recent years, the rhythm and momentum of the story gets blown to pieces and undermined by clever juxtaposition of events and an overly splintered timeline. Watching the characters' interactions, particularly those between Oppenheimer and his paramours, felt like picking on an overcooked chicken thigh that barely has any flesh on the bone. I felt that as a viewer I was clinging on to the will to watch just for the sake of seeing what all the fuss was about.

The saving grace for me was Matt Damon's performance. He was a breath of fresh honest air and his character was the only part of the film that I found convincing in my gut.

RDj is disappointing - Emily Blunt is disturbing.

Casey Affleck played his part with eerie precision but i found his interrogation scene took up way too much time. Almost every scene, besides the bomb test, had me checking my watch to see how long it was still going to go.

And this may well be a fault of mine, a failure on my part to appreciate 'love' scenes, but Florence Pugh was completely wasted on this role. The nudity is completely uncalled for in my opinion and it undermined the credibility of her part. I felt nothing for her and her reappearances throughout the film seemed to bother me rather than add value to the story. I feel like much of the story was left out, as preposterous as that sounds given the inhumane length of the film as it is.

I'm left feeling no richer.

But it's still 100% better than Barbie.

3.title: Disappointing
3.content:
Whoever was responsible for the commercials and promoting the movie needs a raise, awards, promotions, etc.

It was so enticing, movie looked great and was looking forward to watching a quality movie Nope Propaganda Watched a movie full of Government propaganda and it is glorified in this movie. Communism/Marxism. Corruption. Glorified

Obviously don't know the truth about American history (being re written all of the time......) and Los Alamos. Will this movie supply the truth or juat add more questions? Definitely more questions

The big name actors are out in full force.

Going to go back to watching Bluey.

3.title: A Big Hollywood Dud!
3.content:
"Oppenheimer" is in the tradition of Hollywood history films that struggle mightily in building a drama around a central historical figure, but fail to present the truth about a significant moment in history.

In attempting to piece together the complex life of J. Robert Oppenheimer, the filmmakers relied on cameo performances of star actors that bore no resemblance to the real people. Pull up a photo of the obsese Leslie Groves and see if it has the slightest resemblance to Matt Damon.

There was also a sleazy element to the film in the depiction of Oppenheimer's love life. The over-the-top inquisitors grilling Oppenheimer in government committees were also unconvincing. The harassment against him was trivialized in the film with the focus on Lewis Strauss as Oppenheimer's oppressor. The film unsuccessfully conveyed the climate of the McCarthy era.

Murray's performance was a standout. But the Sam Waterston version from the 1980s is in many ways a superior biographical portrayal.

Kai Bird, the author of "American Prometheus" was involved in the screenplay of "Oppenheimer." But it is all too apparent in the production that book was better than the film.

3.title: Trash
3.content:
This movie for the most part was trash. It's basically 3 hour long trailer, with around 4 or 5 timelines happening simultaneously. Why do I say trailer? Because it has the feeling of mish-mashed shots. It's not, really, but feels that way. For the most part, cinematography is good, with some very creative choices I thought were great. On the flip side, there were some conversations with some of the worst cinematography I've ever seen. I was shocked it was approved from someone like Nolan, who historically has excellent cinematography. Not in this case.

Pretty much the entire movie is basically "I generally understand what is happening in this current scene". There's no investment in the characters. The fast-paced trailer-like style is awful, and this movie makes it obvious why this style of editing should never be used for movies. Someone like Nolan should have known better.

Of course, Nolan's notorious audio issues plague this movie as well. I don't need to go there because most folks already know those issues. Nolan, turn your darn volume up. No, everyone isn't wrong, you are wrong.

+3 stars for the fantastic applauding scene.

-7 stars for pretty much everything else about the movie.

3.title: Oppie's 600lb Tumor
3.content: Oliver Stone is calling this a "Classic"? He's right. When I fell for the rope-a-dope of this oversold, overbaked ham, I became $22 poorer and endured 3 hours of wiki-level storytelling, silly "drama-inducing" time jumps, a ridiculously unrealistic Gen. Leslie Groves, made up stories (the poisoned apple, the Einstein conversation), and a pain inducing, punctuated-moment volume level employed as a snore prevention mechanism. My theater's audience was like a zombie convention. No one moved. No one laughed. When I walked outside to the freedom of the early evening sun I did laugh as I exclaimed "They got me! Classic." To be fair though, the popcorn was top notch. It's sad that Hollywood is so desperate to duplicate the "only in theaters" modus to success demonstrated by last year's Top Gun Maverick that they'll use every trick in the book to get us in there. When they have to sell it as the heaviest roll of film ever made "it's a 600lb IMAX reel!!!", you know the movie has some real problems. Halfway through, I begrudgingly admitted to my wife that we should have seen "Barbie", and rented this. I wish we had. Now I'm shock-deaf in my left ear, have a popcorn tummy ache, an empty wallet, and I didn't even earn any brownie points. Seriously, if I had been kidnapped by aliens and "lost" 3 hours, I would still have more to talk about.

3.title: It's just so boring...
3.content:
If you are a physicist or maybe a student of history then yeah this is phenomenal. I can't see how most people would find any interest in this. It's so exhaustingingly boring. Just Physics and Communism over and over and over. They threw in some nudity to spice it up.

Don't get me wrong, the actors are great, cinematography, direction, and all the things needed to make a great move are excellent, it's just not an enthralling story.

It took me a week to watch this thing all the way through because there is just nothing happening at all and it was moving me to sleep every time I tried to watch it. Good luck.

3.title: Disappointed
3.content: I was so excited to watch Oppenheimer. I didn't believe the many reviews on here that said it was boring. Glad I didn't pay to watch in the theatre because I surely would have fallen asleep. I've liked all the other Christopher Nolan films I've seen. This film is slooow. The dialog is often in hushed tones that were hard for me to hear without cranking up the volume. Then the music and special effects would be thunderously loud. I notice this in a lot of modern movies and it makes me crazy. I wish the sound people would do better. I didn't care about any of the characters. Maybe if it had been edited down to a normal 2 hr movie it would have been better. I'm surprised it won best picture and director Oscars, but awards have become a bit of a sham imo.

3.title: Nolan does a movie for critics/awards voters
3.content:
If you think this is Nolan's best movie or even "at the same level" than his best movies... then you actually don't like Nolan. At all.

Yes, this biopic has his style, but no matter how complex Nolan tries to make this... in the end it's just a biopic and nothing can ever change that.

Good for him if this was intentional, to get into good graces with the critics, maybe even win some awards that he should've won with Prestige, Inception, TDK or Tenet.

But this is a (mostly) boring biopic (with two or three 5/10 minutes good sequences and a great 15' ending)... but in 3 freaking hours, and for people that can't and won't accept his big, fun, entertaining movies are also intellectually superior, as they won't ever accept a popular thing can be also smart.

3.title: Yawn-inducing and disorganized film that is also heavily dialogued
3.content:
The cover of the movie -- charismatic protagonist surrounded by atomic bomb effects -- looks intriguing and powerful enough to attract a wide range of audience from fans of Nolan to people who are interested in finding out about Oppenheimer and his biography.

However, the majority of elements the movie provides are sadly yawn-inducing dialogues, constant time skips, and a huge chunk of political and nudity when it had so much potential to show off the invention of atomic bomb in details within 3 hours, especially the talented cast they had.

The Nolan movies tend to start slow and take off dramatically with an amazing sound and cinematic scenes at the climax, but that was overshadowed by rushed exposition and unclear character developments along with a number of scenes thrown in a complete shambles.

I do not recommend this movie to audiences who do not have patience to listen to fast-paced dialogue because if you don't enjoy such a type of movie, your expectation will not be met even at the climax.

3.title: Two Years too early to use the AI dilemma as a modern metaphor
3.content:
This Movie is overrated. Yes, the Cast is Top notch. Yes, the Score and the visuals are good.

But the rest? This is basically House of Cards, the Movie. And i mean the bad, boring aspects of it, the political intricacies. I went to see the Movie for the technical aspects, the making of the Bomb. The Morale implications, which has so many parallels to todays AI dilemma: If we don't develop it, potential Bad actors will, and they will use it against us. Instead of focussing on that, we get to see a political trial that obviously is rigged- We all know it, the chatacters know it, yet we spend 2/3 the time of the Moving on it. This is insanely boring, as we know the outcome early on.

Imagine this movie made 2 Years in the Future: This could have been part Biopic, part Statement around the current AI dilemma: If we don't continue development, bad actors will. If the A Bomb was the defining development of last century, AI is the one of the current one. What a perfect metaphor this one could have been, had it been done a bit later. That's what bums me the most about it.

Like it stands however: In the end, movies should Entertain. Ideally, while educating us a bit. This movie does educate- but it fails to Entertain.

3.title: Pointless & bad movie with a terrible script
3.content:
This is objectively a bad movie. Here are the reasons
Oppenheimer was good administrator with enough physics knowledge to be able to bring the theoretical and experimental physicist together, but they don't bother to explain this in the movie
In fact, most decisions are simply listed without explanation, like if you just make a movie of lists of things that happened, you would have a movie
Then the script is mostly made up of famous things famous people said thrown in at random times, often in non-sensical ways
Then of course, Nolan has to tell his movies in a non-linear fashion despite it adding nothing to the story telling
Even though he adds the hearings into Oppenheimer's security clearance throughout the movie, he still wastes 30 minutes on it at the end only to moralise about something irrelevant rather than address the reality of what happened


Bad movie, don't watch. Pretty much all people get from the movie is the emotional beat from the Nolan overpowering soundtrack. Every commentary on the movie reflects on how stupid the movie is.

3.title: Not great.
3.content:
I missed this at the cinema & have had to rent it on Amazon Prime.

You know those times when you're watching a movie & you keep drifting off to sleep? I'm not drifting off to sleep but I still have that feeling.

I'm glad I didn't pay to watch it at the cinema and somewhat irritated that I had to pay $6.99 AUD to watch it on Prime.

3.title: I expected much more
3.content:
I have seen a number of documentaries and at least one other movie about this period of history and to be honest I expected much more from this movie.

This movie is about the man and his idiosyncrasies and not about what was being achieved. To be honest, you could describe the man in five minutes and I will never get back the rest of the time I invested in this movie.

Watching the movie, I felt like I was watching a mashup on youtube as it missed the concept of story telling (IMO). But this movie found many ways of saying the same thing countless times (keeping count would have benefited from me staying awake).

I only watched it once and fell asleep about 20 minutes in and after being nudged I then found it hard to maintain any level of interest in the movie. I'll watch it again when it comes out on a streaming service, just in case I missed to point the director was trying to make, however this time I will make sure I had a strong coffee before hand and not watch the movie after dinner.

3.title: The wrong genre for Nolan's cinematic storytelling
3.content:
The movie was too long and there were too many characters introduced. Also, the story was not told in a linear fashion, so you didn't always know what was happening. The last third and parts of the first third of the film were not really necessary. I had expected more.

Acting was also rather poor, because the backgrounds of the other characters were not told, because everything was focused only on the main character Oppenheimer. So it was an impressive ensemble of actors, but all actors remained very pale in their roles. The supporting characters could have just as easily been cast by no-name actors. Cillian Murphy in the leading role was good, but not Oscar worthy.

The camera wasn't good either, as there was too much focus on close-ups and too few white-angle shots.

I didn't like the picture either. It was too dark and colors were barely shown.

The best thing about the film was the soundtrack. It was very well nuanced and in tune with the film.

In general, it can be said that biopics are not Nolan's genre. Spielberg (Schindler's List) and Scorsese (Aviator) can do that worlds better. Moreover, there are already excellent documentaries and books on the Manhattan Project.

3.title: a snoozefest
3.content: Many people have mentioned some shortcomings such as no mention of the Trinity downwind sufferers who got cancer from this, no showing of The local workers involved they don't even appear on the screen, it's all white faces, and of course no perspective of the Japanese who were slaughtered innocent people who were slaughtered, Oppenheimer was no hero!, for what it's worth I'm sure it has been demonstrated clearly that the bombs didn't have to be dropped despite all those who say it ended the war the war had already really ended, look it up!, don't just read the history of the victors, also the story jumps around way too much, it's like who's who of atomic energy and quantum physics but so what, a snoozefest to be sure, why all the hoodoo?

3.title: Nolan disappointed, in a hopeless attempt to make a historical film, and not another of his fantasies.
3.content:
It was supposed to be a film about science and characters, mentality, quite consistently and monolithically telling the life story of an outstanding person and his immediate environment, as far as possible, with its gradual interweaving into the largest scientific project of mankind of that time.

But the fabric of the film turned out to be lightweight and at the same time pointlessly confusing, with short dialogues and picks (albeit quite entertaining, especially considering how America has gone to the left by 2023), leading essentially nowhere, with a small set of deep thoughts and subtext. There would be too much emotional stress and self-flagellation on the public for what they have done, forgetting about the main thing along the way. Too little space was devoted to attempts to rationalize terrible decisions. There was also a lack of confrontation and discussion within the team.

The autobiographical film did not work out - the key time of growing up and maturation of the main character was completely rejected. It was necessary to call it something else, like the Manhattan Project or something like that, because... Oppenheimer himself is revealed here extremely superficially as a person.

The sex scenes were completely unnecessary. The cast of actors was almost annoying because the same faces kept becoming familiar, except for the main character. The director and casting team did not have the courage to find new actors, as was once the case in Hollywood.

The director and screenwriter clearly could not resist from pure fantasy during the course of the film, especially towards the end, forgetting that this is not another fantastic creation where they can manipulate reality as they wish...

3.title: Boring
3.content:
Love the story but terribly directed and this story was all over the place.

I did not care for some of the acting as it was too melodramatic and pretentious.

Robert Downey Jr should not have been cast in this movie. He was not credible and extremely boring.

The worst part was the interrogation of Oppenheimer and the incredible pretentious portrayal of his Nazi association. It was representative of the current President administration of Biden and his weaponized of the DOJ. Which, BTW is an insult of every intelligent human being. Kinda like this movie!

I actually started nodding out for a bit.

The greatest waste of almost 3hours...best part was the butter popcorn.

Save your $ and wait for TV.

3.title: They made a great story in history extremely boring
3.content:
The history of story is truly fascinating! Yet the movie is drab, unexciting and stays at the same level of uninterst the whole way through the movie.

Too much focus was placed past events that had no value to the story. And then once the bombs were actually made, all we get to see is them being shipped away in crates to be used at Hiroshima & Nagasaki, yet we are shown zero wartime footage & we dont see the fallout and deaths caused by the biggest bombs the world has ever seen.

Also the high age rating ONLY comes because of the pointless nude sex scenes.

Alot of big names failed to excite us.

3.title: Music! Not for YOUR ears!
3.content:
The casting is right and acting is believable, but that horrid music in a background of a dialogue is simply atrocious! Makes it feel like a typical TV documentary with horrid cliche music that constantly rings in your ears! It was so god damn annoying I simply couldn't finish watching it.

I can't comprehend, how the movie production of such calibre didn't pay close enough attention to sound mix and overall choice of the music.

But wait! Even bigger surprise coming up next: Out of 13 total Oscar nominations, "music" has 2! :) This must be a mockery of the century! :)

What is happening with Hollywood?! Or the Academy?! How many times this same problem needs to repeat for you guys to wake up?

3.title: Arguably Christopher Nolan worst project to date
3.content: What a drag! Jesus. Three hours, really? I almost fell asleep two times during its span, my partner shook me up. Long, long, long, just boring. Goodness me, just how boring it is. If it was cut by half, it wouldn't be short enough even then. I understand the need of character development, but this? A horrible waste of time by moaning, whimpering and regret forever. Those feelings were there for sure, you just shouldn't watch them for three hours as an entertainment. The story is sublime of course, but the screenplay is bad and so is the execution. This movie, with all the hype around it, is a big let down. I am severely disappointed.

3.title: Was that Dutch??? Hoe dan?
3.content:
Great movie, well played, great special effects. Very interesting dialogues, well explained science also for people who are not experts on the subject of quantum fysics.

It is really a must see and totally worth the three hours it takes to get all the nuances and whatch the story develop until the end.

BUT...

...What a bizar choice to spend so much money and time on dialogues, but the one sentence in Dutch is truly incomprehensible.

Either do it well or leave it out, as for now it seems that the makers don't care about Dutch speaking people, which are still over 30 million in the world.

Why? It really puzzles me...

3.title: Well done but I just can't enjoy it.
3.content:
Great acting, extremely well made and constantly questions about the dangers of inventing nuclear weapons as you would expect.

However, it's mostly talking, name dropping, politics and becomes very boring to me as a result. It is also very disjointed, constantly jumping between timelines and locations.

Weirdly the exact thing I wanted to see (how the bomb was made and what Oppenheimer contributed) is not addressed so much!

Christopher Nolan apparently doesn't use much ADR and it might be the reason the dialogue mix has been pretty poor in most of his recent movies. When there IS so much talking this becomes quite a chore to have to put up with I have to say, especially for 3 hours. Swelling of sounds and music when people are talking is just irritating. I know this is done for dramatic effect at times but it's just annoying.

There is very little footage outside of court rooms and offices in this movie, thus I don't see the hype for Imax at all, but Nolan is able to achieve this exact thing for some reason. However I think he is living of past glory here with the awesome Dark Knight setpieces which were great in that format.

Just not a movie for me at all. I love Nolan's Batman movies but everything else he does is just a type of cinema I can't really enjoy.

I'm glad others have a better experience with his movies.

Your mileage may thus vary.

3.title: Ruined by constant background music
3.content: Utterly non-stop background "music" ruins this movie. I give it 3 stars. Remove the music and it gets 6 stars. Has the Director actually lost his mind? Additionally, the scrip-writers seem to think the story of the atom bomb would not be exciting enough for us plebs, so they thought they should labour Oppenheimer's third-rate marriage peccadilloes for much of the time. The rich treasure strove of the atom bomb story gets a passing glance, as we are fed hum-drum bedroom intrigue yet again. The movie add-ons give us plenty of self-congratulatory fluff from the actors and the Director, telling us they have made movie history with this one. Sadly, no. A great story told badly.

3.title: Eight movies crammed into one
3.content:
Robert Oppenheimer... so many stories! Let me tell them all! That seems to be the thinking by director Christopher Nolan, whose directing principles do not include "kill your darlings". Not judging by this three hour, oh so slow movie containing a ridiculous number of talking heads.

And so we end up with a partially very shallow story, driven by dialogue mixed sometimes with sound effects and not much else, apart from some pretty cynical nude shots of one of Oppenheimer's mistresses.

There is a lot to Oppenheimer. His political views. His brilliant physics. His affairs. His ego. His mental issues. The ethics. The persecution. And the reinstallation as a national hero.

All of this is covered pretty briefly in the movie, which in the end be centered around some politician played by Robert Downey jr. And which is by far the least interesting part of Oppenheimer's life.

Emily Blunt portrays a strong, incredibly patient wife (or maybe she had nowhere to turn) who brings some of the best questions to the screen.

Oppenheimer's dilemmas are so many, there is never time to delve into them, even through three long hours. So we are left with loads of unanswered questions, even after this slog.

The relationship with the general played by Matt Damon could have been another centre of this movie - two men with completely different background and ideas, brought together to stop all wars.

Casey Affleck drops by in a few scenes with an interesting character, never to be seen again. Einstein is present in just a few, yet important scenes, and though that works well, I felt there was more to their relationship that could have been explored.

The director gets too obsessed with McCarthyism. A shame. It is a pretty well known story, and got way too much space, I thought. There are so many depositions and testimonies, it never ends.

A two hour story centered around Oppenheimer, his wife and the general would have been so much better.

Great actors all around, Murphy must surely be an Oscar candidate. A shame the editing wasn't of the same standard.

3.title: What a waste of three hours
3.content:
I didn't like this movie.

There was too little theory to call it interesting or science popularisation - something I really liked in Interstellar.

There was a number of factual mistakes, actually unacceptable for a historic movie.

There was background music throughout the entire film, which gave it a dramatic effect. Though, to my taste - if you get to the point to require music to give the dramatic effect, your story is weak.

There was this nonsensical timeline back and forth, where the most recent time was shot, for whatever reason, in black and white - I don't even care why, I just didn't like the timeline hops.

Ultimately and most severely, the glorification of making and using a mass killing bomb - regardless of the intentions of the creators, philosophical dilemmas that haunt them later, catchy lines thrown around by literally everyone in the film - is atrocious and barbaric.

Especially during the scene of preparation for the final test, I would like Nolan to show the citizens of Hiroshima, who didn't know that their days were counted, and nothing that they did actually mattered anymore, because they would've been blown up by these "scientists".

Overall: Terrible story, bad visuals, decent play by a load of very strong actors, distracting music, too much of Cillian Murphy closeups, factual errors, no moral balance.

I wish I hadn't spent time watching this.

3.title: I think it's Not Good. The Soundtrack is a Disaster. .
3.content:
The soundtrack is annoying. It's WAY too LOUD and permeates and ruins the entire film. You struggle to hear the dialogue over really slow, boring segments of the film and the music misinterprets these scenes as being super dramatic and important!!

It's like, "Would you like a cup of coffee, Dr. Oppenheimer?

Que the music: Dah NAH!!! DAH NAH NAH NAH NAH DUH NAH NAH!!! DAAAAAA!!! DAAAAAAAAAAAAAA!!!!!!

DAH NAH NAH NAH NAH NAAAAAH!!!! BOM-BOM!!!

DAH!!! NAH NAH. AH NAH!!!

Incredibly distracting and annoying. 95% of the movie is like this. And the parts where the music finally goes silent make no sense either. Why did the music stop here? This part seems more dramatic! There is no rhyme or reason to it. It's as if someone just played a record of generic "Dramatic Cinema Music" randomly throughout the film.

When the music finally stops, it doesn't even align with what's occurring on screen at all. It's just because the last track of music was over. And then it starts again for no reason at all. Constant oppressive music. Then an argument breaks out. And the music stops!!! You can't fix boring parts with exciting music, then turn the music off when actual excitement happens!! Did anyone review this at all before it was released?

Also annoying is the constant flipping back and forth between color and black and white... we get it. The past is in black and white.

The film is very boring and over-long. It could have been done in 90 minutes. And they could have saved money by not adding a soundtrack of any kind and blowing things up more.

Overall, it's a bore. It's not much more than dramatic music played over boring dialogue read from a history book.

3.title: If you think this is challenging, try "Hiroshima, mon amour"
3.content:
After this movie's Oscar sweep, I came to it expecting much more--from the visuals, the script, the sound (incl. Film score), the acting, and the directing. Perhaps some viewers knew next to nothing about the race for the atomic bomb or about the appeal of the Communist Party to Western intellectuals in the 1930s or about the dog-eat-dog bureaucracy of secretive "war"committees in Washington D. C. Or perhaps viewers have never seen a movie by Fellini ("81/2") or Robert Altman ("Nashville"), or Alain Resnais ("Hiroshima, mon amor").

At the very least, read John Hersey's still relevant "Hiroshima," which I found far more informative and valuable than "Oppenheimer" in spite of the IMAX treatment Nolan's film has received (why the IMAX ratio? For the 5-minute scene of an experimental detonation of Oppenheimer's pet project?).

I was going to flesh out each of my categories, but I see that numerous reviewers have beat me to it. Anyway, how does one review acting when the script is so short on characterization and so preoccupied with the bomb that actors are denied the opportunity to deepen their roles? The scene with Oppenheimer meeting Truman was so brief, rushed and shallow that, for me, it represented the same deficiencies of this entire overrated project--a "glorified documentary.".

Perhaps worst of all, the Oscar noise about this film has given audiences an excuse not to take seriously the film about the virtuoso musician viewed by many as the most important musical artist in American history. Does anyone realize, or even care, that for the brief but powerful scene in which he conducts Mahler's grandiose, epic Second Symphony, Bradley Cooper had worked for 2 years to capture the distinctive conducting style of Bernstein?

If any movie was worthy of the IMAX-treatment--for visual impact as well as awesome sound--that scene alone was more radioactive than Nolan's disappointing 3-hour film about America's first big WMD. At the very least, those who applaud "Oppenheimer" for its subject matter or for the acting of Robert Downey Jr. Would be well advised to view Stanley Kubrick's "Dr. Strangelove" (with Peter Sellers'' unforgettable performance as 3 different characters).

3.title: Overall okay movie but ratings are patriotic
3.content:
Boring movie Don't recommend.

"Oppenheimer," the much-hyped historical drama, directed by a renowned filmmaker, has been making waves in the cinema world. With an abundance of positive reviews and high ratings, the film has been hailed as a patriotic masterpiece. However, after experiencing the movie firsthand, it becomes apparent that the praise is far from justified. "Oppenheimer" suffers from significant flaws that undermine its historical integrity, and while it does offer some valuable insights into history, it fails to captivate the audience's attention, ultimately proving to be a disappointing and time-wasting endeavor.

The primary issue with "Oppenheimer" is the authenticity of its content. While historical dramas often take creative liberties to enhance storytelling, this film goes far beyond that, bending and distorting historical facts to suit its narrative. This reckless approach to history raises concerns about the film's integrity as an accurate portrayal of the events surrounding the Manhattan Project and the life of J. Robert Oppenheimer. By misrepresenting key events and personalities, the movie strays from being a reliable source of information, which is a significant drawback for those looking to learn more about this crucial period in history.

Another glaring problem with "Oppenheimer" is its reliance on misplaced patriotism. Rather than delving into the complex and morally ambiguous aspects of the story, the film chooses to paint Oppenheimer and his team as unflinchingly heroic figures, all in the name of fostering a sense of national pride. This shallow portrayal not only disrespects the nuances of history but also reduces the characters to one-dimensional stereotypes, robbing the audience of a more profound emotional connection with the story.

Despite its lack of authenticity and overemphasis on patriotism, "Oppenheimer" still manages to provide a few valuable history lessons. The movie offers glimpses into the scientific breakthroughs and challenges faced during the development of the atomic bomb. Moreover, it sheds light on the ethical dilemmas that plagued the scientists involved in the project, grappling with the consequences of their inventions and the devastation they could bring upon humanity. These insights into history are undoubtedly enlightening, but they come at the expense of a coherent and engaging narrative.

Regrettably, the movie's failure to captivate its audience is its most damning flaw. Clocking in at an excruciatingly long runtime, "Oppenheimer" struggles to maintain a compelling pace. The lack of a cohesive plot and the meandering storytelling make the movie a tedious watch. Even the most dedicated history enthusiasts may find it challenging to stay invested in the film's plodding narrative, further compounded by its artificial and superficial approach to character development.

While the film's production values are undeniably impressive, with stunning cinematography and convincing period settings, these technical achievements cannot compensate for the movie's underlying issues. A visually captivating film is only as good as its story, and in the case of "Oppenheimer," the lackluster plot undermines its aesthetic appeal.

In conclusion, "Oppenheimer" is a disappointing movie that fails to live up to the hype surrounding it. Its inauthentic portrayal of historical events and reliance on shallow patriotism detract from its credibility as an educational piece. Moreover, the film's slow pace and lack of engaging storytelling make it a tedious and time-wasting experience for many viewers. Despite the movie's few redeeming qualities, such as providing insights into historical facts, it ultimately falls short of delivering a compelling cinematic experience. If you're looking for a genuinely enriching and enjoyable historical drama, "Oppenheimer" may not be the best choice.

3.title: Could have been Oscar worthy... But the sub plots made it an Atomic fail
3.content:
I went to see this movie because I'm Irish and think Cillian Murphy is amazing. I had no idea what the movie was about but wanted to support an Irish actor. I was really impressed by his unfailing acting ability (which has been flawless since the beginning of his public Career), Emily blunt also was brilliant and the other actors - but the writing and script structure was woeful.

The whole movie was written from the pov of audience preknowledge bias, so for someone like me who has never heard of Oppenihemer or have any idea about physics or atomic energy, it felt like I entered into a story half way through. In media, you always start with the 'reset button' and make the assumption that the audience knows nothing and you bring them on a journey. A majority of people will not know about these things and so get lost trying to figure it out. There were actually people in the cinema googling things because it wasn't clear and we had no idea what they were talking about.

Also, the length of the movie was madness... The story wasn't gripping enough to keep your focus for three hours. By 2hrs in people were checking their watches/phones to see what time it was. I think the sub plots and courtroom scenes with Robert Downey Jr (fab acting), could have been totally removed and if the focus had have been on one character and the story of creating the bomb and the moral dilemma he had, it would have been so much more engaging. The side story could have been explained in a few paragraphs at the end and saved us an hour of what felt like pointless b roll and a distraction from the real story which shaped humanity, not some petty narcissistic vengeance plot....

Long movies such as Lord of the Rings keep you gripped the entire time because the storyline and plot is clear And engaging - this was so boring and disappointing script writing.

The acting was fantastic, genuinely brilliant, but if they cut an hour out and stuck to Oppenihemer genius and the dilemma of living with what his intellect produced, it would have been Oscar worthy.

3.title: crap
3.content:
Christopher Nolan's Oppenheimer is a sweeping, epic, and visually stunning film that tells the story of J. Robert Oppenheimer, the man who led the Manhattan Project to develop the atomic bomb. The film is long (nearly three hours) and complex, but it is also incredibly engrossing and thought-provoking.

Nolan's direction is masterful, and he uses his trademark visual style to create a film that is both visually arresting and emotionally powerful. The film is shot in IMAX, and the images are stunning. The film's score by Ludwig Göransson is also excellent, and it perfectly complements the film's visuals.

The performances in Oppenheimer are all top-notch. Cillian Murphy gives a tour-de-force performance as Oppenheimer, and he is supported by an excellent cast that includes Emily Blunt, Matt Damon, Robert Downey Jr., and Kenneth Branagh.

Oppenheimer is not an easy film to watch. It deals with some heavy subject matter, and it is not afraid to show the dark side of science and technology. However, it is also a film that is ultimately hopeful, and it suggests that even the most destructive forces can be used for good.

Overall, Oppenheimer is a masterpiece. It is a film that is both intellectually stimulating and emotionally powerful. It is a film that will stay with you long after you have seen it.

Here are some of the things I liked about the film:

The performances were all excellent, especially Cillian Murphy's performance as Oppenheimer.

The visuals were stunning, especially the IMAX scenes.

The score by Ludwig Göransson was excellent.

The film dealt with some heavy subject matter in a thoughtful and intelligent way.

Here are some of the things I didn't like about the film:

The film was long (nearly three hours).

The film could be slow-paced at times.

The film's ending was a bit ambiguous.

Overall, I highly recommend Oppenheimer. It is a film that is both intellectually stimulating and emotionally powerful. It is a film that will stay with you long after you have seen it.
